nodes.label: Georg Bühler
variants: ゲオルグ・ビューラー
ゲオルク・ビューラー
ヨハン・ゲオルク・ビューラー
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・ビューラー
nodes.summary: Georg Bühler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, Ernst Curtius, Hermann Sauppe, and Heinrich Ewald. He taught at Elphinstone College and Bombay University before holding a professorship at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Franz Kielhorn
variants: フランツ・キールホルン
nodes.summary: Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist who studied at Göttingen, Breslau, and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey. He held chairs at Deccan College (1866–1881) and the University of Göttingen (from 1881).

nodes.label: Ernst Kuhn
nodes.image: Ernst Kuhn - Aufsätze zur Kultur- und Sprachgeschichte.jpg
nodes.description: German indologist, linguist, philologist and orientalist (1846–1920)
nodes.summary: An Indologist and linguist, Ernst Kuhn studied under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth, earning degrees from Tübingen and Halle-Wittenberg. He taught at Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, and Heidelberg, and served as professor at the University of Munich (1877–1917).

nodes.label: Lucian Scherman
nodes.summary: Lucian Scherman was an Indologist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Munich under Ernst Kuhn. He served as a curator and director at the Museum Fünf Kontinente and was a professor at the University of Munich (~1893–1936).

nodes.label: Ernst Windisch
variants: エルンスト・ヴィルヘルム・オスカー・ヴィンディシュ
エルンスト・ヴィンディシュ
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・ヴィンディシュ
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and linguistics, Ernst Windisch earned his doctorate at the University of Leipzig under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Ritschl, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held chairs at Heidelberg, Strasbourg, and the University of Leipzig.

nodes.label: Willem Caland
variants: ウィレム・カーランド
nodes.summary: Indologist Willem Caland earned his doctorate at Leiden University (1877), studying under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Carel Gabriel Cobet. He held posts at Utrecht University as lecturer (1903) and Chair of Sanskrit (1906–1929), and at Leiden University (1913–1914).

nodes.label: Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze
nodes.image: Portrait Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze (Pesne workshop).jpg

nodes.label: August Hermann Francke
nodes.summary: August Hermann Francke specialized in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the Lehrerseminar Niesky, Moravian College, and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he served as Privatdozent (1922) and extraordinary professor (1925).

nodes.label: Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres
variants: Académie des Inscriptions et Belles Lettres
Akademie der schönen Wissenschaften zu Paris

nodes.label: Alexander Johnston
nodes.summary: Alexander Johnston (1775–1849) studied law at the University of Göttingen (~1792–1795) and Lincoln's Inn (~1795–1799). He served as chief justice on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819) and founded the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

nodes.label: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron
variants: アンクティル・デュペロン
アブラアム＝ヤサント・アンクティル＝デュペロン
nodes.image: David d'Angers - Portrait d'Abraham-Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron (1731-1805), orientaliste.jpg
nodes.jawiki: アブラアム＝ヤサント・アンクティル＝デュペロン
nodes.summary: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron studied theology at the Sorbonne (~1746–1751), attended the Old Catholic Seminary of Amersfoort, and studied under Dastur Darab. Working in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies, he held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale and Institut de France.

nodes.label: Johann III Bernoulli
nodes.summary: Johann III Bernoulli worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Neuchâtel and the University of Basel under Daniel Bernoulli, earning a philosophy doctorate (~1757-1758). He was a member of the Prussian, Russian, and Danzig scientific academies.

nodes.label: Joseph Tiefenthaler
nodes.summary: Joseph Tiefenthaler was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as a Jesuit missionary in the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773 and held the post of Rector at the Jesuit High School of Agra.

nodes.label: Nathaniel Brassey Halhed
nodes.description: Civilian of the British East India Company (1751-1830)
nodes.summary: Nathaniel Brassey Halhed (1751-1830) was an Indologist and linguist who was educated at Harrow School and Christ Church, Oxford. He served as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.

nodes.label: East India Company
variants: イギリス東インド会社

nodes.label: Malabar Mission
variants: Mission an der Küste von Malabar

nodes.label: Paulinus a Sancto Bartholomaeo
nodes.summary: Paulinus a Sancto Bartholomaeo was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University, Sapienza University of Rome, and Collegio San Pancrazio. He served at the Malabar Mission (1776–1789), Congregation of the Index (1800), and Pontifical Urban University (1800).

nodes.label: University of Oxford
variants: オックスフォード大学
オックスフォード大學
Faculty of Oriental Studies, University of Oxford

nodes.label: August Fick
variants: フリードリヒ・コンラート・アウグスト・フィック
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・フィック
nodes.summary: August Fick worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen (1852–1856), where he became an extraordinary professor in 1876, later serving as an ordinary professor at the University of Breslau (1887–1891).

nodes.label: Charles Wilkins
variants: チャールズ・ウィルキンズ
nodes.jawiki: チャールズ・ウィルキンズ
nodes.summary: Charles Wilkins (1749–1836) was an Indologist who studied under Kalinatha (~1778–1784). He co-founded The Asiatic Society in 1784 and served as librarian for the East India Company (from 1770 and 1801), librarian at the India Office Library (1800), and examiner at East India Company College (1805).

nodes.label: Henry Thomas Colebrooke
variants: ヘンリー・トーマス・コールブルック
nodes.jawiki: ヘンリー・トーマス・コールブルック
nodes.summary: Henry Thomas Colebrooke was an Indologist who studied under Citrapati. He served the East India Company and Bengal Civil Service, taught Sanskrit at Fort William College (1782–1814), and was President of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1837).

nodes.label: India Office Library
variants: 東インド会社の図書館

nodes.label: William Jones
variants: ウィリアム・ジョーンズ
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ジョーンズ (言語学者)
nodes.description: Anglo-Welsh philologist and scholar of ancient India (1746–1794)
nodes.summary: William Jones was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harrow School, Middle Temple, and University College, Oxford. In 1783, he became Chief Justice at the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William, and founded The Asiatic Society in 1784.

nodes.id: I:Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William
nodes.label: Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William
variants: Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William

nodes.label: Robert Chambers
nodes.summary: Robert Chambers (1737–1803) worked in Indology and law. Educated at Lincoln College, Oxford, he was a fellow at University College, Oxford, Vinerian Professor of English Law (1766), Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William (~1789–1798), and Asiatic Society president (~1797–1798).

nodes.label: John Shore
nodes.summary: John Shore (1751–1834) was an Indology and history scholar who served as President of The Asiatic Society, succeeding William Jones.

nodes.label: Fort William College
variants: College von Fort William in Kalkutta
College of Fort William in Calcutta

nodes.label: William Carey
variants: ウィリアム・ケアリー
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ケアリー (宣教師)
nodes.description: English Baptist missionary and Particular Baptist minister (1761-1834)
nodes.summary: William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ram Ram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma. In 1801, he became Professor of Sanskrit at Fort William College, and he founded BMS World Mission, Serampore College, and several societies.

nodes.label: Otto von Böhtlingk
variants: オットー・フォン・ベートリンク
nodes.jawiki: オットー・フォン・ベートリンク
nodes.summary: Otto von Böhtlingk was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg, Berlin under Franz Bopp, and Bonn under Christian Lassen. He held long-term posts at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (1842–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).

nodes.label: Charles Rieu
nodes.summary: Charles Rieu (1820–1902) was an Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Geneva and the University of Bonn (1840–1843) under Christian Lassen, Jean Humbert, Georg Freytag, and Johann Gildemeister. He served at the British Museum from 1847 and as Adams Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: George Thibaut
nodes.summary: George Thibaut, an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber, served as director of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, principal of Muir Central College and Sanskrit College, and registrar at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta.

nodes.label: Sudhakara Dvivedi
nodes.summary: Sudhakara Dvivedi (1855–1910) was an Indologist who studied under Devakṛṣṇa. He worked at Sanskrit College and University (~1883–1890) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, serving as librarian (1883) and later professor and head of the mathematics faculty (1890, 1898–1905).

nodes.label: Horace Hayman Wilson
variants: ホーラス・ヘイマン・ウィルソン
nodes.jawiki: ホーラス・ヘイマン・ウィルソン
nodes.summary: Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas' Hospital Medical School (~1804–1807). He held posts at the East India Company, the Kolkata Mint, and served as Boden Professor of Sanscrit at Oxford (1831–1860).

nodes.label: Monier Monier-Williams
variants: モニエル・モニエル＝ウィリアムズ
nodes.jawiki: モニエル・モニエル＝ウィリアムズ
nodes.summary: Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Oxford, King's College School, and the East India Company College under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at the East India Company College and Cheltenham before serving as Oxford's Boden Professor (1860-1887).

nodes.label: Vans Kennedy
nodes.description: Scottish major-general of the British Army
nodes.summary: Vans Kennedy was an Indologist and linguist. He served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army (1817–1835) and as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1846).

nodes.label: James Prinsep
variants: ジェームズ・プリンセプ
nodes.jawiki: ジェームズ・プリンセプ
nodes.summary: James Prinsep (1799–1840) was an Indologist and historian. He worked at the Banaras Mint and the Kolkata Mint, led The Asiatic Society (1832–1838), and founded the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal.

nodes.label: Arthur Schopenhauer
variants: アルトゥル・ショーペンハウアー
アルトゥール・ショーペンハウアー
nodes.jawiki: アルトゥル・ショーペンハウアー
nodes.summary: Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Jena. After studying under Friedrich Schleiermacher, August Boeckh, and Friedrich August Wolf, he lectured at the University of Berlin between 1820 and 1831.

nodes.label: Paul Regnaud
nodes.summary: Paul Regnaud (1838–1910) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied as an élève at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and served on the faculty at the University of Lyon from around 1879 to 1908.

nodes.label: École Pratique des Hautes Études
variants: École des Hautes Études in Paris
高等研究実習院第4部門
フランス國立高等研究院
École Pratique des Hautes Études, SHP

nodes.label: John Muir
nodes.summary: John Muir was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Glasgow, East India Company College, and Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), was principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1844), and held a post at Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Johannes Klatt
nodes.summary: Johannes Klatt was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber (1868-1872) and earned a doctorate at the University of Halle (~1869-1873). From 1872 onward, he worked at the Prussian State Library, serving as custodian (1880) and librarian (1889).

nodes.label: Albrecht Weber
variants: アルブレヒト・ヴェーバー
アルブレヒト・フリードリヒ・ヴェーバー
nodes.jawiki: アルブレヒト・ヴェーバー
nodes.summary: Albrecht Weber (1825–1901) was an Indologist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under Stenzler, Lassen, Gildemeister, and Kuhn. He served at the Humboldt University of Berlin from 1848 to 1901 and was a member of the Prussian Academy.

nodes.label: Ignazio Guidi
nodes.summary: Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and history. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome, where he subsequently served as a professor from 1876 to 1919.

nodes.label: Emilio Teza
nodes.description: Italian translator, indo-europeanist, romanist, orientalist and linguist
nodes.summary: Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Anton Boller. He worked at the Marciana and Laurentian libraries, and served as Ordinarius at the universities of Bologna (1860), Pisa (~1862–1886), and Padua (~1886–1904).

nodes.label: Ram Mohan Roy
variants: ラーム・モーハン・ローイ
nodes.image: Portrait of Raja Ram Mohun Roy, 1833.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ラーム・モーハン・ローイ
nodes.description: Indian religious, social, and educational reformer, and humanitarian
nodes.summary: Ram Mohan Roy was active in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded the Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), the Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Mir'at al-Akhbar (1822), Vedanta College (1826), and the Brahmo Samaj (1828).

nodes.label: Alexander Hamilton
nodes.summary: Alexander Hamilton (1762–1824) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit (appointed 1806) and Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu Literature (appointed 1808) at the East India Company College.

nodes.label: Louis-Mathieu Langlès
variants: ルイ＝マチュー・ラングレス
nodes.jawiki: ルイ＝マチュー・ラングレス
nodes.description: French academic, philologist, linguist, translator, author, librarian and orientalist
nodes.summary: Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in Sinology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He was Chief Keeper at the Bibliothèque nationale (~1795–1824) and administrator and Persian chair at INALCO from 1795 to 1824.

nodes.label: Henry Pitts Forster
nodes.summary: Henry Pitts Forster was an Indologist and linguist. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1783 to 1815 and held the post of Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata, from 1803 to 1804.

nodes.label: Joshua Marshman
variants: ジョシュア・マーシュマン
nodes.summary: Joshua Marshman was a scholar of Sinology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Johannes Lassar (~1805–1812), and founded Serampore College in 1818.

nodes.label: Friedrich Majer
variants: フリードリヒ・マイヤー
nodes.summary: Friedrich Majer worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Jena (~1789–1792) and under Johann Gottfried von Herder, and later served as a Privatdozent at the University of Jena (~1799–1801).

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried von Herder
variants: ヨハン・ゴットフリート・ヘルダー
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・ゴットフリート・ヘルダー
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried von Herder (1744–1803) studied philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies at the University of Königsberg under Immanuel Kant. His career included posts at Collegium Fridericianum, Riga Cathedral School, the Court of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach, and Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar.

nodes.label: Friedrich von Schlegel
variants: カール・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・フォン・シュレーゲル
フリードリヒ・シュレーゲル
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュレーゲル
nodes.description: German poet, critic and scholar, editor
nodes.summary: Friedrich von Schlegel worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Göttingen under Heyne, at Leipzig, and in Paris under Hamilton and Chézy. His academic posts included positions at Jena, the University of Cologne, and TU Dresden.

nodes.label: Bibliothèque nationale de France
variants: Bibliothèque Impériale, Département des Manuscrits Orientaux

variants: College of the Honourable the East India Company, Haileybury
East India Company's College at Haileybury
Honourable East India Company's College, Haileybury
Hon. East India Company's College, Haileybury
British East India Company’s Haileybury College

nodes.label: August Wilhelm von Schlegel
variants: アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・シュレーゲル
アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・フォン・シュレーゲル
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・シュレーゲル
nodes.description: German poet, translator, critic, and writer (1767–1845)
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist August Wilhelm von Schlegel studied at Göttingen and under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Alexander Hamilton. He served as professor at the University of Jena (1795, 1798) and held the first Indology chair at the University of Bonn (1818).

nodes.label: William Robertson
nodes.description: British historian, minister of religion, and principal of the University of Edinburgh (1721-1793)
nodes.summary: William Robertson was a historian who studied divinity at the University of Edinburgh (1733–1741). He served as Principal of the University of Edinburgh from 1762 and was a member of the Royal Society of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren
nodes.summary: Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren was a historian and Indologist. After studying at the University of Göttingen (PhD 1779–1784) under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Ludwig Timotheus Spittler, he served as a lecturer and professor at Göttingen from 1784 onward.

nodes.label: Peter von Bohlen
nodes.summary: Peter von Bohlen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Halle, Bonn, and Berlin under Georg Freytag, August Wilhelm von Schlegel, and Franz Bopp. He served as professor of oriental literature at the University of Königsberg from 1825.

nodes.label: Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier
nodes.summary: Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied under the traditional teacher Ramchandra and served as a Colonel in the East India Company.

nodes.label: Othmar Frank
nodes.summary: Othmar Frank was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Paris. He held teaching posts at Banz Abbey, Kaiser-Heinrich-Gymnasium Bamberg, and professorships at the universities of Bamberg, Würzburg, and Munich.

nodes.label: University of Bamberg
variants: Indological Institute at the University of Bamberg

nodes.label: University of Paris
variants: Institute de Civilisation Indienne of the Sorbonne
Institute of Indian Civilization of the University of Paris

nodes.label: Franz Bopp
nodes.summary: Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy, Silvestre de Sacy, Karl Windischmann, and Johann Gottfried Eichhorn, attending Paris and Göttingen. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin (1821–1867).

nodes.label: Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann
variants: カール・ヴィンディシュマン
nodes.summary: Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology, having studied at Mainz and Würzburg. He taught at Gymnasium Aschaffenburg and Karls-Universität Aschaffenburg from 1803, and was appointed professor in the medical faculty at the University of Bonn in 1818.

nodes.label: Friedrich Windischmann
nodes.summary: Friedrich Windischmann worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Bonn under Lassen, Schlegel, and others, then earned a doctorate in theology at Munich. He held posts at Munich, Freising, and Munich and Freising Archdiocese.

nodes.label: Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy
variants: Antoine Isaac, Baron Silvestre de Sacy
アントワーヌ＝イザーク・シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ＝イザーク・シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
nodes.summary: Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He held professorships at INALCO and the Collège de France (1806–1838), and served as president of the Société Asiatique and perpetual secretary of the AIBL.

nodes.label: Antoine-Léonard Chézy
variants: アントワーヌ＝レオナール・ド・シェジー
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ＝レオナール・ド・シェジー
nodes.summary: Antoine-Léonard Chézy worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Louis-Mathieu Langlès and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, taught Persian at INALCO, and held the Sanskrit chair at the Collège de France (1815–1832).

nodes.label: Collège de France
variants: コレージュ・ド・フランス
Institut de Civilisation Indienne of the Sorbonne
Institut de Civilisation Indienne of the University of Paris
コレジュ・ド・フランス
Institut de Civilisation Indienne du Collège de France

variants: Seminar für Indologie und Buddhismuskunde, Universität Göttingen

nodes.label: Wilhelm von Humboldt
variants: Friedrich Wilhelm Christian Carl Ferdinand von Humboldt
Friedrich Wilhelm Christian Karl Ferdinand von Humboldt
ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
カール・ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.description: Prussian philosopher, government official, diplomat, and educator (1767–1835)
nodes.summary: Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Frankfurt (Oder), Göttingen, and Jena under teachers including Lichtenberg and Heyne, and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1809–1810), which he founded.

nodes.label: Ernst Siecke
nodes.description: born:1846|died:1935|; Siecke, Ernst (Ernst Ludwig Albert Karl), 1846-; Siecke, Ernst Ludwig Albert Karl, 1846-1935

nodes.label: Alexandre Langlois
nodes.summary: Alexandre Langlois was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy (~1815–1832). He taught classes at Lycée Charlemagne, served as an inspecteur at the Académie de Paris, and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (~1835–1854).

nodes.label: Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat
variants: ジャン＝ピエール・アベル＝レミュザ
nodes.jawiki: ジャン＝ピエール・アベル＝レミュザ
nodes.summary: Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a scholar of sinology and linguistics who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and at INALCO. He held the Chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and co-founded the Société Asiatique in 1822.

nodes.label: Jean-Louis Burnouf
variants: ジャン＝ルイ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.summary: Jean-Louis Burnouf worked in linguistics and related fields, studying under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held chairs at Lycée Louis-le-Grand (~1808–1826) and the Collège de France (1816–1844), later serving as university librarian at Sorbonne University (1840).

nodes.label: Eugène Burnouf
variants: ウジェーヌ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.jawiki: ウジェーヌ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.summary: Eugène Burnouf worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian studies, studying under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served at the Société Asiatique and held a professorship at the Collège de France from 1832 to 1852.

nodes.label: Christian Gottlob Heyne
nodes.summary: Christian Gottlob Heyne (1729–1812) was a linguistics and history scholar who studied at the University of Leipzig. In 1763 he became a professor at the University of Göttingen, where he also served as library director from 1764 to 1812.

nodes.label: Christian Lassen
variants: クリスチャン・ラッセン
nodes.jawiki: クリスチャン・ラッセン (東洋学者)
nodes.summary: Christian Lassen (1800–1876) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Oslo, Heidelberg, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He taught at the University of Bonn as Privatdozent (1830) and professor of Old Indian language and literature (1840–1876).

nodes.label: Paul Deussen
variants: パウル・ヤーコプ・ドイセン
nodes.summary: Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied under Christian Lassen and at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin. He taught at RWTH Aachen (~1873–1879), Berlin (1881–1887), and Kiel University from 1889.

nodes.label: Otto Strauß
nodes.summary: Otto Strauß was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He held professorships at Kiel (1920), the University of Calcutta (1913–1920), and the University of Breslau (1928–1935).

nodes.label: Société Asiatique
variants: フランスのアジア協会

nodes.label: Alexander von Humboldt
variants: アレクサンダー・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.image: Stieler, Joseph Karl - Alexander von Humboldt - 1843.jpg
nodes.jawiki: アレクサンダー・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.summary: Alexander von Humboldt studied at Frankfurt (Oder), TU Bergakademie Freiberg, Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, and the University of Jena. He held a post at the University of Jena from around 1794 to 1797.
