variants: テオドール・ゴルトシュテュッカー
nodes.jawiki: テーオドール・ゴルトシュテュッカー
nodes.summary: Theodor Goldstücker (1821–1872) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Königsberg, Bonn, and under Eugène Burnouf. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1851/1852 to 1872 and was president of the Philological Society (~1871–1872).

nodes.label: Friedrich Rückert
variants: フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
ヨーハン・ミヒャエル・フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
nodes.description: German poet, translator, and professor of Oriental languages (1788–1866)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Rückert worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and under Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall and Franz Bopp. He held posts at Jena, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Berlin.

nodes.label: University of Erlangen-Nuremberg
variants: International Research Consortium of "Fate, Freedom, and Prognostication in East Asia and Europe"
Internationalen Kolleg für Geisteswissenschaftliche Forschung der Universität Erlangen

nodes.label: Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff
nodes.summary: Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Evangelisches Stift Tübingen and the University of Tübingen. He held professorships at the Imperial University of Dorpat/Tartu (1803), the University of Würzburg (1817), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1818).

nodes.label: Adolf Holtzmann
nodes.summary: Adolf Holtzmann specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Munich under Othmar Frank and Johann Andreas Schmeller, Berlin, and under Eugène Burnouf (~1837–1838). From 1852 to 1870, he served as a professor at Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Johann Andreas Schmeller
nodes.summary: Johann Andreas Schmeller (1785–1852) was a linguist educated at the University of Munich (~1801–1803). He held posts at the Real Instituto Militar Pestalozziano, Kadettenkorps München, Bavarian State Library, and the University of Munich, where he became professor in 1828.

nodes.label: Heidelberg University
variants: South Asia Institute of Heidelberg University

nodes.label: Salomon Lefmann
nodes.summary: An Indologist and linguist, Salomon Lefmann studied at Münster, Berlin (Ph.D. under Franz Bopp), Paris, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Heidelberg University starting in 1866, becoming associate professor in 1870 and honorary professor in 1901.

nodes.label: University of Freiburg
variants: Confucius Institute at the University of Freiburg

nodes.label: Friedrich August Rosen
nodes.summary: Rosen was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at University College London (1828–1831) and Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1834).

nodes.label: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler
variants: アドルフ・フリードリヒ・シュテンツラー
nodes.jawiki: アドルフ・フリードリヒ・シュテンツラー
nodes.summary: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin (PhD 1826–1829), Greifswald, Bonn, and Paris under Bopp, Schlegel, Lassen, Kosegarten, and others. He worked at the East India Company (~1830–1833) and University of Breslau (1833–1872).

nodes.label: Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer
nodes.summary: Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and in Paris under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Antoine-Léonard Chézy, later holding a chair at Leipzig from 1836.

nodes.label: Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary
nodes.summary: Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bonn, Halle, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, where he habilitated and served as a lecturer (1829) and extraordinary professor of theology (1831).

nodes.label: Karl Albert Agathon Benary
nodes.summary: Karl Albert Agathon Benary was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. He held posts at the Köllnisches Gymnasium, Köllnisches Realgymnasium, and Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Köllnisches Gymnasium
variants: ケルン・ギムナジウム

nodes.label: Bernhard Hirzel
nodes.summary: Bernhard Hirzel (1807–1847) was an Indologist who studied at Zurich, Berlin under Franz Bopp (~1829–1832), Göttingen (~1832–1833), and Paris (~1833–1834). He held posts as reader, Dozent, and Privatdozent at the University of Zurich between 1833 and 1845.

nodes.label: Hermann Brockhaus
variants: ヘルマン・ブロックハウス
nodes.summary: Hermann Brockhaus worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn, the latter under August Wilhelm von Schlegel (~1828–1830). He was a professor at the University of Jena (1839) and at the University of Leipzig (~1841–1877).

nodes.label: University of Zurich
variants: Völkerkundemuseum of the University of Zurich
Institute for Social Anthropology and Empirical Cultural Studies at the University of Zurich

nodes.label: Georg Martin Dursch
nodes.summary: Georg Martin Dursch was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen and under Antoine-Léonard Chézy at the University of Paris. In 1829, he became a professor at the Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen.

nodes.label: Friedrich von Adelung
nodes.summary: Friedrich von Adelung worked in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (1787–1790). He held honorary professorships at Kharkiv and Tartu (1809), and later posts at Vienna (1824) and Utrecht (1825).

nodes.label: Johann Christoph Adelung
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・クリストフ・アーデルング
nodes.summary: Johann Christoph Adelung (1732–1806) worked in linguistics. He was educated at the Kloster Berge school and the University of Halle-Wittenberg, and held posts at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and the Saxon State and University Library Dresden (1787–1806).

nodes.label: Colin Mackenzie
nodes.image: Colonel Colin Mackenzie and his Indian pandits by Thomas Hickey.jpg
nodes.summary: Colin Mackenzie (1754–1821) studied at Dollar Academy and worked in indology, history, and archaeology. From 1810 to 1815, he served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India.

nodes.label: William Ward
nodes.description: English pioneer Baptist missionary, author, printer and translator
nodes.summary: William Ward was an Indology and religious studies figure who studied at Ewood Hall Academy under John Fawcett in 1797. He served as a missionary at the Serampore Mission (~1800–1823) and co-founded Serampore College in 1818.

nodes.label: École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr
variants: サン・シール陸軍士官学校

nodes.label: George Turnour
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ターナー (歴史家)
nodes.summary: George Turnour was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service as a Member of the Supreme Council (1818) and Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue (1820).

nodes.label: John Wilson
nodes.description: Christian missionary, orientalist, and educator in Maharashtra, India (1804-1875)
nodes.summary: John Wilson (1804–1875) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religious studies who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1842) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1869).

nodes.label: Asiatic Society of Mumbai
variants: Bombay Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society

nodes.label: Brian Houghton Hodgson
variants: ブライアン・ホートン・ホジソン
nodes.image: Brian Houghton Hodgson by Louisa Starr-Canziani.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ブライアン・ホートン・ホジソン
nodes.summary: Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology educated at East India Company College and Fort William College. He served as the British Resident in Nepal from 1833 to 1843.

nodes.label: Bhagwanlal Indraji
nodes.summary: Bhagwanlal Indraji was an Indologist and archaeologist who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University in 1884. He was an honorary member of the Royal Asiatic Society and a fellow of the University of Mumbai (1882).

nodes.label: Charles Masson
nodes.description: British East India Company soldier and explorer (1800–1853)

nodes.label: Edwin Norris
nodes.summary: Edwin Norris was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and history. He worked for the East India Company (1818–1837), the Foreign Office (1847–1866), and held assistant secretary and librarian posts at the Royal Asiatic Society between 1836 and 1861.

nodes.label: Edward Upham
nodes.summary: Edward Upham was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He held posts as a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1824–1834) and as a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London.

nodes.label: Francis Wilford
nodes.summary: Francis Wilford was an Indologist. He served as a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1822) and as secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1800–1822).

nodes.label: Eugène Jacquet
nodes.summary: Eugène Jacquet was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He pursued his studies under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from circa 1829 to 1832 and under Eugène Burnouf from circa 1832 to 1838.

nodes.label: Daniel Wright
nodes.description: Scottish surgeon and physician; resided in Nepal

nodes.label: William Wright
nodes.summary: Linguist William Wright studied at St Andrews, Halle, and Leiden. He taught Arabic at UCL and held posts at Trinity College, Hartford, Trinity College Dublin, the British Museum, and the University of Cambridge as Adams Professor of Arabic (1870–1889).

nodes.label: Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern
nodes.summary: Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern (1833–1917) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at Utrecht, Leiden (under Antonie Rutgers), and under Albrecht Weber, he held posts at Maastricht, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Leiden University (1865–1903).

nodes.label: Bunyiu Nanjio
nodes.summary: Bunyiu Nanjio was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied at Takakura Gakuryo, Otani University, and Oxford under Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and served as director of Otani University.

nodes.label: Edward Byles Cowell
variants: エドワード・バイルズ・コウェル
nodes.image: Portrait of Edward Byles Cowell by Charles Edmund Brock-1905.jpg
nodes.summary: Edward Byles Cowell worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. Cowell held posts at Sanskrit College, Presidency University, and served as professor at Cambridge (1867-1903).

nodes.label: Julius Eggeling
nodes.summary: Julius Eggeling (1842–1918) was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as secretary to the Royal Asiatic Society, taught Sanskrit at University College London, and was professor at Edinburgh (1875–1914).

nodes.label: Robert Alexander Neil
nodes.image: R A Neil-R H Lord recto.tif
nodes.summary: Robert Alexander Neil (1852–1901) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under William Duguid Geddes at Aberdeen, and under Verrall, Reid, Shilleto, and Cowell at Cambridge, later serving at Cambridge as Lecturer in Sanskrit and Pembroke College Fellow.

nodes.label: Sándor Kőrösi Csoma
variants: ケーレシ・チョマ・シャーンドル
nodes.jawiki: ケーレシ・チョマ・シャーンドル
nodes.summary: Sándor Kőrösi Csoma (1784–1842) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Bethlen Gabor College, the University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn and Johann Dominicus Fiorillo, and in Tibet, later serving as librarian at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Isaak Jakob Schmidt
nodes.summary: Isaak Jakob Schmidt (1779–1847) was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at Rostock. He held posts with the Russian Bible Society and the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences/Russian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire
nodes.description: French philosopher, journalist, statesman, and possible illegitimate son of Napoleon I of France (1805-1895)
nodes.summary: Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and Bourbon College. He served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France from 1838 to 1852.

nodes.id: I:Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques
nodes.label: Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques
variants: Académie des Sciences morales et politiques
Academy of Moral and Political Science

nodes.label: Julius Mohl
nodes.summary: Julius Mohl (1800–1876) was a scholar of Iranian and Chinese studies. He studied at Tübingen and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, and Eugène Burnouf, later serving as professor of Persian at the Collège de France (1847–1876).

nodes.label: Stanislas Julien
variants: エニャン＝スタニスラス・ジュリアン
nodes.jawiki: スタニスラス・ジュリアン
nodes.summary: Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the Lycée Pothier and Collège de France under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, later holding chairs at the Collège de France (from 1821/1832–1873) and INALCO (1863–1871).

nodes.label: Robert Lenz
nodes.summary: Robert Lenz (1808–1836) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tartu and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He taught at the Cathedral School of Tallinn and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (~1835–1836).

nodes.label: Saint Petersburg State University
variants: Faculty of Oriental Languages at St. Petersburg
Faculty of Oriental languages at St. Petersburg

nodes.label: Gaspare Gorresio
nodes.image: Gaspare Gorresio, post 1869 - Accademia delle Scienze di Torino 0015 B.jpg
nodes.summary: Gaspare Gorresio (1808–1891) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Turin, under Eugène Burnouf, and under Stanislas Julien. He held Turin's chair of Sanskrit (1852) and directed the National University Library of Turin (1859).

nodes.label: Émile-Louis Burnouf
nodes.summary: Émile-Louis Burnouf (1821–1907) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at ENS and the University of Paris under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf, later serving as professor at Nancy (1854–1867) and director of the École française d'Athènes (1867–1875).

nodes.label: Théodore Pavie
nodes.image: Théodore Pavie (1811–1896), Orientalist, friend of the artist MET 31523.jpg
nodes.summary: Théodore Pavie was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He succeeded Burnouf as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and taught Hebrew at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

nodes.label: Adolphe Regnier
nodes.summary: Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology, linguistics, and other fields, studying under Eugène Burnouf. He held positions at the Collège de France (1838), École Normale Supérieure (1841–1843), Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1855), and Palace of Fontainebleau (1873).

nodes.label: Félix Nève
nodes.summary: Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate from KU Leuven (~1834–1838) and studied under Christian Lassen, Friedrich Wilhelm Thiersch, and Eugène Burnouf. He became a professor at KU Leuven in 1841 and professor emeritus in 1877.

nodes.label: Abel Bergaigne
variants: アベル・ベルゲーニュ
nodes.summary: Abel Bergaigne was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault. He was a répétiteur at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1877) and a lecturer, then professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics, at the Sorbonne.

nodes.label: Theodor Benfey
variants: テーオドール・ベンファイ
nodes.jawiki: テーオドール・ベンファイ
nodes.summary: Theodor Benfey (1809–1881) was an Indologist and linguist who completed his education and Habilitation at the University of Göttingen. He spent his career there as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881).

nodes.label: Friedrich Max Müller
variants: マックス・ミューラー
フリードリヒ・マックス・ミュラー
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・マックス・ミュラー
nodes.description: German-born British philologist, orientalist and indologist (1823–1900)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Max Müller was an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, and Franz Bopp, among others. He was a Fellow of All Souls College and held professorships at Oxford (1850–1900).

nodes.label: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud
nodes.summary: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, holding posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (from 1824), INALCO (from 1838), and Société Asiatique (1847, 1852).

nodes.label: Heinrich Ewald
nodes.description: German orientalist, theologian, and Biblical exegete (1803–1875)
nodes.summary: Heinrich Ewald worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Eichhorn, Tychsen, and the Plancks. He held posts at Große Schule (1822–1824), Göttingen (1824–1837, 1848–1867), and the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).

nodes.id: I:Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
nodes.label: Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
variants: Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes

nodes.label: Ernst Trumpp
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・トランプ
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and linguistics, Ernst Trumpp studied under Rudolf von Roth at Evangelisches Stift Tübingen (~1846–1850). He held posts at the East India Company (~1853–1854), the University of Tübingen (1871), and the University of Munich (~1874–1885).

nodes.label: August Schleicher
variants: アウグスト・シュライヒャー
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・シュライヒャー
nodes.summary: August Schleicher worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Christian Lassen, and others, he held professorships at Charles University (1850–1857) and the University of Jena from 1857.

nodes.label: Moritz Abraham Stern
variants: モーリッツ・アブラハム・シュテルン
nodes.jawiki: モーリッツ・アブラハム・シュテルン
nodes.summary: Moritz Abraham Stern was a scholar in mathematics and linguistics. He studied at Heidelberg and Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss and Karl Otfried Müller, subsequently serving as a professor at the University of Göttingen from 1829 to 1884.

nodes.label: Rudolf von Roth
variants: ルドルフ・フォン・ロート
nodes.jawiki: ルドルフ・フォン・ロート
nodes.summary: Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Evangelisches Stift Tübingen (~1839–1843) under Heinrich Ewald and under Eugène Burnouf (~1843–1844). He held posts at the University of Tübingen as Privatdozent (1845) and Extraordinarius (1848–1895).

nodes.label: William Dwight Whitney
variants: ウィリアム・ドワイト・ホイットニー
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ドワイト・ホイットニー
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist William Dwight Whitney studied at Williams College, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, Roth, and Lepsius. He spent his career at Yale (1853, 1869–1894) and served in multiple roles for the American Oriental Society.

nodes.label: James Tod
nodes.description: 1782-1835, English officer of the British East India Company and an Oriental scholar
nodes.summary: James Tod (1782–1835) was a scholar of Indology and history who served in the East India Company and studied under Gyanchandra. He later served as Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

nodes.id: I:Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
nodes.label: Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
variants: Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain

nodes.label: Adalbert Kuhn
variants: フランツ・フェーリクス・アーダルベルト・クーン
nodes.jawiki: アーダルベルト・クーン
nodes.summary: Adalbert Kuhn, a linguist and Indologist, studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin (1833–1837). He taught and served as director at Köllnisches Gymnasium between 1837 and 1870, and was a member of the Prussian and Russian Academies of Sciences.

nodes.label: Andrzej Gawroński
nodes.summary: Andrzej Gawroński was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (1902–1906) and the University of Leipzig (~1903–1906). He taught Indo-European linguistics at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917) and contrastive linguistics at the University of Lviv (1917).

nodes.label: Stamford Raffles
variants: トーマス・スタンフォード・ラッフルズ
nodes.image: George Francis Joseph - Sir Thomas Stamford Bingley Raffles.jpg
nodes.jawiki: トーマス・ラッフルズ
nodes.summary: Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served with the East India Company (~1795–1824) and founded the Zoological Society of London in 1825, serving as its president in 1826.

nodes.label: John Crawfurd
nodes.summary: Working in linguistics and history/archaeology, John Crawfurd studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh (~1800–1803). He served as a physician for the East India Company (1803–1808) and succeeded Stamford Raffles in 1823.

nodes.label: James Fergusson
nodes.summary: James Fergusson was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1840.

nodes.label: Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences
variants: Akademie der Wissenschaften zu St. Petersburg
K. Akademie der Wissenschaften zu St. Petersburg
Imperial Academy of Sciences at St. Petersburg
Akademie der Wissenschaften in Sankt Petersburg

nodes.label: Christoph Theodosius Walther
nodes.summary: Christoph Theodosius Walther (1699–1741) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at the University of Halle in 1720 and served as a missionary with the Tranquebar Mission from around 1725 to 1739.

nodes.label: Friedrich Bollensen
nodes.summary: Bollensen, an Indologist, studied theology and Sanskrit at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1832). He held teaching posts at the Gatchina Orphanage Institute, Saint Petersburg State University (~1844–1851), the Main Pedagogical Institute, and Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Geiger
nodes.native: ヴィルヘルム・ルートヴィヒ・ガイガー
variants: ヴィルヘルム・ルートヴィヒ・ガイガー
ヴィルヘルム・ガイガー
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・ガイガー
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Geiger was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who earned his PhD under Friedrich von Spiegel at Erlangen-Nuremberg. He served as professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (from 1891) and the University of Munich (1920–1924).

nodes.label: Friedrich von Spiegel
variants: フリードリヒ・シュピーゲル
フリードリヒ・（フォン・）シュピーゲル
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュピーゲル
nodes.summary: Friedrich von Spiegel was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, Leipzig, and Jena, learning under Rückert, Lassen, and Brockhaus, among others. He was professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1849 to 1891.

nodes.id: I:Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Munich and Freising
nodes.label: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Munich and Freising
Heinrich Uhle
nodes.summary: Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Leipzig (~1863–1867), studying under Hermann Brockhaus. He subsequently served as a classical languages teacher at the Kreuzschule from 1868 to 1911.

nodes.label: Eduard Sachau
nodes.summary: Eduard Sachau worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle under Nöldeke, Brockhaus, and Fleischer. He served as professor at Vienna, Frederick William University Berlin, and director of Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen.

nodes.label: Hermann Camillo Kellner
nodes.summary: Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus from circa 1860 to 1864. He served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Gymnasium Zwickau from circa 1868 to 1904.

nodes.label: Kreuzschule
variants: Dresden College of the Sacred Cross

nodes.label: Richard Fritzsche
nodes.summary: Richard Fritzsche (1851–) was an Indology scholar who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1874–1877) and served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg (attested 1976).

nodes.label: University of Marburg
variants: マールブルク大学大学院

nodes.label: Niels Ludvig Westergaard
variants: ニルス・ルズヴィ・ヴェスタゴー
nodes.image: Niels Ludvig Westergaard by Budtz Müller.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ニルス・ルズヴィ・ヴェスタゴー
nodes.summary: Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1815–1878) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, and Oxford. He spent his career at the University of Copenhagen as Lektor (1844), professor (1850), and Rektor (1867–1868).

nodes.label: Albert Hoefer
nodes.summary: Albert Hoefer (1812–1883) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, and Berlin. He spent his career at the University of Greifswald, where he served as an außerordentlicher Professor from 1847 to 1880.

nodes.label: University of Greifswald
variants: グライフスヴァルト大学

nodes.id: I:Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache
nodes.label: Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache
variants: Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten (1792–1860) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Greifswald and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, later serving as professor at the University of Jena (1817–1824) and Greifswald (1815, 1824–1850).

nodes.label: Siegfried Goldschmidt
nodes.summary: Siegfried Goldschmidt studied Indology and linguistics under Albrecht Weber (1864) and Rudolf von Roth (~1867–1869) across Leipzig, Berlin, Göttingen, and Tübingen (Ph.D. 1867). He later served as an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg in 1881.

nodes.label: Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca
variants: Anton Edmund Xavier Evarist Wollheim da Fonseca
nodes.image: PPN663949858 Bildnis von Anton Eduard Wollheim Dafonseca.jpg
nodes.summary: Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his Dr. phil. at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1828–1831), later serving there as a Dozent (1849–1852) after a post at the Royal Danish Library (~1838–1840).

nodes.label: Richard Pischel
variants: リヒャルト・ピシェル
nodes.jawiki: リヒャルト・ピシェル
nodes.summary: Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He held professorships at Kiel (1875), Halle (1885–1902), and Berlin (1902–1908), and served as Rektor at Halle-Wittenberg.

nodes.label: Alfred Hillebrandt
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Alfred Hillebrandt earned his doctorate at the University of Breslau (~1872–1875) under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and studied at the University of Munich (~1874–1875) under Martin Haug. He held professorships at Breslau starting in 1883.

nodes.label: Adalbert Bezzenberger
nodes.summary: Adalbert Bezzenberger was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen and at the University of Munich. He served as Privatdozent at Göttingen before becoming professor of Sanskrit, prorector, and rector at the University of Königsberg.

nodes.label: Hermann Oldenberg
variants: ヘルマン・オルデンベルク
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・オルデンベルク
nodes.summary: Hermann Oldenberg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Göttingen and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin (1878), Kiel University (1889–1908), and the University of Göttingen (1908).

nodes.label: Jacob Wackernagel
variants: ヤコブ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
ヤーコプ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
nodes.jawiki: ヤーコプ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Jacob Wackernagel studied under Friedrich Nietzsche and Theodor Benfey at Basel, Göttingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at the University of Basel (1876–1902, 1915–1936) and the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).

nodes.label: Leo Meyer
nodes.summary: Leo Meyer was a linguist who studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and at Berlin under Jacob Grimm, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at Göttingen (1862–1865; chair in 1898) and Tartu/Dorpat (1865–1899).

nodes.label: Hermann Collitz
nodes.summary: Hermann Collitz was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Halle, completing doctoral work under August Fick. He held academic posts at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and Johns Hopkins University (1907–1928).

nodes.label: Friedrich Bechtel
nodes.summary: Bechtel worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Heidelberg and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and August Fick. He served as a Dozent at Göttingen (1884) and became Ordinarius in comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg in 1895.

nodes.label: Berthold Delbrück
variants: ベルトルト・デルブリュック
ベルトルト・グスタフ・ゴットリープ・デルブリュック
nodes.jawiki: ベルトルト・デルブリュック
nodes.description: German comparative linguist and Sanskrit scholar (1842–1922)
nodes.summary: A linguist and Indologist, Delbrück completed his Promotion at Berlin and Habilitation at Halle under Pott, Weber, and Bopp. He taught at Gymnasium Marienwerder (1864–1866) and Halle (1867–1870) before serving as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Jena (1870–1913).

nodes.label: University of Copenhagen
variants: University of Copenhagen, Department of Asian Studies
Institute of Oriental Studies, University of Copenhagen
Center for Subjectivity Research at the University of Copenhagen

nodes.label: August Leskien
variants: アウグスト・レスキーン
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・レスキーン
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist August Leskien studied at Leipzig, Kiel, and Jena under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He served as professor at the University of Jena (1868) and the University of Leipzig (1870–1915).

nodes.label: Leopold von Schroeder
nodes.summary: Indologist Leopold von Schroeder studied at Tartu/Dorpat under Leo Meyer, as well as at Jena and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Tartu (1882, 1890), Innsbruck (1896), and the University of Vienna (1899).

nodes.label: Anton Schiefner
variants: フランツ・アントン・シーフナー
nodes.summary: Anton Schiefner worked in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Saint Petersburg State University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences, the Russian Academy of Sciences library, and Saint Petersburg Roman Catholic Theological Academy.

nodes.label: Carl Cappeller
nodes.summary: Carl Cappeller (1840–1925) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied in Berlin, Königsberg, Leipzig, and Jena under teachers including Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, and was appointed professor at the University of Jena in 1875.

nodes.label: Karl Rosenkranz
variants: ヨハン・カール・ローゼンクランツ
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・カール・ローゼンクランツ
nodes.summary: Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied under Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel at Berlin, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held chairs of philosophy at the University of Halle (~1830–1833) and succeeded Johann Friedrich Herbart at the University of Königsberg in 1833.

nodes.label: Raymond West
variants: レイモンド・ウェスト
nodes.summary: Raymond West (1832–1912) was an Indology scholar who studied under Martin Haug (~1860–1866). He served as a puisne judge at Bombay High Court (1873–1887), Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1883–1886), and Reader in Indian Law at Cambridge (~1895–1907).

nodes.label: University of Tübingen
variants: Seminar für Indologie und Vergleichende Religionswissenschaft, Universität Tübingen

nodes.label: Martin Haug
nodes.summary: Martin Haug was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1859–1866) and later as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at the University of Munich from 1868.

nodes.label: Karl Friedrich Geldner
variants: カール・フリードリヒ・ゲルトナー
nodes.jawiki: カール・フリードリヒ・ゲルトナー
nodes.summary: Karl Friedrich Geldner was an Indologist, Iranist, and linguist. He studied at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, later holding academic posts at the University of Tübingen, University of Halle, Humboldt University of Berlin, and University of Marburg.

nodes.label: Bruno Lindner
nodes.summary: Bruno Lindner was an Indologist who studied at the University of Leipzig (1871–1873) and under Rudolf von Roth (~1874–1878). He subsequently served as a Privatdozent at the University of Leipzig from 1878 to 1919.

nodes.label: William Hodge Mill
nodes.summary: William Hodge Mill worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1809–1813), served as Principal of Bishop's College, Kolkata (~1820–1838), and held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1848–1853).

nodes.label: Richard von Garbe
nodes.summary: Richard von Garbe was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen (Ph.D. under Rudolf von Roth) and Königsberg (habilitation). He held professorships at the University of Königsberg (1878–1880; 1894) and the University of Tübingen (1895–1927).

nodes.label: Maurice Bloomfield
variants: モーリス・ブルームフィールド
nodes.jawiki: モーリス・ブルームフィールド
nodes.summary: Maurice Bloomfield was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Furman, Yale, and Johns Hopkins under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He spent his career as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

nodes.label: Julius Grill
nodes.summary: Julius Grill (1840–1930) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tübingen and Jena, completing his doctorate under Rudolf von Roth, and served as professor of Old Testament exegesis at the University of Tübingen from 1888 to 1913.

nodes.label: Adolf Kaegi
nodes.summary: Adolf Kaegi was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Zurich, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and Leipzig, as well as under Karl Friedrich Geldner. He held multiple academic posts at the University of Zurich from 1875 to 1914.

nodes.label: Heinrich Zimmer
nodes.summary: Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tübingen, Strasbourg, and Berlin under Rudolf von Roth, Siegfried Goldschmidt, Wilhelm Scherer, Albrecht Weber, and Ernst Windisch. His posts included Berlin, Greifswald (1881), Heidelberg, and Columbia University.

nodes.label: Theodor Aufrecht
variants: テーオドール・アウフレヒト
nodes.summary: Theodor Aufrecht (1822–1907) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1847). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (1861–1875) and professor at the University of Bonn (1875–1889).

nodes.label: Zeitschrift für vergleichende Sprachforschung
variants: Zeitschrift für Vergleichende Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiete des Deutschen, Griechischen und Lateinischen
Zeitschrift für vergleichende Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiet der indogermanischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Wilhelm Schulze
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Schulze worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Berlin and Greifswald under Johannes Schmidt and Heinrich Zimmer. He held chairs at the University of Marburg (1892), University of Göttingen (1895), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1932).

nodes.label: Johannes Schmidt
variants: ヨハネス・シュミット
nodes.jawiki: ヨハネス・シュミット
nodes.summary: Johannes Schmidt was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Bonn, under August Schleicher at Jena, and under Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at the University of Bonn (1868), University of Graz (1873-1876), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1876).

nodes.label: Gottfried Hermann
nodes.image: Gottfried Hermann, von Carl Christian Vogel von Vogelstein.jpg
nodes.summary: Gottfried Hermann (1772–1848) was a linguistics scholar who studied at Leipzig and Jena. He founded the Griechische Gesellschaft (1799) and served at the University of Leipzig as Professor of Philosophy (1798) and Director of the Philological Seminar (1803–1848).

nodes.label: Moriz Haupt
nodes.summary: Moriz Haupt was a scholar of linguistics and classical literature. He studied under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig, where he taught as professor from 1841 to 1851, before serving as professor at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1853.

nodes.label: Anton Westermann
nodes.summary: Anton Westermann was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig from 1825 to 1830 and served there as co-director from 1830 to 1865.

nodes.label: Reinhold Klotz
nodes.summary: Reinhold Klotz was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He completed his Habilitation at the University of Leipzig (1826–1831), where he served as an assistant professor (1832) and later as an außerordentlicher Professor (1849–1870).

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling
variants: フリードリヒ・ヴィルヘルム・ヨーゼフ・フォン・シェリング
フリードリヒ・シェリング
nodes.image: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling, 1848 daguerreotype - cropped.jpg
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シェリング
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling was a philosopher who studied at Tübingen and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena, Würzburg, Erlangen-Nuremberg, Munich, and Berlin, and served as president of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Hermann Brunnhofer
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Hermann Brunnhofer studied at Bonn, Berlin, Zurich, and under Albrecht Weber (~1867–1868). He held posts at several schools, the University of Oxford (~1872–1875), Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek (~1875–1888), Saint Petersburg State University (1891–1901), and the University of Bern (1901–1914).

nodes.label: Moriz Winternitz
variants: モーリッツ・ヴィンターニッツ
nodes.jawiki: モーリッツ・ヴィンターニッツ
nodes.summary: Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and with Friedrich Max Müller. He taught at the German University Prague from 1902 to 1934 and at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: James Robert Ballantyne
nodes.summary: James Robert Ballantyne (1813–1864) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Edinburgh. He served at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, as Principal of Benares Sanskrit College, and as India Office librarian.

nodes.label: Sampurnanand Sanskrit University
variants: ベナレス大学のサンスクリット・カレッジ

nodes.label: Jean-Baptiste Biot
variants: ジャン＝バティスト・ビオ
nodes.jawiki: ジャン＝バティスト・ビオ
nodes.summary: Jean-Baptiste Biot was a scholar active in archaeology, Sinology, and other fields who studied at the École Polytechnique. He served as professor at the École Centrale de Beauvais (1797) and Collège de France (1800–1862), and taught at the Science Faculty of Paris.

nodes.label: Ebenezer Burgess
nodes.description: United States missionary to the Mahrattas, in western India

nodes.label: Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen
variants: Christian Charles Josias, Baron von Bunsen
nodes.summary: Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen (1791–1860) was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Marburg, Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, Munich, Leiden, Copenhagen, and under Silvestre de Sacy, founding the German Archaeological Institute in 1829.

nodes.label: Ludwig Noire
variants: ルートヴィヒ・ノワレ
nodes.image: Plate 13 Ludwig Noiré, Photograph album of German and Austrian scientists (cropped).png
nodes.jawiki: ルートヴィヒ・ノワレ

nodes.label: Louis Havet
nodes.summary: A linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne, Louis Havet served as professor and Latin philology chair at the Collège de France from 1885 to 1925.

nodes.label: Kenjiu Kasawara
nodes.summary: Kenjiu Kasawara (1851–1883) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879 and was taught by Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.

nodes.label: Heinrich Wenzel
nodes.summary: Heinrich Wenzel was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He studied at Jena, Tübingen (PhD), and Leipzig, learning under Heinrich August Jäschke, Léon Feer, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Friedrich Max Müller, and held a habilitation post at Leipzig in 1887.

nodes.label: Heinrich August Jäschke
variants: ハインリヒ・アウグスト・イェシュケ
nodes.jawiki: ハインリヒ・アウグスト・イェシュケ
nodes.summary: Heinrich August Jäschke was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He served as co-director at Moravian Schools Niesky (1847) and as a missionary for the Moravian Church (1857–1868).

nodes.label: Bruno Liebich
nodes.summary: Bruno Liebich was an Indologist who studied at Munich, Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn, and Breslau. He served as professor of Indology at the University of Breslau (1921–1928) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1921–1928).

nodes.label: Archibald Edward Gough
nodes.description: (1845-1915) British educationalist, translator, editor and academic administrator
nodes.summary: Archibald Edward Gough worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Monier Monier-Williams. He held professorships at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Presidency University, and served as principal of Aliah University (~1881–1895).

nodes.label: John Pickford
nodes.summary: John Pickford was an Indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams and held a post as Professor at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: University of Madras
variants: Department of Sanskrit, University of Madras
Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras
Radhakrishnan Institute for Advanced Study in Philosophy, University of Madras
Radhakrishnan Institute for Advanced Study in Philosophy
Department of Sanskrit in the University of Madras
Centre of Advanced Study in Philosophy, University of Madras

nodes.label: Ralph T. H. Griffith
nodes.summary: Ralph T. H. Griffith was an Indologist educated at Warminster, Uppingham, and The Queen's College, Oxford, studying under Horace Hayman Wilson. He held posts at Oxford (1849), the Indian Educational Service (~1853–1885), and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University as Principal (~1861–1878).

nodes.label: Robert Needham Cust
nodes.summary: Robert Needham Cust (1821–1909) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Eton, Trinity College Cambridge, East India Company College, and Fort William College, and served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1843 to 1867.

nodes.label: Aliah University
variants: Madrassa, il Collegio maomettano di Calcutta
カルカッタ・マドラサ・ムスリム・カレッジ
カルカッタ・マドラサ

nodes.label: Presidency University
variants: Presidency College of the University of Calcutta
Presidency College der University of Calcutta
Presidency College an der University of Calcutta
コルカタ大学プレジデンシー・カレッジ

nodes.label: James Sutherland Cotton
nodes.summary: James Sutherland Cotton (1847–1918) was a scholar in history and Indology. Educated at Trinity College, Oxford, he held posts at Queens' College, Cambridge, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1871 to 1874.

nodes.label: William Wilson Hunter
variants: ウィリアム・ウィルソン・ハンター
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ウィルソン・ハンター
nodes.summary: William Wilson Hunter was a historian and Indologist educated at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1861–1887) and became vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta in 1886.

nodes.label: University of Edinburgh
variants: Professur für Sanskrit und vergleichende Sprachwissenschaft an der Universität zu Edinburg

nodes.label: Adolf Kirchhoff
nodes.summary: Adolf Kirchhoff worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1842–1846) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He held posts at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium (1846), Prussian Academy of Sciences (1860), and Berlin (~1865–1908).

nodes.label: Hermann Jacobi
variants: ヘルマン・ゲオルク・ヤコービ
nodes.summary: Hermann Jacobi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber and Johann Gildemeister. He held posts at the University of Bonn (1875, 1889–1922), the University of Münster (1876–1885), and Kiel University (1885).

nodes.label: Jarl Charpentier
nodes.summary: Jarl Charpentier (1884–1935) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Bonn and Uppsala University (PhD 1908) under Hermann Jacobi and Karl Ferdinand Johansson, whom he succeeded as professor at Uppsala in 1927.

nodes.label: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
variants: バール・ガンガーダル・ティラク
nodes.image: Young India; an interpretation and a history of the nationalist movement from within (1916) (14781987942).jpg
nodes.jawiki: バール・ガンガーダル・ティラク
nodes.description: Indian nationalist leader, writer and journalist (1856–1920)
nodes.summary: Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1856–1920) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Elphinstone College, Deccan College (B.A., 1877), and Government Law College, Mumbai (LL.B., 1879). He later taught at New English School (~1880–1885) and Fergusson College (~1885–1890).

nodes.label: Reinhold Rost
nodes.image: Reinhold Rost, Porträt mit Signatur, um 1890.jpg
nodes.summary: Reinhold Rost was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena. He taught at St Augustine's College and served as head librarian of the India Office Library from 1869 to 1893.

nodes.label: Heinrich Kiepert
nodes.description: German geographer, cartographer and university professor in Berlin (1818–1899)
nodes.summary: Heinrich Kiepert was a historian, archaeologist, and geographer. He studied at Frederick William University and the University of Jena under August Boeckh and Julius Heinrich Petermann. He held positions at Landes-Industrie-Comptoir (1845–1852) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1854, 1874).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Deecke
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Deecke worked in linguistics and Indology, earning a doctorate from Leipzig and studying in Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and others. He directed several schools, including Ernestinenschule (1855–1870), Gymnasium Bouxwiller (1884), and Lycée Albert-Schweitzer (1889).

nodes.label: Ferdinand von Eckstein
nodes.summary: Ferdinand von Eckstein worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Friedrich Creuzer (~1808–1812) and was a member of the Société Asiatique.

nodes.label: Ghent University
variants: Centre for Buddhist Studies, Ghent University

nodes.label: Josef Schick
nodes.summary: Josef Schick was a linguist who studied at Tübingen, under Albrecht Weber, and completed a PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Berlin, Bonn, Heidelberg, and served as ordentlicher Professor at the University of Munich (1896–1925).

nodes.label: Michael Viggo Fausbøll
variants: ミケール・ヴィゴ・ファウスベル
nodes.jawiki: ヴィゴ・ファウスベル
nodes.description: Danish educator, translator, orientalist and linguist (1821–1908)
nodes.summary: Michael Viggo Fausbøll was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Niels Ludvig Westergaard at the University of Copenhagen. He worked at the University of Copenhagen as an assistant librarian (1861) and later Professor of Indian Philology (1878–1902).

nodes.label: Emil Sieg
nodes.summary: Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Berlin, Tübingen, Munich, Kiel, and Göttingen under Albrecht Weber and Franz Kielhorn. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin, Kiel University, and the University of Göttingen (from 1920).

nodes.label: Walther Schubring
variants: ヴァルター・シュブリング
nodes.summary: Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich (~1900–1901) and the University of Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann (~1901–1904). He worked at the Prussian State Library (1907) and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg (1920–1951).

nodes.label: Ernst Leumann
variants: エルンスト・ロイマン
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・ロイマン
nodes.summary: Ernst Leumann worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, studying under Albrecht Weber and completing degrees at Leipzig and Strasbourg. He worked on a dictionary at Oxford and held professorships at the University of Strasbourg and University of Freiburg.

nodes.label: Luigi Suali
nodes.summary: Luigi Suali was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Bologna and under Hermann Jacobi. He held a post at the University of Pavia from around 1907 to 1951.

nodes.label: Helmuth von Glasenapp
variants: ヘルムート・フォン・グラーゼナップ
nodes.summary: Helmuth von Glasenapp worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tübingen, Munich, Berlin, and Bonn, completing his PhD under Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Bonn, Berlin, the University of Königsberg (1928–1944), and the University of Tübingen (1946–1959).

nodes.label: Yale University
variants: Yale University's Interdisciplinary Center for Bioethics
Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures at Yale University
Sheffield Scientific School at New Haven

nodes.label: Edward Elbridge Salisbury
nodes.summary: Edward Elbridge Salisbury was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Yale and under Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Bopp, Burnouf, and Lassen. He was a professor at Yale (1841-1854) and president of the American Oriental Society.

nodes.label: Charles Rockwell Lanman
nodes.image: Charles Rockwell Lanman Professor of Sanskrit Harvard.jpg
nodes.summary: Charles Rockwell Lanman (1850–1941) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Yale, Berlin, Tübingen, and Leipzig under William Dwight Whitney, James Hadley, Theodore Dwight Woolsey, James Dwight Dana, Rudolf von Roth, Albrecht Weber, Georg Curtius, and August Leskien. He taught at Johns Hopkins University (1876–1880) and Harvard University (1880–1926).

nodes.label: John Avery
nodes.summary: John Avery was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Amherst, Tübingen, Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney (~1867–1870). He served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).

nodes.label: Ernst Haas
nodes.summary: An Indologist, Ernst Haas studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber (~1852–1855), the University of Bonn (~1855–1856), and the University of Tübingen (~1856–1859). He held positions at the British Museum (1866) and University College London (1875).

nodes.label: British Museum
variants: Department of Coins and Medals, the British Museum
Department of Oriental Printed Books and Manuscripts in the British Museum
Department of Oriental Antiquities, The British Museum
Department of Manuscripts der Bibliothek des British Museum
Department of Coins and Medals at the British Museum

nodes.label: University College London
variants: Wellcome Trust Centre for the History of Medicine at University College London
Wellcome Trust Centre for the study of the History of Medicine at University College London

nodes.label: Wilhelm Pertsch
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Pertsch worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1851–1853) under Rudolf von Roth and Albrecht Weber, and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding leadership posts at Gotha's library and coin cabinet.

nodes.label: Fritz Johaentgen
nodes.summary: Fritz Johaentgen was an Indologist who studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

nodes.label: Hermann Grassmann
variants: ヘルマン・ギュンター・グラスマン
nodes.summary: Hermann Grassmann worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (1827–1830) under Friedrich Schleiermacher. He taught at several institutions in Stettin and Berlin, notably serving as a professor at Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1852 to 1877.

nodes.label: Alfred Ludwig
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Alfred Ludwig studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber and others. He held a post at Vienna (1858) before serving as professor at Charles University from 1860.

nodes.label: University of Vienna
variants: ウィーン大学インド学研究所
Institut für Indologie der Universität Wien

nodes.label: Friedrich Müller
variants: フリードリヒ・ミューラー
nodes.summary: Friedrich Müller worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna under Anton Boller, Göttingen, and Tübingen, and held posts at the Austrian National Library and the University of Vienna (1858–1866, 1869).

nodes.label: Anton Boller
nodes.summary: Anton Boller was an Indologist and linguist who became a corresponding member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1848. He served at the University of Vienna as Dozent, extraordinary professor, and ordinary professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit from 1845.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Scherer
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Scherer worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1858–1862) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1860) under Moriz Haupt, Franz Bopp, and Karl Müllenhoff, later holding chairs at Vienna (1868–1872), Strasbourg (1872), and Berlin (1877).

nodes.label: University of Cambridge
variants: Mongolia and Inner Asia Studies Unit
Department of East Asian Studies of the University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Edward Granville Browne
variants: エドワード・グランヴィル・ブラウン
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・グランヴィル・ブラウン
nodes.summary: Edward Granville Browne worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history. He studied at Cambridge under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell, becoming a Fellow at Pembroke College and Cambridge's Adams Professor of Arabic in 1902.

nodes.label: Franz Heinrich Trithen
nodes.summary: Franz Heinrich Trithen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held posts at the British Museum (~1844–1848) and as Professor of Modern Languages at the Taylor Institution (~1848–1854).

nodes.label: Friedrich Haag
nodes.description: Swiss classical philologist, linguist and teacher (1846-1914)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Haag worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler, Berlin, and Göttingen. He served at the Cathedral School of Tallinn, Kantonsschule Schaffhausen, Gymnasium Burgdorf, and the universities of Zurich and Bern.

nodes.label: Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler
nodes.summary: Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Zurich under Bernhard Hirzel, Johann Caspar von Orelli, and Hermann Sauppe. He taught at the University of Zurich (Privatdozent 1841, associate professor 1849, Ordinarius 1864) and local schools.

nodes.label: Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren
variants: Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren

nodes.label: Georg Curtius
variants: ゲオルク・クルツィウス
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・クルツィウス
nodes.summary: Georg Curtius was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Bonn and Berlin under Franz Bopp, Christian Lassen, Friedrich Ritschl, and August von Schlegel. He held professorships at Charles University, Kiel University, and the University of Leipzig from 1862 to 1885.

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg (Dr. phil. 1829). He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg, Breslau, Bonn (from 1839; also Rektor), and Leipzig (c. 1865–1875).

nodes.label: Friedrich Zarncke
variants: フリードリヒ・ツァルンケ
nodes.summary: Friedrich Zarncke was a linguistics scholar. He studied at Rostock and at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. After holding a post at Rostock, he became a privatdozent at Leipzig in 1852 and served as its Rektor (1869–1882).

nodes.label: Walter Elliot
nodes.summary: Walter Elliot worked in Indology, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the East India Company College (~1819–1820) and the College of Fort St George (~1821–1823), and served as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in the Government of Madras (1837–1842).

nodes.label: Hermann Reich
nodes.description: German writer, literary scholar and classical philologist

nodes.label: Johannes Hertel
nodes.summary: Johannes Hertel was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Leipzig (1892-1897). He taught at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (~1898-1919) and held the chair for Indian Philology at the University of Leipzig from 1919 to 1937.

nodes.label: August Friedrich Pott
variants: アウグスト・フリードリヒ・ポット
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・フリードリヒ・ポット
nodes.summary: August Friedrich Pott was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Göttingen and under Franz Bopp in Berlin, briefly lecturing at Berlin (1830) before serving as a professor of general linguistics at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1833.

nodes.label: Karl Brugmann
variants: カール・ブルークマン
nodes.jawiki: カール・ブルークマン
nodes.summary: Karl Brugmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Georg Curtius at the University of Leipzig. He held academic posts at Leipzig, the Russian Institute of Classical Philology, and the University of Freiburg.

nodes.label: Eugen Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Eugen Wilhelm was an Indologist and Iranian/Central Asian studies specialist who studied under August Schleicher from circa 1861 to 1865. He served as a professor at the University of Jena from circa 1869 to 1923.

nodes.label: Carl Gaedicke
nodes.summary: Carl Gaedicke is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Jena in 1877, where he studied under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

nodes.label: Ferdinand de Saussure
variants: フェルディナン・ド・ソシュール
nodes.image: Ferdinand de Saussure by Jullien Restored.png
nodes.jawiki: フェルディナン・ド・ソシュール
nodes.summary: Ferdinand de Saussure was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Geneva, Berlin, Paris, and Leipzig, earning his PhD in Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and others. He taught at the EPHE and served as professor at Geneva (1891–1913).

nodes.label: Eduard Sievers
variants: エドゥアルト・ジーファース
nodes.jawiki: エドゥアルト・ジーファース
nodes.summary: Eduard Sievers was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Curtius, Leskien, and Zarncke. He held professorships at the University of Jena (1871-1883), University of Tübingen (1883-1887), University of Halle (1887-1892), and University of Leipzig (1892-1922).

nodes.label: Ernst Curtius
variants: エルンスト・クルツィウス
nodes.summary: Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Bonn and Göttingen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and Christian August Brandis. He held professorships at Berlin (from 1844) and Göttingen (1855–1867), and directed the Altes Museum (ca. 1868–1896).

nodes.label: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli
variants: グラツィアディオ・イザイア・アスコリ
nodes.image: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli, post 1861 - Accademia delle Scienze di Torino 0066 B.jpg
nodes.jawiki: グラツィアディオ・イザイア・アスコリ
nodes.summary: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli (1829–1907) was a linguist and Indologist. He founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano in 1873 and served as a Professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902.

nodes.id: I:Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik
nodes.label: Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik
variants: Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik

nodes.id: I:Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen
nodes.label: Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen
variants: Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Hermann Osthoff
variants: ヘルマン・オストホフ
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・オストホフ
nodes.summary: Hermann Osthoff was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn under Hermann Usener, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He taught at Friedrichsgymnasium Kassel, the University of Leipzig, and held an Ordinarius post at Heidelberg University (1877).

nodes.label: University of Geneva
variants: ジュネーブ大学文学部

nodes.label: Pietro Merlo
nodes.summary: Pietro Merlo was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia and Giovanni Maria Bertini. From 1877 he taught at the University of Pavia, becoming ordinary professor in 1885.

nodes.label: Michele Kerbaker
nodes.summary: Michele Kerbaker was an Italian Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin under Giacomo Lignana. He taught Sanskrit at University of Naples 'L'Orientale' (1870) and philology at the University of Naples Federico II (~1876–1914).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Bardelli
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Bardelli was an Italian scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. From circa 1849 to 1865, he served as lecturer in Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa.

nodes.label: Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti
nodes.jawiki: ジュゼッペ・ガスパロ・メゾファンティ
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti was a linguist who studied at the University of Bologna. He served as professor of Oriental languages and Ancient Greek at Bologna and later became Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library in 1833.

nodes.label: Carlo Giussani
nodes.summary: Carlo Giussani (1840–1900) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) and under Giuseppe Bardelli (~1860–1863), Rudolf von Roth (~1863–1864), and Albrecht Weber (1863).

nodes.label: Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano
variants: Academy of Science and Letters (Italian: Accademia scientifico-letteraria) in Milan
ミラノ科学・文学アカデミー

nodes.label: Francisco García Ayuso
nodes.image: 1897-05-30, La Ilustración Española y Americana, Francisco García Ayuso (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Martin Haug at the University of Munich (~1870–1872).

nodes.label: Ivan Pavlovich Minaev
nodes.summary: Ivan Pavlovich Minaev (1840–1890) was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and Albrecht Weber (1863), and later served as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

nodes.label: Garcin de Tassy
variants: Joseph Héliodore Sagesse Vertu Garcin de Tassy
nodes.dewiki: Joseph Héliodore Sagesse Vertu Garcin de Tassy
nodes.summary: Garcin de Tassy (1794–1878) studied under de Sacy and Kieffer. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he held the chair for Indian language at INALCO/École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1828–1878) and directed the Société Asiatique (~1876–1878).

nodes.label: Philippe-Édouard Foucaux
variants: フィリップ・エドゥアール・フーコー
nodes.jawiki: フィリップ・エドゥアール・フーコー
nodes.summary: Philippe-Édouard Foucaux was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, the University of Paris (~1862–1894), and the Collège de France (1870–1894).

nodes.label: Léon Feer
nodes.summary: Léon Feer (1830–1902) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux and Étienne Marc Quatremère, later holding posts at INALCO (Chair of Tibetan, 1864), the Collège de France (1869–1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale (1872).

nodes.label: Michel Bréal
nodes.summary: Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as professor at the Collège de France (1864–1905) and director at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1882).

nodes.label: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel
nodes.summary: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Halle-Wittenberg and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, August Boeckh, and August Friedrich Pott. He held posts at Beheim-Schwarzbach'sche Realschule, Gymnasium Schneidemühl, and Berlin as comparative philology chair (1872).

nodes.label: Otto Blau
nodes.summary: Otto Blau was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Between 1848 and 1852, he studied at the University of Halle, the University of Leipzig, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott.

nodes.label: József Budenz
nodes.summary: József Budenz was a linguist who studied at Marburg and Göttingen, the latter under Theodor Benfey. He worked at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and served as full professor of Altaic comparative linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University.

nodes.label: Ferdinand Justi
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Justi worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. After studying under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen and completing his Habilitation at Marburg, he served at Marburg as associate professor, full professor, and Rektor (1887–1888).

nodes.label: Ludwig Lange
nodes.summary: Ludwig Lange was a scholar in linguistics and history who studied at Leipzig and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He served as a professor of classical philology at Charles University (1853–1859), University of Giessen (1859), and University of Leipzig (1871–1880).

nodes.label: Theodor Nöldeke
nodes.jawiki: テオドール・ネルデケ
nodes.summary: Theodor Nöldeke (1836–1930) was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Göttingen under Benfey and Ewald. He held professorships at Kiel University (1864–1872) and the University of Strasbourg (1872–1906).

nodes.label: John Peile
nodes.summary: John Peile was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge and under Theodor Benfey. He served at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1860–1910), as Cambridge Reader of Comparative Philology (1884–1891), and as president of Newnham College (~1890–1909).

nodes.label: Émile Senart
variants: エミール・シャルル・マリー・スナール
nodes.summary: Émile Senart (1847–1928) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He became a professor at the Collège de France and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1908–1928).

nodes.label: Johann Ernst Wilhelm Osiander
nodes.summary: Johann Ernst Wilhelm Osiander (1829–1864) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as Repetent at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren (~1853–1854) and Tübingen (1857–1860).

nodes.label: Carl Siegfried
nodes.summary: Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. Educated at Halle and Bonn, he was a Sanskrit professor at Trinity College Dublin and later held a theology professorship for Old Testament at Jena (1875–1901).

nodes.label: Julius Euting
nodes.summary: Julius Euting (1839–1913) was a scholar of linguistics and archaeology who studied at Tübingen under Ernst Heinrich Meier and Rudolf von Roth. He served as director of the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire (1871; 1900–1909) and professor at the University of Strasbourg from 1880.

nodes.label: Matthias von Lexer
nodes.summary: Matthias von Lexer worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Graz, Berlin, and Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held posts at St. Anne's Gymnasium in Kraków (1855–1857), Freiburg (~1868–1870), Würzburg (1868), and Munich (1890).

nodes.label: Sophus Bugge
nodes.summary: Sophus Bugge was a linguist who studied at Oslo, Copenhagen, and Berlin, as well as under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Uppsala University and the University of Oslo, where he became Professor of Comparative Philology and Old Norse in 1866.

nodes.label: Angelo De Gubernatis
nodes.summary: Angelo De Gubernatis was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Turin and Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Florence (1863–1891) and Rome (1890).

nodes.label: Henri Gaidoz
nodes.summary: Henri Gaidoz was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber, and held posts at the École Libre des Sciences Politiques (1872–1908) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 1876).

nodes.label: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Elphinstone College, Mumbai, and Göttingen, learning under Martin Haug. He held professorships at Elphinstone and Deccan College, and served as Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1893–1894).

nodes.label: Heinrich Hübschmann
nodes.summary: Heinrich Hübschmann worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Jena under August Schleicher, Tübingen, Leipzig, and Munich under Martin Haug. He held posts at the University of Leipzig (1876) and the University of Strasbourg (1877).

nodes.label: Julius Jolly
nodes.summary: Julius Jolly (1849–1932) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Munich, Berlin, Leipzig, and Würzburg under Martin Haug and Albrecht Weber, and served as a professor at the University of Würzburg from 1877 to 1920.

nodes.label: University of Florence
variants: Istituto dei Studi Superiori in Florenz
Istituto degli studii superiori in Florenz
Istituto di studi superiori di Firenze

nodes.label: Sapienza University of Rome
variants: Università degli Studi di Roma "La Sapienza"

nodes.label: Trinity College Dublin
variants: ダブリン大学トリニティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Frédéric Baudry
nodes.summary: Frédéric Baudry was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held librarian positions at the Institut National Agronomique and Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, and served as administrator of the Bibliothèque Mazarine from 1874 to 1885.

nodes.label: Peter Peterson
nodes.summary: Peter Peterson was an Indologist. Between ~1873 and 1899, he held posts as Professor at the University of Mumbai and as Sanskrit Professor at Elphinstone College.

nodes.label: James Burgess
nodes.summary: James Burgess worked in Indian history and archaeology. Educated at the universities of Glasgow and Edinburgh, he served as Director and later Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1886-1889) and founded Indian Antiquary and Epigraphia Indica.

nodes.label: Robert Caesar Childers
nodes.summary: Robert Caesar Childers (1838–1876) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Wadham College, Oxford, and under Yatramulle Dhammarama, he worked as sub-librarian at the India Office (1872) and professor of Pali at University College London (~1872–1876).

nodes.label: Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle served as Direttore at Aliah University (circa 1881–1899) and secretary at The Asiatic Society in 1891.

nodes.label: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
nodes.description: Philosopher, academic, writer, translator, entrepreneur, social reformer and philanthropist (1820-1891)
nodes.summary: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (1820–1891) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He held posts at Fort William College, Sanskrit College, and served as director at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Austrian Academy of Sciences
variants: kaiserl. Akademie der Wissenschaften in Wien
オーストリア科学アカデミー
Österreichische Akademie der Wissenschaften Institut für Kultur- und Geistesgeschichte Asiens

Austrian Academy of Sciences in Vienna
Institute for Medieval Research of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Vienna
Institute of Social Anthropology, Austrian Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: Henri Hubert
nodes.summary: Henri Hubert specialized in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and École Normale Supérieure, and held posts at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1927), and École du Louvre (~1906–1927).

nodes.label: Marcel Mauss
nodes.summary: Marcel Mauss worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Bordeaux, EPHE, Leiden, Utrecht, and Oxford under Durkheim, Meillet, Lévi, and Foucher. He held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1901, 1914–1940) and Collège de France (1931–1940).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Grube
variants: ヴィルヘルム・グルーベ
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・グルーベ
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Grube was a scholar of sinology and linguistics who studied at Saint Petersburg and earned a PhD at Leipzig under Georg von der Gabelentz. He held posts at the Asiatic Museum, Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and Berlin University (1884–1908).

nodes.label: Karl Florenz
variants: カール・フローレンツ
カール・アドルフ・フローレンツ
nodes.jawiki: カール・フローレンツ
nodes.summary: Karl Florenz specialized in Japanology, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Leipzig and Berlin under Ernst Windisch, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Friedrich Max Müller, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut, and the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: University of Tokyo
variants: 東京大学文学部印度哲学梵文学科
東京大学大学院人文社会系研究科
東京大学文学部印度哲学科
