東京大学大学院人文社会系研究科博士課程
東京帝大文学部言語学科

nodes.label: Fitzedward Hall
nodes.summary: Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist educated at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Sanskrit College and University before holding a chair at King's College London and serving as librarian at the India Office.

nodes.label: Arthur Berriedale Keith
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Arthur Berriedale Keith studied at Edinburgh under Julius Eggeling and at Balliol College, Oxford, under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He worked at the Colonial Office (~1901–1914) before serving as professor at Edinburgh from 1914 to 1944.

nodes.label: Junjirō Takakusu
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist
nodes.summary: Junjirō Takakusu was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, Berlin, and Leipzig under Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He was a professor and president at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Otto Stein
nodes.summary: Otto Stein was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Charles University under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. He held posts at the Oriental Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences and at Charles University as professor of Indian philology (1930–1939).

nodes.label: Joseph Estlin Carpenter
variants: エストリン・カーペンター
nodes.summary: Joseph Estlin Carpenter worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at University College School and the University of London, he served at Harris Manchester College, Oxford as President (ca. 1876–1915) and at the University of Oxford (ca. 1889–1915).

nodes.label: Robert Chalmers
nodes.description: British civil servant, and Pali and Buddhist scholar (1858-1938)
nodes.summary: Robert Chalmers (1858–1938) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Oriel College, Oxford, and under T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (1924–1931).

nodes.label: Richard Morris
nodes.summary: Richard Morris was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Battersea Training College. He served as Winchester lecturer at King's College School (1869), master at Dedham Grammar School, and headmaster of the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888).

nodes.label: Edmund Hardy
nodes.summary: Edmund Hardy was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. After studying under Kuno Fischer at Heidelberg, he served as a professor of philosophy at Freiburg (1885–1893) and held a chair at Fribourg (1894–1898).

nodes.label: Dines Andersen
nodes.summary: Dines Andersen (1861–1940) was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll. He served as professor of Indian philology there from 1903 to 1927.

nodes.label: William Henry Denham Rouse
nodes.summary: Indologist and Buddhist scholar William Henry Denham Rouse studied at Cheltenham College, Regent's Park College, and Cambridge. He held teaching posts at Bedford, Cheltenham, and Rugby, and served as headmaster of The Perse School (1902–1928).

nodes.label: Caroline Rhys Davids
variants: C. A. F. リス・デヴィッズ
nodes.summary: Caroline Rhys Davids (1857–1942) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar. She studied at UCL and under T. W. Rhys Davids. She was Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society (1907–1942) and lectured at Manchester (1910–1913) and SOAS (1918–1933).

nodes.label: Sylvain Lévi
nodes.summary: Sylvain Lévi (1863–1935) was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, University of Paris, Collège de France (1894–1935), and Maison Franco-Japonaise (1926–1928).

nodes.label: Louis de La Vallée Poussin
variants: ラ・ヴァレー・プーサン
L・ドゥ・ラ・ヴァレー・プーサン
Louis Étienne Joseph Marie de La Vallée Poussin
Louis Étienne Joseph Marie de La Vallée-Poussin
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Louis de La Vallée Poussin studied at Liège, KU Leuven, the Sorbonne, and Leiden. He held Sanskrit chairs at Liège (1891–1892) and Ghent University (1893–1929).

nodes.label: Godefroy de Blonay
nodes.description: Swiss linguist and member of the International Olympic Committee (1869-1937)

nodes.label: Henry Clarke Warren
nodes.summary: Henry Clarke Warren worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard, Johns Hopkins, and Oxford, working under Charles Rockwell Lanman in 1879, Maurice Bloomfield circa 1881–1884, and T. W. Rhys Davids.

nodes.label: Vincent Arthur Smith
nodes.image: The Early History of India by Vincent Arthur Smith.jpg
nodes.summary: Vincent Arthur Smith was an Indologist and historian who earned a doctorate from Trinity College Dublin (-1919). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1871–1900) and later as a curator at the University of Oxford and St John's College (~1910–1920).

nodes.label: Sarat Chandra Das
variants: サラト・チャンドラ・ダス
nodes.image: Sarat Chandra Das, C.I.E. photo from Journey to Lhasa and Central Tibet (page 10 crop).jpg
nodes.jawiki: サラト・チャンドラ・ダス
nodes.description: Indian scholar of Tibetan language and culture (1849-1917)
nodes.summary: Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at Presidency University and University of Calcutta, he was director of the Bhutia Boarding School (1874) and Tibetan translator for the Government of Bengal (1881–1904).

nodes.label: Cecil Bendall
nodes.summary: Cecil Bendall was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and under Theodor Benfey. He worked at the British Museum, British Library, University College London, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge.

nodes.label: Unrai Wogihara
nodes.summary: Unrai Wogihara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. He later held posts at the University of Tokyo, Taisho University, and Shiba Junior & Senior High School.

nodes.label: Vasily Radlov
variants: ヴァシーリー・ヴァシーリエヴィチ・ラドロフ
ヴィルヘルム・ラドロフ
nodes.summary: Vasily Radlov was a linguist and archaeologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Jena. He directed the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and the Peter the Great Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography / Kunstkamera (1894–1918).

nodes.label: Alexander von Staël-Holstein
variants: Alexander Wilhelm Freiherr Staël von Holstein
nodes.summary: Alexander von Staël-Holstein studied under Richard Pischel at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology, he taught at Peking University (1918–1929) and directed the Sino-Indian Institute from circa 1927 to 1937.

nodes.label: Rudolf Seydel
nodes.summary: Rudolf Seydel worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1853–1857) and subsequently held a post there from circa 1860 to 1892.

nodes.label: Masaharu Anesaki
nodes.summary: Masaharu Anesaki was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo, Kiel, and with scholars including Deussen and Oldenberg. He served as a director and library head at the University of Tokyo (1904; 1923–1934).

nodes.id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.label: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
variants: G. A. van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.image: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga.jpg
nodes.enwiki: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.dewiki: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University (~1893–1901). He held academic posts at Utrecht University (1924–1957) and the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944).

nodes.label: Richard Fick
nodes.summary: Richard Fick (1867–1944) was an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Kiel University (~1885–1888). He worked at Kiel University Library, the Prussian State Library, and served as director of Göttingen State and University Library (~1921–1932).

nodes.label: Richard Schmidt
nodes.summary: Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner and his habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He served there as Privatdozent (~1898–1906) and became ordinary professor at the University of Münster in 1910.

nodes.label: Keshub Chunder Sen
nodes.summary: Keshub Chunder Sen was a religious studies and Indology figure who studied at Hindu School, Presidency University (~1853-1858), and the University of Calcutta, and founded the Brahmo Samaj of India.

nodes.label: Helmer Smith
nodes.summary: Helmer Smith worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala and under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner, later holding posts at Lund University (1921) and as professor at Uppsala University (1936–1947).

nodes.label: Louis Finot
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, Louis Finot studied at the École Nationale des Chartes. He served at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1892–1898), directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient from 1898, and taught at the Collège de France (1920–1930).

nodes.label: Édouard Huber
nodes.summary: Édouard Huber (1879–1914) worked in sinology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Sorbonne and under Sylvain Lévi and Johann Baptist Schibenegg, later directing the China and Indochina department at the EFEO from 1901 to 1905.

nodes.label: Kaigyoku Watanabe
nodes.summary: Kaigyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a doctorate at the University of Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann (1900–1907) and later served as professor at Taisho, Toyo, and Kokushikan universities, and principal at Shiba High School.

nodes.label: Robert Gauthiot
nodes.summary: Robert Gauthiot (1876–1916) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1898–1904) and became a member of the Société Asiatique in 1909.

nodes.label: Max Lindenau
nodes.summary: Max Lindenau was an Indologist who studied at the University of Leipzig until 1913 under Ernst Windisch.

nodes.label: Ludwig Heller
nodes.summary: Ludwig Heller was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He served as an associate professor at the University of Greifswald (1904) and held a post at the University of Tartu (1918).

nodes.label: Theodor Zachariae
nodes.summary: Theodor Zachariae (1851–1934) was an Indologist educated at Leipzig, Göttingen under Benfey, and Greifswald. He served as professor at Greifswald (1883) and extraordinary professor of comparative linguistics at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).

nodes.label: Hermann Beckh
nodes.summary: Hermann Beckh worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kiel University (~1899–1901) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1902–1907, PhD), later holding posts at Berlin and the Prussian State Library (~1908–1921), and the Kiel Institute for the World Economy.

nodes.label: Theodor Bloch
nodes.summary: Theodor Bloch (1867–1909) was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1888–1893) under Ernst Windisch, and later studied under Georg Bühler (~1893–1895).

nodes.label: Hermann von Schlagintweit
nodes.summary: Hermann von Schlagintweit was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields who studied at the University of Munich (~1844–1848). He held a teaching post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1851–1854) and was a member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Emil Schlagintweit
nodes.summary: Emil Schlagintweit (1835–1904) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Franz Joseph Lauth and was elected a corresponding member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1864.

nodes.label: Georg Morgenstierne
variants: Georg Valentin von Munthe af Morgenstierne
ゲオルク・モルゲンスティールネ
nodes.dewiki: Georg Valentin von Munthe af Morgenstierne
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・モルゲンスティールネ
nodes.summary: Georg Morgenstierne was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated in Oslo, Bonn, and Berlin under Sten Konow, Heinrich Lüders, and Wilhelm Schulze, he was a professor at Gothenburg (1930–1937) and Oslo (1937–1962).

nodes.label: Sten Konow
nodes.summary: Sten Konow was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Oslo, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg (doctorate ~1891–1893 under Richard Pischel). He was a professor at Oslo (1910–1937) and Hamburg (1914–1919).

nodes.label: Frederick William Thomas
nodes.summary: Thomas was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at King Edward's School, Trinity College, Cambridge, and under Edward Byles Cowell. He served at the India Office Library (1898–1927) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

nodes.label: Tukaram Laddu
nodes.summary: Tukaram Laddu worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Halle until 1912 and held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1920).

nodes.label: Edward Denison Ross
variants: エドワード・デニソン・ロス
nodes.image: Edward Denison Ross by John Lavery (1856-1941).jpg
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・デニソン・ロス
nodes.summary: Edward Denison Ross worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied at UCL and Strasbourg under Theodor Nöldeke. He held posts at UCL, Aliah University, the British Museum, and SOAS University of London (1916-1937).

nodes.label: Satis Chandra Vidyabhusan
nodes.summary: Satis Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Sarat Chandra Das and at Calcutta University (PhD), later serving as Principal of Sanskrit College and Professor of Sanskrit and Pali at Presidency University.

nodes.label: Ganganatha Jha
nodes.summary: Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sanskrit College. Working in Indology and philosophy, he served at Muir Central College (1902–1918), Sanskrit College (1918), and as Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad University (1923–1932).

nodes.label: Edward Washburn Hopkins
nodes.summary: Edward Washburn Hopkins was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Columbia and Leipzig under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch, he taught at Columbia and Bryn Mawr before serving as professor at Yale University from 1895 to 1926.

nodes.label: Arthur Coke Burnell
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Arthur Coke Burnell studied at King's College London under Theodor Goldstücker, as well as under Michael Viggo Fausbøll and Heinrich August Jäschke. He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1860 to 1880.

nodes.label: Peter von Bradke
nodes.summary: Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Dorpat/Tartu, Tübingen, Jena, Leipzig, and Giessen, under scholars including Leo Meyer and Rudolf von Roth. He served as associate professor at the University of Giessen (1886–1896).

nodes.label: Prafulla Chandra Ray
nodes.jawiki: プラフラ・チャンドラ・レイ
nodes.description: Bengali chemist, educationist, poet, historian, industrialist and philanthropist (1861–1944)
nodes.summary: Prafulla Chandra Ray was an Indology and history scholar educated at Vidyasagar College, Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Edinburgh. He held posts at Presidency University (1911–1916) and the University of Calcutta (Palit Professor of Chemistry, 1936).

nodes.label: George Melville Bolling
variants: ジョージ・M・ボーリング
nodes.summary: George Melville Bolling was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Johns Hopkins University. He held professorships at the Catholic University of America (1895–1913) and Ohio State University (1914–1939), and served as president of the Linguistic Society of America (1931).

nodes.label: Bapu Deva Sastri
nodes.description: Indian scholar in Sanskrit and mathematics and translator
nodes.summary: Bapu Deva Sastri (1821–1900) was an Indologist who studied at Sehore Sanskrit School and under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundhiraja Misra, and Sevarama. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

nodes.label: S. M. Natesa Sastri
nodes.summary: S. M. Natesa Sastri was an Indologist who studied at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras (~1877–1881). He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1884–1890) as an assistant to Robert Sewell.

nodes.label: Debendranath Tagore
variants: デヴェンドラナート・タゴール

nodes.label: Rabindranath Tagore
variants: ラビンドラナート・タゴール
nodes.jawiki: ラビンドラナート・タゴール
nodes.summary: Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was a philosopher who studied at University College London (~1878–1880). He founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.

nodes.label: Arthur Anthony Macdonell
variants: アーサー・アンソニー・マクドネル
nodes.jawiki: アーサー・アンソニー・マクドネル
nodes.summary: Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Oxford, Tübingen, and Leipzig. He was Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1888, a fellow at Balliol from 1899, and vice president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1921–1924).

nodes.label: LeRoy Carr Barret
nodes.summary: LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Washington and Lee University (~1894–1898) and completed his studies at Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903) under Maurice Bloomfield.

nodes.label: Franklin Edgerton
variants: フランクリン・エジャトン
フランクリン・エジャートン
nodes.jawiki: フランクリン・エジャートン
nodes.summary: Franklin Edgerton worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. After earning his Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield (1906–1909), he served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Salisbury Professor at Yale University (1926–1953).

nodes.label: Bernhard Geiger
nodes.summary: Bernhard Geiger (1881–1964) specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at Vienna, Bonn, Charles, Göttingen, and Heidelberg. He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1909–1938), the Iranian Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (1951–1953).

nodes.label: Willibald Kirfel
nodes.summary: Indologist Willibald Kirfel completed his PhD and habilitation at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He worked at Bonn University Library (1911–1921) and served as ordentlicher Professor at the University of Bonn from 1922, succeeding Jacobi.

nodes.label: Alfons Fürst
nodes.summary: Alfons Fürst, a scholar of religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology, completed his Promotion and Habilitation under Norbert Brox at the University of Regensburg. He held positions at the University of Bamberg and the University of Münster.

nodes.label: Robert Zimmermann
nodes.summary: Robert Zimmermann worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at St Beuno's and Humboldt University of Berlin, later serving as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and head of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

nodes.label: Leiden University
variants: Leiden University, Department of Indo-European Comparative Linguistics (VIET)

nodes.label: Friedrich Otto Schrader
nodes.summary: Friedrich Otto Schrader worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1898–1902), led the Adyar Library and Research Centre (1905–1916), and was professor of Indology at Kiel University (1921).

nodes.label: Heinrich Lüders
variants: ハインリヒ・リューダース
nodes.jawiki: ハインリヒ・リューダース
nodes.summary: Heinrich Lüders was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Munich and Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held posts at Oxford, Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1909–1935), also serving as secretary of the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Edward Joseph Thomas
nodes.summary: Edward Joseph Thomas was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a master's at the University of St Andrews under John Burnet and studied at Cambridge, later working at Cambridge University Library (~1909–1939) and the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Shwe Zan Aung
nodes.summary: Shwe Zan Aung was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a B.A. from the University of Rangoon in 1891. In 1895, he studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw.

nodes.label: Pe Maung Tin
nodes.native: ဖေမောင်တင်
nodes.summary: Pe Maung Tin was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford. He served as professor and principal at Rangoon (1912; 1937–1946) and principal at the University of Adult Education (1947).

nodes.label: Benimadhab Barua
nodes.description: Bengali Writer, Indologist, and pundit of Pali and Buddhism (1888-1948)
nodes.summary: Benimadhab Barua worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at institutions including Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of London. He served as Lecturer in Pali (1913–1914) and Professor (1918–1948) at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Hakuju Ui
nodes.image: Recent portrait of Dr. Hakuju Ui.jpg
nodes.summary: Hakuju Ui was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu, and later in Tübingen, Oxford, and Cambridge. He held teaching posts at Tokyo, Tohoku, Komazawa (president, 1941), and Nagoya.

nodes.label: Frank Lee Woodward
nodes.summary: Frank Lee Woodward was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from Sidney Sussex College. He served as principal of Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translated texts for the Pali Text Society while studying under Caroline Rhys Davids.

nodes.label: Fyodor Shcherbatskoy
nodes.jawiki: フョードル・イポリトビッチ・シチェルバツコイ
nodes.summary: Fyodor Shcherbatskoy was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi. He was a professor at Saint Petersburg State University (~1900–1941) and founded the Institute of Buddhist Culture.

nodes.label: Chimanlal Dahyabhai Dalal
nodes.description: Sanskrit scholar and librarian of the Central Library in Baroda

nodes.label: Ramesh Chandra Majumdar
nodes.summary: Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was an Indologist and historian educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He held faculty posts at Calcutta and Dhaka, where he was also Provost, and served as Principal at Banaras Hindu University and Nagpur University.

nodes.label: A. B. Gajendragadkar
nodes.summary: An Indologist, he served as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as a lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College Dharwad.

nodes.label: S. Kuppuswami Sastri
nodes.summary: S. Kuppuswami Sastri was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Madras. He served as principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, Thiruvaiyaru, and later as professor at Presidency College and Annamalai University.

nodes.label: Minzu University of China
variants: Central Nationalities University (Zhongyang minzu daxue) in Beijing

nodes.label: Shōren Ihara
nodes.summary: Shōren Ihara was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as an assistant professor at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1965, 1977) and was a member of the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

九州帝国大学国史学科

nodes.label: Amba Kulkarni
nodes.summary: Amba Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology. She completed a PhD at the University of Hyderabad (ending 2009) and later served there as a professor (attested 2018–2026).

nodes.label: Gérard Huet
nodes.summary: Gérard Huet works in computational linguistics and Indology. He studied under George Ernst and Maurice Nivat, and served as a professor at Inria from around 1974.

nodes.label: Sachin Kathale
nodes.summary: Sachin Kathale works in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned an M.Phil. from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and has served as a teacher at Samskrita Bharati.

nodes.label: Sorbonne Nouvelle University
variants: University of Paris III: Sorbonne Nouvelle

nodes.label: Nathan W. Hill
nodes.summary: Nathan W. Hill is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and sinology who studied at Harvard (~2001-2006) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff. He held posts at SOAS (~2008-2019) and Trinity College Dublin (from ~2019).

nodes.label: Cameron David Warner
nodes.summary: Cameron David Warner works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Yudru Tsomu and has held posts at Middlebury College, Dickinson College, and Aarhus University.

nodes.label: Dieter Gunkel
nodes.summary: Dieter Gunkel is a linguist and Indologist who studied at UCLA (~2004–2010). He held posts at the University of Munich (2010–2017), the University of Richmond (2017–2024), and the University of California, Los Angeles (2024).

nodes.label: Peking University
variants: Department of Chinese Language and Literature, Peking University
北京大學東方學研究院

nodes.label: Amrith Krishna
nodes.summary: Amrith Krishna works in computational linguistics and Indology. He held a post at the University of Cambridge and worked at Uniphore (attested 2023) and Learno.AI (attested 2024–2025).

nodes.label: Peter M. Scharf
nodes.summary: Peter M. Scharf is an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona. He held posts at Brown University (2006–2009) and the Sanskrit Library (President attested 2014; attested 2024–2025).

nodes.label: Rajeev Sangal
nodes.description: Professor and author Known for his work in processing of human languages in Computational Paninian Grammar (CPG) framework.
nodes.summary: Rajeev Sangal works in computational linguistics and Indology. He studied at IIT Kanpur and the University of Pennsylvania, and held posts at IIT Kanpur (1982–1998), IIIT Hyderabad (2002–2013, 2018–2022), and IIT (BHU) Varanasi (2013–2018).

クイーンズランド大学

nodes.label: Shagun Sinha
nodes.summary: Shagun Sinha works in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. He completed doctoral studies supervised by Girish Nath Jha (attested 2022) and was taught by Shashi Prabha Kumar, Ram Nath Jha, and several other instructors.

nodes.label: Gopal Lal Meena
nodes.summary: Gopal Lal Meena is an Indologist who taught Shagun Sinha. His career includes posts as Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Professor Emeritus at the University of Delhi (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yoshiyuki Kawazoe
nodes.summary: Yoshiyuki Kawazoe specializes in computational studies and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at Tohoku University (~1972–1975) and served there as an assistant (1975–1990), professor at the Institute for Materials Research (1990–2012), professor emeritus (2012), and senior research fellow (2018).

nodes.label: Silvia Luraghi
nodes.summary: Silvia Luraghi is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Turin (~1976–1980). She held posts at the University of Turin (~1988–1993), Università degli Studi Roma Tre (~1993–1999), and the University of Pavia (~1999).

nodes.label: Hakuyu Hadano
nodes.summary: Hakuyu Hadano was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held posts at Tohoku University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1953–1959) and later became professor emeritus.

Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Sanskrit Vidyapeeth

nodes.label: Benjamin Luk Williams
nodes.summary: Benjamin Luk Williams works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Harvard University in 2017 and held a post at Naropa University.

ハーヴァード大学大学院

nodes.label: Jens-Uwe Hartmann
variants: イエンス＝ウヴェ・ハルトマン
nodes.summary: Jens-Uwe Hartmann (born 1953) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Munich and completed his habilitation at Göttingen (~1985–1992). He held professorships at Humboldt University (1995–2001), Free University of Berlin (~1995–1999), and Munich (1999–2018).

nodes.label: Kazunobu Matsuda
nodes.summary: Kazunobu Matsuda (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and under Shiro Matsumoto, later holding faculty posts at Otani University (attested 1985–1989) and Bukkyo University (attested 1995–2024).

nodes.label: Klaus Röhrborn
nodes.summary: Klaus Röhrborn works in Iranian/Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig, Hamburg (under Bertold Spuler, Wolfgang Lentz, and Annemarie von Gabain), and Giessen. He held posts at Giessen, Göttingen Academy of Sciences, and Göttingen University.

nodes.label: Mitsuyo Demoto
nodes.summary: Mitsuyo Demoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University and held a post at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).

nodes.label: Makio Ueno
nodes.summary: Makio Ueno works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning a PhD from Otani University by 2009, Ueno held posts there as an assistant professor (attested 2010–2012) and faculty member (attested 2022), alongside affiliation with the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hironori Tanaka
nodes.summary: Hironori Tanaka specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. A former doctoral student at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020), Tanaka held a post there and is attested as a lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.

デリー大学大学院ヒンディー語ヒンディー文学専攻

nodes.label: F. B. J. Kuiper
nodes.summary: F. B. J. Kuiper was an indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht and Leiden universities under teachers including Willem Caland. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1939–1972) and directed the Kern Institute (~1946–1977).

nodes.label: Jean Philippe Vogel
nodes.summary: Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Amsterdam. He worked with the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and served as Professor at Leiden University and Director of the Kern Institute.

nodes.label: Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck
nodes.summary: Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck (1866–1951) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Stedelijk Gymnasium Haarlem and Leiden University (~1884–1888). He was an assistant professor at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and a professor at Leiden University (1899–1926).

nodes.label: Nicolaas van Wijk
nodes.summary: Nicolaas van Wijk (1880–1942) was a linguist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1898–1902) and Moscow State University (~1903–1904). He held a post at Leiden University in 1913.

nodes.label: Eugenius Marius Uhlenbeck
nodes.summary: Eugenius Marius Uhlenbeck was a linguist who studied at Leiden University from circa 1932 to 1939. He then served as a professor at Leiden University from 1950 to 1983.

nodes.label: Theodoor Paul Galestin
nodes.summary: Theodoor Paul Galestin (born 1907) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Nicolaas Johannes Krom (~1930–1936) and served as professor of South and Southeast Asian archaeology and ancient history at Leiden University from 1957.

nodes.label: Frederik David Kan Bosch
nodes.summary: Bosch worked in Indology and archaeology after studying under Jacob Samuel Speyer and Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. He headed the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936) and held professorships at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

nodes.label: Jacob Samuel Speyer
nodes.summary: Indologist Jacob Samuel Speyer completed his PhD at Leiden University (~1867–1872) under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He held posts at the University of Amsterdam (1877–1889), University of Groningen (1888–1903), and Leiden University (1903–1913).

nodes.label: Nicolaas Johannes Krom
nodes.summary: Nicolaas Johannes Krom worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and held posts at Leiden University in 1919 and from 1925 to 1945.

nodes.label: Utrecht University

nodes.summary: Gadjin Nagao specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, studying at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hani and Susumu Yamaguchi. He held Kyoto University's Chair of Buddhist Studies (1935–1971) and also served as a professor at Kyushu University (1956–1958).

nodes.label: Noritoshi Aramaki
nodes.summary: Noritoshi Aramaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University. He held posts at Kyoto University, Osaka University, the Institute for Research in Humanities at Kyoto University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.

nodes.label: Shodo Fujita
nodes.summary: Shodo Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1978 to 1987 under Shoko Takeuchi. He held an affiliation as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University, attested between 1995 and 2013.

nodes.label: Toru Funayama
nodes.summary: Toru Funayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held academic posts at Kyushu University and Kyoto University, including its Institute for Research in Humanities.

nodes.label: Nicholson T. Collier
nodes.summary: Nicholson T. Collier works in religious and Buddhist studies and completed a PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.

nodes.label: Paul J. Griffiths
nodes.summary: Paul J. Griffiths (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Oxford and Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota, he held professorships at the University of Chicago, Notre Dame, University of Illinois Chicago, and Duke University.

nodes.label: Otto Rosenberg
variants: オットー・ローゼンベルグ
オットー・カール・ユリウス・ローゼンベルク
nodes.jawiki: オットー・カール・ユリウス・ローゼンベルク
nodes.summary: Otto Rosenberg specialized in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and sinology. He studied at Saint Petersburg under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Sergey Oldenburg, at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi, and with Rudolf Lange. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University from 1911 to 1919.

nodes.label: Enga Teramoto
nodes.summary: Enga Teramoto was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He later served as a lecturer at Kyoto University (~1908–1916) and as a professor at Otani University in 1915.

nodes.label: Susumu Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Susumu Yamaguchi (1895–1976) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University, the University of Paris, and Kyoto University, and served as a professor at Otani University (1934–1964).

nodes.label: Taiken Kimura
nodes.summary: Taiken Kimura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue. He served as professor of Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo from 1912.

nodes.label: Ryugen Tanemura
nodes.summary: Ryugen Tanemura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and indology. Posts include part-time lecturer at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), researcher at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014), and faculty member at Taisho University (attested 2014–2026).

nodes.label: Kazuo Kano
nodes.summary: Kazuo Kano (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned an MA at Kyoto University under Katsumi Mimaki and a PhD at Hamburg under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, later teaching at Koyasan University and Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Kenichi Kuranishi
nodes.summary: Kenichi Kuranishi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held appointments as an associate professor at Taisho University (attested 2013–2026) and as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Toru Tomabechi
nodes.summary: Toru Tomabechi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, and has held posts at the University of Lausanne, the Institute of Humanities Information Studies, and the National Institute for Digital Humanities.

nodes.label: Diwakar Acharya
variants: ディヴァーカル・アーチャーリヤ
nodes.summary: Diwakar Acharya (born 1969) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated under Ramananda Giri and at the University of Hamburg, he taught at Nepal Sanskrit University, Hamburg, and Kyoto University before joining the University of Oxford in 2016.

nodes.label: Somadeva Vasudeva
nodes.summary: Somadeva Vasudeva specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, later serving as a professor at Kyoto University (2011) and as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit at Columbia University.

nodes.label: Yuko Yokochi
nodes.summary: Yuko Yokochi specializes in Indology. She studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Groningen under Minoru Hara, Katsuhiko Kamimura, and Hans T. Bakker. She held posts as associate professor and professor at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Kazuyoshi Soma
nodes.summary: Kazuyoshi Soma (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Meiji Yamada. In 1987, he was attested as a lecturer at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Kenryu Tsukinowa
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Kenryu Tsukinowa studied at Bukkyo University. He served as professor at Koyasan University (1926), Shuchiin University (1955), and Seizan Junior College, and became emeritus professor at Ryukoku University in 1956.

nodes.label: Edward Hamilton Johnston
nodes.summary: Edward Hamilton Johnston worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Eton and New College, Oxford, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1909–1924) and later as a professor at the University of Oxford (~1937–1942).

nodes.label: Zuiei Ito
nodes.summary: Zuiei Ito (1942–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University from 1980 to 2013 and also lectured at other universities.

Yutaka Yuda
nodes.summary: Yutaka Yuda (1931–2009) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Hajime Nakamura at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1969), earned a doctorate from Rissho University (1990), and held assistant professor posts at Kyoritsu College of Pharmacy (1969) and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).

nodes.label: Kanagawa University
variants: 神奈川大学外国語学部

nodes.label: Moriichi Yamazaki
nodes.summary: Moriichi Yamazaki works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University and the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman. He later served as associate professor at Sendai National College of Technology and president of Hosen Gakuen College.

nodes.label: Zuiryu Nakamura
nodes.summary: Zuiryu Nakamura (1915–1995) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and Kenryu Tsukinowa, and served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University beginning in 1945.

nodes.label: Shiro Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Shiro Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Komazawa University, Waseda University, the University of Tokyo, and under Zuiho Yamaguchi and Yasuaki Nara. He was an assistant and later professor at Komazawa University (1995–2020).

nodes.label: Yasuaki Nara
nodes.summary: Yasuaki Nara (1929–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno, and at the University of Calcutta. He served as professor emeritus at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Zuiho Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Zuiho Yamaguchi (1926–2023) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying at the University of Tokyo, EPHE, and under Jacques Bacot and Rolf Alfred Stein. He held posts at CNRS, Toyo Bunko, and was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1970–1986).

nodes.label: Akira Hirakawa
nodes.summary: Akira Hirakawa specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto, later becoming a professor there (1962–1975). He also held posts at Waseda University and the ICPBS.

nodes.label: Zesho Machida
nodes.summary: Zesho Machida worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts as bettō at Kuon-ji (attested 1990) and professor emeritus at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).

nodes.label: Shinkan Murakami
nodes.summary: Shinkan Murakami is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Ryujo Yamada, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as professor (~1974-1996) and professor emeritus at Tohoku University.

nodes.label: Masao Shizutani
nodes.summary: Masao Shizutani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as an assistant professor at Josai University and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, where his post was attested in 1974.

nodes.label: Harunaga Isaacson
variants: ハルナガ・アイザクソン
nodes.jawiki: ハルナガ・アイザクソン
nodes.summary: Harunaga Isaacson works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Groningen and Leiden under Hans T. Bakker, Tilmann Vetter, and Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at Groningen, Oxford, Pennsylvania (2002–2006), Hamburg (from 2000), and the IIBS (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Francesco Sferra
nodes.summary: Francesco Sferra specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Raffaele Torella (~1989–1999) and held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2000), University of Naples Federico II (attested 2010), and Series Minor (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Michael Witzel
nodes.summary: Michael Witzel is an Indologist and linguist who studied under scholars including Paul Thieme, Karl Hoffmann, and F. B. J. Kuiper. He directed the Nepal Research Centre (1972–1978) and held Sanskrit chairs at Leiden (1978–1986) and Harvard (1986, 2022).

nodes.label: Josho Nozawa
nodes.summary: Josho Nozawa worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying under Susumu Yamaguchi. He held a professorship at Koyasan University, attested in 1950.

nodes.label: Junko Sakamoto-Gotō
nodes.summary: Junko Sakamoto-Gotō works in Indology and linguistics. Her academic career includes posts at Tohoku University, attested in 2005, and Ryukoku University, attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Toshifumi Goto
nodes.summary: Toshifumi Goto is a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, studying under Karl Hoffmann and others. He has held professorships at Osaka University and Tohoku University.

nodes.label: George Chemparathy
nodes.summary: George Chemparathy is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Erich Frauwallner (~1966–1969) and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and as a professor at Utrecht University (~1974–1993).

nodes.label: Loyola College, Chennai
variants: マドラス大学ロヨラ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Tetsuro Watsuji
nodes.summary: Tetsuro Watsuji (1889–1960) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studying at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He was Professor of Ethics at Kyoto University (1925–1949) and held the Ethics chair at the University of Tokyo (1934–1949).

nodes.label: Nichidatsu Fujii
nodes.summary: Working in religious and Buddhist studies, Nichidatsu Fujii studied at Rissho University, Taisho University, Kogi Shingonshu Rengo Daigaku, Horyu-ji, and Kennin-ji, and founded Nipponzan-Myōhōji.

nodes.label: Akihiko Akamatsu
nodes.summary: Akihiko Akamatsu specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, Sorbonne Nouvelle/University of Paris, and under Yuichi Kajiyama. He held faculty posts at Kyushu University, Kyoto University, and Kyoto University's Hakubi Center.

nodes.label: Tomoyuki Uno
nodes.summary: Tomoyuki Uno works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as a special researcher for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 1998) and as an assistant professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

nodes.label: Chikushi Jogakuen University
variants: 筑紫女学園大学人間文化研究所

nodes.label: Kyo Kano
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, Kyo Kano studied at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna. Kano held posts as an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and associate professor at Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Shin Fujinaga
nodes.summary: Shin Fujinaga works in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 1992) and as an associate professor at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested 2000).

nodes.label: National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College
Masamichi Ichigo
nodes.summary: Masamichi Ichigo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University, Kyoto University (D.Litt. 1985) under Gadjin Nagao, and taught at Kyoto Sangyo University (professor 1981) and Otani University (professor 1997).

nodes.label: Leslie S. Kawamura
nodes.summary: Leslie S. Kawamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther. He spent his career as a professor at the University of Calgary (~1976–2010).

Kosei Ishii
nodes.summary: Kosei Ishii (born 1950) works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Waseda University under Akira Hirakawa, and later held positions at Waseda, Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006), and Komazawa University (2006–2021).

nodes.label: Yuichi Kajiyama
nodes.summary: Yuichi Kajiyama worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and Vienna under J. Kashab, Satkari Mookerjee, John Brough, and Erich Frauwallner. He held posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and Soka University.

nodes.label: Takeshi Hasegawa
nodes.summary: Takeshi Hasegawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Ryukoku University (attested 1998) and served as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ekyo Uno
nodes.summary: Ekyo Uno is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Uno held posts as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji-ha Shōgakuin (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Shin'ichi Tsuda
nodes.summary: Shin'ichi Tsuda is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and earned his Ph.D. at Australian National University under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham, later teaching at ICPBS (~1996-2008).

nodes.label: Kosei Tada
nodes.summary: Kosei Tada (1938–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies and studied at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1969). He held a post at Taisho University (~1971–2009) and served as board chairman of the Society for the Study of Buddhist Culture (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Michael Hahn
nodes.summary: Michael Hahn (1941–2014) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Wilhelm Rau and earned his PhD at the University of Marburg, where he later held the Indology and Tibetology chair. He also held posts at the University of Bonn.

nodes.label: Gudrun Bühnemann
variants: グドルン・ビューネマン
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Bühnemann studied at Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner and with Michael Hahn. She held research posts in India and Japan before becoming a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.

nodes.label: Janice Dean Willis
nodes.summary: Janice Dean Willis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD in Indic and Buddhist Studies at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and served as a professor at Wesleyan University from 1977 to 2013.

nodes.label: Daniel M. Stuart
nodes.summary: Daniel M. Stuart specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He received his Ph.D. from UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt and held appointments at the University of South Carolina (attested 2017) and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yiu Wing Chan
nodes.summary: Yiu Wing Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Hong Kong by 2013, studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.

nodes.label: So Takahashi
nodes.summary: So Takahashi studied Indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo, earning an M.A. He held posts at Meijo University as an associate professor (attested 1977–1978) and professor (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Yoshihide Yoshizu
nodes.summary: Yoshihide Yoshizu (1943–2014) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata and Shoson Miyamoto. He served as a lecturer (1971) and professor (2001) at Komazawa University and conducted overseas research at Virginia (1985).

nodes.label: Nobuchiyo Kotani
nodes.summary: Nobuchiyo Kotani (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Otani and Kyoto Universities under Yuichi Kajiyama, Noritoshi Aramaki, and others, he served as Professor at Otani University (~1980–2010) and president of Otani Junior College (~2006–2010).

nodes.label: Robert F. Rhodes
nodes.summary: Robert F. Rhodes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. A doctoral candidate at Harvard University, he served as a professor at Otani University, attested during 1993–2000 and 2012–2014.

nodes.label: Fumio Ouchi
nodes.summary: Fumio Ouchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He received his doctorate from Otani University, where he served as assistant professor (attested 1996) and later professor (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Kei Okusa
nodes.summary: Kei Okusa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate in literature at Otani University, where he is attested as a faculty member in 2026.

nodes.label: Atsuyoshi Keika
nodes.summary: Atsuyoshi Keika works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer (attested 1990) and later as a professor (attested 2014) at Otani University.

nodes.label: Kenryu Nishio
nodes.summary: Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who completed doctoral studies at Otani University. He has served as an emeritus professor at Hanazono University (attested 2014 and 2026).

nodes.label: Taikyo Tanigawa
nodes.summary: Taikyo Tanigawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Koyasan University and Toyo University (Ph.D., 1994). He has served on the faculty at Koyasan University, where he became a professor (attested 2005, 2026).

nodes.label: Tissa Rajapatirana
nodes.summary: Tissa Rajapatirana is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD (1966–1974) at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong. He subsequently held a post at ANU's Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies (attested 1988).

nodes.description: Buddhist abbot of Dharma Drum Mountain
nodes.summary: Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University (~1997–2005) under Kenyo Mitomo. He also studied under Sheng Yen, Hoyo Watanabe, and several other teachers.

nodes.label: Mary Anne Cartelli
nodes.summary: Mary Anne Cartelli works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Philip B. Yampolsky.

nodes.label: Philip B. Yampolsky
nodes.summary: Philip B. Yampolsky was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned his degrees from Columbia University and studied under Yoshitaka Iriya, later serving as an adjunct associate professor, librarian, and lecturer at Columbia (1968–1996).

nodes.label: Seishi Karashima
nodes.summary: Seishi Karashima (1957–2019) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University. He was a researcher at the Eastern Institute and later professor and director at IRIAB, Soka University (~1996–2019).

nodes.label: Keikyo Nakamikado
nodes.summary: Keikyo Nakamikado is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Nakamikado was affiliated with Bukkyo University as a research collaborator (attested 2003) and with the Chion'in Jodo Sect Research Institute as a researcher (attested 2015).

nodes.summary: Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (2003) and researcher at Bukkyo University (2003), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (2006), and Musashino University (2006).

nodes.label: Jundo Nagashima
nodes.summary: Jundo Nagashima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seitatsu Matsunami, Alexis Sanderson, and doctoral supervisor Paul Williams at the University of Bristol. Nagashima served as a lecturer at Taisho University, attested between 2006 and 2017.

nodes.label: Yasuo Matsunami
nodes.summary: Yasuo Matsunami was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1995-2006) and was an advisor to the Śrāvakabhūmi Study Group until 2010.

nodes.label: Koshin Suzuki
nodes.summary: Koshin Suzuki (born 1959) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also held an attested researcher post from 1995 to 1998.

nodes.label: Midori Nishino
nodes.summary: Midori Nishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and later served there as a researcher (attested 2010–2015).

nodes.label: Takako Abe
nodes.summary: Takako Abe works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Abe held posts at Taisho University as a lecturer (attested 2013–2017) and faculty member (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Akira Saitō
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Akira Saitō studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikidō Takasaki and at the Australian National University. He held positions at Mie University, the University of Tokyo, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Sungdoo Ahn
nodes.summary: Sungdoo Ahn is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (-2001) under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Director at Geumgang University and Professor at Seoul National University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Eun-young Choi

nodes.summary: Heinz Bechert was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Munich, Hamburg, and Mainz under Erich Frauwallner and Ernst Waldschmidt, holding posts at Saarland University, Mainz, and as Chair of Indology at the University of Göttingen (1965–2000).

nodes.label: Hajime Sakurabe
nodes.summary: Hajime Sakurabe was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, completing his PhD in 1967. He served at Otani University (1949–1986, becoming professor in 1971) and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1959).

nodes.label: Taku Fukuda
nodes.summary: Taku Fukuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hajime Sakurabe (~1986–1993). He has held positions at Doho University, Nagoya University, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Samuels
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Samuels specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Karen C. Lang (attested 2002), also studying under W. S. Karunatillake, and served at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Karen C. Lang
nodes.summary: Karen C. Lang specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, later serving as faculty at the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: W. S. Karunatillake
nodes.summary: W. S. Karunatillake was a scholar in linguistics and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard Divinity School in 1998.

nodes.label: Yukari Kimura
nodes.summary: Yukari Kimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Kenyo Mitomo and was attested in 2026 as a part-time lecturer at Rissho University affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Kenyo Mitomo
nodes.summary: Kenyo Mitomo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley. He served as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University (1968-2015) and held a visiting post at UC Berkeley in 1987.

nodes.label: Minori Nishimura
nodes.summary: Minori Nishimura (b. 1947) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD at Taisho University under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, later serving as associate professor there, researcher at Sanko Cultural Institute, and with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Shunkyo Katsumata
nodes.summary: Shunkyo Katsumata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held a post at Toyo University and served at Taisho University (~1946–1983), where he became professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Koun Kajiyoshi
nodes.summary: Koun Kajiyoshi (1904–1984) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Taisho University.

nodes.label: Shindai Sekiguchi
nodes.summary: Shindai Sekiguchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1928-1934). He later served as a professor at Taisho University (~1957-1977) and Hanazono University (~1977-1982).

nodes.label: Seiren Matsunami
nodes.summary: Seiren Matsunami (born 1903) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930) under Naoshiro Tsuji and under Walther Schubring (~1936–1938). He held professorships at Kyushu University (~1952–1967) and Rissho University (~1969–1974).

nodes.label: Yasuhiko Nagano
nodes.summary: Yasuhiko Nagano (born 1946) is a Tibetologist and linguist educated at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (PhD). He served as professor and professor emeritus at the National Museum of Ethnology, among other administrative roles.

nodes.label: Soshu Nishioka
nodes.summary: Soshu Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Nishioka held a post as professor at Shitennoji University, attested in 2000 and 2015.

nodes.label: Satoru Harada
nodes.summary: Satoru Harada is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo (~1971–1973), was a research member at Toyo Bunko (attested 1978), and served as a professor at Kokushikan University (~2007–2017).

nodes.label: Hajime Kitamura
nodes.summary: Hajime Kitamura was a linguist and Tibetologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada and held posts at the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986), Reitaku University (president, 1986), and the Toyo Bunko (1958; 1990–2001).

nodes.label: Tokan Tada
nodes.summary: Tokan Tada was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Akita High School and Sera Monastery (1913–1923), he held posts at the University of Tokyo (1924), Tohoku University (1925), and Toyo Bunko (1956).

nodes.id: I:National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics
nodes.label: National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics
Takeshiro Kuraishi
nodes.summary: Takeshiro Kuraishi was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1925–1928). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1939–1949) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958).

nodes.label: Akira Suganuma
nodes.summary: Akira Suganuma was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University. He later held academic positions at Toyo University from around 1962 to 1994 and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies in 1981.

nodes.label: Kyoshun Todo
nodes.summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies, Kyoshun Todo held positions at Bukkyo University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1962) and later as a professor (attested 1988–1992).

nodes.label: Narimoto Tamayama
nodes.summary: Narimoto Tamayama (born 1923) is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1974 and 1988).

nodes.label: Xianlin Ji
nodes.description: Chinese academic, linguist, historian, translator and university teacher (1911-2009)
nodes.summary: Xianlin Ji (1911–2009) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tsinghua and under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg at Göttingen (PhD). He served as professor, vice president, and Life Professor at Peking University, and held leadership posts at CASS and CAS.

nodes.label: Florin Deleanu
variants: デレアヌ フロリン
nodes.jawiki: デレアヌ フロリン
nodes.summary: Florin Deleanu works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bucharest, Waseda, Peking University, and Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen), and held posts at Kansai Medical University and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Zhongxin Jiang
nodes.summary: Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) studied under Xianlin Ji at Peking University (~1960–1965). A specialist in Indology and Buddhist studies, he held positions at Peking University, Soka University (1999), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Kanno
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Kanno (born 1952), a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy, studied at the University of Tokyo. He held leadership and editorial roles at the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology and posts at Toho Kenkyukai and Soka University.

nodes.label: Noriyuki Kudo
nodes.summary: Noriyuki Kudo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Bukkyo University. He has held positions at Bukkyo University, the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology, and Soka University (attested 2000–2026).

nodes.label: Akira Yuyama
nodes.summary: Akira Yuyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji, Akira Hirakawa, Jan Willem de Jong, and Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts at the Australian National University, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Soka University.

nodes.label: Michael Zimmermann
variants: ミヒャエル・ツィンマーマン
nodes.summary: Michael Zimmermann is an expert in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Hamburg (PhD) and Soka University under Lambert Schmithausen and others, he held posts at Stanford, directed the Nepal Research Centre (2002), and became professor at Hamburg.

nodes.label: Yusho Wakahara
nodes.summary: Yusho Wakahara specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After graduate studies at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami, Wakahara held teaching posts at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and Ryukoku University (attested 1987–1999 as assistant professor, 2011–2013 as professor).

nodes.label: Reimon Yuki
nodes.summary: Reimon Yuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijo Tokiwa (~1924–1927). His career included professorships at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia and Kyoto Women's University, as well as an emeritus post at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Katsumi Mimaki
nodes.summary: Katsumi Mimaki (born 1947) studied Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology at Kyoto University and in Paris. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (1992; 1996–2010) and became a member of the Japan Academy in 2006.

nodes.label: Masaaki Nohnin
nodes.summary: Masaaki Nohnin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts as an assistant professor (attested 2003) and later professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Osamu Hayashima
nodes.summary: Osamu Hayashima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg. He held professorships at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Akifumi Naito
nodes.summary: Akifumi Naito works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji-ha Shōgakuin, and under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts at Ryukoku University (~1993), Shinshu Otaniha Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

nodes.label: Yuhiko Katsuzaki
nodes.description: Japanese bhikku and Buddhist studies scholar
nodes.summary: Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and later served as the university's president from around 2011 to 2015.

nodes.label: Yoshihiko Sakurai
nodes.summary: Yoshihiko Sakurai specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2001) and was later affiliated with Ryukoku University and the Kyogaku Dendo Research Center (both attested 2003).

nodes.label: Zensho Kitagawa
nodes.summary: Zensho Kitagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1976) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Rissho University, and is affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Kaji
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Kaji (b. 1936) is a Sinologist and philosopher. Educated at Kyoto and Tohoku Universities, he served as a professor at Osaka University (1984–1998), president of Koshien Junior College (1998–1999), and institute director at Ritsumeikan University (2008–2015).

nodes.label: Kosho Kawamura
nodes.summary: Kosho Kawamura (born 1924) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Shunkyo Katsumata, Koshiro Tamaki, and Yoshiro Tamura, later serving at Toyo University (~1957–1995), Minobusan, Hamamatsu, and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

nodes.label: Kosho Mizutani
nodes.summary: Kosho Mizutani (1928–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies, studying at Ryukoku University (~1952–1956) and Bukkyo University. He served as professor and president of Bukkyo University (~1979–1989) and chaired the boards of Bukkyo Kyoiku Gakuen and Tokai Gakuen.

nodes.label: Ichijo Ogawa
nodes.summary: Ichijo Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959), where he later held a post attested from 1977 to 1993, and taught at Otani University Junior College (attested 1978).

nodes.label: Hiroo Kashiwagi
nodes.summary: Hiroo Kashiwagi (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963) and taught Waso Harada. He served as professor at Matsusaka University (~1982) and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College.

nodes.label: Jason Birch
nodes.summary: Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied at the University of Sydney and earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (2013) under Alexis Sanderson. He was a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Gareth Sparham
nodes.summary: Gareth Sparham, a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, studied at McGill, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and UBC (Ph.D. under Ashok Narhar Aklujkar). He later taught Tibetan language at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

nodes.label: Akira Sadakata
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, Akira Sadakata studied under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, completing studies at the University of Tokyo and the University of Paris. He held faculty posts at Tokai University from around 1971 to 2007.

nodes.label: Mayumi Nasu
nodes.summary: Mayumi Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She held posts as a lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2011–2013) and as a specially appointed associate professor at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Shuchiin University
variants: 種智院大学密教資料研究所

nodes.label: Sudan Shakya
nodes.summary: Sudan Shakya works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a professorship at Shuchiin University, attested between 2013 and 2026.

nodes.label: Étienne Lamotte
variants: エティエンヌ・ラモット
エティエンヌ・ラモート
nodes.summary: Étienne Lamotte (1903–1983) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Louis de La Vallée Poussin, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He served as chargé de cours at KU Leuven (1932–1974) and taught at Saint-Louis University, Brussels.

nodes.label: Hubert Durt
nodes.summary: Hubert Durt specialized in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology, studying under Étienne Lamotte (~1959–1968). He held posts at EFEO (~1970–2001), Hōbōgirin Institute (~1978–2004), and International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2011).
