nodes.label: Mitsuji Fukunaga
nodes.summary: Mitsuji Fukunaga was a philosopher and Sinologist educated at Hiroshima Higher Normal School and Kyoto University. He taught at Kitano High School, Aichi University of Education, Kyoto University (1961–1982), University of Tokyo (1974–1979), Kansai University, and University of Kitakyushu.

nodes.label: Yoshitaka Iriya
nodes.summary: Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) studied Sinology and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, Nagoya University, and Kyoto Sangyo University.

nodes.label: Shinjo Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Shinjo Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Hajime Nakamura and Dale Maurice Riepe, attending Columbia University. He taught as a Fulbright lecturer at University at Buffalo and served as professor at the University of Tsukuba (1975-1997).

nodes.label: Kangei Okamoto
nodes.summary: Kangei Okamoto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris (c. 1928–1933). He later held a non-regular appointment at Tokyo National Museum from around 1939 to 1948.

nodes.label: Takamatsu Yoshie
nodes.summary: Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Waseda University, and the University of Paris. Yoshie taught at Waseda Junior and Senior High School and served at Waseda University as a lecturer and later as Dean of Letters in 1930.

nodes.label: Satoshi Hiraoka
nodes.summary: Satoshi Hiraoka specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned degrees including a doctorate from Bukkyo University and studied at the University of Michigan, being taught by Takao Kagawa, Luis O. Gómez, and others. He became president of Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2014.

nodes.label: Kyoto Bunkyo University
variants: 京都文教大学人間学部
京都文教大学総合社会学部

nodes.label: Yoshifumi Honjo
nodes.summary: Yoshifumi Honjo (born 1951) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Kyoto University, he served as a professor at Kobe Women's University (2000–2004), Bukkyo University (2014), and Otani University (2010), and as head priest at Anshin-in (2006).

nodes.label: Shizuka Sasaki
nodes.summary: Shizuka Sasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, Bukkyo University, and under Jikidō Takasaki. In 1990 he joined Hanazono University, becoming an assistant professor in 1992 and professor in 2002.

nodes.label: Stephen Jenkins
nodes.summary: Stephen Jenkins is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctorate at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (attested 2010–2013).

nodes.label: Malcolm David Eckel
nodes.summary: Malcolm David Eckel studied at Oxford and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion, he held posts at Middlebury, Harvard Divinity School, and Boston University (1990–2024), along with visiting professorships at Michigan and Sydney.

nodes.label: Donald S. Lopez Jr.
nodes.summary: Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his degrees at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He taught at Middlebury College (1986) and became a distinguished professor at the University of Michigan in 1990.

nodes.label: Charles Hallisey
nodes.summary: Charles Hallisey is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Colgate, Harvard Divinity School, Penn, and the University of Chicago. He has held faculty positions at Loyola University Chicago, Harvard University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: Seiji Kimura
nodes.summary: Seiji Kimura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and later held posts there (attested 1990) and as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Ernst Steinkellner
variants: エルンスト・シュタインケルナー
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Ernst Steinkellner studied at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner. He served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1971) and as director at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Helmut Krasser
nodes.summary: Helmut Krasser worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna, where he served from around 1989 to 2014, and led the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia in 2007.

nodes.label: Gerhard Oberhammer
variants: G. オーバーハンマー
nodes.summary: Gerhard Oberhammer worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Innsbruck under Erich Frauwallner, at the Sorbonne, and under V. Raghavan, later holding posts at Utrecht University and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Keio University
variants: 慶應義塾大学経済学部
慶應義塾大学言語文化研究所

nodes.label: Yohei Kawashiri
nodes.summary: Yohei Kawashiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013) and as a special research fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Lilian Silburn
nodes.summary: Lilian Silburn (1908–1993) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Paul Masson-Oursel and Lakshman Joo, held a post at the CNRS from circa 1948 to 1974, and taught André Padoux.

nodes.label: Lakshman Joo
nodes.summary: Lakshman Joo was a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan (1926–1933). He founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991 and taught numerous students, including Lilian Silburn, André Padoux, and Alexis Sanderson.

nodes.label: André Padoux
nodes.summary: André Padoux was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Louis Renou, Olivier Lacombe, and Lakshman Joo, among others. He served as director at the Institut Français d'Histoire en Allemagne and Directeur de Recherche at the CNRS.

nodes.label: Bettina Bäumer
nodes.summary: An Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar, Bäumer earned her doctorate at Munich and studied under Lakshman Joo. She held posts at Banaras Hindu University, the Alice Boner Institute, Vienna, IGNCA, and the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

nodes.label: Jaideva Singh
nodes.summary: Jaideva Singh (1893–1986) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Lakshman Joo and Nankoo Bhaya Telang. He served as chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).

nodes.label: Alexis Sanderson
nodes.summary: Alexis Sanderson studied at Balliol College, Oxford, and under Lakshman Joo (1972). Active in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, he served at Merton College, Brasenose College, and as Lecturer and Professor at the University of Oxford (~1977–2015).

nodes.label: Dominic Goodall
nodes.summary: Dominic Goodall is an Indologist who completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and studied under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. He joined the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2000 and lectured at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2005.

nodes.label: Judit Törzsök
nodes.summary: Judit Törzsök is an Indologist who completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1993–1999). She taught as an associate professor at the University of Lille (2001) and became a professor at EPHE in 2018.

nodes.label: Alex Watson
nodes.summary: Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Oxford (BA) and SOAS (MA), and completed his doctorate under Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson. His posts include Harvard, Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2006), and Ashoka University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Isabelle Ratié
nodes.summary: Isabelle Ratié (born 1976) specializes in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Paris 1 and EPHE under Lyne Bansat-Boudon and Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at Leipzig, Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).

nodes.label: University of Lucknow
variants: Abhinavagupta Institute of Aesthetics and Śaiva Philosophy

nodes.label: Kei Kataoka
nodes.summary: Kei Kataoka (born 1969), working in Indology and philosophy, earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo under Hiroshi Marui. After research posts at Oxford, JSPS, and Penn, he joined Kyushu University, becoming associate professor (~2007–2021) and professor (~2021).

nodes.label: Shigeo Kamata
nodes.summary: Shigeo Kamata (1927–2001) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa and the University of Tokyo under Kodo Sawaki. He held professorial posts at Tokyo, Aichi Gakuin, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Edward Winslow Bastian
nodes.summary: Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, training under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Lobsang Tenzin, Geshe Lobsang, and Geshe Lobsang Donyo.

nodes.label: Geshe Lobsang Tenzin
variants: Gyurme Kensur Rinpoche Geshe Lobsang Tenzin
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Drepung Monastery, Geshe Lobsang Tenzin held posts at Central Schools for Tibetans, served as Principal and Director at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and later became Chancellor of Sanchi University.

nodes.label: Sera Monastery
variants: Byes College of Se ra Monastery

nodes.label: Seitatsu Matsunami
nodes.summary: Seitatsu Matsunami was a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

nodes.label: Norio Koyama
nodes.summary: Norio Koyama was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: David P. Jackson
variants: ディヴィッド・ポール・ジャクソン
nodes.summary: David P. Jackson is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his BA, MA, and PhD at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg. He served as a C-3 professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

nodes.label: John E. Cort
nodes.summary: John E. Cort works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1974) and Harvard University (~1980–1984), and he became a professor at Denison University (~1993).

nodes.label: Paul Dundas
nodes.summary: Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Edinburgh, he led Asian studies there (~1976–2023) and served as head of the Pali Text Society.

nodes.label: Christoph Emmrich
nodes.summary: Christoph Emmrich (born 1965) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels in 2004, holding posts at Heidelberg (attested 2001) and the University of Toronto (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Karnatak University
variants: Museum of Art and Archaeology, Karnatak University, Dharwad

nodes.label: Shubhachandra
nodes.summary: Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who held a professorship at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and was affiliated with the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Jayandra Soni
nodes.summary: Jayandra Soni is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned PhDs from Banaras Hindu University (~1975–1978) and McMaster University (~1982–1987). He lectured at the University of Marburg (1991–2012) and became Generalsekretär of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (2012).

nodes.label: Royce Wiles
nodes.summary: Royce Wiles is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held a post at the same institution.

nodes.label: Derek F. Maher
nodes.summary: Derek F. Maher is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has lectured at Virginia and UNC Greensboro, and co-directed the Religious Studies Program at East Carolina University.

nodes.label: Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center
variants: Labsum Shedrub Ling, the Lamaist Buddhist Monastery of America

nodes.label: Georges B. J. Dreyfus
nodes.summary: Georges B. J. Dreyfus is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a Geshe degree at Ganden Shartse Monastery, completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, and became a professor at Williams College.

nodes.label: William Magee
nodes.summary: William Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held posts at the University of Virginia and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Jules Brooks Levinson
nodes.summary: Jules Brooks Levinson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia in 1994, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins and several traditional teachers. He was an assistant professor of religion at Hamline University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Richard B. Martin
nodes.summary: Richard B. Martin (1937–1996) worked in Indology and Tibetology. He held posts at the University of Virginia as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Ngawang Thokmey
nodes.summary: Ngawang Thokmey works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as South Asian bibliographer at the University of Virginia (attested 2003-2008) and as Assistant Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Charles D. Orzech
nodes.summary: Charles D. Orzech is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago. He chaired the Religious Studies Department at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro.

The University of North Carolina at Greensboro

nodes.label: Richard Gombrich
variants: リチャード・F・ゴンブリッチ
nodes.summary: Richard Gombrich (1937–) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner, Walpola Rahula, and Gananath Obeyesekere. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and Balliol College (1965/1976–2004).

nodes.label: Gananath Obeyesekere
nodes.summary: Gananath Obeyesekere (1930–2025) studied at the University of Ceylon (B.A. ~1951–1955) and the University of Washington (M.A. ~1956–1958). He taught at Ceylon, Washington, UC San Diego, and Princeton University (1980–2000), working in religious and Buddhist studies.

nodes.label: Walpola Rahula
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Walpola Rahula studied at Vidyalankara Pirivena, the University of Calcutta, the University of Ceylon under G. P. Malalasekera, and the University of Paris/Sorbonne under Paul Demiéville. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (1964–1969) and held posts at Northwestern, Oxford, UCLA, and Swarthmore.

nodes.label: Sodo Mori
nodes.summary: Sodo Mori is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University under Kogen Mizuno and at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and G. P. Malalasekera, later serving as professor at Aichi Gakuin University (1991–2003).

nodes.label: Issei Yamakawa
nodes.summary: Issei Yamakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sophia University and completed a master's course at Aichi Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Norihiko Tanaka
nodes.summary: Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku University, Bukkyo University, and Visva-Bharati University. He spent his career at Bukkyo University, serving as lecturer, associate professor, and professor between 1976 and 2021.

nodes.label: Takaji Fukita
nodes.summary: Takaji Fukita specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University under Zenno Ishigami, at Bukkyo University under Shozen Kumoi and Yuichi Kajiyama, and under Heinz Bechert. He held a lectureship at Bukkyo University around 1996.

nodes.label: Shunzo Onoda
nodes.summary: Shunzo Onoda is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a D.Lit. at Bukkyo University by 1993. He served at Bukkyo University as an associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Mark L. Blum
nodes.summary: Mark L. Blum specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held faculty posts at the State University of New York (attested 2005) and University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2006), later becoming Professor and Shinjo Ito Distinguished Chair at UC Berkeley (attested 2026).

nodes.label: State University of New York
variants: ニューヨーク州立大学

nodes.label: Mitsunobu Nakasone
nodes.summary: Mitsunobu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a part-time lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and held a post at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Daishun Ueyama
nodes.summary: Daishun Ueyama (1934–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He spent his career at Ryukoku University as assistant professor (~1970–1978), professor (~1978–2003), and president (~1996–2000).

nodes.label: Akira Fujieda
nodes.summary: Akira Fujieda specialized in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University (~1931–1934), he worked at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto University (professor in 1968), and held visiting professorships at Copenhagen and UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Paul B. Donnelly
nodes.summary: Paul B. Donnelly works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Yeshe Thapkay, Losang Yarphel, and Geshe Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

nodes.label: Geshe Lobsang Gyatso
nodes.summary: Geshe Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Drepung Monastery, founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics in 1973, and served as its director until 1997.

nodes.label: Institute of Buddhist Dialectics
variants: Buddhist Dialectic Institute in Dharmsala, India
Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, Dharamsala, India

nodes.label: Hokei Izumi
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist monk and Sanskrit researcher
nodes.summary: Hokei Izumi (1884–1947) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and later served there as a professor from around 1921 to 1944.

nodes.label: Shoshin Fukihara
nodes.summary: Shoshin Fukihara studied Buddhist studies at Otani University and Horyu-ji under Susumu Yamaguchi and Join Saeki. Main posts included professor at Shinshu College, associate professor at Doho University, and professor at Otani University Junior College (~1963–1973).

nodes.label: Otani University Junior College
variants: 大谷大学短期大学部仏教学科

nodes.label: Hoyo Watanabe
nodes.summary: Hoyo Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1951–1961). He spent his career there as a faculty dean (attested 1984–1985), professor (~1973–2004), and special honorary professor (~2004).

nodes.label: Yosho Nomura
nodes.summary: Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1936–1939). He served as a professor at Rissho University (~1957–1987) and as director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra (~1977–1987).

nodes.label: Koken Sasaki
nodes.summary: Koken Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at Rissho University (~1950–1960). He subsequently served there as an assistant professor (~1970–1978), department chair (~1978–2002), and professor emeritus (~2002).

nodes.label: Senkyo Sakawa
nodes.summary: Senkyo Sakawa (born 1937) works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. After studying at Rissho University (graduated 1965), he served there as professor of Buddhist studies (attested 1981–1985) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Enshu Kurumiya
nodes.summary: Enshu Kurumiya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the Australian National University in 1974. He served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University, attested between 1981 and 1985.

nodes.label: K. L. Dhammajoti
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, K. L. Dhammajoti studied at the University of Kelaniya and under Yinshun and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. He taught at Kelaniya, held posts at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and was a chair at Calgary.

nodes.label: Yakupitiyage Karunadasa
nodes.summary: Yakupitiyage Karunadasa (1934–2026) studied at the University of Ceylon and the University of London under David Friedman (PhD). A specialist in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he was Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and taught at Kelaniya and HKU.

nodes.label: Yinshun
nodes.summary: Yinshun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and Qingnian, and at Taisho University and Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes. He taught at Minnan and Wuchang, served as Fawang Buddhist Institute's head, and led the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

nodes.label: Huifeng
nodes.summary: Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Daniel M. Veidlinger
nodes.summary: Daniel M. Veidlinger works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, served as a research associate at Chiang Mai University in 1999, and held a post at California State University, Chico.

nodes.label: Steven Collins
nodes.summary: Steven Collins (1950–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Michael Carrithers, later holding posts at the universities of Bristol, Indiana, and Chicago, among other institutions.

nodes.label: Chiang Mai University
variants: Social Research Institute at Chiang Mai University

nodes.label: Hideo Mineshima
nodes.summary: Hideo Mineshima was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Yamagata Higher School, Taisho University, and Waseda University. He held faculty posts at Waseda University (1960–1998) and Bunkyo Gakuin University (~1976–1998).

nodes.label: Zenno Ishigami
nodes.summary: Zenno Ishigami (1929–2020) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Taisho University, later serving as professor and emeritus professor there, and held posts at Shukutoku Junior College, Shukutoku University, and the Sanko Research Institute.

nodes.label: Susumu Otake
nodes.summary: Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Makio Takemura at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2002). He held teaching posts at Kyoto University (~2008), Hanazono University (attested 2008–2013), and Bukkyo University (attested 2012–2013).

nodes.label: Dan Arnold
nodes.summary: Dan Arnold (born 1965) specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Carleton College, Columbia, Iliff, and the University of Chicago, he held posts at McGill University and the University of Chicago (2004–2011).

nodes.label: Barbara Stoler Miller
nodes.summary: Barbara Stoler Miller (1940–1993) was an Indologist. Educated at Barnard College, Columbia University, and the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D. under W. Norman Brown and Stella Kramrisch), she served on the faculties of Barnard College (1968–1979) and Columbia University (~1968–1993).

nodes.label: Theodore Riccardi
nodes.summary: Theodore Riccardi (born 1937) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served on the faculty of Columbia University, where he is attested as a faculty member in 2014 and as professor emeritus in 2026.

nodes.label: Robert A. F. Thurman
nodes.summary: Robert A. F. Thurman (1941–2026) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studying under Geshe Wangyal, Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale, Gelek Rimpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He served as professor at Amherst College (1973–1988) and director at Columbia University (1988–2019).

nodes.label: José Ignacio Cabezón
nodes.summary: José Ignacio Cabezón works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1978–1986) under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and became the Dalai Lama Professor at UC Santa Barbara in 2001.

nodes.label: Albrecht Wezler
variants: アルブレヒト・ヴェッツラー
nodes.summary: Albrecht Wezler (1938–2023) was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Tübingen under Paul Thieme. He served as Director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and directed the Nepal Research Centre and Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project.

nodes.label: Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan
nodes.summary: Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan (1932–2019) was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Hamburg (~1961–1967). He later served there as Privatdozent für Indologie from 1973 to 1997.

nodes.label: Satoru Noriyama
nodes.summary: Satoru Noriyama studied Buddhist studies under Esho Mikogami. He served as a part-time lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and at Ryukoku University (attested 2003), later becoming a lecturer there (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Silvio Vita
nodes.summary: Silvio Vita studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton University. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he held posts at "L'Orientale", the Italian School of East Asian Studies, Sapienza University, and University of Naples Federico II.

nodes.summary: Shōshin Ichishima is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a visiting lecturer at the University of Hawaiʻi. At Taisho University, he served as Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and was attested as professor emeritus in 2014.

nodes.label: David B. Gray
nodes.summary: David B. Gray is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. He served as a postdoctoral fellow at Rice University and Associate Professor at Santa Clara University (attested 2008–2017).

nodes.label: Ryuichi Abe
nodes.summary: Ryuichi Abe studied at Keio, Johns Hopkins, Taisho, and Columbia under several scholars. Active in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, he was Kao Associate Professor at Columbia (1998–2004) before becoming Reischauer Institute Professor at Harvard around 2003.

nodes.label: Ryushin Uryuzu
nodes.summary: Ryushin Uryuzu studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Ryukoku University (ca. 1951–1956). He was affiliated with the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute in 1962 and served as professor at Kyoto Women's University from around 1972 to 1998.

nodes.label: Yasunori Ejima
nodes.summary: Yasunori Ejima (1939–1999) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his degrees at the University of Tokyo and researched at Göttingen. He served as assistant professor at Nagaoka University of Technology and later as professor at Tokyo.

nodes.label: Fernando Tola
nodes.summary: Fernando Tola worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at the National University of San Marcos (~1932–1940), he taught at the University of Buenos Aires and directed the Center of Buddhist Studies (~1990–2017).

nodes.label: Carmen Dragonetti
nodes.summary: Carmen Dragonetti (1937–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at the National University of San Marcos and held posts at the Center of Buddhist Studies (~1987–2018), University of Buenos Aires, IIBS (1989), and Nyingma Institute (1996).

nodes.label: Tsugunari Kubo
nodes.summary: Tsugunari Kubo was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as President of Reiyukai (~1970–1993, ~1996–2013) and President of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1995–2019).

nodes.label: Tarthang Tulku
nodes.summary: Tarthang Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Tarthang Monastery and under several traditional teachers. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968), Padma Ling (~1969), Tibetan Nyingma Meditation Center (~1969), and Nyingma Institute (~1972).

nodes.label: Yeshe De Project
variants: Yeshe De Buddhist Research and Translation Project

nodes.label: Yohei Furukawa
nodes.summary: Yohei Furukawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Ryuji Hayashi. By 2026, he was attested as an associate professor at Soka University.

nodes.label: Ryuji Hayashi
nodes.summary: Ryuji Hayashi, a scholar of Buddhist studies and indology, studied at the University of Delhi. Hayashi held academic posts at Tohoku University, Sendai National College of Technology, Kodomo Education Hosen University, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Takao Kagawa
nodes.summary: Takao Kagawa was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University and taught Satoshi Hiraoka.

nodes.label: Shoju Inaba
nodes.summary: Shoju Inaba worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor at Otani University (~1957–1980) and part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.

nodes.label: Michitoshi Baraida
nodes.summary: Michitoshi Baraida is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He held posts at Otani University, Toho Gakuin, Toho Kenkyukai, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: V. Raghavan
nodes.summary: V. Raghavan was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Madras (1934–1968) and helped found and run the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

nodes.label: Juro Watanabe
nodes.summary: Juro Watanabe is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held a post at the University of Tsukuba, attested between 1989 and 1990.

nodes.label: Kiyotaka Yoshimizu
nodes.summary: Kiyotaka Yoshimizu specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held academic posts at Hokkaido University, Tohoku University, and Toyo Bunko.

nodes.label: Atsushi Uno
nodes.summary: Indologist and philosopher Atsushi Uno studied at Kyoto University, Banaras Hindu University, and under Raghunath Giri, Vamacharana Bhattacharya, and T. R. V. Murti. He held professorships at Tokai, Hiroshima (1974–1986), and Kindai (~1986–1993) universities.

nodes.label: Raghunath Giri
nodes.summary: Raghunath Giri was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya. He served as department head (科長) at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith and taught Atsushi Uno.

nodes.label: Keisho Tsukamoto
nodes.summary: Keisho Tsukamoto (1929–2010) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctorate at Tohoku University (-1964). He served as dean at Rissho University, professor at Tohoku University (~1977–1993), and president of Hosen Gakuen College (~1994–2000).

nodes.label: Endō Asai
nodes.summary: Endō Asai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saga High School, the University of Tokyo, and Rissho University. He held academic posts at Minobusan University, Nihon Fukushi University, Rissho University Junior College, and Rissho University, ultimately serving as president of Minobusan University.

nodes.label: Noriaki Inoue
nodes.summary: Noriaki Inoue is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953) and later served as a professor there, attested in 1982.

nodes.label: Ensho Kanakura
nodes.summary: Ensho Kanakura was an Indologist and philosopher of Buddhism who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University (1926–1960) and Rissho University (1957–1974), and served as president of Miyagi University of Education in 1967.

nodes.label: Shuyu Sakurai
nodes.summary: Shuyu Sakurai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University until 1943. He was attested as professor emeritus at Komazawa University between 1982 and 1992.

nodes.label: Takushu Sugimoto
variants: すぎもと・たくしゅう
nodes.summary: Takushu Sugimoto is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Tohoku University. He held professorships at Kanazawa University (~1986–2001, emeritus ~2001), Komazawa University (attested 1990), and Kinjo University (~2001–2006).

nodes.label: Yutaka Takagi
nodes.summary: Yutaka Takagi (born 1928) specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University (~1972–1999).

Tsuguhito Takeuchi
nodes.summary: Tsuguhito Takeuchi was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University Bloomington (PhD 1994) under Christopher I. Beckwith and others. He was Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~2001–2017).

nodes.label: Hisashi Sato
nodes.summary: Hisashi Sato (1913–2008) was a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He later served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1964–1977), Komazawa University, and Toyo University, and held a post at Bukkyo University (~1977–1984).

nodes.label: Tatsuo Nishida
nodes.summary: Tatsuo Nishida (1928–2012) was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology who studied and earned a doctorate at Kyoto University (1948–1962). He held multiple professorial and administrative posts at Kyoto University (1956–1992) and at NACSIS (1992–1994).

nodes.label: Helmut Hoffmann
nodes.summary: Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Freiburg, Berlin (Dr. phil. under Heinrich Lüders), and Marburg. He held posts at the Prussian Academy of Sciences, Munich (1948–1968), and Indiana University Bloomington (1969–1980).

nodes.label: Christopher I. Beckwith
variants: クリストファー・I・ベックウィズ
nodes.jawiki: クリストファー・ベックウィズ
nodes.summary: Christopher I. Beckwith works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After degrees at Ohio State (BA) and Indiana University (MA, PhD under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu), he joined Indiana University Bloomington, becoming Professor of Central Eurasian Studies in 1982.

nodes.label: Shindo Kusumoto
nodes.summary: Shindo Kusumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under the supervision of Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

nodes.label: Hideyo Ogawa
nodes.summary: Hideyo Ogawa is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics who taught Shindo Kusumoto. He held posts at Hiroshima University as assistant professor (~1989–1999), Professor of Indian Philosophy (~1999–2019), and professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yoshihito Muroji
nodes.summary: Yoshihito Muroji works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1992 under Lambert Schmithausen, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, later holding posts at Kyoto, Koyasan, and Shiga universities.

nodes.label: Robert Kritzer
nodes.summary: Robert Kritzer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (1995) under Padmanabh S. Jaini and served as Associate Professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).

ノートルダム女子大学

nodes.label: Kazufumi Oki
nodes.summary: Kazufumi Oki (born 1946) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He served on the faculty at Shuchiin University, where he was attested as assistant professor (1982–1988) and professor emeritus (2006–2013).

nodes.label: Hiromi Yoshimura
nodes.summary: Hiromi Yoshimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Shindo Kusumoto and held posts at Ryukoku University, including as a full-time lecturer (専任講師, attested 1987) and further affiliation attested in 2006.

nodes.label: Toshihiko Kimura
nodes.summary: Toshihiko Kimura works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tohoku University, he held posts at Tohoku University, Tokai Gakuin University, and Shitennoji University.

nodes.label: Toshihide Unebe
nodes.summary: Toshihide Unebe is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Issai Funahashi and served as a professor at Doho University.

nodes.label: Sengaku Mayeda
nodes.summary: Sengaku Mayeda (1931–2026) specialized in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, he held faculty posts at Pennsylvania, Tokyo, and Musashino University.

nodes.label: Hideto Ono
nodes.summary: Hideto Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University. His career includes a post as an assistant professor (助教授) at Aichi Gakuin University, attested in 1991.

京城私立恵化専門学校

nodes.label: Masaaki Nitta
nodes.summary: Masaaki Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1960–1967). He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1983–1991) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).

神戸大学文学部哲学科

nodes.label: Taiken Tanaka
nodes.summary: Taiken Tanaka studied at Hiroshima University and worked in Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Johannes Bronkhorst
nodes.summary: Johannes Bronkhorst was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Rajasthan, Pune University under Shivram Dattatray Joshi, and Leiden University. He served as professor at the University of Lausanne from 1987 to 2011.

nodes.label: Karin Preisendanz
nodes.summary: Karin Preisendanz specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. Her career includes posts at Freie Universität Berlin, the University of British Columbia, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Konrad Klaus
nodes.summary: Konrad Klaus (born 1956) works in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Göttingen and the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn (~1980–1985), held Vertretungsprofessor posts at Bochum, Marburg, and Bonn (1999–2001), and succeeded Claus Vogel in 2001.

nodes.label: Shujun Motegi
nodes.summary: Shujun Motegi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and at Kyoto University, later serving as Professor of Ethics at Shinshu University.

nodes.label: Beatrix Pfleiderer
nodes.summary: Beatrix Pfleiderer worked in Indology and medical anthropology, studying at the University of Maryland and Heidelberg University. She held positions at the University of Maryland, Heidelberg University, the University of Hamburg, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the European University Viadrina.

nodes.label: Tsultrim Kelsang
nodes.summary: Tsultrim Kelsang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the International Buddhist Association (attested 1973), Otani University as lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002), and Ryukoku University as a researcher in 2015.

nodes.summary: Paul Demiéville (1894–1979) was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. His career included posts at EFEO (1920–1924), INALCO, EPHE, and the Collège de France (1946–1964).

nodes.label: Kiyotaka Kimura
nodes.summary: Kiyotaka Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Shitennoji University, Tsurumi Women's University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Fumihiko Sueki

nodes.summary: Fumihiko Sueki specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned degrees at the University of Tokyo, studying under Hajime Nakamura and others. He was a professor at Tokyo and at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

nodes.label: Hajime Okayama
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist studies scholar and bhikku
nodes.summary: Hajime Okayama was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, Peking University under Xianlin Ji, and CASS. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo from 1995 to 2012.

nodes.label: Koyu Tamura
nodes.summary: Koyu Tamura (1931–2022) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Department of Cultural Affairs, Nishogakusha University, and Toyo University (assistant professor in 1972, professor emeritus 1977–2000).

nodes.label: Ryoshu Misaki
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Misaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from around 1947 to 1952. Misaki later served as a professor emeritus at Waseda University (attested 1988–2000).

nodes.label: Katsumi Okimoto
nodes.summary: Katsumi Okimoto (1943–2014) studied at the University of Tokyo. Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1988–2009) and directed the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (~1999–2009).

nodes.label: Takao Maruyama
nodes.summary: Takao Maruyama is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1957–1962). He held faculty posts at Rissho University (attested 1972, 1981), Shinshu University (attested 1983–1984, 2001), and Mejiro University (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Kiyoshi Kato
nodes.summary: Kiyoshi Kato was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA at Otani University under Enga Teramoto. He held posts at Higashi Honganji Kobe Betsuin and Hyanghwa Girls' Vocational School.

nodes.label: Ryuzan Nishimoto
nodes.summary: Ryuzan Nishimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.

nodes.label: Eli Franco
nodes.summary: Eli Franco (born 1953) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Charles Malamoud at EPHE and Paris Nanterre, habilitating at the University of Hamburg. He held the chair of Indology at the University of Leipzig from 2004 to 2021.

nodes.label: Xinchuan Huang
nodes.summary: Xinchuan Huang (1928–2021) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. After studying at Peking University (~1956–1958), he served at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–2010), including as a researcher at its Institute of Asia-Pacific Studies (~1988–1993).

nodes.label: Robert DeCaroli
nodes.summary: Robert DeCaroli (born 1970), a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and art history, studied at UCLA under Robert L. Brown. He taught at UCLA and Loyola Marymount, and joined the faculty at George Mason University in ~2002.

nodes.label: Robert L. Brown
nodes.summary: Robert L. Brown (1943–2014) worked in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a South and Southeast Asian art curator at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1983–2014) and professor emeritus at UCLA (~1986–2014).

nodes.label: Iwao Shima

nodes.summary: Kanchu Onoe worked in Buddhist studies. He held teaching posts at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and Eizan Gakuin, where he served as professor (attested 1976).

nodes.label: Tetsuei Sato
nodes.summary: Tetsuei Sato (1902–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University from ~1925 to ~1931. He served as professor at Taisho University, professor at Gifu Kyoritsu University (~1968), and professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1968–1989).

nodes.label: Minoru Hara
nodes.summary: Minoru Hara (1930–2021) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo, Harvard, and Cambridge. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1975–1991), president of ICABS (1996–2006), and director of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~2000–2009).

nodes.label: Keiichi Miyamoto
nodes.summary: Keiichi Miyamoto (born 1948) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his degrees, including a DLitt, at the University of Tokyo, studying under Minoru Hara. He held posts as lecturer, associate professor, and professor (1995) at Kokugakuin University.

nodes.label: Karl H. Potter
nodes.summary: Karl H. Potter was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of California (~1947–1950) and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and was a professor at the University of Minnesota (~1956–1970) and the University of Washington (~1970–1997).

nodes.label: Haraprasad Shastri
nodes.summary: Haraprasad Shastri studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Presidency University, and Sanskrit College. A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Hare School, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Presidency University, Sanskrit College, The Asiatic Society, and the University of Dhaka.

nodes.label: Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel
nodes.summary: Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel is an Indologist who headed the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (attested 1989), worked in the Prussian State Library's Oriental Department (attested 1992–1994), and served as project director at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Shobha Rani Dash
variants: ダシュ・ショバ・ラニ
ダシュ ショバ ラニ
nodes.summary: Shobha Rani Dash works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was an open-recruitment researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010, a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012), and a professor at Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Makoto Yoshimura
nodes.summary: Makoto Yoshimura works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his doctoral studies at Waseda University around 1996–2002 and served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University around 2007.

nodes.label: Ryogon Fukuhara
nodes.summary: Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1931–1936) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1938–1941). He taught at Humboldt University of Berlin and held a professorship at Ryukoku University (~1960–1980).

nodes.summary: Taijun Inokuchi worked in Buddhist studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1963–1987) and served as representative of the Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Yusen Kashiwahara
nodes.summary: Yusen Kashiwahara (1916–2002) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Otani University circa 1937–1941 and served as a professor there circa 1961–1987.

nodes.label: Shuyu Kanaoka
nodes.summary: Shuyu Kanaoka specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1952) and earning a doctorate from Toyo University (1962). He served as an assistant professor at Toyo University (~1968–1992).

nodes.label: Hiromu Kitanishi
nodes.summary: Hiromu Kitanishi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University (~1945–1948) and later served as a professor there (~1969–1991).

nodes.label: Masahiro Kusunoki
nodes.summary: Masahiro Kusunoki was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1948–1953). He served as professor and chair of religious studies and history of religion at Tohoku University (~1968–1985).

nodes.label: Encho Tamura
nodes.summary: Encho Tamura was a Buddhist studies scholar and historian. Educated at Kyushu and Kyoto universities, he held long-term academic appointments at Kumamoto University (~1954–1982) and Kyushu University (1941–1980), later directing the Kyushu Historical Museum and Fukuoka Human Rights Center.

nodes.label: Yoshiro Tamura
nodes.summary: Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He held professorships at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo, and Rissho University, and was a visiting professor at Chicago.

nodes.label: Jōryū Chiba
nodes.summary: Jōryū Chiba was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied and taught extensively at Ryukoku University, later serving as emeritus professor. He also directed the Honganji Historical Materials Research Institute and the Shinshu Otaniha Institute.

nodes.label: Kyosho Hayashima
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kyosho Hayashima held teaching posts at Yokohama City University and Toyo University (attested 1962), and served as a professor at the University of Tokyo, attested in 1980.

nodes.label: Yukei Matsunaga
nodes.summary: Yukei Matsunaga worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Koyasan University, Tohoku University, and Kyushu University. He served as director at Koyasan University in 1983 and held a post at Shuchiin University around 1998.

nodes.label: Satoshi Hayashima
nodes.summary: Satoshi Hayashima specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a research student at Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2014) and later served as a lecturer there (attested 2015–2017).

nodes.label: Giyu Nishi
nodes.summary: Giyu Nishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from the University of Tokyo, studying under Taiken Kimura, Sylvain Lévi, and Junjirō Takakusu, among others. He was an assistant at the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Toyo University in 1927.

nodes.label: Seishin Kato
nodes.summary: Seishin Kato (1872–1956) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He served as president of Buzan University (1918, 1923), president of Taisho University (1940), and president of Toyo University (1952, 1955).

nodes.label: Yukio Sakamoto
nodes.summary: Yukio Sakamoto studied Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura and Daito Shimaji, earning a doctorate from Tohoku University. He held posts at Rissho University, including president in 1968, and was a professor at Toyo University (~1956–1970).

nodes.label: Koshiro Tamaki
nodes.summary: Koshiro Tamaki (1915–1999) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. nodes.label: Nobuo Otsuka
nodes.summary: Nobuo Otsuka (b. 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University, where he also served as a researcher (attested 1995).

nodes.summary: Keiya Noguchi (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies and completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1980–1985). He has held faculty posts at Shuchiin University, becoming professor around 2003, and served as institute director at Taisho University (attested 2017).

nodes.summary: Hideomi Yaita is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. Yaita held posts at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1991–1995) and as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Shinya Moriyama
nodes.summary: Shinya Moriyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo, the University of Vienna, and under Eli Franco in 2002. He held a teaching post at Shinshu University around 2008.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Marui
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Marui (born 1952), an Indology and philosophy scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo and under Albrecht Wezler. He taught at Musashino University and served as associate professor at the University of Tokyo (1992, 1995, 1999–2018).

nodes.label: Atsushi Kanazawa
nodes.summary: Atsushi Kanazawa specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1980), lectured at the Meteorological College (attested 1986–1989), and held posts at Komazawa University from around 1993 to 2003.

nodes.label: Yoichi Fukuda
nodes.summary: Yoichi Fukuda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003 and 2015).

nodes.label: Péter-Dániel Szántó
nodes.summary: Péter-Dániel Szántó specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College, Oxford, under Alexis Sanderson, and has held positions at All Souls College, Oxford, and Eötvös Loránd University.

nodes.label: William M. Gorvine
nodes.summary: William M. Gorvine works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Connecticut College and completed his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, where he studied under David Germano and others.

nodes.label: Sara L. McClintock
nodes.summary: Sara L. McClintock works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Columbia, CIHTS, Lausanne, and Harvard (PhD, 2002), she has held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Emory University.

nodes.label: John B. Carman
nodes.summary: John B. Carman was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as Director of the Center for the Study of World Religions and held a faculty appointment at Harvard University (attested 1999).

nodes.label: A. K. Ramanujan
nodes.summary: A scholar in linguistics and Indology, he studied at Mysore and completed his PhD at Indiana University. He held positions at Baroda, Deccan College, and notably the University of Chicago from 1962, becoming William E. Colvin Professor in 1983.

nodes.label: Elliot Sperling
nodes.summary: Elliot Sperling (1951–2017) specialized in Tibetology, sinology, and history. Educated at CUNY Queens College and Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Lynn A. Struve, he taught at Indiana (1987–2015), Harvard, and Delhi.

nodes.label: Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe
nodes.summary: Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe (born 1930) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. His career includes posts as a scholar at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 1991, 2004, and 2014–2019.

nodes.label: Takashi Ogawa
nodes.summary: Takashi Ogawa is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University (1986–1989), and the University of Tokyo. In 1991, he held an assistant professor post at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Kenji Kinugawa
nodes.summary: Kenji Kinugawa specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1971 to 1979 under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.

nodes.label: Kyoko Fujii
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kyoko Fujii studied at the University of Tokyo. She served as professor at Hokkaido University (~1996–2008) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2008–2018), and president of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~2015).

nodes.label: Kenryo Minowa
nodes.summary: Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Aichi Gakuin University (2000-2010), the University of Tokyo (professor from 2010), and Rissho University (director in 2025).

nodes.label: Shogo Watanabe
nodes.summary: Shogo Watanabe is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University (circa 1973–1983). He held posts at Toyo University from around 1988 to 2021, serving as professor from circa 2002 to 2021.

nodes.label: Ikuro Hattori
nodes.summary: Ikuro Hattori is a scholar of Indology and philosophy holding a PhD from Pune University. He held researcher posts at Toho Kenkyukai (attested 2003) and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026), also lecturing at Aichi Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Ryutoku Kimura
nodes.summary: Ryutoku Kimura studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Komazawa University (~1966–1973). He was a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1978), lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996), and head priest at Kaichō-ji (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Michihiko Yajima
nodes.summary: Michihiko Yajima, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, pursued graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1992) and as professor at Tsurumi Women's University (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Gyoei Takahashi
nodes.summary: Gyoei Takahashi is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Takahashi held posts at Rissho University as assistant professor (attested 2003–2004) and professor (attested 2026), and was a staff member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Shunei Mori

nodes.label: Kaiten Nukariya

nodes.summary: Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Komazawa and Keio universities. He lectured at Harvard (~1913–1915) and served as dean and first president of Komazawa University (1921; 1925–1934).

nodes.label: Shumpei Ueyama

nodes.label: Gustav Roth
nodes.summary: Roth worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Breslau, Leipzig, Halle-Wittenberg, Munich, and Patna, he studied under Paul Thieme, Gaurinath Sastri, and others. He served at the University of Göttingen (1965–1981) and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

nodes.label: Reinhold Grünendahl

nodes.label: Petra Kieffer-Pülz

nodes.label: Sen Wang
nodes.summary: Sen Wang (1912–1991) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Peking University (~1932–1936) and served as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1952–1978).

nodes.label: Syed Hasan Askari

nodes.label: Minoru Kiyota

nodes.label: John P. Keenan

nodes.label: Ryosei Fukuda

nodes.label: Ryojin Soga
nodes.summary: Ryojin Soga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Otani University, Shinshu University, Kōkōdō, and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served as a professor at Toyo University and Otani University, where he also became the 17th president.

nodes.label: Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale

nodes.label: Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar

nodes.label: Lisa Grumbach
nodes.summary: Lisa Grumbach is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held a post at Stanford University, attested in 1996, and has served as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Hiromichi Kato
nodes.summary: Hiromichi Kato works in Buddhist studies. He studied under Ryogon Fukuhara, taught Collett Cox, and held a post as lecturer (講師) at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Shinya Yasutomi
nodes.summary: Shinya Yasutomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and Otani University. He held multiple academic posts at Otani University, including professor (~1991–2010), and directed the Shinshu Otani-ha Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies (~2008–2014).

nodes.label: Kogi Kudara
nodes.summary: Kogi Kudara (1945–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held a professorship at Ryukoku University (attested 1979) and an editorial post at Ryukoku Buddhist Society (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Ryoichi Kondo
nodes.summary: Ryoichi Kondo is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has held posts as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Lobsang Gyatso
nodes.summary: Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under and taught Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso, taught Guy Newland and Yaroslav Komarovski, and served as Head of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (ca. 1973–1997).

nodes.label: Geshe Rabten
nodes.description: tibetan Buddhist geshe born in Tibet
nodes.summary: Geshe Rabten (1920–1986) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Sera Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche, earning a Geshe Lharampa degree, and taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from around 1969 to 1974.

nodes.label: Christian Lindtner
nodes.summary: Christian Lindtner (1949–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his filosofiske doktorgrad from the University of Copenhagen in 1982 and served there as a professor (attested 1980–1991).

nodes.label: Migmar Tsering
nodes.summary: Migmar Tsering was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He served as head of Sakya College (attested 1991–2003) and held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences.

nodes.label: Joseph Hackin
nodes.summary: Joseph Hackin worked in archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sciences Po, INALCO, EPHE under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot, and Paris. He held posts at Musée Guimet, EPHE, École du Louvre, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and DAFA.

nodes.label: René Grousset
nodes.summary: René Grousset studied at the University of Montpellier and worked in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He held posts at the Musée Guimet, Musée Cernuschi, École du Louvre, and the Louvre Museum.

nodes.label: Bunzaburo Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Bunzaburo Matsumoto specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Rikkyo University, the First Higher School, and Kyoto University, where he also served as president (1908–1915), later directing the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto Institute.

nodes.label: Shoson Miyamoto
nodes.summary: Shoson Miyamoto studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Otani, Tokyo, and Oxford universities. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1942), Toyo University (~1947–1952), Komazawa University (~1954–1973), and Waseda University (~1954–1964).

nodes.label: Giei Honda
nodes.summary: Giei Honda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1910 to 1914. He lectured at Kyoto University, served as assistant professor there (1935–1948), and held professorships at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.

nodes.label: Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a Pandit and supervisor of collation at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1929–1944) and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Tucci
variants: ジュゼッペ・トゥッチ
nodes.jawiki: ジュゼッペ・トゥッチ
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Tucci was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Carlo Formichi and Giovanni Vacca. He taught at Visva-Bharati and Dhaka, served as professor at Sapienza, and became president of IsMEO.

nodes.label: Shuntaro Matsuyama
nodes.summary: Shuntaro Matsuyama specialized in Indology and religious studies, studying at the University of Tokyo and under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1949–1953). He taught at Bigakko, Kokugakuin University, Tama Art University, and as a professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design.

nodes.id: I:Joshibi University of Art and Design
nodes.label: Joshibi University of Art and Design
Rikizan Ishikawa
nodes.summary: Rikizan Ishikawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University (~1962–1974) and served there as Professor of Buddhist Studies (~1991–1997).

nodes.label: Shuken Ito
nodes.summary: Shuken Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He spent his career at Komazawa University rising from research assistant (1973) to professor (1991), and was a visiting professor at Aichi Gakuin University (1998).

nodes.label: Masashi Nagai
nodes.summary: Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral degrees at Komazawa University. He served Komazawa as lecturer, assistant professor, professor emeritus, and chancellor, and was a chief researcher at the Soto Zen Research Center.

nodes.label: Peter N. Gregory
variants: ビーター・N・グレゴリー
ピーター・N・グレゴリー
nodes.summary: Peter N. Gregory is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed his PhD at Harvard (1981) under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (attested 1986–1994) and Smith College (attested 2005).

nodes.label: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
variants: Japan House at the University of Illinois

nodes.label: Rosan Ikeda
nodes.summary: Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from 1960 to ~1969. He served Komazawa University as assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor (1969–2012), and directed the Soto Zen Research Center in 2009.

nodes.label: Ichiro Katayama
nodes.summary: Ichiro Katayama is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa and Otani Universities under Kogen Mizuno. He taught at Komazawa University from 1975, serving as professor from 1985 to 2013.

nodes.label: Tatsugen Sato
nodes.summary: Tatsugen Sato (1924–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Komazawa University in 1978. He held teaching posts at Komazawa University (~1964–1995), Tokai University, and Ryukoku University (attested 1974).

nodes.label: Morten Schlütter
variants: モルテン・シュルター
nodes.summary: Morten Schlütter is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen, Komazawa University, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. He has taught at Victoria University of Wellington and serves as associate professor at the University of Iowa.

nodes.label: Seiki Kudo
nodes.summary: Seiki Kudo (born 1931) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held academic positions as an assistant at Kyoto University and as an assistant professor at both Shuchiin University and Shitennoji University (attested 1972–1973).

nodes.label: University of Calcutta
variants: Department of Ancient Indian History, Calcutta University
Council of Post-Graduate Teaching in Arts, Calcutta University
Centre of Advanced Study in AIHC, Calcutta University
Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture of the Calcutta University

nodes.label: Makoto Kitada
nodes.summary: Makoto Kitada is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed doctoral studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. Kitada held a post at Toho Kenkyukai (attested 2008–2010) and is a base member at Osaka University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Dhammapala
nodes.summary: Dhammapala is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under K. L. Dhammajoti. He served as a visiting assistant professor there in 2013.

Institut National des Langues et Civilisations Orientales

nodes.label: Yutaka Ochihara
nodes.summary: Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania under Louis Renou, Atsuuji Ashikaga, W. Norman Brown, and Armand Minard, holding posts at Kyoto University (1957–1986) and Collège de France (1985).

nodes.label: Hideaki Nakatani
nodes.summary: Hideaki Nakatani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and computational fields. He studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, with Yutaka Ochihara, and earned a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He held a professorship at Kobe Gakuin University (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Louis Renou
nodes.summary: Louis Renou was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch at the EPHE. He held posts at the University of Lyon (~1925–1937), EPHE (~1928–1966), University of Paris (~1937–1966), and Maison Franco-Japonaise (1954–1956).

nodes.label: Vincent Eltschinger
nodes.summary: Vincent Eltschinger specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Lausanne (~1995–2003) under Tom Tillemans, worked at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and became Directeur d’études at EPHE in ~2015.

nodes.label: Danielle Feller
nodes.summary: Danielle Feller is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst. She also studied under Ganesh Umakant Thite.

nodes.label: Yael Bentor
nodes.summary: Yael Bentor specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University Bloomington under Gregory Schopen, and became a professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2000, 2026).

nodes.label: Hebrew University of Jerusalem
variants: Center for the Study of Christianity der Hebräischen Universität Jerusalem
Franz Rosenzweig Minerva Research Center for German-Jewish Literature and Cultural History
Center for the Study of Christianity

nodes.label: David Dean Shulman
nodes.description: Israeli-American indologist, historian of religion, and poet
nodes.summary: David Dean Shulman (1949–) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his B.A. at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Ph.D. at the University of London under John Ralston Marr, later holding posts at Hebrew University and the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies.

nodes.label: Lydia Aran
nodes.description: Professor emerita:Hebrew University of Jerusalem/scholar of Buddhism (1921–2013)

nodes.label: Thubten Jigme Norbu
nodes.image: Thubten Jigme Norbu, The Dalai Lama opens art exhibit in Tokyo, 1967 (cropped) (cropped).jpg
nodes.description: lama, writer, civil rights worker, university and college faculty member
nodes.summary: Thubten Jigme Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Ngawang Nyima. He served as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and as professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1992).

nodes.label: Gregory Schopen
variants: グレゴリー・ショペン
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Schopen earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington (~1984–1991), UT Austin (~1991–1999), and UCLA (~1999–2019).

nodes.label: Dan Martin
nodes.summary: Dan Martin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University Bloomington (~1983–1991), studying under Elliot Sperling, and held posts at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, Carnegie Mellon, and Hebrew University.

nodes.label: Fukuoka Human Rights Center
variants: 福岡県人権啓発情報センター

nodes.label: Yutaka Iwamoto
nodes.summary: Yutaka Iwamoto (1910–1988) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1930–1933) under Atsuuji Ashikaga, Toru Haneda, and Hidenaka Tanaka. He taught at Kyoto, Tokai, Tokyo University of Science, Kyoto Tachibana, and Soka Universities.

nodes.label: Gherardo Gnoli
nodes.description: Italian historian of religions and Iranologist (1937–2012)
nodes.summary: Gherardo Gnoli (1937–2012) studied at Sapienza University of Rome, specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993) and Sapienza University of Rome (1993–2008).

nodes.label: Italian Institute for Africa and the East

ナポリ東洋大學文學部

nodes.label: Mauro Maggi
nodes.summary: Mauro Maggi specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Naples "L'Orientale", served as Director at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East, and held a post at Sapienza University of Rome.

nodes.label: Ryuyu Saito
nodes.summary: Ryuyu Saito is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyo Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Research Association.

nodes.label: Yasuo Sano
nodes.summary: Yasuo Sano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyo Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Research Association.

nodes.label: Toshio Sako
nodes.summary: Toshio Sako is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikidō Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and completed doctoral studies at Columbia University under Alex Wayman.

nodes.label: Anna-Pya Sjödin
nodes.summary: Anna-Pya Sjödin specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Uppsala University (2007), where she was supervised by Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, and also studied under Barbro Eriksson.

nodes.label: Gunilla Gren-Eklund
nodes.summary: Gunilla Gren-Eklund specialized in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Stig Wikander and held an academic post at Uppsala University from around 1968 to 2003.

nodes.label: Jonardon Ganeri
nodes.summary: Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge, King's College London, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, NYU, and became Bimal K. Matilal Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at Toronto around 2020.

nodes.label: K. Venugopalan
variants: K・ヴェーヌゴーパラン

nodes.label: Toshihiro Wada
nodes.summary: Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha. He has held academic posts at Nagoya University.

nodes.label: Tadashi Tani
nodes.summary: Tadashi Tani worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University, studied at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama (1995), and served as a professor at National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (attested 1996–2000).

nodes.id: I:National Institute of Technology, Kochi College
nodes.label: National Institute of Technology, Kochi College
variants: 高知工業高等専門学校

nodes.label: Ryudo Fujii
nodes.summary: Ryudo Fujii is a scholar of indology and philosophy who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (2003), Kokushikan University (2010), and Kyoto Women's University (2015).

nodes.label: Kosuke Nakazawa
nodes.summary: Kosuke Nakazawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi. He held posts as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Rissho University, and was attested at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra in 2001.

nodes.label: Karl Jettmar
nodes.summary: Karl Jettmar studied at the University of Vienna (1936–1941), specializing in archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held posts at Weltmuseum Wien, the University of Vienna, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, and was a director at Heidelberg University (1964–1986).

nodes.label: Gérard Fussman
nodes.summary: Gérard Fussman specialized in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure from around 1960 to 1964 and became a professor at the Collège de France in 1984, succeeding Jean Filliozat.

nodes.label: Ahmad Hasan Dani
nodes.description: Pakistani intellectual, archaeologist, historian, and linguist (1920–2009)
nodes.summary: Ahmad Hasan Dani was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, London, and under Altekar, Wheeler, and Codrington. He held posts at Dhaka, University of Peshawar (1962–1971), and Quaid-i-Azam University (1971, 1997).

nodes.label: Jan Van Bragt
nodes.jawiki: ヤン・ヴァン・ブラフト
nodes.summary: Jan Van Bragt (1928–2007) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at KU Leuven from around 1948 to 1957 and served as Director at Nanzan University (~1976–1992), where he was later named professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Klaus Mylius
variants: クラウス・ミューラーダイス
nodes.summary: Klaus Mylius worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Leipzig. His teaching posts included Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, Bayreuth, the University of Göttingen, and Goethe University Frankfurt.

nodes.label: Gessho Sasaki
nodes.summary: Gessho Sasaki (1875–1926) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Otani University under Manshi Kiyozawa, later serving at Otani University as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925).

nodes.label: Koichi Hokazono
nodes.summary: Koichi Hokazono works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn, earned a PhD at Kyushu University, and held a professorship at The International University of Kagoshima (attested 1991–2000).

nodes.label: Ryuken Sato
nodes.summary: Ryuken Sato specialized in Buddhist studies. In 2014, he was attested as professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Akitoshi Saito
nodes.summary: Akitoshi Saito was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held posts at Taisho University, attested between 1982 and 2014, and served as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Kotetsu Yoshida
nodes.summary: Kotetsu Yoshida (born 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar attested in 2014 as professor emeritus at Taisho University and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Ryushin Kitao
nodes.summary: Ryushin Kitao is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has served as a professor at Shuchiin University, attested in 2014 and 2026.

nodes.label: Chisan Denpōin
variants: 真言宗智山派智山伝法院

Research Institute for Zen Culture (Zenbunka kenkyujo)
