variants: 浙江省立甲種工業学校

nodes.label: Yumi Katayama
nodes.summary: Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Katayama was a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under supervisor Kenyo Mitomo (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Yamagiwa
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Yamagiwa (b. 1963) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002) and as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Geshe Lobsang Tharchin
nodes.summary: Geshe Lobsang Tharchin (1921–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies at Sera Mey Monastery, earning a Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953, and also studied at Gyume Tantric College.

nodes.label: Meiji Yamada
nodes.summary: Meiji Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962). Publications attest his post as professor at Ryukoku University in 1963 and 2007.

nodes.label: Frank-Richard Hamm
nodes.summary: Frank-Richard Hamm was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring (1940–1948) and held posts at Hamburg, the International Academy of Indian Culture, and Bonn (Professor, 1965).

nodes.label: Daniel Cozort
nodes.summary: Daniel Cozort specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, studied under several traditional teachers, and held academic positions at Bates College and Dickinson College.

nodes.label: Kensur Yeshe Thupten
nodes.summary: A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Kensur Yeshe Thupten held posts as a visiting Tibetan scholar at the University of Virginia in 1982 and at Middlebury College in 1982.

nodes.label: Geshe Bel-den-drak-ba
nodes.summary: Geshe Bel-den-drak-ba worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi, attested in 1988.

nodes.label: Shaoyong Ye
nodes.summary: Shaoyong Ye is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies at Peking University in 2009 under Qing Duan. He has served as an associate professor and faculty member at Peking University (attested 2010–2026).

nodes.label: Qing Duan
nodes.description: Chinese scholar of Indian and Iranian languages; Professor of Indo-Iranian Studies and Boya Chair Professor of Peking University
nodes.summary: Qing Duan was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University and the University of Hamburg (PhD under Ronald Eric Emmerick), and served as a professor at Peking University (~1987–2022).

nodes.label: Zhaohua Yang
nodes.summary: Zhaohua Yang works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He held an affiliation at Stanford University (attested 2007), taught Kevin Buckelew, and was a faculty member at Columbia University (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Shinsho Hanayama
nodes.summary: Shinsho Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo from around 1934 to 1959, and served as professor at Toyo University and Kokugakuin University.

nodes.label: Naoshiro Tsuji
nodes.summary: Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Oxford. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960) and later directed the Toyo Bunko (1974).

nodes.label: Paul Hacker
nodes.summary: Paul Hacker (1913–1979) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Bonn, Heidelberg, Frankfurt, and Berlin, he held posts at Mithila Research Institute, University of Bonn, and the University of Münster.

nodes.id: I:Wiener Studien zur Tibetologie und Buddhismuskunde
nodes.label: Wiener Studien zur Tibetologie und Buddhismuskunde
variants: Wiener Studien zur Tibetologie und Buddhismuskunde

nodes.label: Michael Friedrich
nodes.summary: Michael Friedrich is a sinologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich (~1976–1984), where he was an assistant from 1983 to 1986. He subsequently served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.

nodes.label: Jowita Kramer
nodes.summary: Jowita Kramer specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her dissertation under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg (~2000–2004) and her Habilitation at Munich (~2005–2010), becoming a professor at the University of Leipzig in 2021.

nodes.label: Masaru Akimoto
nodes.summary: Masaru Akimoto is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyoto Women's University, including as a professor of contemporary society attested in 2002 and later attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Sergey Oldenburg
variants: セルゲイ・フョードロウィッチ・オルデンブルク
セルゲイ・フョードロヴィチ・オルデンブルク
セルゲイ・オルデンブルク
nodes.jawiki: セルゲイ・オルデンブルク
nodes.description: Russian scholar of Sanskrit and Buddhism (1863-1934)
nodes.summary: Sergey Oldenburg (1863–1934) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Minayev. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University and director of the Asiatic Museum.

nodes.label: George R. Elder
nodes.summary: George R. Elder is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman (attested 1978).

nodes.label: Ikuhisa Takigawa
nodes.summary: Ikuhisa Takigawa is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. In 2002, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at both Waseda University and Tokai University.

nodes.label: Angelika Krebs
nodes.summary: Angelika Krebs is a philosopher who studied at Freiburg, Konstanz, UC Berkeley, New College, and Goethe University Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt (1993–2001), and the Chair of Practical Philosophy at the University of Basel (2001).

nodes.label: Thomas A. Tweed
nodes.summary: Thomas A. Tweed (born 1954) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (~1979–1984) under William R. Hutchison and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).

nodes.label: William A. Clebsch
nodes.description: American church historian, developer of religious studies, and university professor (1923-1984)

nodes.label: Robert E. Buswell Jr.
nodes.summary: Robert E. Buswell Jr. (born 1953) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at UC Berkeley under Lewis Lancaster and others, and under Kusan Sunim, before a long career at UCLA as professor (~1986–1992) and later Distinguished Professor Emeritus.

nodes.label: Luis O. Gómez
variants: Luis O. GÓMEZ ルイス・ゴメス
nodes.description: Puerto Rican buddhologist, translator and psychologist
nodes.summary: Luis O. Gómez was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Yale under Stanley Insler. He held long-term professorships and chair roles at the University of Michigan and served as academic director at the Mangalam Research Center (~2010–2017).

nodes.label: Van Austin Harvey
nodes.image: Van A. Harvey and a dog.jpg
nodes.summary: Van Austin Harvey was a religious studies scholar who studied at Occidental College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale University. He taught at Princeton, Southern Methodist University, and the University of Pennsylvania before serving as a professor at Stanford University.

nodes.label: Lee Yearley
nodes.summary: Lee Yearley is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He held a faculty career at Stanford University, serving as Professor (attested 1989–1992) and later as Emeritus (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Gordon D. Kaufman
nodes.summary: Gordon D. Kaufman (1925–2011) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar educated at Bethel College, Northwestern, and Yale. He held posts at Pomona College, Vanderbilt University, and Harvard University (~1963–1995), serving as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity.

nodes.label: Carl Bielefeldt
nodes.summary: Carl Bielefeldt works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki, Seizan Yanagida, and at UC Berkeley (~1974–1980). He held posts at Stanford University (~1980–2017; emeritus ~2017) and the Numata Center (attested 2017).

nodes.label: William R. Hutchison
nodes.summary: William R. Hutchison was a religious studies and history scholar. He studied at Oxford and Yale, taught at American University (~1959–1968), and spent the remainder of his career as a professor at Harvard University (~1968–2000).

nodes.label: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
nodes.summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Kurtis R. Schaeffer earned his MA at the University of Washington and his PhD at Harvard University under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp. He taught at the University of Alabama before joining the University of Virginia in 2005.

nodes.label: Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute and earned a PhD from Harvard University (~1997–2004) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Satkari Mookerjee
variants: サトカリ・ムカージー
サトカーリ・ムケルジー
nodes.summary: Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1951) and became the second director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.

nodes.label: John Brough
nodes.summary: John Brough studied at Edinburgh and Cambridge under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Harold Walter Bailey. An Indologist and linguist, he held posts at the British Museum, SOAS, the University of London (1948–1967), and Cambridge (1967–1984).

nodes.label: Chitai Takenaka
nodes.summary: Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1964–1968). Takenaka served as an associate professor at Hanazono University (~1975–1989) and as a professor at Tokoha University (~1989).

nodes.label: Hideki Kiyoshima
nodes.summary: Hideki Kiyoshima is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Delhi. Kiyoshima held a lecturer post at Kindai University, attested in 1989.

nodes.label: Jun Takashima
nodes.summary: Jun Takashima specializes in Indology, religious studies, and computational fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, and later held positions at Aichi Prefectural University, Toyo University, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as professor in 2020.

nodes.label: Muneo Tokunaga
variants: Muneo Tokunaga (徳永 宗雄, Tokunaga Muneo)
nodes.summary: Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) studied Indology and computational studies at Kyoto University (~1969–1971) and Harvard (PhD, ~1974–1984). He held an associate professorship at Tokyo Institute of Technology (attested 1983) and taught at Kyoto University as associate professor (~1988–1990) and professor (~1990–2009).

nodes.label: Yasumasa Sekine
nodes.summary: Yasumasa Sekine (born 1949) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology educated at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS. He held faculty posts at Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Watase
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Watase (b. 1941) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed a master's degree at Kyoto University. He served as an associate professor at Tokai University (~1985–2007) and president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2011).

nodes.label: Katsuhiko Kamimura
nodes.summary: Katsuhiko Kamimura (1944–2003) studied Indology and philosophy at the University of Tokyo and University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He taught at Kokugakuin University and served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Michio Yano
nodes.summary: Michio Yano is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi, earning a doctorate in 1996, and at Brown University under David Pingree. He served as a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from 1973 to 2015.

nodes.label: Issei Suzuki
nodes.summary: Issei Suzuki (1863–1943) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University, where he also served as a professor.

nodes.label: Ryoshu Michihata
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Michihata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Otani University (~1925–1928). Michihata later held posts at Otani University (~1946–1965) and served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1965–1980).

nodes.label: Mizumaro Ishida
nodes.summary: Mizumaro Ishida was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Tokai University (attested 1976 and 1987).

nodes.label: Rosemarie Fuchs
nodes.summary: Rosemarie Fuchs is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Tenzin Dorjee
nodes.summary: Tenzin Dorjee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Geshe Dawa, and served as General Secretary at Pullahari Monastery and translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

nodes.label: Allen Wright Thrasher
nodes.summary: Indologist Allen Wright Thrasher completed doctoral studies under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1968–1972) and studied under several traditional teachers. He held a post at the Library of Congress (~1987–2012).

nodes.label: Daniel H. H. Ingalls
variants: ダニエル・インゴールス
nodes.summary: Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher. Educated at Harvard and in India under Kalipada Tarkacharya and Walter Eugene Clark, he was a Junior Fellow and served as Wales Professor of Sanskrit at Harvard University.

nodes.label: T. Shrinivas Shastri
nodes.summary: T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indology scholar who held posts as Pandit and Professor at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1993, 2026).

nodes.label: Stefan Anacker
nodes.summary: Stefan Anacker (1939–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1964–1970) under Alex Wayman.

nodes.label: T. V. Venkatachala Sastry
nodes.description: Kannada writer, lexicographer, grammar expert, critic and editor
nodes.summary: T. V. Venkatachala Sastry (born 1933) is an Indologist and linguist. Educated at the University of Mysore, he held lectureships at Rural College, St. Joseph's, and Osmania University, and was a professor at the University of Mysore (1984–1994).

nodes.label: University of Mysore
variants: Institute of Kannada Studies, University of Mysore
Department of Jainology and Prakrits, University of Mysore
Kuvempu Institute of Kannada Studies at the university

nodes.label: Jacques May
nodes.summary: Jacques May (1927–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as editor-in-chief of Hōbōgirin (~1964–1981) and as a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1974–1992).

nodes.label: Richard Hugh Robinson
nodes.summary: Richard Hugh Robinson worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Alberta and London under Arthur Waley, David Friedman, and David Snellgrove, he taught at Toronto (1954) and became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1961.

nodes.label: University of Wisconsin-Madison
variants: Buddhist studies department at the University of Wisconsin
Memorial Library at the University of Wisconsin

nodes.label: Kyojun Shimizudani
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Kyojun Shimizudani studied under Keijun Shimizudani and at Taisho University. He served as professor at Taisho University (1919; 1926–1945), head of Hieizan Junior High School, and chief abbot of Sensō-ji (~1952–1979).

nodes.label: Manabendu Banerjee
nodes.summary: Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist. He served as Secretary of The Asiatic Society and was DSA Sanskrit Co-ordinator at Jadavpur University, attested in 2003.

nodes.label: John D. Dunne
nodes.summary: John D. Dunne, a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Malcolm David Eckel. He taught at Emory (~2005–2016) and held a Distinguished Chair at UW–Madison (1999).

nodes.label: Margaret R. Miles
nodes.summary: Margaret R. Miles is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at San Francisco State University and the Graduate Theological Union. She held posts at Harvard (1978–1996) and served as dean at the Graduate Theological Union (1996–2001).

nodes.label: Gary A. Tubb
nodes.summary: Gary A. Tubb (born 1950) is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He has held teaching posts at Harvard (attested 1999), Columbia (attested 2007), and the University of Chicago (attested 2011, Emeritus 2026).

nodes.label: James W. Benson
nodes.summary: James W. Benson is an Indologist who taught James McHugh and Susan J. Rosenfield. He was an Assistant Professor in Sanskrit at Harvard University (attested 1999–2003) and held a post at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

nodes.label: National Institute of Japanese Literature
variants: 国文学研究資料館文献資料部

nodes.label: Tokyo Woman's Christian University
variants: 東京女子大学文理学部

nodes.label: Leela Aditi Wood
nodes.summary: Leela Aditi Wood specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan (2005) under supervisors Luis O. Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

nodes.label: Walter M. Spink
nodes.summary: Walter M. Spink was a scholar of history/archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College (~1945–1949) and Harvard University (~1949–1954, PhD), and held posts at Brandeis University (1956–1961) and the University of Michigan (~1961–2000).

nodes.label: Thomas E. Crow
nodes.summary: Thomas E. Crow is a historian and archaeologist educated at Pomona College (BA 1965–1969) and UCLA (MA 1971–1975). He taught at CalArts, Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, and directed the Getty Research Institute before joining NYU in 2007.

nodes.label: Marvin Eisenberg
nodes.summary: Marvin Eisenberg (1922–2016) was an art historian. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954), and held a post at the University of Michigan from circa 1949 to 1983.

nodes.label: Cyrus Stearns
nodes.summary: Cyrus Stearns is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA under Turrell V. Wylie and a PhD under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp at the University of Washington (-1996), later working as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.

nodes.label: Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima
variants: Sde gzhung Rin po che, Kun dga' bstan pa'i nyi ma
デシュン・リンポチェ
nodes.image: Buddhist scholars - Dezhung Rinpoche III seated on a stool, Chris Wilkinson, student seated at the feet of his lama, wearing Buddhist robes, malas, likely Seattle, Washington, USA (16134833232) (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Gaton Ngawang Lekpa, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and Ngawang Nyima, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington from 1960 to 1972.

nodes.label: Chogye Trichen Rinpoche
variants: Bco brgyad Khri chen Rin po che, Ngag dbang legs bshad rgya mtsho
Bco brgyad Khri chen Rin po che
nodes.summary: Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Geshe Tshechok, Kunga Chöphel, and Zimwok Rinpoche, and became the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery in 1928.

nodes.label: Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche
variants: Dil mgo Mkhyen brtse Rin po che, Rab gsal zla ba
ディルゴ・キェンツェ
キャブジェ・ディルゴ・ケンツェ・リンポチェ
nodes.description: Buddhist Vajrayana master, scholar, poet, and teacher (1910–1991)
nodes.summary: Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (1910–1991) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied traditionally under Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje from 1987 to 1991.

nodes.label: Jong-Nam Choi
nodes.summary: Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Shitennoji University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1998 under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying with Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

nodes.label: David Seyfort Ruegg
nodes.summary: David Seyfort Ruegg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the Sorbonne and EPHE under Filliozat, Renou, Lalou, and Stein. He held chairs at Leiden (1966–1972), Washington (1972–1984), Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (~1983–1996).

nodes.label: Edward Garrett
nodes.summary: Edward Garrett is a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at UCLA in 2001 under Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, later mentored by Anna Szabolcsi, and held research posts at UCLA and the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Carson T. Schütze
nodes.summary: Carson T. Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997.

nodes.label: Dominique Sportiche
nodes.summary: Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1979–1984). He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles from around 1988.

nodes.label: Anna Szabolcsi
nodes.summary: Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (PhD). She worked at the Hungarian Research Centre for Linguistics (~1976–1989), UCLA (~1990–1998), and became professor of linguistics at New York University (~1998).

nodes.label: Naomi Appleton
nodes.summary: Naomi Appleton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. A former British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff University, she serves as Professor and Co-Director at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Lancaster University
variants: Department of Religious Studies in Lancaster
The Institute for Philosophy and Public Policy, Lancaster University

nodes.label: Laurie L. Patton
nodes.summary: Laurie L. Patton (b. 1961) works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Harvard and the University of Chicago (PhD), she held posts at Emory and Duke, served as President of Middlebury College (2015–2024), and became President of the AAAS (~2023).

nodes.label: Anna Aurelia Esposito
nodes.summary: Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and Tübingen (MA 1998). She was an assistant professor at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and holds a post at the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jonathan Geen
nodes.summary: Jonathan Geen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his doctorate at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff by 2001. He has taught at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

nodes.label: Phyllis Granoff
nodes.summary: Phyllis Granoff, a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, earned her BA at Radcliffe College and PhD at Harvard University. She was a professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and was appointed at Yale University in 2004.

nodes.label: McMaster University
variants: Department of Religious Studies at McMaster

nodes.label: Ryusei Keira
nodes.summary: Ryusei Keira works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Lausanne in 2003 under the supervision of Tom Tillemans.

nodes.label: Koichi Shinohara
nodes.summary: Koichi Shinohara is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He served as a professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and later as a senior lecturer in religious studies at Yale University (~2004).

nodes.id: I:The Okurayama Institute for the Study of Cultural Sciences
nodes.label: The Okurayama Institute for the Study of Cultural Sciences
Hidetoshi Yoshizawa
nodes.summary: Hidetoshi Yoshizawa works in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Taisho University as a researcher (研究員, attested 1998–2008) and later as chief research fellow (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Hirofumi Toda
nodes.summary: Hirofumi Toda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University (~1968–2001) and was a special member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra.

nodes.label: University of Texas at Austin
variants: The University of Texas at Austin
テキサス大学オースティン校

nodes.label: Hiroko Matsuoka
nodes.summary: Hiroko Matsuoka is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who pursued doctoral studies at Hiroshima University (attested 2006). She has held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (attested 2016) and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Sueki
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Sueki (born 1952) is a Buddhist studies scholar who undertook short-term study at Tübingen University Library (1990–1991). He held positions at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, serving as deputy director.

nodes.label: Michael Torsten Much
nodes.summary: Michael Torsten Much is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner and was a fellow at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Helmut Tauscher
nodes.summary: Helmut Tauscher is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He held faculty and professorship posts at the University of Vienna, attested between 1983 and 2026, and served as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

nodes.label: Zeff Bjerken
nodes.summary: Zeff Bjerken is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr., and held a post at the College of Charleston (attested 2001).

nodes.label: T. Griffith Foulk
nodes.summary: T. Griffith Foulk specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1978–1987) under Luis O. Gómez, later teaching there (~1987–1995) and serving as Riggs Professor of Religion at Sarah Lawrence College.

nodes.label: Lopon Tenzin Namdak
nodes.summary: Lopon Tenzin Namdak (born 1926) specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Tingchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri monasteries, he served as lopön at Menri and Triten Norbutse, and was a visiting scholar at SOAS (1961) and Munich (1969).

nodes.label: Ryoken Nawa
nodes.summary: Ryoken Nawa works in indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at Osaka University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Makoto Nagai
nodes.summary: Makoto Nagai (1881–1970) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1934–1942), Nihon, Toyo, and Kamakura Women's universities, and president of Chuo Shoka Junior College (1951).

nodes.label: Shun Hidaka
nodes.summary: Shun Hidaka is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Rajendra Chandra Hazra
nodes.summary: Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) was an Indologist who earned his B.A. and completed doctoral study under Sushil Kumar De at the University of Dhaka. He taught at Dhaka (1939–1951) and was Associate Professor at Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

nodes.label: Sushil Kumar De
nodes.summary: Sushil Kumar De (1890–1968) was an Indologist who studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, SOAS, and University of Bonn. He held professorships at the University of Calcutta and University of Dhaka, and headed the Bengali department at Jadavpur University.

nodes.label: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar
nodes.summary: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar was an Indologist educated at the University of Mumbai and Heidelberg University. He held positions at Fergusson College, served as Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1939–2001), and was a professor and dean at Pune University.

nodes.label: Izumi Hoshi
nodes.summary: Izumi Hoshi is a Tibetologist and linguist who completed her degrees at the University of Tokyo between ~1987 and 1997. She joined the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as an assistant professor in 1997 and served as director from 2019 to 2023.

nodes.label: Michiyo Hoshi
nodes.summary: Michiyo Hoshi is a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. She has held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa as a collaborative researcher and at Toyo Bunko as a researcher (attested 2003).

variants: アジア・アフリカ言語文化研究所

variants: ガワン・トゥンドゥプ

nodes.label: Temba Gyaltsen
variants: テンバ・ギェンツェン

nodes.label: Jitsuaki Oshika
nodes.summary: Jitsuaki Oshika is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Tohoku University from circa 1941 to 1944 and served as a professor at Toyo University from circa 1965 to 1990.

nodes.label: Yasuo Goto
nodes.summary: Yasuo Goto is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1991) and as a part-time lecturer at both Ryukoku University and Shuchiin University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Ronald Y. Nakasone
nodes.summary: Ronald Y. Nakasone is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1974–1980). He held positions at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (assistant professor ~1987) and Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Hirofumi Isoda
nodes.summary: Hirofumi Isoda works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1961–1966), where he served as lecturer (~1966–1974) and associate professor (~1974–2001), and is attested as professor emeritus at Shimane University (1974).

nodes.label: Leonid Kulikov
nodes.summary: Leonid Kulikov is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who has held posts at Leiden University (attested 2007) and Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Werner Abraham
nodes.summary: Werner Abraham was a linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna. He held posts at Illinois (~1965–1967), Tübingen (1970–1971), and Groningen (1971), alongside guest professorships at Cologne, Vienna (2001), and Lund.

nodes.label: Tarab Tulku XI
nodes.summary: Tarab Tulku XI (1934–2004) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1966–1998) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen (~1970–2000).

nodes.label: Hartmut Buescher
nodes.summary: Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhāl Tripathi, later holding a post at Copenhagen and an affiliation with the Royal Danish Library (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Burkhard Quessel
nodes.summary: Burkhard Quessel is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was a member (attested 1997). He later served as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).

nodes.label: British Library
variants: British Library’s Oriental and India Office Collections

nodes.label: Kenneth G. Zysk
nodes.summary: Kenneth G. Zysk is an Indologist and historian educated at UC Santa Barbara and the Australian National University. He held posts at UCLA, Wisconsin-Madison, Toronto, Eastern Michigan University, and the University of Copenhagen (attested 2012–2026).

nodes.label: Christian K. Wedemeyer
nodes.summary: Christian K. Wedemeyer (b. 1969), a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, studied at Wesleyan and Columbia. He held posts at Copenhagen (2000–2003) and the University of Chicago (2003–2011).

nodes.label: Ole Holten Pind
nodes.summary: Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (~2003–2009) under the supervision of Ernst Steinkellner.

nodes.label: John Ronald Newman
nodes.summary: John Ronald Newman is a specialist in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).

nodes.label: Kyogaku Dendo Research Center
variants: 浄土真宗本願寺派教学伝道研究センター

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Ueno
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004) and held a research post at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Eric David Mortensen
nodes.summary: Eric David Mortensen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD from Harvard University (attested 2003) under the supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton.

nodes.label: Kimberley C. Patton
nodes.summary: Kimberley C. Patton is a religious studies scholar who completed her dissertation at Harvard University. She was an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (1991) and served as professor at Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Yoshiki Motoaki
nodes.summary: Yoshiki Motoaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with Otani University (attested 2013) and the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Christopher S. George
nodes.summary: Christopher S. George works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler (1965) and with Geshe Wangyal and Padma Gyaltsan, later founding the American Institute of Buddhist Studies (1972) and teaching at IASWR (1982).

nodes.label: Geshe Wangyal
nodes.summary: Geshe Wangyal (1901–1983) studied at Drepung Monastery and under Agvan Dorzhiev. A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he directed the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center from circa 1958 to 1983 and taught at Columbia University from circa 1960 to 1972.

nodes.label: Joe Bransford Wilson
nodes.summary: Joe Bransford Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, taught there from 1981 to 1985, and later taught at the University of North Carolina Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

nodes.label: Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin
nodes.summary: Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at MSU Institute of Asian and African Studies and under George de Roerich, he held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies and Moscow State University.

nodes.label: Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya
variants: マルガリータ・ヴァラビヨーヴァ=デシャトフスカヤ
マルガリータ・ヴァラビョーヴァ=デシャトフスカヤ

nodes.summary: Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya studied at St. Petersburg University and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology, she was a researcher and manuscript curator at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts from 1956 to 2021.

nodes.label: Ryojun Mitomo
nodes.summary: Ryojun Mitomo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a professorship at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and served as a professor in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Raghu Vira
nodes.summary: Raghu Vira (1902–1963) was an Indologist educated at University of the Punjab and Leiden University. He headed Sanskrit at Sanatan Dharma College (~1931–1946) and founded the International Academy of Indian Culture, serving as its director in 1934.

nodes.label: Lokesh Chandra
nodes.jawiki: ローケーシュ・チャンドラ
nodes.summary: Lokesh Chandra (born 1927) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Punjab University and Utrecht University (Ph.D. under Jan Gonda), long directed the International Academy of Indian Culture, and later chaired the ICCR and ICHR.

nodes.label: Richard F. Nance
nodes.summary: Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (-2004) and held Assistant (attested 2013) and Associate Professor (attested 2026) posts at Indiana University Bloomington.

nodes.label: Toshio Horiuchi
nodes.summary: Toshio Horiuchi works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his PhD at the University of Tokyo. He has held positions as a postdoctoral researcher at Zhejiang University and as a visiting researcher at Toyo University.

nodes.label: Atsushi Ibuki
nodes.summary: Atsushi Ibuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University (~1978–1989) and became a professor at Toyo University (~2007).

nodes.id: I:Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies
Tomoyuki Komine
nodes.summary: Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University, where he also served as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Ruriko Sakuma
nodes.summary: Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Nagoya University. She held posts at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2015, 2026), International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Daiki Sasaki

nodes.label: Masahide Mori
nodes.summary: Masahide Mori works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his MA at Nagoya University and his PhD at the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, later serving as assistant professor (~1999–2006) and professor (from ~2006) at Kanazawa University.

nodes.label: Tsutomu Yamaguchi

nodes.label: Kazuyoshi Hotta
nodes.summary: Kazuyoshi Hotta works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo, where he also served as director of the Buddhist Youth Association (attested 2007), and was an assistant professor at Otani University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Steven Weinberger
nodes.summary: Steven Weinberger is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College and the University of Virginia, completing his Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins, and held an affiliation with the University of Virginia (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga
nodes.summary: Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under teachers including Tritsho Khenpo Rinchen, Khenpo Appey, and Chogye Trichen. He founded the Sakya Centre (1964), Sakya College, and Sakya Institute, and taught numerous students.

nodes.label: Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche (1920–2009) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Dudjom Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He taught at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (1960–1970) and at the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Ralf Kramer
nodes.summary: Ralf Kramer (born 1971), a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and at the University of London. He became Aris Librarian for Tibetan & Himalayan Studies at the Bodleian Library.

nodes.label: Achim Bayer
nodes.summary: Achim Bayer specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his MA under David P. Jackson and his PhD at the University of Hamburg (2005) under Lambert Schmithausen, later working as a research associate at the University of Munich (2004–2006).

nodes.label: Lore Sander
nodes.summary: Lore Sander (born 1936) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (ca. 1960–1965) and held positions at the Museum für Indische Kunst (curator, 1987) and Free University of Berlin (lecturer, 1994).

nodes.label: Arjo Vanderjagt
nodes.summary: Arjo Vanderjagt, a philosopher and historian, studied at the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), the University of Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

nodes.label: Seiji Kumagai
nodes.summary: Seiji Kumagai (born 1980) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2003–2008) and became an associate professor there around 2013.

nodes.label: Seizan Yanagida
nodes.summary: Seizan Yanagida (1922–2006) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto universities under Kaiten Nukariya and Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, later serving on faculties at Hanazono, Kyoto, and Chubu universities.

nodes.label: Yoshio Kawakatsu
nodes.summary: Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Kyoto University (~1945–1948) and under Paul Demiéville (~1967–1969). He spent his career on the library assistant staff at Kyoto University (~1952–1984).

nodes.summary: Tsung-i Jao was a Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Shantou Jinshan Middle School (~1929–1930). He held posts at the University of Hong Kong (~1952–1968), National University of Singapore (~1968–1973), Yale (~1970–1971), and EPHE (~1978–1979).

nodes.label: Serinity Young

nodes.label: Nicholas Dirks

nodes.label: Ann Laura Stoler

nodes.label: Samuel M. Grupper
nodes.summary: Samuel M. Grupper is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, studying under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.

nodes.label: Join Saeki
nodes.summary: Join Saeki (1867–1952) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji under Jōchō Chihaya. He served as head of Horyu-ji (1903–1950) and held appointments at Kangakuin, the University of Tokyo, and the Japan Academy (1929).

nodes.label: Shoko Takeuchi
nodes.summary: Shoko Takeuchi specialized in Buddhist studies, studying at Ryukoku University. Takeuchi later served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University, attested between 1987 and 1995.

nodes.label: Yasutoshi Murakami

nodes.summary: Takatoshi Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who held a professorship at Komazawa University, attested in 1981 and 1991.

nodes.summary: An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Pāsādika earned degrees from Magadh and Punjabi universities. He held academic posts at Punjabi University, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences, Marburg, Würzburg, and Bochum, and directed the Frankfurt Buddhist Academy in 2022.

nodes.label: Sherab Gyatso
nodes.summary: Sherab Gyatso (1884–1968) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Gori, Labrang, Drepung, Guru, and Detsha monasteries under numerous teachers. nodes.label: Susumu Shimazono

nodes.label: John Brockington
nodes.summary: John Brockington is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He held a post as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (attested 1987 and 2003).

ウォルフソン・カレッジ

nodes.label: Barbara Nimri Aziz
nodes.summary: Barbara Nimri Aziz (born 1940) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. She completed a B.A. at Queen's University at Kingston and earned a Ph.D. under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf at SOAS in 1974, later holding a post at the University of Oran (2007).

nodes.label: Kōjirō Yoshikawa
nodes.summary: A Sinologist, Kōjirō Yoshikawa studied at Kyoto University from circa 1923 to 1926. He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and as board chairman of Toho Gakkai (~1973–1980).

nodes.label: Tokuryu Yamauchi
nodes.summary: Philosopher Tokuryu Yamauchi studied at Kyoto University, the University of Freiburg, and under Kitaro Nishida and Martin Heidegger. His career included professorships at Hitotsubashi University, Kyoto University, Ryukoku University, and the presidency of Kyoto University of Education.

nodes.label: Ludwig Alsdorf
nodes.summary: Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist who studied under Walther Schubring at Hamburg and Heinrich Lüders at Berlin. He taught at the University of Allahabad (1930–1932), Humboldt University of Berlin (1935, 1944), and held a chair at Hamburg (1950–1972).

nodes.label: Annemarie von Gabain
nodes.summary: Annemarie von Gabain was a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and archaeology who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1920–1925). She held posts at Humboldt University (circa 1935–1945) and as professor at the University of Hamburg (circa 1950–1966).

nodes.label: Johannes Nobel
nodes.summary: Johannes Nobel specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Greifswald and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. After posts at the Prussian State Library and Berlin, he held the Indology chair at the University of Marburg from 1928 to 1955.

nodes.label: Guy Newland
nodes.summary: Newland specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning his PhD at the University of Virginia and studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and several Tibetan teachers. He served as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).

nodes.label: Harvey B. Aronson
nodes.summary: Harvey B. Aronson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Supervised by Richard Hugh Robinson and taught by scholars including Stephan Beyer and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, he held a professorship at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and co-directed the Dawn Mountain Center.

nodes.label: Tibet House, New Delhi
variants: Tibet House cultural center in New Delhi

nodes.label: Shunei Tsuboi
nodes.summary: Shunei Tsuboi was a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Bukkyo University, with his tenure attested in 1963 and 1972.

nodes.label: Honsho Ueda
nodes.summary: Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992, 1996) at Minobusan University. He was also attested as director at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia in 1996.

nodes.label: Shoku Bando
nodes.summary: Shoku Bando studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg. In 1987, Bando held posts at the Abhidharma Research Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

nodes.label: Shodo Yamagami
nodes.summary: Shodo Yamagami is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University between 1958 and 1964 and served as an assistant professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from circa 1972 to 2009.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Kuroda
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Kuroda (born 1952) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University (~1974–1976). Around 1982, he served as an associate professor at both Osaka Gakuin University and Osaka Gakuin College.

nodes.id: I:Society for the Study of the History of Indian Thought
nodes.label: Society for the Study of the History of Indian Thought
variants: Society for the Study of the History of Indian Thought

nodes.label: Osamu Takata
nodes.summary: Osamu Takata was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Baiei Henmi and served as the director of the fine arts department at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.

nodes.label: Baiei Henmi
nodes.description: Japanese historian of Indian and Buddhist art
nodes.summary: Baiei Henmi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (circa 1915–1918) and held a post at Tama Art University.

nodes.label: Bimal Krishna Matilal
nodes.summary: Bimal Krishna Matilal was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and Harvard University (Ph.D. under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), taught at the University of Toronto (~1968–1977), and was Spalding Professor at Oxford (1977–1991).

nodes.id: I:Association for the Study of Indian Thought
nodes.label: Association for the Study of Indian Thought
Taishu Tagami
nodes.summary: Taishu Tagami specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. His main academic career included serving as a professor at Komazawa University from around 1978 to 2005.

nodes.label: Colette Caillat
nodes.description: French professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar (1921–2007)
nodes.summary: An Indology and linguistics scholar, Caillat studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at CNRS, the University of Lyon, Sorbonne University (1967–1988), Collège de France (Director ~1987–1999), and Institut de France (~1987–2007).

nodes.label: Bibliothèque de l'Institut de France
variants: フランス学士院図書館

nodes.label: Toshikazu Watanabe
nodes.summary: Toshikazu Watanabe specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He has worked as a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and was appointed professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.

nodes.label: Harry Falk
nodes.summary: Harry Falk specializes in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He held a post at the University of Freiburg (~1976–1990) and served as Professor of Indology and Director at the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2012).

nodes.label: Nancy Hock
nodes.summary: Nancy Hock is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (1987), where she was supervised by Joanna Gottfried Williams, and held a post at the Asian Art Museum (attested 1987).

nodes.label: American Institute of Indian Studies
variants: A.I.I.S. Centre for Art and Archaeology
Centre for Art and Archaeology at the American institute of Indian Studies in Gurgaon

nodes.label: Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky
nodes.summary: Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky (1927–2016) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After graduating from Fergusson College (~1947–1951), he founded the Archeology Research Group in 1951 and served as Associate Director (1976–1996) and director emeritus of research (~1976–2005) at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

nodes.label: Lewis Lancaster
nodes.jawiki: ルイス・ランカスター
nodes.summary: Lewis Lancaster studied at Roanoke, Claremont, and Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Sinology, he held appointments at the University of California, Berkeley (~1967–2002) and as president of the University of the West (1992).

nodes.label: Asian Art Museum
variants: Asian Art Museum in San Francisco
Asian Art Museum of San Francisco

nodes.label: Joanna Gottfried Williams
nodes.summary: Joanna Gottfried Williams was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. She studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University, and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1971 to 2011.

nodes.label: Debala Mitra
nodes.summary: Debala Mitra was an archaeologist and scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.

nodes.label: Koichi Furusaka
nodes.summary: Koichi Furusaka specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Hakuyu Hadano and served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas
nodes.summary: Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas (1916–1999) earned degrees from Mysore, Mumbai, and Oxford. An Indologist, he taught at Oxford (~1948–1951), Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1951–1959), University of Delhi (1959), and chaired the Institute for Social and Economic Change (1972–1979).

nodes.id: I:Institute for Social and Economic Change
nodes.label: Institute for Social and Economic Change
variants: Institute for Social and Economic Change
Institute for Social and Economic Change, Bangalore

nodes.label: Govind Sadashiv Ghurye
nodes.summary: Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (1893–1983) studied at Elphinstone College and Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and A. C. Haddon. An Indologist, he headed the Department of Sociology at the University of Mumbai (1924–1959) and founded the Indian Sociological Society.

nodes.label: W. H. R. Rivers
nodes.description: English anthropologist, neurologist, ethnologist and psychiatrist (1864-1922)
nodes.summary: W. H. R. Rivers (1864–1922) was an anthropologist and medical scholar who studied at London and St Bartholomew's. He held medical posts, taught at Cambridge and UCL, became a Fellow at St John's, and presided over the Anthropological Society.

nodes.label: Peter Haskel
nodes.summary: Peter Haskel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued graduate studies at Columbia University under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

nodes.label: Bruce John Stewart
nodes.summary: Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and earned his PhD at Columbia University (attested 1983) under Alex Wayman, also studying under Joel Brereton and Christopher S. George.

nodes.label: John Gombojab Hangin
nodes.summary: John Gombojab Hangin worked in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies, earning degrees from Columbia (-1963) and Indiana University (~1965–1970). After posts at Johns Hopkins and Georgetown, he was a full professor at Indiana (1965–1989).

nodes.label: Francis Woodman Cleaves
nodes.description: American orientalist historian. mongolist and sinologist (1911-1995)
nodes.summary: Francis Woodman Cleaves was a scholar of sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Dartmouth, Harvard (PhD 1942), and under Paul Pelliot (1935), serving as a Harvard professor from 1941 to 1980.

nodes.label: Brian Gregory Baumann
nodes.summary: Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Buddhist studies. He received his Ph.D. from Indiana University Bloomington under György Kara and served as a Mongolian language lecturer at UC Berkeley and Numata Center.

nodes.label: György Kara
nodes.summary: György Kara worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Gyula Németh, Lajos Ligeti, and Barnabás Csongor. He served at ELTE, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and Indiana University Bloomington (1993–2022).

nodes.label: Stephen R. Bokenkamp
nodes.summary: Stephen R. Bokenkamp, a scholar of sinology and religious studies, studied at the University of California, Berkeley (1976–1986). He served at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2007) and Arizona State University (~2007), and was a visiting fellow at ANU (1999).

nodes.label: Maho Iuchi
nodes.image: Maho Iuchi in the video 'From teaching networks to reincarnation The transformation of Kadampa monasteries in early Tibet'.png
nodes.summary: Maho Iuchi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Otani University by 2008 and served as a visiting researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Jon Kabat-Zinn
variants: ジョン・カバット・ジン
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・カバット・ジン
nodes.description: American professor emeritus of medicine and the creator of the Stress Reduction Clinic and the Center for Mindfulness in Medicine
nodes.summary: Jon Kabat-Zinn studied at Haverford College and MIT under Salvador E. Luria, also learning from Jack Kornfield, Joseph Goldstein, and others. He founded the Stress Reduction Clinic and served as a professor at the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School (~1979–2000).

nodes.label: Jack Kornfield
nodes.summary: Jack Kornfield studied at Dartmouth under Wing-tsit Chan, at Saybrook University, and under Ajahn Chah, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Dipa Ma. Working in Buddhist and religious studies, he co-founded the Insight Meditation Society (1974) and Spirit Rock Meditation Center (1987).

nodes.label: Joseph Goldstein
nodes.summary: Joseph Goldstein is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Columbia and under teachers including Anagarika Munindra and Mahasi Sayadaw. He taught at Naropa University (1974) and founded the Insight Meditation Society (1974) and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (1989).

nodes.label: Philip Kapleau
nodes.summary: Philip Kapleau was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Soen Nakagawa, Daiun Sogaku Harada, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani between 1950 and 1967. He founded the Rochester Zen Center and Chapin Mill Retreat Center.

Dibner Institute for the History of Science and Technology at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

Daniel B. Stevenson
nodes.summary: Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He held assistant professorships at Butler University (attested 1986) and the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003), and was a guest scholar at Soka University.

variants: University of Kansas Center for East Asian Studies
カンザス大学大学院東洋美術史研究科

nodes.label: Jinhua Chen
nodes.summary: Jinhua Chen works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at McMaster University and completed postdoctoral research at Kyoto University under Noritoshi Aramaki. He held positions at the University of Virginia and as professor of East Asian Buddhism at the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Ming-Wood Liu
nodes.summary: Ming-Wood Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hong Kong and earned his PhD at UCLA under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en, later serving as professor at the University of Hong Kong (~1980–2008).

nodes.label: Robert Epp
nodes.summary: Robert Epp (born 1926) is a scholar in the field of Japanology. He studied at Harvard University and held an academic post at the University of California, Los Angeles, from ~1969 to 1972.

nodes.label: Etsuaki Teraishi
nodes.summary: Etsuaki Teraishi works in Indology and philosophy. Teraishi held an attested post as assistant professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College in 1999 and as a special researcher with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science in 2001.

variants: School of Languages, Cultures and Religions
Scottish Centre for Japanese Studies, University of Stirling
Scottish Centre for Japanese Studies at the University of Stirling

nodes.label: Dipak Kumar Barua
nodes.summary: Dipak Kumar Barua (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a Dean at the University of Calcutta in 1987 and headed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara from circa 1996 to 2002.

nodes.label: Saswati Mutsuddy
nodes.summary: Saswati Mutsuddy works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Dipak Kumar Barua and served on the teaching staff in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Jacob Dalton
nodes.summary: Jacob Dalton specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD from the University of Michigan (2002) under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held positions at SOAS, Yale (2005), and UC Berkeley, where he is Distinguished University Professor.

nodes.label: Itsuo Asako
nodes.summary: Itsuo Asako is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He served at Hanazono University as an assistant professor (attested 1997) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yutaka Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Yutaka Kawasaki specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Kawasaki studied under Seio Okuda and held positions at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Mai Mishiro
nodes.summary: Mai Mishiro is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held an attested post at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science in 2011 and at Waseda University in 2016.

nodes.label: Junko Matsumura
nodes.summary: Junko Matsumura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Matsumura completed an MA in Asian Studies at the Australian National University and a doctoral dissertation at the University of Göttingen, later serving as professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Henk Bodewitz
nodes.summary: Henk Bodewitz was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Utrecht University, completing his PhD under Jan Gonda, and held teaching posts at Utrecht (including chair of Sanskrit, 1976–1992) and Leiden University (~1973–1976; 1992–2002).

nodes.label: Yusho Miyasaka
nodes.summary: Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Chizan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe, holding posts at Koyasan University (1954, 1965–1967), Nagoya University (1977–1984), Chisan Denpōin (1987), and Shuchiin University (2001).

nodes.label: John R. McRae
nodes.description: born:1947-04-28|died:2011|; McRae, John R., 1947-2011; McRae, John R.
nodes.summary: John R. McRae (1947–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. His career included faculty posts at Cornell University, Indiana University Bloomington, Komazawa University, and the Numata Center.

nodes.label: Ryosho Tanaka
nodes.summary: Ryosho Tanaka studied at Komazawa University, working in Buddhist studies and sinology. He served Komazawa University as assistant, professor, dean, museum director, and president, and also held a professorship at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Chishō Namai
nodes.summary: Chishō Namai (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Namai served as a professor (attested 1996) and later as president (attested 2008) of Koyasan University.

nodes.label: Chikyo Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Chikyo Yamamoto (1910–1993) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Yamamoto held positions at Koyasan University, serving as a professor in 1970 and as a part-time lecturer in 1980.

nodes.label: Shintei Hinonishi
nodes.summary: Shintei Hinonishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shigeru Gorai. He held academic posts at Koyasan University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and later as a professor (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Akira Mukai
nodes.summary: Akira Mukai is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Hokkaido University (~1969–1975). He served as an assistant at Hokkaido University (~1975) and professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Klaus Wille
nodes.summary: Klaus Wille is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He was attested as holding academic and research positions at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1997 and at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities between 2000 and 2026.

nodes.label: Kongo Jushinkai
variants: 社会福祉法人金剛樹心会

nodes.label: Takanori Fukita
nodes.summary: Takanori Fukita works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Fukita studied as a graduate student at Bukkyo University (attested 2017), held a post at Bukkyo University, and was appointed special appointment faculty (lecturer) at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: M. G. Dhadphale
nodes.summary: M. G. Dhadphale (born 1937) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000) and as editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

nodes.label: S. D. Laddu
nodes.summary: S. D. Laddu specialized in Indology and linguistics. He was associated with Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1968) and served as Editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Saroja Bhate
nodes.summary: Saroja Bhate (b. 1942) is an Indologist and linguist. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1988–2002) and as Honorary Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1999–2005).

nodes.label: Amrit Madhav Ghatage
nodes.summary: Amrit Madhav Ghatage (1913–2003) was an Indologist and linguist. He was Professor of Indo-European Philology, General Linguistics, and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College (c. 1961–1978), and Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (c. 1993–2003).

nodes.label: Yuto Kawamura
nodes.summary: Yuto Kawamura is an Indology scholar who was a postdoc fellow at Kyoto University (2015–2018) and held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), the University of Oxford (attested 2019), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Tokyo University of Education
variants: 東京教育大学文学部倫理学科
東京教育大学大学院文学研究科

nodes.label: Laura Harrington
nodes.summary: Laura Harrington works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi, Gary A. Tubb, Lobsang Jamspal, Kirti Rinpoche, Nathaniel Dickson, and Gregory A. Hillis.

nodes.label: Gregory A. Hillis
nodes.summary: Gregory A. Hillis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA at the University of Virginia (1993), where he held a post (attested 2002), and became a Continuing Lecturer at UC Santa Barbara (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Satoshi Ito
nodes.summary: Satoshi Ito is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1980–1989) and became a professor at Ibaraki University (~2003).

nodes.label: Osamu Izumoji
nodes.summary: Osamu Izumoji is a scholar in sinology and other fields. He held academic posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Charles Goodman
nodes.summary: Charles Goodman is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Allan Gibbard. He has served as an Associate Professor at Binghamton University.

nodes.label: Allan Gibbard
nodes.description: American philosopher and social choice theorist
nodes.summary: Philosopher Allan Gibbard studied at Swarthmore College (~1959–1963) and Harvard University (~1965–1971). He held posts at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and University of Michigan (1977–2016).

nodes.label: Stephen F. Teiser
nodes.summary: Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religion who earned his bachelor's from Oberlin and master's and doctorate from Princeton (~1979–1986). In ~1996, he became D. T. Suzuki Professor at Princeton.

nodes.label: Franciscus Verellen
nodes.summary: Franciscus Verellen is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned doctorates at Oxford and EPHE under Kristofer Schipper. He taught at EPHE and Columbia before serving as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021).

プリンストン高等研究所

nodes.label: Monica Esposito
nodes.description: Italian translator and historian of Chinese Religion, Daoism (1962-2011)
nodes.summary: Monica Esposito was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She studied at Venice, Fudan, Ghent, Shanghai, and Paris (PhD 1993), and later served as an associate professor at Kyoto University from around 2003 to 2011.

nodes.label: Michael Puett
nodes.summary: Michael Puett is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu. He has held professorships at Harvard University, including the Walter C. Klein Professorship.

nodes.label: Jean-Noël Robert
nodes.summary: Jean-Noël Robert is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under Bernard Frank and at INALCO. He held posts at the CNRS (1975–1990), EPHE (from 1979), and served as director at Collège de France (2010–2022).

nodes.label: Ryoshu Koda
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Koda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and indology who studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. Koda held researcher posts at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Institute for Buddhist Culture (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Satoshi Kono
nodes.summary: Satoshi Kono specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

nodes.label: Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies
Nobukatsu Komai
nodes.summary: Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University. He held a post as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Paul G. Hackett
nodes.summary: Paul G. Hackett is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Richard B. Martin at the University of Virginia, where he served as a bibliographer and curator, and later held research and lecturer positions at Columbia University.

nodes.label: Masaaki Chikusa
nodes.summary: Masaaki Chikusa (1930–2015) was a scholar of history, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned three degrees including a doctorate from Kyoto University, where he was a professor (1981–1993), before serving as professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).

nodes.label: Yeshe Thubten
nodes.summary: Yeshe Thubten was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Sera Monastery and under teachers including Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He taught at UC Santa Cruz (1977-1978) and founded Kopan Monastery, Tushita Meditation Centre, and FPMT.

nodes.label: University of California, Santa Cruz
variants: Oakes College, University of California at Santa Cruz

nodes.label: Jean Filliozat
nodes.summary: Jean Filliozat was an Indologist who studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He founded and directed the French Institute of Pondicherry (1955–1977), directed the EFEO (1956–1977), and held chairs at EPHE (1941–1978) and the Collège de France (1951–1978).

nodes.label: Thomas Freeman Yarnall
nodes.summary: Thomas Freeman Yarnall works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and Columbia University (PhD 2003) under Robert A. F. Thurman, among others, and served as Executive Editor in Columbia's Department of Religion (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Wayne Proudfoot
nodes.summary: Wayne Proudfoot (born 1939) works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University, taught at Fordham University (~1970–1972), and served as Professor of Religion at Columbia University (~1972–2018).

nodes.label: G. Thomas Tanselle
nodes.summary: G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University. He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978), served as vice president of the Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978–2006), and was adjunct professor of English at Columbia University (~1978–2006).

nodes.label: E. Gene Smith
nodes.summary: Tibetologist E. Gene Smith studied under Turrell V. Wylie and several Tibetan masters. He served at the Library of Congress (1968–1985, 1994–1997) and founded and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (1999–2010).

nodes.label: 14th Dalai Lama
variants: His Holiness the Fourteenth Dalai Lama
His Holiness the Dalai Lama Tenzin Gyatso
nodes.description: 14th Dalai Lama, the spiritual and temporal leader of Tibetans
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, he studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and others. He founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists (1989) and the Mind and Life Institute (1990).

nodes.label: Jigdal Dagchen Sakya
nodes.summary: Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He held a post at the University of Washington from circa 1960 to 1963.

nodes.label: Mario D'Amato
nodes.summary: Mario D'Amato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He held posts at Hampshire College (attested 2001) and Rollins College as an assistant professor.

nodes.label: Bunkyo Aoki
nodes.summary: Bunkyo Aoki worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University and under Kozui Otani (~1908–1914), later serving as a Tibetan language lecturer at the University of Tokyo from 1951, succeeding Tokan Tada.

nodes.label: Ekai Kawaguchi
variants: Ekai Kawaguchi (河口慧海, Kawaguchi Ekai)
nodes.summary: Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Toyo University (graduated 1892), Sera Monastery, and with teachers including Enryo Inoue and Sarat Chandra Das. He served as rector of Gohyaku Rakan-ji (~1888–1891) and professor at Toyo University (1916).

nodes.label: Johan Elverskog
nodes.summary: Johan Elverskog works in Buddhist studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at UC Berkeley and Indiana University Bloomington under scholars including Christopher P. Atwood and Jan Nattier. He held posts at UCSB, IMASS, and Southern Methodist University (~2002).

nodes.id: I:Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences
nodes.label: Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences
variants: Inner Mongolia Academy of Social Sciences

nodes.label: Eun Hino
nodes.summary: Eun Hino is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed a master's course at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and Musashino University.

nodes.label: Hiromi Habata
nodes.summary: Hiromi Habata, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a Ph.D. at the University of Freiburg. She held posts at the University of Munich, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Takayasu Suzuki
nodes.summary: Takayasu Suzuki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1985–1994). He served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University (~2008).

nodes.label: Yamaguchi Prefectural University
variants: 山口県立大学国際文化学部
