nodes.label: Shinten Sakai
nodes.summary: Shinten Sakai worked in the fields of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teacher Shindo Shiraishi and held an academic post at Koyasan University, attested in 1959.

nodes.label: Günter Schweiger
nodes.summary: Günter Schweiger is a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Gert Klingenschmitt and at Vienna University of Economics and Business. He served as a full university professor at Vienna University of Economics and Business (1974–2009).

nodes.label: Gert Klingenschmitt
nodes.summary: Gert Klingenschmitt specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Karl Hoffmann and habilitated at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, later holding the chair for Indo-European linguistics at the University of Regensburg.

nodes.label: Rosemarie Lühr
nodes.summary: Rosemarie Lühr is a linguist and Indologist who earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg. She held posts at the University of Regensburg, University of Giessen, University of Jena (1994–2013), and Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Michael Janda
nodes.summary: Michael Janda works in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Jochem Schindler and Heiner Eichner, habilitated at the University of Zurich, and was appointed to the Indo-European linguistics chair at the University of Münster in 2002.

nodes.label: Chlodwig H. Werba
nodes.summary: Chlodwig H. Werba (b. 1947) is an Indologist and linguist. He held academic posts as a professor at the University of Vienna, attested between 1997 and 2022.

nodes.label: Harumi Hirano Ziegler
nodes.summary: Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. She completed both her MA (awarded 1994) and her PhD (awarded 2001) at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she was supervised by Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.label: Tairyō Makita
nodes.summary: Tairyō Makita worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Shinryo Iwai and at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto Universities. He held posts at Kyoto University from 1949 to 1976 and served as president of Saitama Institute of Technology in 1997.

nodes.id: I:École Nationale des Langues Orientales Vivantes
nodes.label: École Nationale des Langues Orientales Vivantes
Rolf Alfred Stein
nodes.summary: Rolf Alfred Stein worked in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, studying at SOS, INALCO, and EPHE under Pelliot, Maspero, Chavannes, and Bacot, among others. He was directeur d'études at EPHE (1951–1975) and professor at the Collège de France (1965–1982).

nodes.label: Samten Gyaltsen Karmay
nodes.summary: A Tibetology and religious studies scholar, he studied at Drepung Monastery and the University of London (PhD under David Snellgrove). He held posts at SOAS, Collège de France, and CNRS, and was President of the IATS (1995-2000).

nodes.label: Klemens Karlsson
nodes.summary: Klemens Karlsson specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under Peter Schalk and received his Doctor of Philosophy from Uppsala University in 2000.

nodes.label: Stockholm University
variants: Institutionen for Orientaliska Språk, Universitet i Stockholm

nodes.label: Susan L. Huntington
nodes.summary: Susan L. Huntington (born 1943) is a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She was a professor at Ohio State University from approximately 1970 to 2011.

nodes.label: Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan
nodes.summary: Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2003 under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a fellowship at Grinnell College.

nodes.label: Kashi Prasad Jayaswal
nodes.summary: Kashi Prasad Jayaswal was an Indologist and historian who studied at Allahabad, Jesus College, Oxford (M.A. ~1906–1909), and Lincoln's Inn. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at Calcutta (1917) and president of the Numismatic Society of India (~1936–1937).

nodes.label: Masako Keta
nodes.summary: Masako Keta is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied under Yoshinori Takeuchi at Kyoto University. She held positions at Kanazawa University (1988, 1998) before serving as professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University (2000–2018).

nodes.label: Keiji Nishitani
nodes.summary: Keiji Nishitani (1900–1990) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied under Kitaro Nishida and Hajime Tanabe at Kyoto University and under Martin Heidegger at Freiburg. He served as associate professor (1935) and professor (1943–1964) at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Kitaro Nishida
nodes.summary: Kitaro Nishida was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, he taught at the Fourth Higher School before serving as Professor of Philosophy at Kyoto University from 1910 to 1928.

nodes.label: Om Prakash
nodes.summary: Om Prakash worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma and Bisheshwar Prasad, later teaching there, at Kirori Mal College, and as professor of economic history at Delhi School of Economics.

nodes.label: Dasharatha Sharma
nodes.summary: Dasharatha Sharma (1903–1976) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Delhi, he held leadership posts at Hindu College, Jai Narain Vyas University, the University of Delhi, and the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute.

nodes.label: Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala
nodes.summary: Indologist and historian Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow. He was curator at the Mathura Museum, director of the State Museum, Lucknow, and head of Indology at Banaras Hindu University (1951).

nodes.label: Bahadur Chand Chhabra
nodes.summary: Bahadur Chand Chhabra specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology, studying at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1935–1966) and became a professor at Panjab University around 1965.

nodes.label: Leah Zahler
nodes.summary: Leah Zahler worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia, where she was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and also studied under Harvey B. Aronson, Geshe Wangyal, and Joe Bransford Wilson.

nodes.label: University of North Carolina Wilmington
variants: University of North Carolina at Wilmington

nodes.label: Lati Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and Gyume Tantric College, served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse Monastery (~1976–1984), and held posts at Namgyal Monastery and the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Geshe Gendün Lodrö
nodes.summary: Geshe Gendün Lodrö specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, training at Drepung Gomang Dratsang under Ngawang Lekden. He served on the faculty at Drepung Gomang, taught at the University of Hamburg, and visited the University of Virginia in 1979.

nodes.label: Mikisaburo Mori
nodes.summary: Mikisaburo Mori was a philosophy and sinology scholar who studied at Kyoto University and earned a doctorate from Osaka University. He held posts at Kyoto University, the Academy of Oriental Culture, Osaka High School, Osaka University (professor 1966–1973), and Bukkyo University.

nodes.label: Fok Tou-hui
nodes.summary: Fok Tou-hui was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, and Otani University, and taught at CUHK from ~1972 to 1999.

nodes.id: I:New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies
nodes.label: New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies

nodes.id: I:The Chinese University of Hong Kong
nodes.label: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
variants: Institut für Chinastudien der Chinesischen Universität Hongkong
Department of History at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Centre for China Studies at the Chinese University of Hong Kong

nodes.label: Jérôme Ducor
nodes.summary: Jérôme Ducor is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Jacques May. Attested in 2006, he served at the University of Lausanne in the Department of Oriental Languages and Cultures.

nodes.label: Egaku Mayeda
nodes.summary: Egaku Mayeda (1926–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno, later holding professorships at Meijo University and Aichi Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Fumimaro Watanabe
nodes.summary: Fumimaro Watanabe was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto (Ph.D. 1976 under A. K. Warder). He held professorships at Kindai University and Aichi Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Genryu Kagoshima
nodes.summary: Genryu Kagoshima was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his studies at Komazawa University (~1930–1934) and later served as a professor there from around 1960 to 1983.

nodes.label: Chaesong Kim
nodes.summary: Chaesong Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Kim pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995) under Yasunori Ejima.

nodes.label: Shingon Buzan Comprehensive Research Institute
variants: 真言宗豊山派総合研究院宗学研究所

nodes.label: Eshun Otsuka
nodes.summary: Eshun Otsuka worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University and held a post there as a research student (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Piotr Balcerowicz
nodes.summary: Piotr Balcerowicz works in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Warsaw, Banaras Hindu University, Hamburg, and the Polish Academy of Sciences, he served as Professor of Indology at the University of Warsaw (2011) and Professor of International Relations at SWPS University (2008–2011).

nodes.label: Marek Mejor
nodes.summary: Marek Mejor is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He held a Junior Research Fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and was a professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

nodes.label: Nosei Fuji
nodes.summary: Nosei Fuji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University. He has held posts at Daegu University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, Bukkyo University, the Institute of Religious Culture, and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Rupert Gethin
nodes.summary: Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Manchester (~1977–1987) under Lance S. Cousins. His career includes posts at the University of Bristol (1987; 2009–2023) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: University of Bristol
variants: University of Bristol's Department of Theology and Religious Studies
University of Bristol's Centre for Buddhist Studies
Centre for Buddhist Studies of the University of Bristol
Centre for Buddhist Studies, University of Bristol

nodes.label: Peter Ebbatson
nodes.summary: Peter Ebbatson is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.

nodes.label: Hu Shih
nodes.summary: Hu Shih worked in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cornell, Columbia (PhD 1915–1917), and Teachers College under John Dewey and Kaiten Nukariya, he served as Peking University chancellor (1946–1948) and Academia Sinica president (1957–1962).

nodes.label: John Dewey
nodes.description: American philosopher, psychologist, and educational reformer (1859–1952)
nodes.summary: Philosopher John Dewey studied at the University of Vermont (~1875–1879) and Johns Hopkins (~1882–1884). He held posts at the universities of Michigan (~1884–1894), Minnesota (~1888–1889), Chicago (~1894–1904), and Columbia (~1904–1930).

nodes.label: Noriaki Hosoda
nodes.summary: Noriaki Hosoda is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at Hokkaido University (attested 1986 and 2003) and at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Haruhiko Masaki
nodes.summary: Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Gakushuin University (~1957–1961) and completed master's and doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1967), later serving as professor at Nagasaki University (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Shokin Furuta
nodes.summary: Shokin Furuta studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at Matsue High School, University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of Education, and Shimane University, studying under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He held professorships at Hokkaido University (~1952–1964) and Nihon University (~1964–1981).

nodes.label: Shōkō Kabutogi
nodes.summary: Shōkō Kabutogi was a Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from Rissho University in 1936. He later served as a professor at Rissho University, attested in 1972.

nodes.label: Taion Satomi
nodes.summary: Taion Satomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1930–1933). He later served as a professor at Minobusan University (attested 1972).

nodes.label: Nobumasa Hibi
nodes.summary: Nobumasa Hibi (b. 1932) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University (~1955–1959) and later served there as an assistant professor (~1968–1975).

nodes.label: Taishun Mibu
nodes.summary: Taishun Mibu worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Taisho University from approximately 1934 to 1937 and later served there as library director from around 1953 to 1983.

nodes.label: Senchu Murano
nodes.summary: Senchu Murano (1908–2000) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1934–1938). He served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1957 to 1979.

nodes.label: Michihiro Ikeda
nodes.summary: Michihiro Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar. His career includes posts as a lecturer at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), as well as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Natalie Maxwell
nodes.summary: Natalie Maxwell (born 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1975) under Stephan Beyer. She also studied under Geshe Wangyal, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, and Minoru Kiyota.

nodes.label: Stephan Beyer
nodes.summary: Stephan Beyer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1977).

nodes.label: David M. Knipe
nodes.summary: David M. Knipe is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as Professor from 1975, Chair of Religious Studies in 1989, and ultimately Professor Emeritus (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Robert J. Miller
nodes.summary: Robert J. Miller (1923–1994) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor on the faculty of the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1955–1989) and as a professor at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

nodes.label: Awadh Kishore Narain
nodes.summary: Awadh Kishore Narain worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Arthur Llewellyn Basham at SOAS, later serving as professor at BHU and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

nodes.label: Jun Fujii
nodes.summary: Jun Fujii is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo. He served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University from around 2010 to 2013.

nodes.label: John W. Schroeder
nodes.summary: John W. Schroeder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his bachelor's and PhD at the University of Oregon under Don Levi, and joined the faculty at St. Mary's College of Maryland in 1996.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Rau
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Rau was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Leipzig under Friedrich Weller (~1941–1945) and Marburg under Johannes Nobel (1946–1949). He was a professor at Frankfurt (1955) and Ordinarius at Marburg (1958–1987).

nodes.label: Sheng Yen
nodes.description: Taiwanese Buddhist monk, religious scholar, and writer (1931–2009)
nodes.summary: Sheng Yen (1931–2009) was a Buddhist studies figure who earned doctorates at Rissho University. He founded Dharma Drum Mountain and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and served as a lecturer at Shandao Temple and National Cheng Kung University.

nodes.label: Shuntaro Kondo
nodes.summary: Shuntaro Kondo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD from Ryukoku University by 2011. He was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University in 2012.

nodes.label: Yoshiyasu Yonezawa
nodes.summary: Yoshiyasu Yonezawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held appointments at Taisho University (attested 1998–2026) and at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Douglas Duckworth
nodes.summary: Douglas Duckworth is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia. He has held teaching posts at Rangjung Yeshe Institute and East Tennessee State University (~2011–2014).

nodes.label: Sallie B. King
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, Sallie B. King studied under Leon Hurvitz at the University of British Columbia (~1973-1975). She served as a professor and later Professor Emerita at James Madison University (~1992-2008).

Kathmandu University - Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute

Kathmandu University's Center for Buddhist Studies
Rangjung Yeshe Institute for Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: Thomas Doctor
nodes.summary: Thomas Doctor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery and the University of Lausanne under Tom Tillemans, and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Erik Pema Kunsang
nodes.summary: Erik Pema Kunsang is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who has served as director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications (from ca. 1981) and as a resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

nodes.label: Gendün Chöphel
nodes.summary: Gendün Chöphel was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Drisha, Kumbum, Labrang, and Drepung monasteries under Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso, and he was affiliated with the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.

nodes.label: George de Roerich
variants: ユーリー・ニコラエーヴィチ
ユーリイ・リョーリフ
nodes.summary: George de Roerich studied at Harvard, London, and Paris under scholars including Sylvain Lévi and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He directed the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute (~1930–1942) and headed a department at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1957–1960).

nodes.label: Anagarika Dharmapala
variants: アナガーリカ・ダルマパーラ
nodes.jawiki: アナガーリカ・ダルマパーラ
nodes.description: Sri Lankan Buddhist revivalist and writer (1864-1933)
nodes.summary: Anagarika Dharmapala (1864–1933) was an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated in Sri Lanka, including at S. Thomas' College and Royal College, Colombo, he founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

nodes.label: Albion Moonlight Butters
nodes.summary: Albion Moonlight Butters works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard Divinity School, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University (PhD), supervised by Robert A. F. Thurman among numerous other academic and traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Ngawang Samten
nodes.summary: Ngawang Samten works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and CIHTS, where he was Director (attested 1990–2019), and held visiting posts at Smith, Hampshire, Amherst, and the University of Tasmania.

nodes.label: Alexander von Rospatt
nodes.summary: Alexander von Rospatt is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of London and completed a PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg. He held posts at Leipzig and the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Shintaro Kitano
nodes.summary: Shintaro Kitano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He held posts as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and as a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Yönten Gyatso
nodes.summary: Yönten Gyatso (1932–2002) was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang (~1947–1959) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he served as a Tibetan Studies research advisor (~1970–1997).

nodes.label: Gelek Rimpoche
nodes.summary: Gelek Rimpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery, Young Lamas Home School, and Cornell University under teachers including Ling and Trijang Rinpoches. He served as director of Tibet House, New Delhi (1965), and founded Jewel Heart (1988).

nodes.label: Per Kvaerne
nodes.summary: Per Kvaerne (b. 1945) works in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed a Ph.D. at the University of Oslo by 1973 and later held posts there as a professor (attested 1978, 1991–1996) and served as Secretary General of the IATS.

nodes.label: Anne-Marie Blondeau
nodes.summary: Anne-Marie Blondeau is a tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. She held an academic post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

nodes.label: Kenneth K. Inada
nodes.summary: Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and served as chair at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research from 1996 to 1999.

nodes.label: Todd A. Gibson
nodes.summary: Todd A. Gibson is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington, where he completed his PhD under the supervision of György Kara (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Jong Cheol Lee
nodes.summary: Jong Cheol Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Seoul National University and earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima. He was a researcher at Mysore (1992) and associate professor at AKS (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Thomas A. Forsthoefel
nodes.summary: Thomas A. Forsthoefel, an Indology and religious studies scholar, earned degrees at Georgetown, Loyola University Chicago, and a PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He became associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Katherine Janiec Jones
nodes.summary: Katherine Janiec Jones is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Davidson College and earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul J. Griffiths, William K. Mahony, and Karl A. Plank.

nodes.label: W. Randolph Kloetzli
variants: W・ランドルフ・クレツリ
nodes.summary: W. Randolph Kloetzli is a scholar of religious, Indological, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago in 1964. He has taught courses at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

variants: ミルトン・クライントップ

nodes.label: Margaret Armers
variants: マーガレット・アーマース

nodes.label: Joseph Haroutunian
variants: ジョセフ・ハロウトゥニアン
nodes.summary: Joseph Haroutunian was a religious studies scholar educated at the American University of Beirut, Columbia University, and Union Theological Seminary. He held teaching posts at Wellesley College (1932–1940), McCormick Theological Seminary (1940–1962), and the University of Chicago (1962–1968).

nodes.label: Frank E. Reynolds
variants: フランク・レイノルド
nodes.description: American historian of religion and Buddhist studies scholar (1930-2019)
nodes.summary: Frank E. Reynolds was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from around 1967 to 2019.

nodes.label: Dartmouth College
variants: Department of Religion at Dartmouth College

nodes.label: Akira Unete
nodes.summary: Akira Unete works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He has been affiliated with Otani University, attested as an associate professor in 2010, and with the Otani Academic Society, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Eiichi Yamaguchi
variants: やまぐち えいいち
nodes.summary: Eiichi Yamaguchi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed graduate studies at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990), where he was also attested as a research assistant in 1991.

nodes.label: Gyosho Takahashi
nodes.summary: Gyosho Takahashi worked in Buddhist studies. He held a post as professor (教授) at Minobusan University, attested in 1992 and 1996.

nodes.label: Toshiya Unebe
nodes.summary: Toshiya Unebe is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. He served as an associate professor in the Department of Indian Studies at Nagoya University (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Chizuko Yoshimizu
nodes.summary: Chizuko Yoshimizu (b. 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at Gakushuin University, the University of Tokyo under Zuiho Yamaguchi, and the University of Vienna. She held faculty positions at the University of Tsukuba from 2003.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Nemoto
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Nemoto specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having earned an MA at Hiroshima University. At Hiroshima University, he served as associate professor (attested 2015) and later as professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kazuyoshi Kino
nodes.summary: Kazuyoshi Kino (1922–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (1942–1948). He served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989), vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993), and founded Shinnyokai.

nodes.label: Tanso Hirose
nodes.summary: Tanso Hirose (1782–1856) was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801) and under Hōdō, and he founded the Kangien academy in 1801.

nodes.label: Masao Abe
variants: Masao Abe (阿部 正雄, Abe Masao)
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist, professor in religious studies
nodes.summary: Masao Abe was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a doctorate from Kyoto University and also studied at Osaka City University, Union Theological Seminary, and Columbia University. He held professorships at Kyoto, Hanazono, and Nara universities.

nodes.label: Shripad Krishna Belvalkar
nodes.description: Indian historian and scholar of Sanskrit
nodes.summary: Shripad Krishna Belvalkar was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak (~1898–1904). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1904–1927), honorary secretary at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1917–1942), and General Secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference (~1919–1943).

nodes.label: Alberto Todeschini
nodes.summary: Alberto Todeschini is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has held a post as a guest at the Institute for Research in Humanities at Kyoto University and an affiliation at the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

nodes.label: Sojo Hirano
nodes.summary: Sojo Hirano was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and later held a post at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996).

nodes.id: I:Research Institute of Soto Zen Studies
nodes.label: Research Institute of Soto Zen Studies
Xuesong Zhang
nodes.summary: Xuesong Zhang works in Buddhist and religious studies. Zhang earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2008) and served as an associate professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Hsing Yun
nodes.summary: Hsing Yun was a Buddhist leader who founded Fo Guang Shan, serving as abbot (~1967–1985). He studied under teachers including Zhikai and Yinshun, and later held posts at Chinese Culture University (1980) and Tunghai University (1981).

nodes.label: Fo Guang Shan
variants: Fo Guang Shan Buddhist monastic order

nodes.label: Taixu
nodes.summary: Taixu was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Jichan, Yang Wenhui, and Jing'an, and at Jinling Scriptural Press. He founded several institutes, including Wuchang Buddhist Institute, and led the Minnan Buddhist Institute in 1927.

nodes.id: I:Tohoku Association for Indology and Study of Religion
nodes.label: Tohoku Association for Indology and Study of Religion
Takao Yamagata
nodes.summary: Takao Yamagata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1951–1960). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1970–2002) and served as president of the Society for Indian Philosophy and Religion (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Carlo Formichi
nodes.summary: Carlo Formichi (1871–1943) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Michele Kerbaker, Georg Bühler, Paul Deussen at Kiel University, and Hermann Oldenberg. He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).

nodes.label: Alfred Foucher
variants: アルフレッド・フーシェ
アルフレッド・A・フーシェ
nodes.jawiki: アルフレッド・フーシェ
nodes.summary: Working in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Alfred Foucher studied at École Normale Supérieure and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at EFEO, EPHE, and the University of Paris (1907; 1929–1936).

nodes.label: Marcelle Lalou
nodes.summary: Marcelle Lalou worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Paris and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, Paul Pelliot, and Jean Przyluski. She taught at EPHE (1938–1963) and served as chief editor of Journal Asiatique (1950–1966).

nodes.label: Jean Przyluski
nodes.description: French linguist and scholar of religion
nodes.summary: Jean Przyluski was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held professorships at INALCO (1923–1930), EPHE (1926–1944), and the Collège de France (1930–1944).

nodes.label: Velcheru Narayana Rao
nodes.description: Indian author, critic, and literary translator
nodes.summary: Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Sir C. R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University. He served as a lecturer and associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (from 1971).

nodes.label: Shingo Einoo
nodes.summary: Shingo Einoo is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He worked at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1986-1989) and the University of Tokyo (~1989-2013).

nodes.label: Takanobu Takahashi
nodes.summary: Takanobu Takahashi specialized in Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Tamilannal, and Utrecht University. He served as associate professor of Indian literature at Shitennoji University and associate professor at the University of Tokyo (1999–2016).

nodes.label: Tadashi Toda
nodes.summary: Tadashi Toda was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under teachers Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

nodes.label: Kevin A. Vose
nodes.summary: Kevin A. Vose works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Bates College and the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teacher Ngawang Jinpa.

nodes.label: Ngawang Jinpa
nodes.summary: Ngawang Jinpa is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery. He served as a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Drepung Loseling Monastery
variants: デプン寺ロサーリン学堂

nodes.label: National Taiwan University
variants: Department of Philosophy, National Taiwan University
台灣大學音樂學研究所

nodes.label: University of Warsaw
variants: Institute of Oriental Studies at the University of Warsaw

nodes.label: Maria Krzysztof Byrski
nodes.summary: Maria Krzysztof Byrski is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Warsaw from 1955 to 1960. He served as Head of the Indology Department at the University of Warsaw (~1990–1993) and held a post at Civitas University.

nodes.label: Helmut Eimer
nodes.summary: Helmut Eimer was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Humboldt University, Hamburg, and Bonn under Frank-Richard Hamm, subsequently holding a post at the University of Bonn from ~1974 to 2001.

nodes.label: Esho Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, Esho Yamaguchi studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1943). He held posts as professor at Osaka University (~1967–1982) and at Ritsumeikan University (~1982–1989).

nodes.label: Norio Harada
nodes.summary: Norio Harada is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology who studied at Ryukoku University. He held a professorship at Kyoto Women's University, attested in 1964.

nodes.label: Taichiro Kobayashi
nodes.summary: Taichiro Kobayashi worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying at Kyoto University (1919–1923) under Sentaro Sawamura, Kitaro Nishida, and others. He later held posts at the Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts and Kobe University (1950).

nodes.label: Sentaro Sawamura
nodes.summary: Sentaro Sawamura (1884–1930) specialized in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1908–1911) and later held an academic post there from around 1921 until 1930.

nodes.label: Naoki Kano
nodes.image: Mr. Naoki Kano, Advisor of the Education Association of Kyoto Prefecture.jpg
nodes.summary: Naoki Kano (1868–1947) was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1895). He took up a post at Kyoto University in 1906 and taught Taichiro Kobayashi.

nodes.label: Kosaku Hamada
nodes.summary: Kosaku Hamada (1881–1938) worked in history/archaeology, sinology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1901–1905), he held posts there (~1909–1913) and at Kyoto University (~1913–1938), teaching Taichiro Kobayashi and Seiichi Mizuno.

nodes.label: Konan Naito
nodes.summary: Konan Naito (1866–1934) worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Akita Normal School (~1880–1885) and held a post at Kyoto University (~1907–1926), where he taught Taichiro Kobayashi.

nodes.label: Kazuo Osumi
nodes.summary: Kazuo Osumi (born 1933) is a scholar of Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. He completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo, later serving as an assistant professor at Hokkaido University and professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977–2001).

nodes.label: Chandrabhāl Tripathi
nodes.summary: Chandrabhāl Tripathi was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen (~1957–1960) under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Göttingen (~1960–1970), the University of Cologne (~1970–1977), and the Free University of Berlin (~1977–1994).

nodes.label: Romila Thapar
nodes.summary: Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and completed her doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. She held professorships at the University of Delhi (1963–1970) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (1970–1991; Chair 1993).

nodes.label: Arthur Llewellyn Basham
nodes.summary: Indologist and historian Arthur Llewellyn Basham completed his BA and PhD at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He taught at SOAS (1948–1965), headed Asian Civilizations at the Australian National University (~1965–1978), and held visiting posts at Toronto and The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Masatoshi Konishi
nodes.summary: Masatoshi Konishi worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at International Christian University, the University of Calcutta, the University of Tokyo, and Rikkyo University, and held posts at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

nodes.label: Toshio Yamazaki
nodes.summary: Toshio Yamazaki was a specialist in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as professor and professor emeritus at the University of Tokyo (~1956–1977) and as professor at Chuo University (~1977–1987).

nodes.label: Keinin Hayashi
nodes.summary: Keinin Hayashi is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He has served as a full-time researcher at the Eastern Institute (attested 1998) and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026), and was formerly a lecturer at Waseda University.

nodes.label: Myles Dillon
nodes.description: Irish academic, historian, philologist and celticist (1900–1972)
nodes.summary: Myles Dillon (1900–1972) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at University College Dublin. He taught at Trinity College Dublin (1928–1930), University College Dublin (1930–1937), University of Wisconsin-Madison (1937), and directed the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (1960–1968).

nodes.label: James Kenneth Powell II
nodes.summary: James Kenneth Powell II is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Northwestern University, the University of Chicago under David Tracy, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

nodes.label: Ichiro Numata
nodes.summary: Ichiro Numata works in Buddhist studies and Indology. In 2026, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Tomomichi Nitta
nodes.summary: Tomomichi Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a lecturer post at Otani University (attested 2012) and a professorship at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Chang-geun Hwang
nodes.summary: Chang-geun Hwang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

nodes.label: Luo Changpei
nodes.summary: Luo Changpei (1899–1958) was a scholar in linguistics and Sinology. After studying at Peking University (~1916–1921), he held posts at Northwest University (~1924–1926), Xiamen University (~1926–1927), Sun Yat-sen University (~1928–1929), and Peking University (~1934–1950).

nodes.label: Hugh B. Urban
nodes.summary: Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1992–1998) studying under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart, and was appointed associate professor at Ohio State University (~1998).

nodes.label: Wendy Doniger
nodes.summary: Wendy Doniger (born 1940) specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned doctorates at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner, joining the University of Chicago faculty in 1978.

nodes.label: Bruce Lincoln
nodes.summary: Bruce Lincoln specializes in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Haverford College and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, he held posts at the University of Minnesota and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Clinton B. Seely
nodes.summary: Seely is an Indology scholar affiliated with the University of Chicago (attested 2007), where he is Professor Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jeffrey J. Kripal
nodes.summary: Jeffrey J. Kripal (born 1962) specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1987–1993). In ~2002, he held a chair and department headship at Rice University.

nodes.label: Tony K. Stewart
nodes.summary: Tony K. Stewart is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976). He held posts at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011).

nodes.label: Joachim Prandstetter
nodes.summary: Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna, completing his Magister by 1994, and studied under Gerhard Oberhammer.

nodes.label: Ferdinand Lessing
nodes.image: Professor Ferdinand Deiderich Lessing, Univ. of California, Berkeley. 1952.jpg
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Lessing worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin, he taught at Deutsch-Chinesische Hochschule, Peking University, China Medical University, Ethnological Museum of Berlin, Humboldt University, and UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Ronald M. Davidson
nodes.summary: Ronald M. Davidson works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at UC Berkeley (-1985) studying under Lancaster, Jaini, Strickmann, and Staal, among others, and held an academic post at Fairfield University (attested 2002–2005).

nodes.label: Gil Fronsdal
nodes.summary: Gil Fronsdal is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Stanford University, studying under teachers including Jan Nattier, Carl Bielefeldt, and Bernard Faure. He taught at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies and was affiliated with the Insight Meditation Center.

nodes.label: Bernard Faure
nodes.jawiki: ベルナール・フォール
nodes.summary: Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Sciences Po, Paris Diderot University, and under Paul Demiéville and Seizan Yanagida. His posts include Cornell University (~1983–1987), Stanford University (~1987–2006), and Columbia University (~2006–2021).

nodes.label: Vesna A. Wallace
nodes.summary: Vesna A. Wallace is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed her doctorate at UC Berkeley. She held the Numata Chair at the University of Oxford and served as professor and department chair at UC Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: A. K. Warder
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, he completed his doctorate at SOAS under John Brough around 1949–1954. He held posts at the University of Edinburgh (1955–1963) and the University of Toronto (1963–1990).

nodes.label: Peter Skilling
variants: ピーター・スキリング
nodes.summary: Peter Skilling is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub at the EPHE (2004). He founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and taught at EFEO, Chulalongkorn University, and Pune University.

nodes.label: Kunio Harikai
nodes.summary: Kunio Harikai is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed his BA and PhD degrees at Kyushu University, studying under Seiren Matsunami and Shōren Ihara. He served as an associate professor at Saga Medical School from circa 1978 to 1993.

nodes.label: Futoshi Omae
nodes.summary: Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Yasuke Ikari
nodes.summary: Yasuke Ikari (born 1940) is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Chicago (PhD). He spent much of his academic career at Kyoto University, rising to professor in 1989 and professor emeritus in 2004.

nodes.label: Keiki Nakayama
nodes.summary: Keiki Nakayama specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (attested 2019–2020), held a JSPS DC2 fellowship (2020), and was attested as a visiting scholar at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

nodes.label: Hisashi Matsumura
nodes.summary: Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. His career includes posts at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and as an associate professor at Kobe Shinwa University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Yoshinobu Kimoto
nodes.summary: Yoshinobu Kimoto is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities. He held academic posts at Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College (1993–2000), Koshien Junior College (2000–2012), and Ryukoku University (2013–2021).

nodes.id: I:Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College
nodes.label: Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College
variants: 山形県立米沢女子短期大学

nodes.label: Kazuo Oyamada
nodes.summary: Kazuo Oyamada (born 1952) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Tamagawa University and held an academic post at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Koyo Shimizu
nodes.summary: Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. In 1995, Shimizu was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: National Archives of Nepal
variants: ネパール国立古文書館

nodes.label: Ernst Waldschmidt
nodes.summary: Ernst Waldschmidt was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. After studying under Heinrich Lüders, August Hermann Francke, Albert Grünwedel, and Emil Sieg, he held the chair of Indology at the University of Göttingen (1936–1965).

nodes.label: Kyushu Otani Junior College
variants: 九州大谷短期大学仏教科

nodes.label: Gerald James Larson
nodes.summary: Gerald James Larson worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University, later holding posts at UC Santa Barbara from 1972 and Indiana University Bloomington from 1995.

nodes.label: Sayori Tsubota
nodes.summary: Sayori Tsubota specializes in Indology. She was a PhD student at Osaka University (attested 2020) and became a JSPS postdoctoral fellow at Tohoku University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Toshiki Osada
nodes.summary: Toshiki Osada is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Hokkaido University. He held posts as a professor and project leader at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature and at Kyoto University of the Arts.

nodes.label: Tomoyasu Oshima
nodes.summary: Tomoyasu Oshima is an Indologist who studied under Toshifumi Goto and held a part-time lecturer post at Kyoto University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Naoko Nishimura
nodes.summary: Naoko Nishimura is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD at Tohoku University by 2002 under Toshifumi Goto. She worked at Tohoku University as a researcher (attested 2012) and later as a professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak
nodes.image: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak introducing himself for Voice intro project.jpg
nodes.summary: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He founded and directed the Central Institute of Indian Languages (~1969–1989) and served as chairman of the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

nodes.label: Central Institute of Indian Languages
variants: Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysore

nodes.label: Sumitra Mangesh Katre
nodes.summary: Sumitra Mangesh Katre (1906–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of London (~1928–1931). He held the Chair of Indo-European Philology at Deccan College (1942–1971) and taught at UT Austin (~1971–1976).

nodes.label: Satoshi Naiki
nodes.summary: Satoshi Naiki works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a PhD from Kyoto University, where he served as an assistant professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (attested 2016–2020).

variants: ニューヨーク州立大学バッファロー校

State University of New York at Buffalo

nodes.label: Sonam Gyatso
nodes.summary: Sonam Gyatso is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Shinjo Kawasaki and Chogye Shabdrung. He served as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko (~1961–1968) and held a professorship at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Chijo Akamatsu
nodes.summary: Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. Akamatsu served as a professor at Ryukoku, Koyasan, Hanazono, Keijo Imperial (1927–1941), and Yamaguchi universities, and lectured at Kyoto and Kyushu.

nodes.label: Kazuhiko Yoshida
nodes.summary: Kazuhiko Yoshida (born 1955) works in linguistics, history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Sophia, Kyoto, Cornell (under Jay Jasanoff), and Osaka universities, he held professorships at Nagoya City Women's College, Kyoto University (c. 1999–2020), and Nagoya City University.

nodes.label: Tokuno Oda
nodes.summary: Tokuno Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu. He held teaching posts at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Prefectural Fujishima High School, and Toyo University.

nodes.label: Mokurai Shimaji
nodes.summary: Mokurai Shimaji was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū. He held leadership posts at Nishi Hongan-ji and Hongan-ji, served as the 25th chief priest at Gankyo-ji (1892–1905), and founded Chiyoda Jogakuen.

nodes.label: Enryo Inoue
nodes.summary: Enryo Inoue was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded the Philosophical Society of Japan and Toyo University, where he taught from 1887 to 1905.

nodes.label: Teun Goudriaan
nodes.summary: Teun Goudriaan is an Indologist who held posts at Utrecht University, where his affiliation is attested in 1989 and as professor emeritus in 2000.

nodes.label: Sanjukta Gupta
variants: サンジェクタ・グプタ
nodes.summary: Sanjukta Gupta is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. She held posts at Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, Jadavpur, Utrecht University, and the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Kojun Fukui
nodes.summary: Kojun Fukui (1898–1991) was a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sokichi Tsuda at Waseda University. He was a professor at Waseda University (1941–1969) and president of Taisho University (1928–1968; 1972–1975).

nodes.label: Joen Imai
nodes.summary: Joen Imai is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a professor at Shuchiin University (attested in 2010 and 2026).

nodes.label: Takudo Ishikawa
nodes.summary: Takudo Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a research post at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005) and teaching posts at Taisho University (attested 2015 and 2026).

nodes.label: Kengo Harimoto
nodes.summary: Kengo Harimoto specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyushu University and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass in 1999. He later held posts at Mahidol University and the University of Naples "L'Orientale."

nodes.label: Kenji Takahashi
nodes.summary: Kenji Takahashi specializes in Indology. He studied at Leiden University (2015–2016) and under Diwakar Acharya, Yuko Yokochi, and Peter C. Bisschop, later holding a JSPS-sponsored fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II from 2019 to 2021.

nodes.label: Peter C. Bisschop
nodes.summary: Peter C. Bisschop studied Indology and religious studies at the University of Groningen (PhD -2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He was a Fellow at Wolfson College, Oxford, and taught Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010).

nodes.label: Andrey Klebanov
nodes.summary: Andrey Klebanov is an Indologist who earned his MA (2010) and PhD (2016) at the University of Hamburg, supervised by Harunaga Isaacson. He later served as a professor at Kyoto University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: James L. Fitzgerald
nodes.summary: James L. Fitzgerald is an Indologist who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He held posts as professor at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004-2006) and Das Professor of Sanskrit at Brown University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Ryosaburo Sakaki
nodes.summary: Ryosaburo Sakaki studied at the Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo, working in indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He lectured at Ryukoku University (1897) and held professorships at the Third Higher School (1899) and Kyoto University (1908).

nodes.label: Gikyo Ito
nodes.summary: Gikyo Ito specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at Kyoto University, studying under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki. He taught at Kyoto University, serving as professor (1968–1972), and later at Kyoto Sangyo University.

nodes.label: Koji Kamioka
nodes.summary: Koji Kamioka (1938–2024) specialized in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Yutaka Ochihara at Kyoto University, became a lecturer at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969), and worked at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

nodes.label: Norihiko Uchida
nodes.summary: Norihiko Uchida is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held a post at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, attested in 1962.

nodes.label: Takao Hayashi
nodes.summary: Takao Hayashi is an Indology and history scholar. Educated at Tohoku, Kyoto, and Brown universities under David Pingree, Otto Neugebauer, Abraham Sachs, and Gerald J. Toomer, he held posts at Harish-Chandra Research Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and Doshisha University (1986–1989; 1995–2015).

nodes.label: Mizuho Okita
nodes.summary: Mizuho Okita is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Tokai and Gakushuin universities under Katsuhiko Kamimura and Atsuhiko Yoshida. She served as a part-time lecturer at Meisei University around 2008.

nodes.label: Atsuhiko Yoshida
nodes.summary: Atsuhiko Yoshida studied at Seikei, Tokyo, Athénée Français, Strasbourg, and EPHE under Georges Dumézil. Specializing in religious studies and history/archaeology, he worked at CNRS, lectured at Geneva and UCLA, and held professorships at Seikei (1970) and Gakushuin (2006).

nodes.label: Gakushuin University
variants: 学習院大学文学部哲学科

nodes.label: Wako University
variants: 和光大学人文学部芸術学科

nodes.label: Masanori Shono
nodes.summary: Masanori Shono is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held an assistant professor post at Osaka University (attested 2012) and served as a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Michael Radich
variants: マイケル・ラディッチ
nodes.summary: Michael Radich, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and computational methods, completed his PhD at Harvard under Robert M. Gimello. He held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and became Professor of Buddhist Studies at Heidelberg University in 2018.

nodes.label: Yumiko Ishihama
nodes.summary: Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University circa 1980–1989 and held a post there circa 1998.

nodes.label: Shinkai Sugawara
nodes.summary: Shinkai Sugawara was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Waseda University and received a doctorate from Taisho University. He served on the faculty at Waseda University (~1966-1996), where he became professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Jikai Fujiyoshi
nodes.summary: Jikai Fujiyoshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Kyoto University (attested 1967) and served as a professor at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Ryodo Kudo
nodes.summary: Ryodo Kudo is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has held academic teaching appointments at Taisho University (attested 2015–2026) and Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Anand Venkatkrishnan

nodes.label: Michael Willis

nodes.summary: Niharranjan Ray (1903–1981) was an Indologist and historian who completed a doctorate at Leiden University (~1935–1936). He was Bageswari Professor of Fine Arts at the University of Calcutta (1946–1965) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1965–1970).

nodes.label: Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov
nodes.summary: Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1935–1940). He held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies, the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, and Pravda.

nodes.label: Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta. He taught philosophy at City College, Kolkata, and served as a visiting professor at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Haridas Sinharay
nodes.summary: Haridas Sinharay is an Indology scholar who held an academic post at Maulana Azad College, attested in both 1970 and 1990.

nodes.label: Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) was a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1967, attested 1990 and 1999).

nodes.label: Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held academic positions at Vidyasagar College in the 1970s and 1990, and served as a lecturer in the Sanskrit Department at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Vidyasagar College
variants: Department of Sanskrit, Vidyasagar College, Calcutta

nodes.label: Suniti Kumar Chatterji
nodes.summary: Suniti Kumar Chatterji (1890–1977) was an Indian linguist and Indologist. He studied at Scottish Church College, Presidency University, University of Calcutta, University of London, and University of Paris under Jules Bloch, and served at the University of Calcutta and the Government of India.

nodes.label: François Gros
nodes.summary: François Gros specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Lyon (~1951–1957) and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1977–2002).

nodes.label: Csaba Kiss
nodes.summary: Csaba Kiss is an indology and religious studies scholar. He earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (2003–2009) under Alexis Sanderson and has held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2024) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Édouard Chavannes
variants: エドゥアール・シャヴァンヌ
nodes.jawiki: エドゥアール・シャヴァンヌ
nodes.summary: Édouard Chavannes (1865–1918) was a sinologist and scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied at ENS and under Marie-Jean-Léon d'Hervey de Saint Denys. He served as a professor at the Collège de France from 1893 to 1918.

nodes.label: Bavarian State Library
variants: kgl. bayer. Hof- und Staatsbibliothek in München

nodes.label: Isaline Blew Horner
nodes.summary: Isaline Blew Horner (1896–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied under Caroline Rhys Davids and at Newnham College and Cambridge. She served at Newnham, Cambridge, and held long-term secretary roles at the Pali Text Society.

nodes.label: Thanon Chitkament
nodes.summary: Thanon Chitkament is a scholar in history and archaeology who studied under guide Vishwas D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Eugen Hultzsch
nodes.summary: Eugen Hultzsch was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig and under Georg Bühler in Vienna. He served as epigraphist for the Government of Madras and India (circa 1886–1903) and held a chair at Halle-Wittenberg from 1903 to 1925.

nodes.label: Hosakote Krishna Sastri
nodes.summary: Hosakote Krishna Sastri was an epigraphist and scholar of Indology and archaeology. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (~1891–1925) and served as Government Epigraphist for India (~1920–1925).

nodes.label: Georg von Simson
nodes.summary: Georg von Simson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Mainz and the University of Göttingen, worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and served as professor at the University of Oslo from 1977 to 2003.

nodes.label: Thích Minh Châu
nodes.summary: Thích Minh Châu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University (~1957–1961). He lectured at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1961) and served as Vice Chancellor of Van Hanh University (~1964–1975).

nodes.label: Ashok Narhar Aklujkar
nodes.summary: Ashok Narhar Aklujkar studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and completed his Ph.D. at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. Specializing in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, he taught in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

nodes.label: Tatiana Oranskaia
nodes.summary: Tatiana Oranskaia works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1967–1972) and the Central Institute of Hindi (1988), and held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996, 1998–2016).

nodes.label: Arthur William Ryder
nodes.summary: Indologist Arthur William Ryder studied at Harvard, Berlin, and Leipzig, learning under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He taught Sanskrit at Harvard (1902–1906) and subsequently served as professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (~1906–1938).

nodes.label: Vempati Kutumba Sastry
nodes.summary: Vempati Kutumba Sastry is an Indologist. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the Central Sanskrit University (2003–2008) and as president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~2006–2018).

nodes.label: Mamata Dash
nodes.summary: Mamata Dash is an Indologist who completed her education at Ravenshaw Girls' School and Utkal University.

nodes.label: Krishna Venkateswara Sarma
nodes.summary: Krishna Venkateswara Sarma (1919–2005) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kerala under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri, holding posts at Panjab University, Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, and the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation.

nodes.label: Mark Singleton
nodes.summary: Mark Singleton (born 1969) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge, studying under Elizabeth De Michelis. He served as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Eivind Kahrs
nodes.summary: Eivind Kahrs works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He was attested at Queens' College, Cambridge in 2010, and as a council member of the Pali Text Society in 2026.

nodes.label: Elizabeth De Michelis
nodes.summary: Elizabeth De Michelis specializes in religious studies and Indology. She completed a master's at SOAS and a PhD at the University of Cambridge (~1997–2001), where she became a director in 2000, later joining the University of Oxford's theology faculty.

nodes.label: Suzanne Newcombe
nodes.summary: Suzanne Newcombe is a religious studies and Indology scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at the Open University, Inform, and King's College London.

nodes.label: Gangs zhun
nodes.summary: Gangs zhun is a Tibetologist who studied at Qinghai Nationalities Normal College (until 1989) and Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001), where he earned a master's degree under Alak Dorzhi Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Qinghai Nationalities Normal College
variants: Teachers Training College for Nationalities in Chab-cha

nodes.label: Mysore Hiriyanna
nodes.description: Indian philosopher, Sanskrit scholar and authority on Indian aesthetics
nodes.summary: Mysore Hiriyanna (1871–1950) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Madras Christian College (~1890–1895). He served as librarian at Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1891) and as professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College and the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).

nodes.label: Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi
nodes.summary: Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi was an Indology scholar. He served as a Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Baroda and held a post at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, attested in 1939.

nodes.label: K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar
variants: R. B. Prof. K. V. Rangaswami Iyengar

nodes.label: Sukhlal Sanghvi
nodes.description: Jain Scholar and Philosopher from India
nodes.summary: Sukhlal Sanghvi (1880–1978) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Balakrishna Mishra. He taught Indian philosophy at Gujarat Vidyapith (1922) and held the Chair of Jain Philosophy at Banaras Hindu University (1934–1944).

nodes.label: Benoytosh Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (1897–1964) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Calcutta (~1917–1919) and a doctorate from the University of Dhaka (~1922–1925), later serving as Director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (1927).

nodes.label: Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt
nodes.summary: Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indology scholar. He held posts at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda as a Professor (attested 1933–1939) and later as Director (attested 1953–1957).

nodes.label: Lothar von Falkenhausen
variants: ロータール・アレクサンダー・フォン・ファルケンハウゼン
nodes.jawiki: ロータール・フォン・ファルケンハウゼン
nodes.description: German-American Archaeologist, Sinologist, and Art Historian
nodes.summary: Specializing in archaeology and Sinology, Lothar von Falkenhausen studied at Bonn, Peking University, Kyoto, and Harvard (MA ~1979–1982, PhD ~1982–1988). He taught at UC Riverside (~1991–1993) and became a professor at UCLA in 1993.

nodes.label: Soma Thera
nodes.summary: Soma Thera was an active figure in Buddhist studies who studied at St. Benedict's College in Colombo and under Jetavana Sayadaw in 1936.

nodes.label: Dieter George
nodes.summary: Dieter George was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who served at the Prussian State Library from around 1972 to 1985.

nodes.label: Michael Schmidt
nodes.summary: Michael Schmidt worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a dictionary editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1981) and held posts at the KOHD (1992) and the University of Göttingen (attested 1995).
