nodes.label: Vishvanath Narayan Mandlik
nodes.description: Indian lawyer, writer and social activist
nodes.summary: Vishvanath Narayan Mandlik (1833–1899) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Elphinstone College under Ramachandra Balkrishna, he later served as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and as an examiner in Marathi and Law at Mumbai University.

nodes.label: Steven Heine
nodes.summary: Steven Heine is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Pennsylvania, Temple University, and under Shudo Ishii. He held posts at Villanova, La Salle, Pennsylvania State University, and Florida International University.

nodes.label: Charles S. Prebish
nodes.summary: Charles S. Prebish (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Case Western Reserve University and under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Pennsylvania State University (~1972–2007) and held posts at the University of Toronto and University of Calgary.

nodes.label: Raoul Birnbaum
nodes.summary: Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He served as a professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003 and 2017).

nodes.label: Christopher S. Queen
nodes.summary: Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held academic posts at Harvard University as a lecturer on Buddhism and world religions (~1989) and as Dean of Students for Continuing Education (~1989–2008).

nodes.label: Manfred Mayrhofer
variants: マンフレート・マイルホーファー
nodes.jawiki: マンフレート・マイルホーファー
nodes.summary: Manfred Mayrhofer was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz and held professorships at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

nodes.label: Ernst Johann Eitel
nodes.summary: Working in Sinology and Buddhist studies, Ernst Johann Eitel studied at the University of Tübingen (MA ~1856–1860, PhD by 1871). He served at the London Missionary Society (~1865–1879) and as professor/lecturer at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1908).

nodes.label: Raffaele Torella
nodes.summary: Raffaele Torella (born 1950) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Raniero Gnoli. He served as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome from approximately 1976 to 2020.

nodes.label: August Fischer
nodes.summary: August Fischer specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1885–1889) and served as a professor at the University of Leipzig from around 1900 to 1930.

nodes.label: Anant Sadashiv Altekar
nodes.description: historian, archaeologist, and numismatist from Maharashtra, India
nodes.summary: Anant Sadashiv Altekar (1898–1959) was an Indologist and historian. He was a professor and department head at Banaras Hindu University (c. 1930–1949), professor at Patna University (c. 1949–1957), and director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1955).

nodes.label: Kenneth de Burgh Codrington
nodes.image: Kenneth de Burgh Codrington, negative, 1927 (Lafayette; NPG x41720).png
nodes.summary: Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Kenneth de Burgh Codrington studied at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, and Wadham College, Oxford. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum (~1931-1948), University of London (~1948-1965), and University of Cincinnati.

nodes.label: Cyril Henry Philips
nodes.summary: Cyril Henry Philips was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Liverpool (1931–1934) and SOAS (~1935–1940), later serving as SOAS Director (1957) succeeding Ralph Lilley Turner, and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).

nodes.label: Ying-shih Yü
nodes.summary: Ying-shih Yü was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy who earned his PhD at Harvard. He held professorships and posts at Harvard, Yale, Princeton, the University of Michigan, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Arunoday Natvarlal Jani
nodes.summary: Indologist Arunoday Natvarlal Jani earned his Ph.D. under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt at the University of Mumbai (~1946–1953) and studied under M. V. Upadhyay. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (1967–1981).

nodes.label: Parashuram Krishna Gode
nodes.image: Dr. Parshuram Krishna Gode, M.A., D. Litt.jpg

nodes.label: K. R. Norman
nodes.summary: K. R. Norman (1925–2020) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist who studied at Downing College, Cambridge. He served at the University of Cambridge from 1955 and was President of the Pali Text Society (1981–1994).

nodes.label: Frank Raymond Allchin
nodes.summary: Frank Raymond Allchin was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at SOAS under Kenneth de Burgh Codrington. He taught at SOAS (1954–1959) and the University of Cambridge (1959–1989), and co-founded the Ancient India and Iran Trust.

nodes.label: David Roy Shackleton Bailey
nodes.summary: David Roy Shackleton Bailey (1917–2005) was a classicist and Tibetologist educated at Cambridge. He held fellowships and lectureships at Cambridge, taught at the University of Michigan, and served as Pope Professor of Latin at Harvard University (1975–1988).

nodes.label: Paul Mus
nodes.summary: Paul Mus (1902–1969) studied Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. His career included posts at EFEO, EPHE, École nationale de la France d'outre-mer, Yale, and the Collège de France.

nodes.label: Kun Chang
nodes.summary: Kun Chang was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua University and Yale University under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Nornang. He held academic posts at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington, and UC Berkeley (1963–1987).

nodes.label: Samuel Beal
nodes.summary: Samuel Beal was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Trinity College, Cambridge, and a DCL from Durham University. He held posts at Bramham College, the India Office Library, and the University of London.

nodes.label: Trinity College, Cambridge
variants: ケンブリッジ大学トリニティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Cornelis Petrus Tiele
nodes.jawiki: コルネーリス・ティーレ
nodes.summary: Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) studied at the Remonstrant Seminary and University of Amsterdam. A scholar of religious studies and history, he was a professor at the Remonstrant Seminary (1873) and held the history of religions chair at Leiden (1877–1901).

nodes.label: Teruji Ishizu
nodes.summary: Teruji Ishizu (1903–1972) studied at the University of Tokyo. Active in religious studies and philosophy, he held posts at Nihon University and the University of Tokyo, served as president of Tohoku University and Miyagi University of Education, and taught at Keio and Komazawa.

nodes.label: Ichiro Hori
nodes.summary: Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies and archaeology scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Kunio Yanagita, he taught at Nishogakusha, Kokugakuin, Tohoku (~1952–1965), Seijo, and the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).

nodes.label: Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha
nodes.description: Indian archeologist and historian from Bihar
nodes.summary: Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Patna University and SOAS University of London under Lionel David Barnett, later serving as head of department at Patna University (1958) and joint director of K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1969–1980).

nodes.label: Patna University
variants: Department of History and Archaeology at Patna University

nodes.label: Thomas Oberlies
nodes.summary: Thomas Oberlies is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme. He held a post at the University of Freiburg (attested 2001) and serves as Arbeitsstellenleiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Peter Schreiner
nodes.summary: Peter Schreiner is an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Paul Hacker at Münster (~1968–1972) and habilitated at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen (1974–1982), SOAS (1988), and the University of Zurich (professor 1990; emeritus ~2010).

nodes.label: August Hjalmar Edgren
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist August Hjalmar Edgren studied at Uppsala, Cornell, and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale (1874–1880), Lund (1880–1884), Nebraska-Lincoln (~1885–1891), and served as rector of the University of Gothenburg (1891–1893).

nodes.label: Per Kjeld Sørensen
nodes.summary: Per Kjeld Sørensen (b. 1950) studied Tibetology at the University of Copenhagen (1971–1982, ~1980–1990) under Erik Haarh. He lectured at Copenhagen (1982–1989), held a fellowship at the University of Bonn (1991–1992), and was a professor at the University of Leipzig (1994–2017).

nodes.label: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche (b. 1961) works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Geshe degree at Menri Monastery and served as director of the Dialectic School of Menri before founding Ligmincha International in 1992.

nodes.label: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima
variants: H. H. Menri Khen Rinpoche Lungdog Denpa Nyima
nodes.summary: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima (1927–2017) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery and studied under Horwa Drungrampa Tendzin Lodro Gyatso. He founded Menri Monastery, serving as its abbot from 1969.

nodes.label: Anne C. Klein
nodes.summary: Anne C. Klein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned degrees from Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison (MA), and Virginia (PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins), while studying with multiple traditional teachers. She held posts at Harvard Divinity School (~1981–1982) and Rice University (~1987).

nodes.label: Namkhai Norbu
nodes.summary: Namkhai Norbu (1938–2018) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Derge Gonchen, Khams-bre Shedra, and Kuse Serjong Shedra under various traditional teachers. He held posts at Southwest Minzu University, IsMEO, and the University of Naples (1962–1992), and founded the Shang Shung Institute in 1990.

nodes.label: Geshe Tsondru Kongpel
nodes.summary: Geshe Tsondru Kongpel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned Geshe degrees while studying at both Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

nodes.label: Rice University
variants: Center for Cultural Studies, Rice University
Center for Cultural Studies at Rice University

nodes.label: Gergely Hidas
nodes.summary: Gergely Hidas is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, later serving as a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University and as a researcher at the British Museum.

nodes.label: Hermann Hirt
nodes.summary: Hermann Hirt was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Leipzig. He served as a Privatdozent at Leipzig (1891–1912) and as a professor at the University of Giessen (1912–1936).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Streitberg
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Streitberg was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Münster, Leipzig (under Karl Brugmann and Ernst Windisch), and Berlin. He held posts at Fribourg (~1889–1899), Münster (1899), Munich (1909–1920), and Leipzig (1898, 1920–1925).

nodes.label: Donald R. Davis Jr.
nodes.summary: Donald R. Davis Jr. is an Indologist who studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Patrick Olivelle, and Ludo Rocher. He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2012) and the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Richard W. Lariviere
nodes.summary: Richard W. Lariviere is an Indologist who studied under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania. He served as dean and professor emeritus at UT Austin, provost at the University of Kansas, president of the University of Oregon, and president of the Field Museum.

nodes.label: Patrick Olivelle
nodes.description: Sri Lankan Indologist and Sanskrit scholar (born 1942)
nodes.summary: Patrick Olivelle is an Indologist who studied at the University of Oxford and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. He held posts at Indiana University Bloomington (1974–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin (1991).

nodes.label: Timothy Lubin
nodes.summary: Timothy Lubin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at Columbia University in 1994. He holds an academic post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Louis Dumont
nodes.summary: Louis Dumont was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Marcel Mauss at the Institut d'ethnologie. He held posts at the Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires, Oxford University (1951–1955), and the EHESS/EPHE from 1955.

nodes.label: Anne Casile
nodes.summary: Anne Casile is a scholar in indology and archaeology who studied under Claudine Bautze-Picron. She served as an AHRC research assistant at the British Museum (circa 2008–2011) and held a post at the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development (circa 2011).

nodes.label: Heidi Rika Maria Pauwels
nodes.summary: Heidi Rika Maria Pauwels works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at KU Leuven, Vrindaban Research Institute, University of Cologne, and University of Washington under Alan Entwistle. She taught at SOAS (1994–1996) before becoming Professor at the University of Washington (1996, 2002).

nodes.label: Karl Benedikt Hase
nodes.summary: Karl Benedikt Hase worked in linguistics and related fields. Educated at the universities of Jena and Helmstedt, he held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and the Faculty of Arts of Paris.

nodes.label: Helga Uebach
nodes.summary: Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Munich (~1960–1967) and served as a research associate at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities beginning in 1964.

nodes.label: Jampa Losang Panglung
nodes.summary: Jampa Losang Panglung was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He obtained his Geshe Lharamapa at Sera Monastery and his Magister and doctorate at the University of Munich, later working at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Erich Haenisch
variants: エーリヒ・ヘーニシュ
nodes.jawiki: エーリヒ・ヘーニシュ
nodes.summary: Erich Haenisch specialized in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin under Wilhelm Grube. He held professorships at Göttingen (1925), Leipzig (ca. 1925–1932), Berlin (1932), and Munich (1927–1951).

nodes.label: Chhime Rigdzing
nodes.summary: Chhime Rigdzing (1922–2002) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and held a post at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Tatsushi Tamai
nodes.summary: Tatsushi Tamai specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He served as a Visiting Researcher at the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology at Soka University (attested 2010–2016).

nodes.label: Saraju Rath
nodes.summary: Saraju Rath is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who held positions at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

nodes.label: Max Sparreboom
nodes.image: 2015 Erasmus Prize - 25 November 2015 - Stichting Praemium Erasmianum (4).JPG

nodes.label: Christopher Minkowski
nodes.summary: Christopher Minkowski is an Indologist educated at Harvard and the University of Delhi. He held positions at Wolfson College, Brown, University of Iowa (~1989–1999), and Cornell (1989–2006) before serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and Balliol College (2005–2023).

nodes.label: Gérard Colas
nodes.summary: Gérard Colas specializes in Indology and religious studies. He held posts as Directeur de recherche at the CNRS (attested 2004) and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Jagiellonian University
variants: Institute of English Studies Jagiellonian University

nodes.label: Heike Oberlin
nodes.summary: Heike Oberlin is an Indologist who studied at Kerala Kalamandalam and the universities of Tübingen and Würzburg. She held positions at Tübingen (2005–2008), Kerala Kalamandalam (2018), and Sapienza University of Rome (2025).

nodes.label: Saraswathi Mahal Library
variants: Thanjavur Maharaja Serfoji's Saraswathi Mahal Library

nodes.label: Kim Plofker
nodes.summary: Kim Plofker works in indology and history/archaeology. She earned her bachelor's from Haverford College and her PhD from Brown University under David Pingree. She held positions at MIT, Brown, Utrecht, and Union College, becoming Associate Professor in 2019.

nodes.label: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma
nodes.description: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma, Dept. of Sanskrit, Aligarh Muslim U., Aligarh-202002
nodes.summary: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history scholar who studied at Visva-Bharati, Andhra University, and the University of Marburg (PhD ~1963–1966). He served as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University from ~1976 to 1997.

nodes.label: Jack Goody
nodes.summary: Jack Goody, an archaeologist and historian, was educated at St Albans School and St John's College (~1938–1946). He held a post as a retired professor at the University of Cambridge from circa 1984 to 2015.

nodes.label: S. N. Savadi
nodes.summary: S. N. Savadi was an Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.

nodes.label: Sao Htun Hmat Win
nodes.summary: Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University and under Bhaddanta Nārada. He held posts at the University of Rangoon, the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

nodes.id: I:International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies
nodes.label: International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies
variants: International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies at Kaba-Aye

nodes.id: I:Ministry of Religious Affairs and Culture
nodes.label: Ministry of Religious Affairs and Culture
variants: Ministry of Religious Affairs, Union of Myanmar

nodes.label: Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar
nodes.summary: Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1915–1945) and as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1956–1970).

nodes.label: Subhash Kak
nodes.image: Subhash Kak at Single Photon Workshop, Geneva, July 2015.jpg
nodes.summary: Subhash Kak is an Indologist and engineer who studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under P. V. Indiresan. He held major professorships at Louisiana State University (1979) and Oklahoma State University (2007).

nodes.label: Albert Debrunner
nodes.summary: Albert Debrunner (1884–1958) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Jacob Wackernagel, Ferdinand Sommer, Friedrich Leo, and Alfred Körte. His academic posts included Zurich, Greifswald, Jena, the University of Basel, and the University of Bern.

nodes.label: Robert B. Ekvall
nodes.description: missionary, explorer, ethnographer, curator of Asian ethnology (1898-1983)
nodes.summary: Robert B. Ekvall (1898–1983) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. His appointments included research associate at the University of Chicago, research fellow and chairman at the University of Washington (1958), and honorary curator at the Burke Museum (attested 1983).

nodes.label: Csaba Dezső
nodes.summary: Csaba Dezső (born 1973) is an indologist who earned master's degrees at Eötvös Loránd University (~1992–1997) and a PhD at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1998–2004). He served as an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University around 2003.

nodes.label: R. Sathyanarayana
nodes.summary: R. Sathyanarayana (1927–2020) was an Indology scholar who earned a master's in chemistry at the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984) and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.

nodes.label: Surendranath Dasgupta
variants: スレンドラナート・ダスグプタ
nodes.description: Bengali scholar of Sanskrit and philosophy (1887-1952)
nodes.summary: Surendranath Dasgupta (1887–1952) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Sanskrit College, Calcutta, and Cambridge under J. M. E. McTaggart and James Ward. He held posts at Chittagong, Cambridge, Presidency University, Sanskrit College, and Calcutta.

nodes.label: Mircea Eliade
variants: ミルチャ・エリアーデ
nodes.jawiki: ミルチャ・エリアーデ
nodes.description: Romanian-American historian, writer, philosopher and professor at the University of Chicago (1907–1986)
nodes.summary: Mircea Eliade (1907–1986) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Bucharest and Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, he taught at Bucharest, EPHE, and the Sorbonne, and became professor at the University of Chicago in 1957.

nodes.label: Tübingen University Library
variants: テュービンゲン大学図書館

nodes.label: Christopher D. Wallis
nodes.summary: Christopher D. Wallis specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Rochester (BA), Oxford (MPhil under Alexis Sanderson), and UC Berkeley (PhD, 2014, under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt), later serving as guest lecturer at Naropa University.

nodes.label: Robert P. Goldman
nodes.summary: Robert P. Goldman is an Indologist who studied at Columbia and Penn under Ludo Rocher. Beginning in ~1971, he served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, where he is attested as Professor Emeritus in 2026.

nodes.label: M. Seshagiri Sastri
nodes.summary: M. Seshagiri Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. In 1899, he was attested as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University and as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library.

nodes.label: K. Kunjunni Raja
nodes.summary: K. Kunjunni Raja (1920–2005) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned doctorates at the University of Madras under Chittenjoor Kunhan Raja and at SOAS, University of London under John Brough, later serving as Reader In-Charge at Madras and honorary director of the Adyar Library.

nodes.label: Harald Hauptmann
nodes.description: German praehistorian and near eastern archaeologist
nodes.summary: Harald Hauptmann worked in archaeology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After studying at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg, and FU Berlin, he held posts at the German Archaeological Institute, FU Berlin, Heidelberg University, the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and Istanbul.

nodes.label: Shivram Dattatray Joshi
nodes.summary: Shivram Dattatray Joshi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Śaṅkarśāstri Mārulkar, Maheshvarshastri Joshi, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard. He served as professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University and headed the Sanskrit Dictionary Department at Deccan College.

nodes.label: Peri Sarveswara Sharma
nodes.summary: Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Wilhelm Rau (~1967–1971) and held a post at the University of Marburg (~1971–1991).

nodes.label: Karl Richard Lepsius
nodes.jawiki: カール・リヒャルト・レプシウス
nodes.summary: Karl Richard Lepsius, an archaeologist, historian, and linguist, studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin. He held a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1846–1884) and served as chief librarian at the Prussian State Library (~1873–1884).

nodes.label: Florinda De Simini
nodes.summary: Florinda De Simini works in Indology and religious studies. She held posts at the University of Naples Federico II (attested 2016) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2019).

nodes.label: Nirajan Kafle
nodes.summary: Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University (-2015) under Peter C. Bisschop. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2019) and Leiden University (attested 2021).

nodes.label: John Myrdhin Reynolds
nodes.summary: John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (~1968–1987), Lopon Tenzin Namdak (~1971), and Namkhai Norbu (~1976).

nodes.label: Megumu Honda
nodes.summary: Megumu Honda, active in Indology and Buddhist studies, studied under Johannes Rahder, Paul Tedesco, and Rulon Wells. A 1996 publication attests him as a professor at Doho University.

nodes.label: Johannes Rahder
nodes.summary: Johannes Rahder worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology. He earned a doctorate at Utrecht University (~1920-1926), later serving as professor at Utrecht (1930-1931), Leiden (1931-1946), and Yale University (1947-1965).

nodes.label: Paul Tedesco
nodes.summary: Paul Tedesco (1898–1980) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at the University of Vienna, he worked in research at Princeton and served as a professor at Yale University.

nodes.label: Rulon Wells
nodes.summary: Rulon Wells worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942), and held a long-term post at Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.

nodes.label: Eng Jin Ooi
nodes.summary: Eng Jin Ooi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Mahidol University by 2021. The doctorate was supervised by Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.

nodes.label: Walter Clawiter
nodes.description: born:1923|died:1970|; Clawiter, Walter 1923-1970; Clawiter; Clawiter, Walter ....-1970; Clawiter, Walter, m. 1970

nodes.label: Zhihua Yao
nodes.summary: Zhihua Yao works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel (~1997–2002), taught at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2005), and joined The Chinese University of Hong Kong around 2005.

nodes.label: Dipesh Chakrabarty
variants: ディペシュ・チャクラバルティ
nodes.jawiki: ディペシュ・チャクラバルティ
nodes.summary: Dipesh Chakrabarty (born 1948) is a historian and philosopher. He studied at Presidency University, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University under Donald Anthony Low. He taught at the University of Melbourne and has served as a professor at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Ronald Inden
nodes.summary: Ronald Inden is a scholar of Indology and history. He held a long-term academic post at the University of Chicago, serving as Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations (attested 2007, 2026).

nodes.label: C. M. Naim
nodes.summary: C. M. Naim was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1959–1961) and served as a faculty member and Professor Emeritus at the University of Chicago (~1961–2001).

nodes.label: John D. Kelly
nodes.summary: John D. Kelly is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He has been affiliated with the University of Chicago (attested 2007, 2026), where he serves as Christian W. Mackauer Professor of Anthropology and of Social Sciences.

nodes.label: Christopher Pinney
nodes.image: The President, Shri Pranab Mukherjee presenting the Padma Shri Award to Prof. Christopher Pinney, at an Investiture Ceremony-II, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, in New Delhi on April 20, 2013.jpg
nodes.summary: Christopher Pinney works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the Australian National University (~1988–1992) and University College London (from ~1993), alongside visiting or faculty roles at Chicago, Cape Town, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Northwestern University.

nodes.label: Donald Anthony Low
nodes.summary: Donald Anthony Low was an historian and Indologist who studied at Exeter College and Clare Hall, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Sussex (~1964–1973), Australian National University (~1973–1982), and the University of Cambridge (~1983–1994).

nodes.label: Siniruddha Dash
nodes.summary: Siniruddha Dash is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Madras (2000–2014) and as Director at the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation in 2020.

nodes.label: Godabarish Mishra
nodes.summary: Godabarish Mishra (1886–1956) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. Educated at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta, he taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya (1913–1919), was headmaster at Chakradharpur High School (1919–1921), and directed at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: Chittenjoor Kunhan Raja
nodes.description: born:1895|died:1963|; Kunhan Raja, Chittenjoor, 1895-1963; Chittenjoor Kunhan Raja; KunhanRaja, Chittenjoor 1895-1963; Raja, Chittenjore Kunhan n. 1895; Kunhan Raja, C.

nodes.label: N. Veezhinathan
nodes.summary: N. Veezhinathan is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under T. M. P. Mahadevan, T. S. Srinivasa Sastri, and doctoral supervisor A. Sankaran, earning a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964. He was a research scholar at Deccan College (1960–1963) and became Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1964.

nodes.label: Elisa Freschi
nodes.summary: Elisa Freschi (born 1977) specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her doctorate under Raffaele Torella, held posts at Sapienza University of Rome and the University of Vienna (~2012–2019), and became Associate Professor at the University of Toronto in ~2020.

nodes.label: John Taber
nodes.summary: John Taber is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl, later holding faculty posts at Case Western Reserve University (~1982–1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989).

nodes.label: Alessandro Graheli
nodes.summary: Alessandro Graheli is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held posts as a university assistant at the University of Vienna and principal investigator at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022), and at the University of Toronto (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Nirmal Chandra Sinha
nodes.summary: Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) was a historian and Tibetologist. Educated at the University of Calcutta and Presidency University, he was founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987) and Centenary Professor at the University of Calcutta (1971).

variants: B. J. Institute of Learning and Research

nodes.label: Swami Siddheswarananda
nodes.summary: Swami Siddheswarananda (1897–1957) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras (~1916–1919) and served in the Ramakrishna Order (~1920–1957).

nodes.label: K. Srinivasan
nodes.summary: K. Srinivasan works in Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College and held the Brahmasri Anna Subramaniam Chair at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020–2026).

nodes.label: Khammai Dhammasami
nodes.image: ၸဝ်ႈၶူးလူင်ထမ်ႇမသႃႇမိ.jpg
nodes.summary: Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (~2000-2004). He served as a fellow at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (~2004) and founded the Shan State Buddhist University in 2014.

nodes.label: Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies
variants: Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies, University of Oxford

nodes.label: Volker Grabowsky
nodes.summary: Volker Grabowsky (born 1959) is a historian of Southeast Asia educated at Kiel and Chiang Mai. He held posts at Passau, Münster, and the National University of Laos, before becoming Chair of Thai language and culture at Hamburg in 2009.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Guthrie
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Guthrie (born 1955) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Canterbury (~1998) and served as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago (~2004).

nodes.label: Ian Charles Harris
nodes.summary: Ian Charles Harris (1952–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge and Lancaster (PhD 1985), and held posts at Lancaster, St Hugh's College, Oxford, and the University of Cumbria.

nodes.label: University of Cumbria
variants: University College of St. Martin, Lancaster

nodes.label: Peter Koret
nodes.summary: Peter Koret is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London. He has held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: John Marston
nodes.summary: John Marston is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington in 1997 and held a post at El Colegio de México.

nodes.label: El Colegio de México
variants: Center for Asian and African Studies at El Colegio de México

nodes.label: Juliane Schober
nodes.summary: Juliane Schober specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and served as an associate professor (attested 2007) and professor of religious studies (attested 1997) at Arizona State University.

nodes.label: Hugo David
nodes.summary: Hugo David is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned a PhD from École Pratique des Hautes Études (-2012) and studied under multiple traditional teachers. He held a fellowship at Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member of EFEO (2015).

nodes.label: Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute
variants: The Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, Madras

nodes.label: Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi
nodes.summary: Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi works in Indology and philosophy. After studying at Central and National Sanskrit Universities, he held posts at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha, the French Institute of Pondicherry, Rajasthan Sanskrit University, and Karnataka Samskrit University.

nodes.label: N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya
nodes.summary: N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya (1928–2017) was an indologist and philosopher. He served as Vice Chancellor of the National Sanskrit University (1989–1994) and was a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1989–2017).

nodes.label: Stewart McFarlane
nodes.summary: Stewart McFarlane is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology who held posts in the Department of Religious Studies at Lancaster University (attested 1991, 2001).

nodes.label: Turrell V. Wylie
variants: タレル・ヴァール・ワイリー
nodes.summary: Turrell V. Wylie worked in Tibetology and sinology. He studied at the University of Washington (~1948–1958) and under Giuseppe Tucci and Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, holding faculty posts at the University of Washington from 1957 onward.

nodes.label: Bret W. Davis
nodes.summary: Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Vanderbilt University and Kyoto University, he served as a research fellow at Kyoto and Otani Universities, and became an Associate Professor of Philosophy at Loyola University Maryland.

nodes.label: Masakatsu Fujita
nodes.summary: Masakatsu Fujita is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied at Kyoto University (~1968–1972). He later served as head of the department of the History of Japanese Philosophy at Kyoto University (~2002–2014).

nodes.label: Jake H. Davis
nodes.summary: Jake H. Davis is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from CUNY Graduate Center. He has held teaching posts at Brown University, City College of New York, and NYU.

nodes.label: City University of New York
variants: the City University of New York
ニューヨーク市立大学

nodes.label: Sayadaw U Pandita
nodes.native: ဆရာတော် ဦးပဏ္ဍိတ
nodes.summary: Sayadaw U Pandita was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and Nandasiri Sayadaw. He succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw (1982–1991) and served as abbot of the Paṇḍitārāma Meditation Center, which he founded.

nodes.label: William Edelglass
nodes.summary: William Edelglass works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has taught philosophy at Colby College (attested 2007) and held positions as a professor at Marlboro College (attested 2013) and visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

nodes.label: Alan Fox
nodes.summary: Alan Fox is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and sinology who earned his PhD from Temple University. He has held faculty appointments in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Delaware.

nodes.label: Richard P. Hayes
nodes.summary: Richard P. Hayes is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his doctorate at Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He taught at McGill (attested 1997–2009) and the University of New Mexico (attested 2011–2016).

nodes.label: Fordham University
variants: フォーダム大学のリンカーンセンターキャンパスの人類学研究室

nodes.label: Marc Tiefenauer
nodes.summary: Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Lausanne in 2016 under the supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

nodes.label: Christine Chojnacki
nodes.summary: Christine Chojnacki is an Indologist who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991. She held a post as professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Ingo Strauch
nodes.summary: Ingo Strauch is an indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Freie Universität Berlin in 2000. He taught Andrea Schlosser and Kathrin Holz, and held a professorship at the University of Lausanne (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Emi Matsushita
nodes.summary: Emi Matsushita is a historian and archaeologist. She studied at Nanzan University, University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, holding posts at the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education (1994–1996) and Ohio State (1999–2001).

nodes.label: University of East Anglia
variants: Sainsbury Institute for the Study of Japanese Arts and Cultures (SISJAC), University of East Anglia
イースト・アングリア大学

nodes.label: Nalinaksha Dutt
nodes.summary: Nalinaksha Dutt (1894–1973) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Chittagong College, Presidency University, University of Calcutta (PhD ~1918–1921), and SOAS/University of London (DLitt ~1923–1925) under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served at Judson College (~1917–1920), University of Calcutta (~1924–1958), The Asiatic Society (1959–1961), and Maha Bodhi Society (1959–1973).

nodes.label: Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He held professorships at Narasinha Dutt College, Scottish Church College, Sanskrit College and University, and the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Shaman Hatley
nodes.summary: Shaman Hatley is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at Goddard College, he completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (1999–2007), taught at Concordia University (~2007–2015), and became chair of Asian studies at UMass Boston in 2015.

nodes.label: G. B. Palsule
nodes.summary: G. B. Palsule was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He worked as a sub-editor in the Dictionary Department at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1957) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Natasja Bosma
nodes.summary: Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen between circa 2013 and 2018, supervised by Hans T. Bakker.

nodes.label: Martine Kropman
nodes.summary: Martine Kropman is an Indologist. She has been a PhD researcher at the University of Groningen and an external PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop.

nodes.label: Dale S. Wright
nodes.summary: Dale S. Wright (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, W. Pachow, and Robert P. Scharlemann, and was appointed Gamble Professor at Occidental College around 1980.

nodes.label: Sarah Lawrence College
variants: サラ・ローレンス大学

nodes.label: Michel Mohr
nodes.summary: Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied under Seizan Yanagida and earned his PhD at the University of Geneva, later holding posts at Hanazono University (attested 2000–2006) and the University of Hawaiʻi.

nodes.label: Mario Poceski
nodes.summary: Mario Poceski specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning his PhD from UCLA in 2000 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., he taught at the University of Iowa (2001) and the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

nodes.label: University of Florida
variants: University of Florida College of Medicine
Center for the Study of Hindu Traditions

nodes.label: David E. Riggs
nodes.summary: David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Los Angeles. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and the University of Hawaiʻi, later holding research posts at Nichibunken and Oberlin College.

nodes.label: Albert Welter
nodes.summary: Albert Welter works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University, studying under Koichi Shinohara, Yun-hua Jan, and Ryosho Tanaka, and held posts at the University of Winnipeg and the University of Arizona.

nodes.label: Anthony Tribe
nodes.summary: Anthony Tribe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and indology who studied at the University of Bristol and earned a DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, Steven Collins, and Paul Williams. He held posts at the University of Montana and University of Arizona.

nodes.label: University of Arizona
variants: Center for Buddhist Studies at the University of Arizona

nodes.label: Merton College
variants: Merton College an der Universität Oxford

nodes.label: Libbie Mills
nodes.summary: Libbie Mills is an Indologist who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2011. In 2020, she was attested as a teacher of Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: Nina Mirnig
nodes.summary: Nina Mirnig is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held posts at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2020) and as Deputy Head at the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

nodes.label: John Nemec
nodes.summary: John Nemec is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Rochester, UCSB, Oxford, and Penn, under teachers including Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher. He is Associate Professor of Indian Religions and South Asian Studies at Virginia.

nodes.label: Stephen C. Berkwitz
nodes.summary: Stephen C. Berkwitz is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held a Fulbright fellowship at the University of Kelaniya (1995–1997). He serves as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Missouri State University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: M.L. Pattaratorn Chirapravati
nodes.native: พัตราภรณ์ จิรประวัติ
nodes.summary: M.L. Pattaratorn Chirapravati (born 1958) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and art history. Educated at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell universities, she served as Associate Professor at California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016), among other museum and academic posts.

nodes.label: Natasha Heller
nodes.summary: Natasha Heller is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2005. She has held academic positions at UC Berkeley, UCLA, and the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Justin McDaniel
nodes.summary: Justin McDaniel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and holds an endowed professorship in the humanities at the University of Pennsylvania.

nodes.label: University of California, Riverside
variants: カリフォルニア大学リバーサイド校

nodes.label: Zenno Ikuno
nodes.summary: Zenno Ikuno (born 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Elke Rogersdotter
nodes.summary: Elke Rogersdotter specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006), supervised by Bozena Werbart, Karin Viklund, and P. Ajithprasad.

nodes.label: Katragadda Paddayya
nodes.summary: Katragadda Paddayya (born 1943) is an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1963–1968) and served as Professor and Professor of Geo-archaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1974–2008).

nodes.label: Vasant Shivram Shinde
nodes.summary: Vasant Shivram Shinde is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts as Professor and Professor of South Asian Archaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2006 and 2026).

nodes.label: Asko Parpola
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Asko Parpola studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held positions at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies and the Academy of Finland, and served as Professor at the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).

nodes.label: University of Helsinki
variants: Institute for Asian and African Studies of the University of Helsinki
Institute of Asian and African Studies, University of Helsinki
Helsinki Collegium for Advanced Studies, University of Helsinki

nodes.label: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer
nodes.description: American Archaeologist, worked on the Indus Valley Civilization sites and other places in South Asia
nodes.summary: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley (~1974–1983) and became the George F. Dales Jr. & Barbara A. Dales Professor of Anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1985).

nodes.label: German Archaeological Institute
variants: Abteilung Istanbul des Deutschen Archäologischen Instituts

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Bodhi
nodes.description: American Theravada Buddhist monk and scholar (born 1944)
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Bodhi earned a BA at Brooklyn College and a PhD at Claremont Graduate University, studying under Balangoda Ananda Maitreya and Nyanaponika Thera. He edited for the Buddhist Publication Society (1984–2002) and presided over BAUS (2013).

nodes.label: Nyanaponika Thera
nodes.summary: Nyanaponika Thera (1901–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon, under Nyanatiloka Mahathera (1937), and under Mahasi Sayadaw (~1952–1953). He co-founded the Buddhist Publication Society, serving as leader/editor (1958–1984) and president (~1958–1988).

nodes.label: Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne
nodes.summary: Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Ceylon and earned a PhD from SOAS. He held posts at the University of Ceylon (1952–1973) and the University of Kelaniya (~1956–1986).

nodes.label: University of Ceylon
variants: Department of Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon

nodes.label: David Friedman
nodes.summary: David Friedman (1903–1984) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS and Professor at the University of London from circa 1950 to 1970.

nodes.label: Guang Xing
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Guang Xing earned his PhD at SOAS, University of London (~1999–2002) under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy H. Barrett. He became an assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong around 2003.

nodes.label: Jing Yin
nodes.summary: Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. He served as Director at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2006–2010).

nodes.label: Maurizio Taddei
nodes.summary: Maurizio Taddei was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was a professor at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and directed the editorial committee at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East.

nodes.label: Hemchandra Raychaudhuri
nodes.summary: Hemchandra Raychaudhuri was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the University of Calcutta as Carmichael Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture, attested in 1939 and 1965.

nodes.label: Edeltraud Harzer
nodes.summary: Edeltraud Harzer works in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Charles University and the University of Washington, with traditional training under Shree Narayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya, she held posts at Washington, Stanford, Indiana, and Texas at Austin.

nodes.label: Hisayoshi Miyamoto
nodes.summary: Hisayoshi Miyamoto is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi. Formerly a professor at Toyo University, his positions attested in 2026 include lectureships at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi
nodes.summary: Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi is an Indologist who studied under Kshetreṣa Chandra Chaṭṭopādhyāya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of the Kalidas Sanskrit Academy, and Advisor at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

nodes.label: Steven Edward Lindquist
nodes.summary: Steven Edward Lindquist is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under Patrick Olivelle, also studying with traditional teachers. He held a post at Concordia University.

nodes.label: Matthew R. Sayers
nodes.summary: Matthew R. Sayers specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Patrick Olivelle and Joel Brereton, and held an academic post at Lebanon Valley College attested in 2013.

nodes.label: International Academy of Indian Culture
variants: International Academy of Indian Culture, New Delhi
International Academy of Indian Culture (Saraswati Vihar)

nodes.label: Ram Shankar Tripathi
nodes.summary: Ram Shankar Tripathi worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as Head of Bauddhadarśana at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1989–1998) and Dean of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1989–1994).

nodes.label: Stanley Wolpert
nodes.summary: Stanley Wolpert (1927–2019) was a scholar of Indology and history. After studying at the City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania, he served at the University of California, Los Angeles, rising from assistant professor (1959) to department chair (1967).

nodes.label: Rosalind O'Hanlon
nodes.summary: Rosalind O'Hanlon is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. After earning her PhD at SOAS University of London (~1977–1982), she held posts at Clare College, Cambridge (~1988–2006) and the University of Oxford (~2006–2021).

nodes.label: Wannaporn Rienjang
nodes.summary: Wannaporn Rienjang is a scholar in history/archaeology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Cambridge. Her posts include positions at the British Museum, the University of Oxford (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).

nodes.label: Peter Stewart
nodes.summary: Peter Stewart is an art and archaeology scholar who completed his MA, MPhil, and PhD at Clare College, Cambridge (~1989–1998). He held posts at Cambridge, Reading, the Courtauld Institute, and Oxford (Associate Professor and CARC from 2011).

nodes.label: Quaid-i-Azam University
variants: Taxila Insititute of Asian Civilizations, Quaid-i-Azam University, Islamabad
Taxila Institute of Asian Civilizations at Quaid-i-Azam University, Islamabad

nodes.label: Luca Maria Olivieri
nodes.summary: Luca Maria Olivieri is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who earned his doctorate from Freie Universität Berlin (attested 2010). He directed the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and became an associate professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice around 2020.

nodes.label: Juhyung Rhi
nodes.summary: Juhyung Rhi specializes in Buddhist studies and art history/archaeology, receiving a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. In 1992, he became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University.

nodes.label: Thammasat University
variants: Faculty of Sociology and Anthropology, Thammasat University

nodes.label: Elphinstone College
variants: ボンベイ大学のエルフィンストーン・カレッジ
エルフィンストーン・カレッジ

nodes.label: H. G. Quaritch Wales
nodes.summary: H. G. Quaritch Wales was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He studied at Cambridge and earned a PhD at SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden. He served as Field Director for the Greater India Society (~1934–1941).

nodes.label: John Allan
nodes.summary: An Indologist and historian, John Allan studied at Edinburgh (~1902–1906) and Leipzig (~1906–1907). He served at the British Museum from 1907, becoming Keeper of Coins and Medals in 1931, and taught Sanskrit at UCL, SOAS, and Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti (1893–1956) was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned a PhD at Cambridge. He had an extensive career with the Archaeological Survey of India, culminating as Director General of Archaeology in India (1948–1950).

nodes.label: Bhadriraju Krishnamurti
nodes.summary: A linguist and Indologist, Krishnamurti earned his AM and PhD at Pennsylvania and studied under Murray B. Emeneau. He taught at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (where he was professor 1962–1986), and the University of Hyderabad (1986–1999).

nodes.label: Osmania University
variants: Department of Linguistics at Osmania University

nodes.label: Angelika Malinar
nodes.summary: Angelika Malinar is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the University of Tübingen. She held teaching posts at Freie Universität Berlin and SOAS, becoming extraordinary professor of Indology at the University of Zurich (2009).

nodes.label: Heinrich von Stietencron
nodes.image: Pranab Mukherjee conferring the first ‘Distinguished Indologist’ Award to the Prof. Emeritus Heinrich Freiherr Von Stietencron of the Federal Republic of Germany at the inauguration of the International Conference of.jpg
nodes.summary: Heinrich von Stietencron was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Munich, SOAS, and Heidelberg, and held posts at Heidelberg University (1965) and the University of Tübingen, where he was chairholder from 1973 to 1998.

nodes.label: Ryutaro Tsuchida
nodes.summary: Ryutaro Tsuchida studied Indology at the University of Tokyo and completed doctoral studies at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He was an assistant at Marburg (~1979–1983) before serving as professor and emeritus at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Tej Ram Sharma
nodes.summary: Tej Ram Sharma (born 1941) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral thesis at Banaras Hindu University in 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University around 1972.

nodes.label: Vishwa Nath Pathak
nodes.summary: Vishwa Nath Pathak (1926–2003) was a scholar of Indology and history who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, serving as professor (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Travis L. Smith
nodes.summary: Travis L. Smith is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from Columbia University under John Stratton Hawley. He has taught at Barnard College, the University of Florida, and the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Barnard College
variants: バーナード・カレッジ

nodes.label: D. Max Moerman
nodes.summary: D. Max Moerman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held posts at Barnard College (attested 2007–2008) and Columbia University (attested 2026), serving as Professor and Chair of Asian and Middle Eastern Cultures at Barnard.

nodes.label: Vasudha Dalmia
nodes.description: professor of Hindi and Modern South Asian Studies
nodes.summary: Indologist Vasudha Dalmia studied at Miranda House, the University of Cologne, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Heidelberg University. She lectured at the University of Tübingen and served as professor at UC Berkeley (2001–2012) and Yale University (2013–2014).

nodes.label: Sally J. Sutherland Goldman
nodes.summary: An Indologist, Sally J. Sutherland Goldman earned her PhD at UC Berkeley (1979) and studied under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and T. Shrinivas Shastri. She held posts at UC Berkeley, where she is Senior Lecturer Emerita.

nodes.label: Bisheshwar Nath Reu
nodes.summary: Bisheshwar Nath Reu worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha (~1910–1915). He served as Superintendent at Sumer Public Library (~1920–1950) and headed the Sardar Government Museum (~1920–1950) and Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre.

nodes.label: C. S. Srinivasachari
nodes.summary: C. S. Srinivasachari was a historian and Indologist who held posts as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).

nodes.label: Adinath Neminath Upadhye
nodes.summary: Adinath Neminath Upadhye was an Indologist who earned his BA and D.Litt. at the University of Mumbai. He taught Prakrit at Rajaram College (1930–1962), served as Professor Emeritus at Shivaji University, and became founding professor and Head of the Jaina Chair at the University of Mysore.

nodes.label: Haridas Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Haridas Bhattacharyya studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. An Indologist and philosopher, he held posts at Scottish Church College (1915), the University of Calcutta (1917), the University of Dhaka (1921), and Banaras Hindu University (1947).

nodes.label: Tiruvengadu Narayanayajwa Ramachandran
nodes.summary: Tiruvengadu Narayanayajwa Ramachandran was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He served as an archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (attested 1933) and as curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi.

nodes.label: Alfred Cooper Woolner
nodes.description: British academic (1878–1936); Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab
nodes.summary: Alfred Cooper Woolner, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Principal of the Oriental College (~1903–1936) and held positions as Registrar, Honorary Librarian, and Vice Chancellor (1928–1936) at the University of the Punjab.

nodes.label: Kshetreṣa Chandra Chaṭṭopādhyāya
nodes.summary: Kshetreṣa Chandra Chaṭṭopādhyāya (1896–1974) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ganganatha Jha. He held posts at the University of Allahabad (1924–1956) and was director of the Research Institute at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Sheldon Pollock
nodes.summary: Sheldon Pollock (born 1948) is an Indologist educated at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago, and Columbia University, and served as founding editor of the Murty Classical Library.

nodes.label: David N. Lorenzen
nodes.summary: David N. Lorenzen is an Indologist and historian of religion. After studies at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under A. L. Basham, he held a long-term post at El Colegio de México (1970–2010), becoming emeritus in 2019.

nodes.label: Sonam Kachru
nodes.summary: Sonam Kachru, specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, earned a PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold. He held fellowships at Forum Transregionale Studien and MPIWG, and became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jitendra Nath Mohanty
nodes.summary: Jitendra Nath Mohanty was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Göttingen. He held teaching posts at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, Oklahoma, and Temple University (circa 1986–2012).

nodes.label: Edward C. Dimock Jr.
nodes.summary: Edward C. Dimock Jr. worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Yale and earned his Ph.D. from Harvard Divinity School (~1953-1959). He held posts at the University of Chicago (1966-1993) and the American Institute of Indian Studies.

nodes.label: Kashinath Trimbak Telang
nodes.description: Indian judge, Indologist, writer and translator (1850–1893)
nodes.summary: Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai. He served as syndic (1881) and vice-chancellor (1892–1893) of the University of Mumbai, and president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1892–1893).

nodes.label: Mahesh A. Deokar
nodes.summary: Mahesh A. Deokar works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He has served as Professor (attested 2011) and Head (attested 2020–2021) at Savitribai Phule Pune University, and as Regional Representative for the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

nodes.id: I:Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies
nodes.label: Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies
variants: Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies

nodes.label: David Drewes
nodes.summary: David Drewes specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Karen C. Lang. He held teaching posts at Virginia and Indiana University, and became Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Manitoba (attested 2009–2010).

nodes.label: Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh
nodes.summary: Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indologist and historian. He earned a BA at Fergusson College (~1914–1918) under Ramchandra Dattatrya Ranade, also studying under Sukhlal Sanghvi and Muni Jinavijaya. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Ancient Indian History at Gujarat Vidyapith (~1920–1930).

nodes.label: Ramchandra B. Athavale
nodes.summary: Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at L.D. Arts College (attested 1938) and Gujarat Vidyapith.

nodes.label: James McHugh
nodes.summary: James McHugh is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard, he completed his PhD under Lawrence J. McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil, and held posts at USC and Cornell.

nodes.label: Lawrence J. McCrea
nodes.summary: Lawrence J. McCrea is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Sheldon Pollock. Attested in 2026, he serves as a Professor at Cornell University.

nodes.label: Anne E. Monius
nodes.summary: Anne E. Monius was a scholar of indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her undergraduate, master's, and doctoral degrees at Harvard, studying under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart. She taught at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) and Harvard (2002–2019).

nodes.label: Parimal G. Patil
nodes.summary: Parimal G. Patil is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard University and the University of Chicago (~1994–2002). He has served as a professor at Harvard University (~2001).

nodes.label: University of Southern California
variants: USC Shinso Ito Center for Japanese Religions and Culture
南カリフォルニア大学

nodes.label: Jayashree Sathe
nodes.summary: Jayashree Sathe is an Indologist and linguist. She has held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, serving as editor in chief (attested 2011) and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Pondicherry University
variants: Subramania Bharathi School of Tamil Language and Literature, Pondicherry University

nodes.label: K. A. Subramania Iyer
nodes.summary: K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indology scholar who served as a professor at the University of Lucknow and as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.id: I:Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library
nodes.label: Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library
variants: Department for the Publication of Oriental Manuscripts, Trivandrum
University Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library

nodes.label: Victor Turner
variants: ヴィクター・ターナー
nodes.jawiki: ヴィクター・ターナー
nodes.summary: Victor Turner worked in religious studies and anthropology. He studied at University College London and the University of Manchester (PhD, ~1950–1955). His career included posts at Manchester (~1955–1963), Cornell (1963), Chicago (1968–1977), and the University of Virginia (1977).

nodes.label: Lawrence E. Sullivan
nodes.summary: Lawrence E. Sullivan is a religious studies scholar. He served as Professor of the History of Religions at Harvard Divinity School, Director of the Center for the Study of World Religions (attested 2000–2004), and Professor of Theology at the University of Notre Dame.

nodes.label: Joseph Kitagawa
nodes.summary: Joseph Kitagawa worked in religious studies, Japanology, and history. He studied at Rikkyo, CDSP, Bexley Seabury, and Chicago under Joachim Wach. He spent his career at Chicago (1951–1987), including as Dean of the Divinity School.

nodes.label: Shimane Prefectural Junior College
variants: 島根県立国際短期大学

nodes.label: Alexandra van der Geer
nodes.summary: Alexandra van der Geer works in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied under Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Sondaar.

nodes.label: Kern Institute
variants: Kern Institute, Leiden University, the Netherlands
Kern Institute of Indology, Leiden University
Kern-Institut für Indische Archäologie und Geschichte der Universität Leiden
Kern Institute for Archaeology and Indian History, Leiden University

nodes.label: Shoshun Hayashidera
nodes.summary: Shoshun Hayashidera specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Hayashidera held a post at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2011) and serves as professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Herbert Härtel
nodes.summary: Herbert Härtel was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen. He served as Director of the Museum für Asiatische Kunst Berlin (1963–1986) and held an honorary professorship at the Free University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Oliver Philipp Frey
nodes.summary: Oliver Philipp Frey works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and later held a post there.

nodes.label: Yasutaka Muroya
nodes.summary: Yasutaka Muroya is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was a project research associate at the University of Vienna (attested 2007) and the University of Leipzig (attested 2015), and a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022).

nodes.label: Elena Mucciarelli
nodes.summary: Elena Mucciarelli specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Tübingen, where she held a post from 2016 to 2017, and became Assistant Professor for Hinduism in the Sanskrit Tradition at the University of Groningen in 2020.

nodes.label: Annette L. Heitmann
nodes.summary: Annette L. Heitmann is a scholar in tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) and completed her doctoral degree at the University of Vienna in 2002, studying under Christian Lindtner and David Seyfort Ruegg.

nodes.label: Eshin Nishimura
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Eshin Nishimura studied at Hanazono University and Kyoto University (PhD). He served as president of Hanazono University (2002–2005) and director of the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (~1999–2004).

nodes.label: Ensho Kobayashi
nodes.summary: Ensho Kobayashi is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Hanazono University, attested in 1988, and later as professor emeritus, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Paul Pelliot
variants: ポール・ユジェーヌ・ペリオ
nodes.summary: Paul Pelliot (1878–1945) was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, educated at Paris, Sorbonne, and INALCO. He held professorships at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and the Collège de France.

nodes.label: Henri Cordier
nodes.image: Gustave Caillebotte - Henri Cordier - Google Art Project.jpg
nodes.description: French linguist, historian, ethnographer, author, editor and Orientalist (1849–1925)
nodes.summary: Henri Cordier was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at Lycée Chaptal. He held long-term professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1881–1925) and the École Libre des Sciences Politiques (~1886–1925).

nodes.label: Noël Péri
nodes.summary: Noël Péri (1865–1922) worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He taught Western music at Tokyo Fine Arts School (1896–1906), founded Mélanges japonais in 1904, and served at École française d'Extrême-Orient as resident (1907) and secretary-librarian (1911).

nodes.id: I:Institut Belge des Hautes Études Chinoises
nodes.label: Institut Belge des Hautes Études Chinoises
variants: ベルギー中國學高等研究所
Institut Belge des Hautes Études Chinoises

nodes.label: Gaston Renondeau
variants: ガストン・ルノンドー
nodes.image: Major Gaston Renondeau - Allied missions at Vladivostock LCCN2014708663 (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Gaston Renondeau (1879–1967) was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Polytechnique (~1898–1900).

nodes.label: Henri Maspero
nodes.image: 201230 camp de Buchenwald dessins de prisonniers par Léon Mazeaud Henri Maspéro Bloc 61 1944 JB (2) (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Henri Maspero was a Sinologist, linguist, and historian of religion who studied under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at EFEO, Collège de France (1918–1945), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1920–1944), and the University of Paris/Sorbonne (~1932–1944).

nodes.label: Marcel Granet
nodes.summary: Marcel Granet studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. A scholar of sinology and religious studies, he held professorships at EPHE, INALCO, and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises, which he founded.

nodes.label: Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises
variants: パリ大學中國學高等研究所

nodes.label: Étienne Balazs
variants: エティエンヌ・バラ―シュ
エティエンヌ・バラーシュ
nodes.summary: Étienne Balazs (1905–1963) was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology who studied under Otto Franke (1923–1930). He later held posts at the CNRS (1949) and as professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1950–1963).

nodes.label: Otto Franke
nodes.summary: Otto Franke was a scholar of sinology and Indology who studied at Freiburg, Göttingen, and under Wilhelm Grube. He held the chair of Chinese Language and Culture at Hamburg and served as professor of sinology at Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Jacques Gernet
nodes.summary: Jacques Gernet (1921–2018) was a sinologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE, he held chairs and positions at EPHE/EHESS (1955–1976), the University of Paris (from 1957), Paris Diderot University (~1969–1973), and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

nodes.label: André Bareau
nodes.summary: André Bareau was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Sorbonne, EPHE, and Collège de France under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville, later serving as directeur d'études at EPHE (1956–1973) and directeur at Collège de France (1971–1991).

nodes.label: Bernard Frank
variants: ベルナール・フランク
nodes.summary: Bernard Frank (1927–1996) specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies, studying under Rolf Alfred Stein (~1950–1956). He was director at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and held the chair of Japanese civilization at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

nodes.label: Michel Soymié
nodes.summary: Michel Soymié was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at INALCO. He held posts at CNRS, EFEO, and held the Chair of History and Philosophy of Mediaeval China at EPHE (~1966–1992).

nodes.id: I:Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente, Kyoto Center
nodes.label: Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente, Kyoto Center
Kenji Shimada
nodes.summary: Kenji Shimada (1917–2000) was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and history who studied at Kyoto University (~1938–1941). He held positions at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities (~1949–1973) and as a researcher at Kyoto University (~1973–1981).

nodes.label: Annette Schmiedchen
nodes.summary: Annette Schmiedchen is an indologist and historian who earned her PhD at Humboldt University and completed her Habilitation at MLU Halle-Wittenberg, where she was a faculty member (circa 1996–2009). She has held appointments at Humboldt University, JNU, and the IASS.

nodes.label: Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson
nodes.summary: Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson was an Indologist and historian who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1857–1861). He served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and as Accountant General for the Government of Bengal.

nodes.label: Atsushi Kiyozawa
nodes.summary: Atsushi Kiyozawa is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Delhi. In 1989, he held an attested lecturer position at Kindai University.

nodes.label: Joseph E. Schwartzberg
nodes.summary: Joseph E. Schwartzberg was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Brooklyn College, University of Maryland, the Sorbonne, and Wisconsin under Richard Hartshorne. He taught at Pennsylvania (1960), Jawaharlal Nehru University (1979–1980), and Minnesota (1964–2000).

nodes.label: Russian Academy of Sciences
