nodes.label: Adam Bowles
nodes.summary: Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Greg Bailey (attested 2004) and served as senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).

nodes.label: Greg Bailey
nodes.summary: Greg Bailey is an Indologist who studied under Madeleine Biardeau and doctoral supervisor J. Durham. He held academic posts at La Trobe University, attested in 1994 and as Professor in 2004.

nodes.label: Julia Leslie
nodes.summary: Julia Leslie (1948–2004) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 1990 to 2004.

nodes.label: Palmira Brummett
nodes.summary: Palmira Brummett is a historian of Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She served at the University of Tennessee (~1989–2011) and as visiting professor at Brown University (2011–2016).

nodes.label: Robin Coningham
nodes.summary: Robin Coningham works in archaeology and Indology. After earning his PhD at Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin, he held chairs at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (appointed 2005).

nodes.label: Ryuo
nodes.summary: Ryuo was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Tō-ji (serving as sōgaku) and at Koyasan University.

nodes.label: Friedrich Hirth
nodes.summary: Friedrich Hirth worked in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald, and served in the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870–1897) before becoming Dean Lung Professor of Chinese at Columbia University (1902).

nodes.label: William Woodville Rockhill
variants: ウィリアム・ウッドヴィル・ロックヒル
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ウッドヴィル・ロックヒル
nodes.summary: Working in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, William Woodville Rockhill studied at Lycée Condorcet, École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871–1873), and under Léon Feer and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (~1876–1880).

nodes.label: Phra Brahmapundit
nodes.native: พระพรหมบัณฑิต
nodes.summary: Phra Brahmapundit is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Chief Abbot of Wat Prayurawongsawat (~1996), Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), and President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities (~2007).

nodes.id: I:Educational Department of the Bombay Presidency
nodes.label: Educational Department of the Bombay Presidency
A. V. Kathavate
nodes.summary: An Indologist who succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Andrew J. Nicholson
nodes.summary: Andrew J. Nicholson works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shree Narayan Mishra and serves as Associate Professor and Director of South Asian Studies at Stony Brook University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: John Marshall
nodes.summary: John Marshall worked in archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge and the British School at Athens under Arthur John Evans, and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1902–1931).

nodes.label: Kashinath Narayan Dikshit
nodes.summary: Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1944).

nodes.label: Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist and historian. He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910) and Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of India's Western Circle (1911–1917).

nodes.label: George Abraham Grierson
variants: ジョージ・エイブラハム・グリアソン
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・エイブラハム・グリアソン
nodes.description: Irish linguistic scholar and civil servant (1851–1941)
nodes.summary: George Abraham Grierson was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1868–1871). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1871–1898), as Superintendent of the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and as Governor at SOAS (1917–1925).

nodes.label: M. H. Krishna
nodes.image: Portrait photograph of M. H. Krishna.jpg
nodes.summary: M. H. Krishna (1892–1947) was a historian and Indologist. Educated at Maharaja's College, Mysore, University of Madras, and UCL under Ernest Arthur Gardner, he served as Professor of History, department head, and dean of arts at the University of Mysore.

nodes.label: Charles Duroiselle
nodes.summary: Charles Duroiselle was a scholar of Buddhist studies, archaeology, and linguistics. He served as professor of Pali at the University of Rangoon and was Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma from 1912 to 1940.

nodes.label: Madeleine Biardeau
nodes.summary: Madeleine Biardeau (1922–2010) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres/de jeunes filles (~1943–1946) and the University of Kerala (~1952–1954). She served as an instructor at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1958–1989).

nodes.label: Geoffrey Samuel
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Cambridge under Edmund Leach, Peter Wilson, and Stanley Tambiah, later serving as professor at Newcastle, Lancaster, and as Emeritus Professor at Cardiff University.

nodes.label: University of Newcastle
variants: University of Newcastle, New South Wales

nodes.label: Sandra Bell
nodes.summary: Sandra Bell is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University in 1991 and also held an academic post there.

nodes.label: Jules Oppert
variants: ジュール・オッペール
nodes.jawiki: ジュール・オッペール
nodes.summary: Jules Oppert (1825–1905) worked in linguistics, archaeology, and Iranian studies. Educated at Heidelberg, Bonn, Berlin, and Kiel (Ph.D. 1847), he taught Sanskrit at INALCO and served as professor at the Collège de France and University of Paris from 1874 to 1905.

nodes.label: R. Venkatraman
nodes.summary: R. Venkatraman is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, and was attested there as Reader in 1990.

nodes.label: Madurai Kamaraj University
variants: Department of Art History, M.K. University, Madurai

nodes.label: Kamil Václav Zvelebil
nodes.summary: Kamil Václav Zvelebil was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Charles University. He held posts at the Oriental Institute, Charles University, the University of Chicago, Heidelberg, Collège de France, and Utrecht University (c. 1976–1992).

nodes.label: Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat
nodes.summary: Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry, École française d'Extrême-Orient, the Chair of Sanskrit at EPHE (1967–2004), and served as Vice-President of the Société Asiatique (2000–2019).

nodes.label: V. Kameswari
nodes.summary: V. Kameswari is an Indologist associated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where she has served as an Editorial Committee member and research supervisor.

nodes.label: K. S. Balasubramanian
nodes.summary: K. S. Balasubramanian is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served on the Editorial Committee (attested 2001) and later as Director (attested 2026) at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

nodes.label: T. V. Vasudeva
nodes.summary: T. V. Vasudeva is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He has served as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and Deputy Director (attested 2026) at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

nodes.label: Ralph Lilley Turner
nodes.description: Indic languages philologist and university administrator (1888–1983)
nodes.summary: Ralph Lilley Turner worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1906–1910), and held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1913), Banaras Hindu University (1920–1922), and SOAS University of London, serving as Director (1922–1957).

nodes.label: Harold Walter Bailey
variants: ハロルド・ウォルター・ベイリー
nodes.jawiki: ハロルド・ウォルター・ベイリー
nodes.summary: Harold Walter Bailey worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Western Australia and Oxford under F. W. Thomas. Bailey taught at SOAS (1929) and held the Sanskrit chair at Cambridge (1936–1967).

nodes.label: Jules Bloch
nodes.summary: Jules Bloch was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet. He held posts as directeur d’études at EPHE (1919–1951) and Chair of Sanskrit language and literature at the Collège de France (1936–1951).

nodes.label: Bernhard Breloer
nodes.summary: Bernhard Breloer (1894–1947) was an Indology scholar who succeeded Heinrich Lüders. He held a professorship at the Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1935 to 1945.

nodes.label: Friedrich Weller
nodes.summary: Friedrich Weller specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Leipzig under August Conrady, later serving there as Privatdozent (~1922–1928) and chair of Indian Philology (1938–1958).

nodes.label: Paul Thieme
nodes.summary: Paul Thieme (1905–2001) studied Indology and linguistics at Göttingen and Berlin. He held professorships at the universities of Breslau, Halle-Wittenberg, Frankfurt, and Tübingen, as well as the Edward E. Salisbury chair at Yale University.

nodes.label: Herbert Niel Randle
nodes.summary: Herbert Niel Randle worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as professor of philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1910–1927) and as Librarian of the India Office Library from 1927 to 1949.

nodes.label: Minobusan University
variants: 身延山大学東洋文化研究所
身延山短期大学宗教科

nodes.label: Gensho Imanari
nodes.summary: Gensho Imanari was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral degrees at Waseda University. He was an assistant professor at Kokushikan University (~1958–1964) and professor emeritus at Rissho University (1980–1996).

nodes.label: Gyoshu Nakajo
nodes.summary: Gyoshu Nakajo worked in Buddhist studies. He served as a professor (教授) at Minobusan University (attested 1996), where he was also a professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Masumi Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Masumi Mochizuki is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Mochizuki held positions at Minobusan University, serving as a faculty of Buddhist studies lecturer (attested 2001), professor (attested 2015), and special appointment professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kanji Tamura
nodes.summary: Kanji Tamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held academic posts at Rissho University, serving as a part-time lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as an associate professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yukio Kotani
nodes.summary: Yukio Kotani is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Hanjiro Tominaga. He served at Rissho University from ~1970 to 2002, becoming professor emeritus of comparative literature.

nodes.label: Annie Besant
nodes.description: British socialist, theosophist, women's rights activist, writer and orator (1847-1933)
nodes.summary: Annie Besant was an indology and religious studies figure who studied at Birkbeck, University of London (circa 1879–1883). She founded Banaras Hindu University in 1898, serving as its president, and was president of the Theosophical Society (circa 1907–1933).

nodes.label: Theosophical Society
variants: Kyoto branch of the Theosophical Society

nodes.label: Surama Dasgupta
nodes.summary: Surama Dasgupta (1907–1998) worked in philosophy and Indology. She studied at the University of Calcutta and under Surendranath Dasgupta, earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge, and served as Reader in Philosophy at the University of Lucknow.

nodes.label: Elizabeth A. Cecil
nodes.summary: Elizabeth A. Cecil (born 1981) works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Brown University under James L. Fitzgerald. She taught at Leiden University (~2016–2018) before becoming Assistant Professor of Religion at Florida State University (~2018).

nodes.label: Sam van Schaik
nodes.summary: A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under teachers including Lama Jampa Thaye and earned his PhD at Manchester (~1996-2000). He held posts at the British Library (from 1999) and SOAS University of London.

nodes.label: Lewis Doney
nodes.summary: Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel's MA supervision and held posts at the University of Munich (attested 2018) and University of Bonn (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Dániel Balogh
nodes.summary: Dániel Balogh is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology who has held posts at the British Museum (attested 2021) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Charles DiSimone
nodes.summary: Charles DiSimone is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held positions at the University of Munich and Ghent University, where he is a permanent member and co-director.

nodes.label: Anna Filigenzi
nodes.summary: Anna Filigenzi is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She joined the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East in 1984, directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003), and held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2012) and Federico II (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Metropolitan Museum of Art
variants: Department of Asian Art, The Metropolitan Museum of Art
Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

nodes.label: Jason Neelis
nodes.summary: Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a master's at UT Austin and a PhD in 2001 at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon, later becoming Associate Professor and Chair at Wilfrid Laurier University.

nodes.label: Richard Payne
nodes.summary: Richard Payne is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 2007) and held a post at the University of Chicago (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Max Deeg
nodes.summary: Max Deeg specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg, later holding posts at Cardiff University as Head of School and at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies as a research fellow.

variants: Department of Philosophy at the University of Luxembourg

nodes.label: Lhagpa Phuntshogs
nodes.summary: Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist who served as president of the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991), secretary-general of the China Society of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), and Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center (2000).

nodes.label: Prods Oktor Skjærvø
nodes.summary: Prods Oktor Skjærvø works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oslo (PhD 1981) and Mainz (habil. 1984), and served as Aga Khan Professor of Iranian Studies at Harvard (~1993–2015).

nodes.label: Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya (1836–1906) was an Indology scholar who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested in 1882 and 1914).

nodes.label: Rama Misra Shastri
nodes.summary: Rama Misra Shastri worked in Indology and philosophy, serving as an assistant Professor of Sáṅkhya at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1882 and 1914).

nodes.label: Vitus Angermeier
nodes.summary: Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who completed his MA under Karin Preisendanz and studied with Chlodwig H. Werba and Roque Mesquita. As of 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Thomas Edward Colebrooke
nodes.summary: Thomas Edward Colebrooke was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Eton College and the East India Company College. He served as president (1864–1882) and later vice-president (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

nodes.label: Pascale Hugon
nodes.summary: Pascale Hugon works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Friedhelm Hardy
nodes.summary: Hardy was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Oxford, and held posts as Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London (~1974–2004) and Wilde Lecturer at Oxford (1985–1987).

nodes.label: A. N. Narasimhia
nodes.summary: A scholar of linguistics and Indology, he earned his PhD at SOAS under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933). He held posts at the University of Mysore and Maharaja's College, Mysore.

nodes.label: Heinrich Hettrich
nodes.summary: Heinrich Hettrich was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Saarland, Giessen, and Munich, and held posts at Saarland, Munich, Salzburg, Zurich, Marburg, and Würzburg, where he was Chair of Comparative Linguistics from 1989.

nodes.label: Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis
nodes.summary: Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1934-1939) and held academic posts at SOAS University of London (~1957-1979) and as professor at Leiden University (1978-1986).

nodes.label: Nalini Balbir
nodes.summary: Nalini Balbir is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Colette Caillat (~1977–1986). She held posts at CNRS (1982–1988), INALCO (~1988–2000), Sorbonne Nouvelle University (from 1988), EPHE (from 2000), and the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sylvain Brocquet
nodes.summary: Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1980) and under Marie-Claude Porcher (~1990–1996), and held a post at Aix-Marseille University around 1997.

nodes.label: Aix-Marseille University
variants: エクス＝マルセイユ大学

nodes.label: Whitney Cox
nodes.summary: Whitney Cox specializes in Indology and religious studies. Cox studied at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock, Wendy Doniger, and others, later serving as professor at Chicago (~2013).

nodes.label: Bard College
variants: Institute of Advanced Theology, Bard College

nodes.label: Albert Lutz
nodes.description: Swiss art historian, director Museum Rietberg
nodes.summary: Albert Lutz is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Zurich under Eberhard Fischer and Helmut Brinker, later serving at Museum Rietberg as curator for Chinese art and as director from 1998 to 2019.

nodes.label: Michael Jansen
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, Michael Jansen studied at Bonn, RWTH Aachen (earning his Promotion), Rome, and Delhi. He served as Dean of the Faculty of Architecture at RWTH Aachen (1988–1999) and founding rector of GUtech (2007–2008).

nodes.label: Christoph Cüppers
nodes.summary: Christoph Cüppers (born 1948) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1973–1983) under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler, later serving as director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (~1993–2013).

nodes.label: Christopher Key Chapple
nodes.summary: Christopher Key Chapple is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He served as a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982) and as Doshi Professor at Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).

nodes.label: Bloomfield College
variants: Bloomfield College of Montclair State University

nodes.label: Ramesh Shankar Gupte
nodes.summary: Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. In 1967 he was attested as Head of History & Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and visiting lecturer at Wake Forest, Salem, and Winston-Salem State.

nodes.label: Radha Krishna Choudhary
nodes.summary: Radha Krishna Choudhary (1921–1985) was an Indologist and historian educated at Patna University. He headed history at Ganesh Dutt College (1946), served as principal of Shankar Sah Vikramshila Mahavidyalaya, and taught history at Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University (1974–1984).

nodes.label: Dineschandra Sircar
nodes.summary: Dineschandra Sircar (1907–1985) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and held posts at the University of Calcutta as Lecturer in 1937 and Carmichael Professor in 1962.

nodes.label: Ram Sharan Sharma
nodes.summary: Ram Sharan Sharma was a historian and Indologist. Educated at Patna University and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, he held chairs at Patna University (1958–1973) and the University of Delhi (1973–1978), and founded the Indian Council of Historical Research.

nodes.label: Madhav M. Deshpande
nodes.summary: Madhav M. Deshpande (born 1946) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor at the University of Michigan, with his position attested in 1976 and from 2006 to 2009.

nodes.label: Pandurang Vaman Kane
nodes.image: Pandurang Vaman Kane 2022 stamp of India.jpg
nodes.summary: Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880–1972) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai. His posts included teaching at Elphinstone College (1909), Government Law College (~1917–1923), and serving as vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949).

nodes.label: Scindia Oriental Institute
variants: Scindia Oriental Institute at Vikram University, Ujjain

nodes.label: Amalananda Ghosh
nodes.summary: Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1947–1948). He served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968), as a fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study, and as a UNESCO adviser.

nodes.label: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
variants: サルヴパッリー・ラーダークリシュナン
nodes.image: Photograph of Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan presented to First Lady Jacqueline Kennedy in 1962.jpg
nodes.jawiki: サルヴパッリー・ラーダークリシュナン
nodes.description: 2nd President and 1st Vice President of India, Indian philosopher and politician (1888–1975)
nodes.summary: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975), a philosopher and Indologist educated at Madras Christian College, held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra and Banaras Hindu Universities, President of Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Chancellor of Delhi University.

nodes.label: Edwin Whitfield Fay
nodes.summary: Edwin Whitfield Fay was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield and Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve. He held professorships at Washington and Lee University (1893–1899) and the University of Texas at Austin.

nodes.label: Rhodes College
variants: South-Western Presbyterian University of Clarksville, Tennessee

nodes.label: Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve
nodes.summary: Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He served as Professor of Greek at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Professor at Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

nodes.label: John Henry Wright
nodes.image: John Henry Wright young age photo.jpg
nodes.summary: Classicist John Henry Wright studied at Dartmouth and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He held posts at Ohio State (1873–1876), Dartmouth (1878–1886), and Johns Hopkins (1886), before serving as Professor at Harvard University (~1887–1908).

nodes.label: Herbert Weir Smyth
nodes.summary: Herbert Weir Smyth was a linguist who studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe. He held teaching posts at Williams College, Bryn Mawr, and became Eliot Professor of Greek Literature at Harvard in 1901.

nodes.label: Minton Warren
nodes.summary: Minton Warren (1850–1907) was a linguist educated at Tufts, Yale (under William Dwight Whitney), Leipzig, Bonn, and Strasbourg. He held posts at Johns Hopkins University (1879–1899), the American Academy in Rome (1896–1899), and Harvard University (1899).

nodes.label: Francis Asbury Wood
variants: フランシス・A・ウッド

nodes.label: James Wilson Bright
nodes.summary: James Wilson Bright was a linguist who studied at Lafayette College and Johns Hopkins University. He taught at Cornell University in 1885 and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins from 1905 to 1925.

nodes.label: Yukio Yamanaka
nodes.summary: Yukio Yamanaka specializes in Indology and philosophy. He was a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and was attested in 2015 as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen.

nodes.label: Jin Kyoung Choi
nodes.summary: Jin Kyoung Choi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Choi studied at the University of Munich and Ghent University, later holding posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University.

nodes.label: Chion'in Jodo Sect Research Institute
variants: 知恩院浄土宗学研究所

nodes.label: Eisaku Okada
nodes.summary: Eisaku Okada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014). Okada held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (2014), Kyoto University (2015), and Koyasan University (2014, 2026).

nodes.label: Huanhuan He
nodes.summary: Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Posts include Zhejiang University (professor, attested 2015), University of Tokyo (attested 2015), Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (research fellow, attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hisataka Ishida
nodes.summary: Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser, also studying under Akira Saitō, Hiroshi Marui, Yoichi Fukuda, and Masahiro Inami, and became a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Yukihiko Matsumura
nodes.summary: Yukihiko Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Tohoku University (attested 2015), where he was also attested as a specialist researcher in 2026.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Tokushige
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Tokushige is a Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with Koyasan University, where he served as a commissioned researcher (attested 2015) and as a specially appointed lecturer (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Davaadorj Purevdorj
variants: ダワードルジ・プルプドルジ

nodes.label: Kaie Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Kaie Mochizuki (b. 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has served as a professor of Buddhism (attested 2015) and university president (attested 2026) at Minobusan University.

nodes.label: Tomoko Makidono
nodes.summary: Tomoko Makidono works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She held a researcher post at Minobusan University (attested 2015) and was a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jianming Hu
nodes.summary: Jianming Hu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (attested 2015). In 2015, he held a researcher position at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Shigeki Moro
nodes.summary: Shigeki Moro (born 1972) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and computational fields. Educated at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai universities under Ryoshun Okubo and Koyu Tamura, he held posts at Hanazono University (2002–2015) and Waseda University (professor, 2025).

nodes.label: Soto Zen Research Center
variants: 曹洞宗総合研究センター

variants: Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts

nodes.label: Hideyuki Matsumori

nodes.summary: Zijie Li specializes in Buddhist studies. In 2015, he was attested as studying at Komazawa University and holding a DC research fellowship from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.

nodes.label: Siegfried Lienhard
nodes.summary: Indologist Siegfried Lienhard studied at Vienna (Dr. phil. 1949), Paris, and Stockholm (Habilitation ~1966). He held posts at Göttingen, Banaras Hindu University, Kiel University (professor 1962–1968), and Stockholm University (professor 1968–1990), and was General Secretary of the IASS (~1972–1984).

nodes.label: Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar
nodes.summary: Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar (1887–1943) was an Indologist who studied at St. Xavier's, St John's, Edinburgh, and Berlin (PhD under Heinrich Lüders). He served at the Archaeological Survey of India and was General Editor of the Mahabharata at BORI.

nodes.label: Paul Fredericq
nodes.description: historian, teacher, professor and rector from Belgium (1850-1920)
nodes.summary: Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a historian who studied at Ghent University and the University of Liège (doctorate ~1875). He was a professor at Liège (~1879–1883) and at Ghent University from 1883, serving as its rector in 1919.

nodes.label: Peter Giles
nodes.summary: Peter Giles was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1878–1882) and Gonville and Caius College (~1882–1887). He served as Reader in Comparative Philology at Cambridge (~1891–1935) and Master of Emmanuel College (~1911–1935).

nodes.label: Edward James Rapson
nodes.summary: Edward James Rapson worked in Indology, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at St John's College, Cambridge, he served at the British Museum (1887–1906), UCL (1903), and as Cambridge's Professor of Sanskrit from 1906 to 1936.

nodes.label: Kisari Mohan Ganguli
nodes.summary: Kisari Mohan Ganguli was an indology scholar who was educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya (1840–1932) was an Indologist educated at Sanskrit College and Presidency University. He held academic posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

nodes.label: Michael Hutt
nodes.description: Professor of Nepali and Himalayan Studies
nodes.summary: Michael Hutt works in Indology and linguistics. He earned his BA and doctorate at SOAS University of London and the University of London, later serving at SOAS as Head of the South Asia Department and Associate Dean.

nodes.label: Yoshifumi Mizuno
nodes.summary: Yoshifumi Mizuno (born 1958) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, Toyo Bunko, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

nodes.label: Francis Vincent Tiso
nodes.summary: Francis Vincent Tiso specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary, later teaching Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University and serving as a visiting lecturer at Sapienza University of Rome.

nodes.label: Lobsang Shastri
nodes.summary: Lobsang Shastri specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Albrecht Hanisch
nodes.summary: Albrecht Hanisch works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn, and has served as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and Local Representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

nodes.label: S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri
nodes.summary: S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri worked in philosophy and Indology. He served at the University of Madras, where he was attested as Reader in Indian Philosophy in 1929 and as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy in 1942.

nodes.label: R. Balasubramanian
nodes.summary: R. Balasubramanian was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under the traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras (~1975–1989).

nodes.label: Harold G. Coward
nodes.summary: Harold G. Coward works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate in philosophy at McMaster University (until 1973) and served as a professor at the University of Calgary, director of its press (1981–1983), and director at the University of Victoria.

nodes.label: Claus Vogel
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and Tibetology, Vogel earned his PhD and completed his habilitation at the University of Marburg under Friedrich Müller and Wilhelm Rau. He taught at Marburg, the University of Göttingen, and the University of Bonn (Ordinarius 1976–1998).

nodes.label: Siran Upendra Deraniyagala
nodes.summary: Siran Upendra Deraniyagala was an archaeologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, the University of London, and Harvard University, learning under Frank Raymond Allchin. He served as Director General of Sri Lanka's Department of Archaeology (~1992–2001).

nodes.label: Tse-fu Kuan
nodes.summary: Tse-fu Kuan works in Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (1999–2004), conducted postdoctoral research at National Cheng Kung University, and held a post at Yuan Ze University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Alexander Yiannopoulos
nodes.summary: Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery and was supervised by Karin Myers (attested 2012–2017), alongside studying under teachers including Sherab Sangpo and Khenpo Sherab Dorje.

nodes.label: John J. Makransky
nodes.summary: John J. Makransky specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, among others, and taught as a professor of comparative theology and Buddhist studies at Boston College (attested 1996–2007).

nodes.label: Jay L. Garfield
nodes.summary: Jay L. Garfield works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied with teachers including Robert A. F. Thurman and Ngawang Samten. His appointments include Hampshire College (1980–1995), Smith College (~1999 onward), Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Melbourne.

nodes.label: T. S. Srinivasa Sastri
variants: シュリーニヴァーサ・シャーストリー
nodes.summary: T. S. Srinivasa Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts, including professor, at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1972, 1984–1992).

nodes.label: Umakant Premanand Shah
nodes.summary: Umakant Premanand Shah was an Indologist and historian. His career included serving at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda as deputy director in 1954 and as head of the Ramayana Project in 1965.

nodes.label: Yao Wang
nodes.summary: Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar in Tibetology who studied under Gongkar Tulku. He served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Susan J. Rosenfield
nodes.summary: Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2004, where she studied under teachers including Stephanie W. Jamison and George L. Hart.

nodes.label: Bhagavan Das
nodes.summary: A scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, Das earned an MA at the University of Calcutta. He co-founded Banaras Hindu University, served on its managing board (~1916), and was headmaster of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1921–1926).

nodes.label: Raniero Gnoli
nodes.summary: Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Mario Praz (~1948–1953) and Giuseppe Tucci (~1948–1954), later serving as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.

nodes.label: John W. Spellman
nodes.summary: John W. Spellman (1934–2021) was an Indology and history scholar. He held an academic post at the University of Washington (~1964–1967) and served as a professor at the University of Windsor (~1967–1999).

nodes.label: Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri
nodes.summary: Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held a professorship at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1991 and 2026.

nodes.label: Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi
nodes.summary: Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi was a historian of religion who studied under Mohammad Habib and at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University. He held posts at Aligarh Muslim University, Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, JNU, and the Australian National University (1967–1986).

nodes.label: Thomas R. Trautmann
nodes.summary: Thomas R. Trautmann is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He served as professor of history and anthropology at the University of Michigan (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Bala Sahai Shastri
nodes.summary: Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist. He served at Panjab University as an Assistant (attested 1932) and later as in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1941).

nodes.label: Wolfgang Morgenroth
nodes.summary: Wolfgang Morgenroth studied at Jena under Richard Hauschild and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He held teaching posts at Jena and Greifswald, and was Professor of Indology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1972–1994).

nodes.label: Richard Hauschild
nodes.summary: Richard Hauschild was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Jena under Johannes Hertel and Albert Debrunner. He was a professor at the University of Jena (1951–1967) and a member of the Saxon Academy of Sciences (1949–1972).

nodes.label: Karl Ammer

nodes.label: Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti

nodes.label: Ram Karan Sharma

nodes.label: Arvind Sharma
nodes.summary: Arvind Sharma, working in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, studied at Allahabad, Syracuse, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard (Ph.D.). He held posts at Queensland (1976), Sydney (1980), Harvard, and held the Birks Chair in Comparative Religion at McGill (1994).

nodes.label: Ellen M. Raven

nodes.label: Bruce B. Lawrence

nodes.label: B. N. K. Sharma
nodes.summary: B. N. K. Sharma worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Satyadhyana Tirtha and at the University of Madras and Presidency College, later serving at Annamalai University, Rajah's College, and Ramnarain Ruia Autonomous College (1953–1969).

nodes.label: Arinde L. Jonker
nodes.summary: Arinde L. Jonker works in the field of Indology. She completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), where she studied with Jonathan A. Silk and was supervised by Peter C. Bisschop.

nodes.label: Daniele Cuneo

nodes.label: Katrin Querl

nodes.label: Ihsan Ali
nodes.summary: Ihsan Ali is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Peshawar and under Frank Raymond Allchin, he has served as Professor at Peshawar, Vice Chancellor of Hazara University (~2006–2009), and Director of Archaeology and Museums.

nodes.label: Pratapaditya Pal

nodes.label: Joe Cribb

nodes.label: Charles Burnett
nodes.summary: Charles Burnett is a historian, philosopher, and Indologist who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held posts at St John's College, the University of Sheffield, and the Warburg Institute, where he became a professor in 1999.

nodes.label: Jan P. Hogendijk

nodes.label: Gustaaf Houtman

nodes.summary: Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at King's College London by 2014 and later served there as a postdoctoral research fellow (attested 2017).

nodes.summary: Asatoshi Kamiya is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. at Komazawa University (attested 1973) and served as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School (attested 1978).

nodes.label: Prahlad Pradhan

nodes.label: Martin Baumann
nodes.description: German university teacher in religious studies at university of Lucerne (Switzerland)
nodes.summary: Martin Baumann is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Leibniz University Hannover and completed his Habilitation at Leipzig, becoming Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

nodes.label: J. Gordon Melton
nodes.summary: J. Gordon Melton is a religious studies scholar educated at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held posts at UC Santa Barbara and Baylor University.

nodes.label: George D. Bond
nodes.summary: George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD at Northwestern University (~1968–1972), where he served as Professor of Religion (~1974–2012).

nodes.label: Richard Kieckhefer
nodes.summary: Richard Kieckhefer is a historian and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Saint Louis University and the University of Texas at Austin. He became a professor of history and religious studies at Northwestern University in 1975.

nodes.label: Gavin Flood
nodes.summary: Gavin Flood specializes in Indology and religious studies, having studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith (~1983–1989). He held professorships at Oxford (2005–2015), Stirling (~2005–2008), and Yale-NUS College (2016), directing the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies (2005–2015).

nodes.label: Carola Roloff
nodes.summary: Carola Roloff is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied at the University of Hamburg under Geshe Thubten Ngawang and David P. Jackson. Her posts include CIHTS (2006–2007), Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg, and visiting professor at the University of Hamburg (2018–2025).

nodes.label: Erling von Mende
nodes.summary: Erling von Mende is a Sinologist who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne (PhD 1964–1969, habilitation by 1979). He served as professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin from 1983 to 2007.

nodes.label: Lutz Bieg
nodes.summary: Lutz Bieg (born 1943) is a Sinologist who earned his Dr. phil. at Heidelberg University (~1965–1971) and his Habilitation at Freie Universität Berlin (by 1986). From 1989 to 2008, he was a full professor at the University of Cologne.

nodes.label: Monika Zin
nodes.summary: Monika Zin works in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Jagiellonian University, the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, and the University of Munich. She held professorships at Munich (c. 2000-2015) and Freie Universität Berlin (c. 2014-2016).

nodes.label: Dalsukh Malvania
nodes.summary: Dalsukh Malvania (1910–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1948–1959), Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, the University of Toronto, and served as Director of the L. D. Institute of Indology (~1963–1973).

nodes.label: Douglas Osto
nodes.summary: Douglas Osto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Washington and earned his PhD at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. He held posts at Massey University starting in 2005, becoming Senior Lecturer in ~2007.

nodes.label: Dan Lusthaus
nodes.summary: Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Temple University under several scholars, taught at institutions including Grinnell, Georgia, UCLA, and Florida State, and was a research associate at Harvard in 2005.

nodes.label: Gunapala Dharmasiri
nodes.summary: Gunapala Dharmasiri worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held an academic post at the University of Ceylon, attested in 1991 and 2008.

nodes.label: Ulrich Pagel
nodes.summary: Ulrich Pagel works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 2013–2020).

nodes.label: Carola S. Carstens
nodes.summary: Carola S. Carstens is an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her doctorate at the University of Hamburg (by 2006) and held a post at Rice University (1998–1999).

nodes.label: Ratna Basu
nodes.summary: Ratna Basu is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1989. She served as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Michael Balk
nodes.summary: Michael Balk specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He was a doctoral student at the University of Bonn until 1988 and held a post at the Prussian State Library, attested in 1991.

nodes.label: Friedrich Alexander Bischoff
nodes.summary: Bischoff was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Paris, Peking University, Hamburg, and the Mongolian Academy of Sciences, working under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held professorships at Indiana (1964–1982), Hamburg (1982–1993), and Vienna (~1992–2009).

nodes.label: William C. Kirby
nodes.summary: Sinologist and historian William C. Kirby studied at Dartmouth College and Harvard University under Philip A. Kuhn. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1980–1992) and Harvard University (from 1992), with visiting professorships at Heidelberg and Berlin.

nodes.label: Philip A. Kuhn
nodes.summary: Philip A. Kuhn was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown, and later held posts as associate professor of history at the University of Chicago (1963–1978) and professor and center director at Harvard University (1978; 1980–1986).

nodes.label: Nicola Di Cosmo
nodes.summary: Working in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history, Di Cosmo earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington. He held positions at Cambridge, Harvard, and Columbia, and became Henry Luce Foundation Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study around 2003.

nodes.label: Arthur Waley
variants: アーサー・デイヴィッド・ウェイリー
nodes.jawiki: アーサー・ウェイリー
nodes.summary: Arthur Waley was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at King's College, Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum (1913–1929) and later served as an honorary lecturer in Chinese poetry at SOAS (1948).

nodes.label: William Theodore de Bary
variants: ウィリアム・セオドア・ド・バリー
nodes.summary: William Theodore de Bary was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and religion. He studied at Columbia and Harvard, and served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia University from 1953 to 2017.

nodes.label: Charles A. Moore
nodes.summary: Charles A. Moore was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his A.B. and Ph.D. at Yale University. He taught at Yale and served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from 1936 to 1967, also founding Philosophy East and West.

nodes.label: William James

nodes.label: Maurice O'Connell Walshe
nodes.summary: Maurice O'Connell Walshe was a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Walpola Rahula. He held a post at the Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies from around 1955 to 1979.

nodes.label: Lisa N. Owen
nodes.summary: Lisa N. Owen works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Janice Leoshko, and she studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.

nodes.label: Janice Leoshko
nodes.summary: Janice Leoshko specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Susan L. Huntington and is attested as Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.

nodes.label: Daud Ali
nodes.summary: Daud Ali (born 1964) is an Indologist and historian. He studied at the College of William & Mary and the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught history at SOAS (circa 1995–2005) and joined the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.

nodes.label: Harold Hargreaves

nodes.summary: Harold Hargreaves was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. After serving as headmaster of Government High School, Amritsar (~1904–1908), he worked at the Archaeological Survey of India as Superintendent (1914) and Deputy Director General (1928–1931), having succeeded Jean Philippe Vogel and John Marshall.

nodes.label: Frederick M. Asher
nodes.summary: Frederick M. Asher worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota from circa 1971 to 2021, where he served as Professor from circa 1980 until 2021.

nodes.label: Shailendra Bhandare
nodes.summary: Shailendra Bhandare is a historian and Indologist who held posts as a British Museum curator and a Fitzwilliam Museum fellow. He served as Assistant Keeper at the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022) and became a Fellow at St Cross College.

nodes.label: Dilip K. Chakrabarti
nodes.summary: Dilip K. Chakrabarti (born 1941) is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Calcutta, the University of Delhi, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Cambridge (1990–2008).

nodes.label: Suryya Kumar Bhuyan
nodes.summary: Suryya Kumar Bhuyan (1892–1964) was an Indian historian and Indologist. He earned degrees from Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and SOAS, and held posts including Principal of Cotton University and Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University.

nodes.label: Banikanta Kakati
nodes.summary: Banikanta Kakati (1894–1952) was a linguist and scholar of religion and Indology. Educated at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, he was a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and later Dean and Assamese department head at Gauhati University (1948).

nodes.label: Cathy Cantwell
nodes.summary: Cathy Cantwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Kent (circa 1983–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

nodes.label: Robert Mayer
nodes.summary: Robert Mayer specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a dissertation at Bristol and a PhD at Leiden under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen, joining Oxford's Oriental Studies Faculty in 2002.

nodes.label: Esho Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Esho Kawasaki worked in Buddhist studies. He served as director at Bukkyo University (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Fang-Kuei Li
nodes.summary: Fang-Kuei Li was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist who earned his PhD at Chicago under Edward Sapir. He held major appointments at Academia Sinica (1929, 1973), the University of Washington (1949–1969), and the University of Hawaiʻi (1969–1974).

nodes.label: Hellmut Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Hellmut Wilhelm was a sinologist who studied at Frankfurt, Kiel, Grenoble, and Berlin under Otto Franke. He taught German at Peking University (~1933–1948) and held the chair of sinology at the University of Washington from 1948 to 1971.

nodes.label: Joseph Rock

nodes.summary: Joseph Rock worked in linguistics, Sinology, and history. He held positions at Mid-Pacific Institute (1908), University of Hawaiʻi (1908–1920), the USDA (ca. 1920–1924), the Army Map Service (1944), and Mills College.

nodes.label: Qian Lin
nodes.summary: Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and the University of Washington (PhD under Collett Cox), and later joined the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2026).

nodes.summary: Amy Snyder Ohta is a linguist and Japanologist. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1990 and 1993, and served as a professor at the University of Washington around 1995.

nodes.label: Izumi Matsuda-Kiami
nodes.summary: Izumi Matsuda-Kiami is a linguist and Japanologist who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She has served as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Itsuko Nishikawa
nodes.summary: Itsuko Nishikawa is a linguist and Japanologist who studied at Teachers College, Columbia University. She has served as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Chi-chiang Huang
nodes.summary: Chi-chiang Huang specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. Huang completed a PhD at the University of Arizona in 1986 under the supervision of Jing-shen Tao and studied with Robert M. Gimello.

nodes.label: John Jorgensen
nodes.summary: John Jorgensen is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA from the Australian National University under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner, and held posts at ANU, Griffith University, and La Trobe University.

nodes.label: Miriam Levering
nodes.summary: Miriam Levering was a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).

nodes.label: Whalen Lai
nodes.summary: Whalen Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a BA at International Christian University and a PhD at Harvard, later teaching at the University of Illinois (~1975–1976) and UC Davis (~1976–2008).

nodes.label: Taigen Dan Leighton
nodes.summary: Taigen Dan Leighton is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned degrees from Columbia University and the Graduate Theological Union. He has taught at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1994) and Loyola University Chicago (attested 2010), among other institutions.

nodes.label: Shohaku Okumura
nodes.summary: Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies specialist who studied at Komazawa University and under Kōshō Uchiyama. He held positions at Pioneer Valley Zendo, Kyoto Soto Zen Center, Minnesota Zen Meditation Center, and directed the Sōtō Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).

nodes.label: Ruth Fuller Sasaki
variants: ルース・フラー・エヴェレット
nodes.summary: Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Chicago (1927–1929) and under teachers including D. T. Suzuki, Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki, Mukai Kono, and Zuigan Goto. She directed the First Zen Institute of America (~1945–1967).

nodes.label: Ashin Nandamālābhivaṃsa
nodes.native: နန္ဒမာလာဘိဝံသ

nodes.label: Wilhelm Halbfass
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Halbfass was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed his doctorate at the University of Göttingen. He served as an assistant at Göttingen (~1968–1970) and was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1982–2000).

nodes.label: Harogadde Manappa Nayak
nodes.summary: Harogadde Manappa Nayak was a scholar of linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1967–1984) and as Vice-chancellor at Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

nodes.label: Patrick de Silva Kularatne
nodes.summary: Patrick de Silva Kularatne (1893–1976) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at University College London and the University of London (~1913–1917) and served as principal of Ananda College (~1918–1943).

nodes.label: Ryosho Nakamura
nodes.summary: Ryosho Nakamura studied indology and philosophy at Seventh Higher School Zoshikan, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, and Rissho University. He served as a professor at The International University of Kagoshima from around 1965 to 1998.

nodes.label: Masanori Nakagawa
nodes.summary: Masanori Nakagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and assistant professor in the Faculty of Literature (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

nodes.label: M. Shinoda
nodes.image: Linkin Park - From Zero Lead Press Photo - James Minchin III (Mike Shinoda).jpg
nodes.description: American musician, rapper, singer and songwriter
nodes.summary: M. Shinoda (born 1977) is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda's education includes studies at Agoura High School, Art Center College of Design, and study under teacher Seiren Matsunami.

nodes.label: Mun-keat Choong
nodes.summary: Buddhist studies scholar Mun-keat Choong studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute (1982), Komazawa University (~1986–1990), and the University of Queensland (~1991–1998 for MA and PhD), where he was supervised by Roderick S. Bucknell.

nodes.label: Roderick S. Bucknell
nodes.summary: Roderick S. Bucknell worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Queensland (~1976–2002), where he served as an associate professor from ~1995 to 2002.

nodes.label: Asim Kumar Chatterjee
nodes.description: indologist; writer; taught at Dept. of Ancient Hist. and Culture, Calcutta U., India
nodes.summary: Asim Kumar Chatterjee, an Indologist and historian, earned his Ph.D. under D. Mukherjee at the University of Calcutta (~1963–1967). He served as a Senior Research Fellow at the University of Calcutta and as a lecturer in English at Jangipur College.

nodes.label: Lobsang Dargyay
nodes.summary: Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (ca. 1952–1959), and completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Munich (ca. 1971–1974).

nodes.label: K. V. Raman
nodes.summary: K. V. Raman (1934–2024) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Madras Christian College, the University of Madras, and the Archaeological Survey of India, where he worked (~1956–1976) before becoming Professor and Head at Madras (1976–1995).

nodes.label: Elisa Ganser
nodes.summary: Elisa Ganser is an Indologist who is attested in 2026 as a Lektorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and as a visiting researcher at the University of Zurich.

nodes.label: Vincenzo Vergiani
nodes.summary: Vincenzo Vergiani is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Raffaele Torella. Around 2008, he took up a post as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson
nodes.image: Jeffrey Masson appearing on "After Dark", 23 September 1989.jpg
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson (born 1941) is an Indologist who studied at Harvard (BA ~1960–1964; PhD ~1964–1970) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, as well as in France, India, and Toronto. He held posts at the University of Toronto (1969–1980) and UC Berkeley (1981–1992).

nodes.label: Anukul Chandra Banerjee
nodes.summary: Anukul Chandra Banerjee worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, earned his PhD at the University of Calcutta, where he was assistant lecturer in Pali (attested 1943), and directed the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1981).

nodes.label: Richard D. Mann
nodes.summary: Richard D. Mann is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at McMaster University under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Elizabeth Errington
nodes.description: specialist on the archaeology of Gandhara and the collections of Charles Masson, and a numismatist specialising in Asian coins
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Errington (born 1951) works in history/archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar and became curator of pre-Islamic South and Central Asian coins at the British Museum in 1993.

nodes.label: Dorji Banzarov
nodes.summary: Dorji Banzarov was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at the First Kazan Male Gymnasium, the école militaire russo-mongole, and Kazan University, completing a doctoral dissertation under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski (~1842–1846).

nodes.label: Gombojab Tsybikov
nodes.summary: Gombojab Tsybikov (1873–1930) worked in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University (1895–1899), later serving as Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University (~1902–1917).

nodes.image: Базар Барадийн и Лыксык Жабэ в кругу родственников и гостей из Монголии.jpg

nodes.label: Tsyben Zhamtsarano

nodes.summary: Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University. He held positions at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan (1991).

nodes.label: Iwao Nakajima

nodes.label: Lodrö Sangpo

nodes.label: Robert M. Gimello

nodes.summary: Mathieu Boisvert is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under A. K. Warder and Ravindra Panth. He founded Université du Québec à Montréal and became a professor there in 1992.

nodes.label: Larry DeVries
nodes.summary: Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Minnesota. He taught at Minnesota, Hawaiʻi, and Washington, held a research post at Chicago, and was affiliated with Langara College in 2005.

nodes.label: Mavis L. Fenn
