nodes.summary: Robert Gardner (1925–2014) earned his BA from Harvard University (~1943–1947). He served as an assistant at the Fogg Museum, taught at the University of Puget Sound, founded Harvard University in 1957, and was a professor there (1956–1997).

nodes.label: R. Gordon Wasson
variants: ロバート・ゴードン・ワッソン
nodes.jawiki: ロバート・ゴードン・ワッソン
nodes.summary: R. Gordon Wasson (1898–1986) worked in religious studies and Indology. Educated at Columbia and the LSE, he worked for newspapers, Guaranty Trust Company (1928–1934), and J.P. Morgan & Co. (1934–1963), serving on the ACLS Executive Committee in 1951.

nodes.label: Ernest Bender
nodes.summary: Ernest Bender was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig S. Harris, and Henry Hoenigswald. He taught at the University of Pennsylvania as professor from 1950 to 1989.

nodes.label: David Webster
nodes.summary: David Webster is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: Thibaut d'Hubert
nodes.summary: Thibaut d'Hubert is an Indologist who held posts at the University of Chicago and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026 as Vertretungsprofessor).

nodes.label: Manan Ahmed Asif
nodes.description: historian and professor at Columbia University

nodes.label: Yigal Bronner
nodes.summary: Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock. He became an associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem around 2011.

nodes.label: Kiel University
variants: Historisches Seminar, Asiatische Geschichte, Universität Kiel

nodes.label: George C. O. Haas
nodes.summary: George C. O. Haas was an Indologist. He served as Recording Secretary for the American Oriental Society (~1914–1918) and was an editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1916–1918).

nodes.label: Kanai Lal Hazra
nodes.summary: Kanai Lal Hazra worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and completed his PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune, later lecturing in Pali at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Paul Fuller
nodes.summary: Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under Rupert Gethin, also studying under Paul Dundas, and held a post at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

nodes.label: John Dowson
nodes.summary: John Dowson was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Edwin Norris. He served as a tutor at East India Company College (~1855–1858) and as Professor of Hindustani at University College London and Staff College, Camberley (1855–1877).

nodes.label: Krishna Mohan Banerjee
nodes.summary: Krishna Mohan Banerjee (1813–1885) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Educated at Hare School, Presidency University, and Bishop's College under Alexander Duff, he held posts at Hare School and Bishop's College.

nodes.label: Edward Backhouse Eastwick
nodes.summary: Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Charterhouse School, Merton College, and the University of Oxford, later holding posts at East India Company College (1845) and the Foreign Office.

nodes.label: K. N. Jayatilleke
nodes.summary: K. N. Jayatilleke (1920–1970) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera and under Ludwig Wittgenstein at Cambridge (1945–1948), later serving as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon (~1955–1963).

nodes.label: Ludwig Wittgenstein
variants: ルートヴィヒ・ヨーゼフ・ヨーハン・ウィトゲンシュタイン
nodes.jawiki: ルートヴィヒ・ウィトゲンシュタイン
nodes.summary: Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at TU Berlin, Manchester, and Cambridge, where he earned his PhD. He spent his academic career at Cambridge, serving as a fellow and lecturer at Trinity College and as professor of philosophy (1930–1947).

nodes.label: Simo Parpola
nodes.summary: Simo Parpola is a linguist and historian who completed his PhD at the University of Helsinki (1961–1968). He held positions at Heidelberg, the University of Chicago (1977–1979), and the University of Helsinki (Docent 1973–1976; Professor 1978).

nodes.label: Pentti Aalto
nodes.summary: Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1935–1949) under Gustaf John Ramstedt and served there as Docent of Comparative Linguistics (1958–1980).

nodes.label: Kimmo Koskenniemi
nodes.summary: Kimmo Koskenniemi is a computational linguistics scholar educated at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu. He was Professor of Computer Linguistics at the University of Helsinki from circa 1989 to 2013 and directed its BAULT research community.

nodes.label: Frank Ernest Keay
nodes.birth_place: London Borough of Richmond upon Thames

nodes.label: Thomas Zehnder
nodes.summary: Thomas Zehnder is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Zurich, studying under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

nodes.label: Alexander Lubotsky
nodes.summary: Alexander Lubotsky (born 1956) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University (PhD under Robert S. P. Beekes), where he became full professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics in 1999.

nodes.label: Kristen De Joseph
nodes.summary: Kristen De Joseph is an Indology scholar who studied under Arlo Griffiths and pursues doctoral studies at Leiden University under supervisor Peter C. Bisschop.

nodes.label: M. S. Nagaraja Rao
nodes.summary: M. S. Nagaraja Rao (1932–2011) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Mysore, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and under M. N. Deshpande. He held posts at Karnatak University, Karnataka State Archaeology Department, and the ASI.

nodes.label: Govind Swamirao Gai
nodes.summary: Govind Swamirao Gai (1917–1995) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India and the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), and as epigraphy consultant to the American Institute of Indian Studies.

nodes.label: Wei-jen Teng
nodes.summary: Wei-jen Teng specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Chicago and Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, Teng taught at Dharma Drum and Chung-Hwa Institute.

nodes.label: Dylan Esler
nodes.summary: Dylan Esler works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from KU Leuven by 2018, where he also held a post as a research scholar.

nodes.label: University of Zagreb
variants: Faculty of Law at the University of Zagreb

nodes.label: Chen-kuo Lin
nodes.summary: Chen-kuo Lin (born 1950) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Temple University (graduated 1991) and served as Professor and Distinguished Professor at National Chengchi University (attested 1997–1999, 2014–2018), with visiting posts at Leiden University and IIAS.

nodes.label: Andrea Schlosser
nodes.summary: Andrea Schlosser specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her master's and PhD (2014) at Freie Universität Berlin, studying under Richard G. Salomon and Ingo Strauch. By 2026, she held research posts at Göttingen Academy and the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Yao-ming Tsai
nodes.summary: Yao-ming Tsai works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After earning a PhD from the University of California by 1997, he became Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.

nodes.label: Cristina Pecchia
nodes.summary: Cristina Pecchia studied at Sapienza University of Rome (PhD ~1999–2003) and the University of Vienna. Active in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, she worked as a researcher at IKGA (~2008) and as a lecturer at the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sanne Dokter-Mersch
nodes.summary: Sanne Dokter-Mersch is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She completed her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under the supervision of Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

nodes.label: K. Meenakshi
nodes.summary: K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist who earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under Madhukar Anant Mehendale in 1964. She was affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

nodes.label: Madhukar Anant Mehendale
nodes.summary: Madhukar Anant Mehendale (1918–2020) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and as Professor of Sanskrit and Sanskrit (Vedic) Literature at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970, 1983, 2026).

nodes.label: Jiryo Masuda
nodes.summary: Jiryo Masuda worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Unrai Wogihara. He later served as a professor at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Adyar Library and Research Centre
variants: The Adyar Library and Research Centre
Adyar Library of Theosophical Society Adyar

nodes.label: James Haughton Woods
nodes.summary: James Haughton Woods was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Harvard, Strasbourg, and under Paul Deussen, Arthur Venis, and Charles Rockwell Lanman, later holding a post at Harvard University (~1903-1935).

nodes.label: Arthur Venis
nodes.summary: Indologist Arthur Venis studied at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as professor and principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1881 to 1888 and later taught post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad (~1914–1918).

nodes.label: University College, Oxford
variants: オックスフォード大学ユニヴァーシティ・カレッジ
ユニバーシティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Corpus Christi College, Oxford
variants: Corpus Christi College Centre for the Study of Greek and Roman Antiquity
オックスフォード大学のコーパス・クリスティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Charles Henry Tawney
nodes.summary: Charles Henry Tawney was an Indologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served at Presidency University from 1866 to 1892, including as head, and later worked as Librarian of the India Office Library from 1892 to 1903.

nodes.id: I:Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences
nodes.label: Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences
variants: Institute of Oriental Studies, Russian Academy of Sciences
Institute of Oriental Studies, Russian Academy of Science
Leningrad branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute of Oriental Studies
Institute of Oriental Studies, Saint Petersburg

nodes.label: Robert Ford Campany
nodes.summary: Robert Ford Campany is a sinologist and religious studies scholar. He was a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2006), taught at the University of Southern California (~2006–2010), and became a colleague at Vanderbilt University in 2010.

nodes.label: D. N. Shukla
nodes.summary: D. N. Shukla was an Indology scholar who completed a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer. He held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1958).

nodes.label: Jitendra Nath Banerjea
nodes.summary: Jitendra Nath Banerjea was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri. Around 1918 to 1959, he served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Tiziana Pontillo
nodes.summary: Tiziana Pontillo is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.

nodes.label: David Burton
nodes.summary: David Burton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). By 2010, he served as Senior Lecturer in Theology and Religious Studies at Canterbury Christ Church University.

nodes.label: Kodai Akino
nodes.summary: Kodai Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership roles at Komazawa University, including president, and lectured at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Nyoten Jimbo
nodes.summary: Nyoten Jimbo (1880–1946) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami. He held a professorship at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Kodo Yamada
nodes.summary: Kodo Yamada was a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He taught at both Komazawa University and Keio University.

nodes.label: Totsudo Kato
nodes.summary: Totsudo Kato was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Seiran Ouchi, Enryo Inoue, and Bankon Shimada. He held teaching posts at Toyo University (~1899), Komazawa University, and Nihon University.

nodes.label: Seiran Ouchi
nodes.summary: Seiran Ouchi (1845–1918) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a tutor at Nishi Hongan-ji and later served as president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918.

nodes.label: Tetsuo Otani
nodes.summary: Tetsuo Otani (born 1939) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and Komazawa University. He held multiple academic posts, including professor and president at Komazawa University, and president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

nodes.label: Sokuo Eto
nodes.summary: Sokuo Eto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. He served as president of Komazawa Junior College (~1950–1958) and as professor at Komazawa University (1953).

nodes.label: John Firminger Duthie
nodes.summary: John Firminger Duthie served as Superintendent of the Botanical Gardens, Saharanpur (~1876–1903) and as Director of the Botanical Survey of India (~1891–1903).

nodes.label: George Watt
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ワット (植物学者)
nodes.summary: George Watt studied medicine at the universities of Aberdeen and Glasgow. He served as professor of botany at Presidency College/Presidency University and held positions at the University of Calcutta, the Indian Museum, and the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Moodeen Sheriff
nodes.description: Indian surgeon and practitioner of native medicine
nodes.summary: Moodeen Sheriff was active in medicine and Indology. He studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

nodes.label: Penor Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Palyul Monastery and under Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Karma Tekchok Nyingpo, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Jampel Gyepai Dorje. In 1978, he founded Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.

nodes.label: Govind Vinayak Devasthali
nodes.summary: Govind Vinayak Devasthali (1906–1994) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hari Damodar Velankar and served as Professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts & RYK Science College (attested 1944) and Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

nodes.label: Ram Niwas Pandey
nodes.summary: Ram Niwas Pandey works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Institute of Archaeology, Archaeological Survey of India, under doctoral supervisor Hit Narayan Jha.

nodes.id: I:Institute of Archaeology, Archaeological Survey of India
nodes.label: Institute of Archaeology, Archaeological Survey of India
variants: School of Archaeology at New Delhi

nodes.label: Francis X. Clooney
nodes.summary: Francis X. Clooney is an Indologist and religious studies philosopher who studied at Fordham and the University of Chicago (PhD 1984). He held professorships at Boston College (1984–2005) and Harvard University, including Harvard Divinity School (from 2005).

nodes.label: Jacqueline Suthren Hirst
nodes.summary: Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral studies under Julius Lipner. She has held posts at the University of Manchester, including as an Honorary Research Fellow (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Julius Lipner
nodes.summary: Julius Lipner (born 1946) is a scholar of Indology and religion. He studied at Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, Jadavpur, and King's College London under Hywel David Lewis. After teaching at Birmingham, he was professor of Hinduism at the University of Cambridge (1975–2013).

nodes.label: T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar
nodes.summary: T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and Professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

nodes.id: I:Administrative Commission of Cultural Relics of Tibet Autonomous Region
nodes.label: Administrative Commission of Cultural Relics of Tibet Autonomous Region
variants: Administrative Commission of Museum and Archaeological Data, Tibet

nodes.label: Peter Gaeffke
nodes.summary: Peter Gaeffke was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at PTH Regensburg, under Ernst Schwarz at Mainz (PhD 1952), and at DIAS. He held posts at Utrecht University (professor 1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (1972; professor 1975–2003).

nodes.label: James Morison
nodes.summary: James Morison was an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler as a Specialschüler. He held a post as Librarian at the University of Oxford, attested between 1917 and 1920.

nodes.label: Kenneth Somerled Macdonald
nodes.image: Kenneth S. Macdonald, M.A., D.D. (page 8 crop).jpg

nodes.id: I:United Free Church of Scotland Mission
nodes.label: United Free Church of Scotland Mission
Erik Zürcher
nodes.summary: Erik Zürcher was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Leiden University, also studying under Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and J. J. L. Duyvendak. He directed Leiden University (1961–1993) and co-edited T'oung Pao (1975–1992).

nodes.label: John Powers
nodes.summary: John Powers specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at College of the Holy Cross, McMaster University, and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding positions at the Australian National University, Deakin University, and the University of Melbourne.

nodes.label: Geshe Palden Dragpa
nodes.summary: Geshe Palden Dragpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as Librarian at Tibet House in New Delhi, an affiliation attested between 1987 and 1992, and was also attested there in 2004.

nodes.label: Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi
nodes.summary: Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi was an Indologist and historian who studied at Deccan College and the University of Mumbai. He served as Principal of Morris College and Vidarbha Institute, and later as professor at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University (1957–1966).

nodes.label: Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University
variants: College of Indology of Nagpur University

nodes.label: Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz
nodes.summary: Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz specializes in Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, completing her degrees at the University of Bonn. At the University of Bern, she became a full professor (1999) and served as dean (2007–2010).

nodes.label: Youru Wang
nodes.summary: Youru Wang works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Temple University under supervisors Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean. Wang held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 1999) and Rowan University (attested 2007, 2018).

nodes.label: Charles Wei-hsun Fu
nodes.summary: Charles Wei-hsun Fu (1933–1996) specialized in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed his studies at National Taiwan University (~1952–1960) and the University of Illinois System (~1965–1969), and held an academic post at Ohio University (~1969–1972).

nodes.label: Marc Aurel Stein
variants: マーク・オーレル・スタイン
nodes.summary: Marc Aurel Stein studied under Rudolf von Roth at Tübingen. An expert in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held leadership roles at Oriental College, Aliah University, Peshawar Museum, and the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Mithilesh Chaturvedi
nodes.summary: Mithilesh Chaturvedi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics affiliated with the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Delhi, where he was attested in 2009 and as professor emeritus in 2026.

nodes.label: P. K. Mukhopadhyay
nodes.summary: P. K. Mukhopadhyay is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as a Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and was a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Andrew Glass
nodes.summary: Andrew Glass works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and computational fields. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington (MA 2000, PhD 2006 under Richard G. Salomon), also studying under teachers including Mark Allon and Ulrich Pagel.

nodes.label: Mark Allon
nodes.summary: Mark Allon, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his PhD from Cambridge (~1989–1994) under K. R. Norman. He worked at SOAS (~1994–1998) before joining the University of Sydney, where he served as department chair (attested 2015–2017).

nodes.label: Timothy Lenz
nodes.summary: Timothy Lenz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox at the University of Washington, where he subsequently held faculty posts (attested 1998–2026).

nodes.label: Embar Krishnamacharya
nodes.summary: Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He held positions as Pandit at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, and posts at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937) and Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, Vadodara (attested 1939).

nodes.label: Noémie Verdon
nodes.summary: Noémie Verdon specializes in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2015 under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and held a post at Kyoto University attested in 2019.

nodes.label: John Faithfull Fleet
nodes.summary: John Faithfull Fleet, an Indology and history/archaeology scholar, studied at University College London (~1865–1867). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1865–1897), Bombay Civil Service (~1867–1897), and as Epigraphist to the Government of India (1883–1886).

nodes.label: Robert Sewell
nodes.summary: Robert Sewell worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1868 to 1894 and held the post of Keeper at the Tamil Nadu Archives.

nodes.label: Masato Kobayashi
nodes.summary: Masato Kobayashi is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Kyoto University and completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona. He was a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from circa 2000 to 2003.

nodes.label: Junglan Bang
nodes.summary: Junglan Bang specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. After studying under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn at Dongguk University, Bang completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and held a visiting researcher post at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Karma Lekshe Tsomo
nodes.description: Buddhist nun, scholar and social activist
nodes.summary: Karma Lekshe Tsomo specializes in religious and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi under the 14th Dalai Lama. She taught at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and University of Hawaiʻi (2023).

nodes.id: I:Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women
nodes.label: Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women
variants: Sakyadhita: International Association of Buddhist Women
Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women

nodes.label: Michael Alram
nodes.summary: Michael Alram works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer. His posts include positions at the Kunsthistorisches Museum and vice presidency of the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Kunsthistorisches Museum
variants: Münzkabinett des Kunsthistorischen Museums in Wien
Vienna Coin Cabinet at the Kunsthistorisches Museum

nodes.label: Deborah Klimburg-Salter
nodes.description: Austrian art historian and professor for non-European art history
nodes.summary: Deborah Klimburg-Salter is a scholar of Tibetology and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD under Oleg Grabar at Harvard and completed her Habilitation at the University of Vienna, where she held the chair of Asian art history from 1994 to 2015.

nodes.label: Durga Prasad Dikshit
nodes.summary: Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under R. K. Dikshit, Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi, and doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri.

nodes.label: Baij Nath Puri
nodes.summary: Baij Nath Puri was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. He served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow from circa 1956 to 1976.

nodes.label: Akira Hataya
nodes.summary: Akira Hataya is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held an assistant professorship at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and is an emeritus professor at Otani University (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Reiner Wiehl
nodes.summary: Reiner Wiehl was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977).

nodes.label: University of Lille
variants: Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III

nodes.label: R. N. Gadre
nodes.summary: R. N. Gadre was an Indologist. In 1959, he is attested as Professor of Sanskrit at both Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Raghunath Purushottam Paranjpye
nodes.summary: Raghunath Purushottam Paranjpye (1876–1966) studied under Vaman Shivram Apte. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).

nodes.label: Klaus Rüping
nodes.summary: Klaus Rüping is an Indologist who studied under Paul Hacker. He held a post as Dozent Dr. at the University of Münster, attested in 1978.

nodes.label: Volker Caumanns
nodes.summary: Volker Caumanns is a Tibetologist who earned his MA at Hamburg under David P. Jackson and his PhD at Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at Munich and LIRI, and teaches at Leipzig, Bern, and Hamburg.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Wackernagel
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Wackernagel worked in linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1824–1827) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh, and later served on the faculty at the University of Basel (1833; 1835–1869).

nodes.label: Haruka Yanagisawa
nodes.summary: Haruka Yanagisawa was a scholar of Indology and history-archaeology. He held academic posts at Chiba University from around 1974 to 1988 and subsequently at the University of Tokyo from around 1988 to 2007.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Yamashita
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Yamashita (born 1953) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).

nodes.label: Nobuhiro Ota
nodes.summary: Nobuhiro Ota (b. 1969) is an Indology and history scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. After a fellowship at Tokyo, he joined Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, becoming associate professor in 2007 and professor in 2021.

nodes.label: Akio Tanabe
nodes.summary: Akio Tanabe is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees including a doctorate at the University of Tokyo and held academic positions at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Kyoto University, and the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Nicolas Tournadre
variants: ニコラ・トゥルナドル
nodes.jawiki: ニコラ・トゥルナドル
nodes.summary: Nicolas Tournadre (born 1959) is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Claude Hagège. He held positions at INALCO (~1995–2004), University of Provence (~2004–2011), and Aix-Marseille University (~2012).

nodes.label: Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje
nodes.summary: Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (1932–1999) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Nyoshul Monastery (~1944–1955) and Katok Monastery, learning under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

nodes.label: Khenpo Appey
nodes.summary: Khenpo Appey (1927–2010) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Dzongsar Shedra under Khenpo Dragyab Lodrö. He served as director of Sakya College (1972–1985) and held a post at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Young Lamas Home School and Rumtek Monastery (~1964–1974) under teachers including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He became abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery in 1976 and founded Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981.

nodes.label: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Samten Gyatso (~1933–1940), Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Karsé Kongtrul, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

nodes.label: John Clifford Holt
nodes.summary: John Clifford Holt works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Gustavus Adolphus, GTU, and Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, later holding posts at Bowdoin (~1978–1988), Calgary (2006), and Chicago (~2020).

nodes.label: P. D. Premasiri
nodes.summary: P. D. Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ceylon, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi (PhD under Eliot Deutsch). He held multiple posts at the University of Ceylon, including department head (1997–2004) and professor (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Asanga Tilakaratne
nodes.summary: Asanga Tilakaratne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Professor, Department Head, and Emeritus Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, University of Kelaniya, and became a Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Alvappillai Veluppillai
nodes.summary: Alvappillai Veluppillai was an Indologist and linguist who studied under K. Kanapathypillai at the University of Ceylon and Thomas Burrow at the University of Oxford. His career included posts at the University of Ceylon, University of Jaffna, Uppsala University, and Arizona State University.

nodes.label: Mahinda Deegalle
nodes.image: Mahinda Deegalle in the video 'Imagine a Buddhist AI...'.png
nodes.summary: Mahinda Deegalle (born 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Ceylon, Harvard, and Chicago under Wendy Doniger and Frank E. Reynolds, he has held posts at IIBS, McGill, Harvard, Colgate, and Bath Spa University (~2002–2018).

nodes.label: Abdur Rehman
nodes.summary: Abdur Rehman worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, also studying under Ahmad Hasan Dani, and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Luise Hercus
nodes.summary: Luise Hercus was an Indologist and linguist educated at St Anne's College, Oxford, and the Australian National University. She tutored at St Anne's (1948–1954) and lectured in Sanskrit at the Australian National University (~1969–1991).

nodes.label: Pamela Gutman
nodes.summary: Pamela Gutman (1944–2015) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her studies at the University of Vienna and the Australian National University (~1972–1976).

nodes.label: Sakda Hemthep
nodes.summary: Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Peter Harvey and Max Deeg, earning an M.Phil. from Cardiff University by 2014. He was attested as a PhD researcher at Ghent University in 2026.

nodes.label: Radhika Herzberger
nodes.summary: Radhika Herzberger (born 1938) works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal (~1976–1982) and became Director of Rishi Valley School around 1982.

nodes.label: Alois Anton Führer
nodes.summary: Alois Anton Führer was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned a PhD from the University of Würzburg (1874–1879) and studied under Julius Jolly and Georg Bühler. He held posts at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, the State Museum, Lucknow, and the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Jean Dantinne
nodes.summary: Jean Dantinne was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Étienne Lamotte and held a position as a librarian at the University of Liège.

Königliche Akademie der Wissenschaften, Literatur und Schönen Künste Belgiens

nodes.label: Michael Carrithers
nodes.summary: Michael Carrithers is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Oxford. He held lectureships at Oxford and the London School of Economics before serving as Professor of Anthropology at Durham University.

nodes.label: Caroline Humphrey
nodes.summary: Caroline Humphrey is a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and religion. She studied at Cambridge (under Edmund Ronald Leach) and Leeds. Her career includes posts at Girton College, the Scott Polar Research Institute, King's College, and Cambridge university professor (1978–2010).

nodes.label: Klaus Bruhn
nodes.summary: Indologist Klaus Bruhn studied at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf and Walther Schubring, completing his doctorate and habilitation. He later served as Professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1991/1996.

nodes.label: Mary Jaksch
nodes.summary: Mary Jaksch (b. 1947) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey and also studied under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

nodes.label: Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez
nodes.summary: Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at the University of Sunderland, where he studied under Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: Jane Caple
nodes.summary: Jane Caple works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of Leeds and at the University of Manchester, where she is attested as a Research Fellow in 2026.

nodes.label: Sanjay Subrahmanyam
nodes.summary: Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam studied at the University of Delhi, including St. Stephen's College and the Delhi School of Economics. He has held chairs and posts at the University of Oxford, EHESS, UCLA, and the Collège de France.

nodes.label: Calambur Sivaramamurti
nodes.summary: Calambur Sivaramamurti was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Presidency University under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He held curatorial and leadership positions at the Government Museum in Chennai, the Indian Museum, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the National Museum, New Delhi.

nodes.label: Mortimer Wheeler
nodes.summary: Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London. He directed the National Museum of Wales and the London Museum, and served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1944 to 1948.

nodes.label: Hermann Beythan
nodes.summary: Hermann Beythan was a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Radscha Pillai.

nodes.label: Lance E. Nelson
nodes.summary: Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, earning his doctorate at McMaster University by 1986. Attested as a professor at the University of San Diego in 1997, he also taught James Blumenthal.

nodes.label: Sanskrit College and University
variants: Department of Postgraduate Training and Research, Sanskrit College, Calcutta
Postgraduate Training and Research Department of the Sanskrit College

nodes.label: Sibani Das Gupta
nodes.summary: Sibani Das Gupta was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and earned a doctorate from the University of Calcutta in 1954. Her mentors included teacher Rajendra Chandra Hazra and doctoral supervisor Sushil Kumar De.

nodes.label: Ram Chandra Kak
nodes.summary: Ram Chandra Kak was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Sri Pratap College and under John Marshall, later serving at the Archaeological Survey of India, the Sri Pratap Singh Museum, and the Government of Jammu and Kashmir.

nodes.label: John Collinson Nesfield
nodes.summary: John Collinson Nesfield worked in linguistics and Indology after studying at Merton College. He taught at Presidency University (~1867–1872) and Krishnagar Government College (~1872–1874), and served as principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1878).

nodes.label: Thupten Jinpa
nodes.image: HH the Dalai Lama enlightened translator, Dr. Thupten Jinpa.jpg
nodes.summary: Thupten Jinpa is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery, Zongkar Choede Monastery, and Cambridge, and founded the Institute of Tibetan Classics, where he became chief editor around 1999.

nodes.label: Tashi Tsering
nodes.summary: Tashi Tsering works in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at Central School for Tibetans, Dalhousie, and under numerous teachers, he served at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1979–1992), Amnye Machen Institute (~1992), and Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014–2019).

nodes.label: Elizabeth Napper
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Geshe Wangyal, and Paul Groner, and served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).

nodes.label: Rory Mackenzie
nodes.summary: Rory Mackenzie works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Peter Harvey and held a teaching post at International Christian College.

nodes.label: Kodo Kawamura
nodes.summary: Kodo Kawamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his master's and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from around 1966 to 2004.

nodes.label: Georg Heinrich Pertz
nodes.summary: Georg Heinrich Pertz was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1813 to 1816 under Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren and served as head of the Prussian State Library from circa 1842 to 1873.

nodes.label: Kurunegoda Piyatissa
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kurunegoda Piyatissa was affiliated with the New York Buddhist Vihara, serving as its head as attested in 1998.

nodes.label: Rajendra Mishra
nodes.summary: Rajendra Mishra (born 1943) is an Indologist who studied under Rambhadracharya. He served as head of the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University and as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Pascale Haag
nodes.summary: Pascale Haag is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat and Paris Nanterre University under Marie-Claire Gay, holding a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~2003).

nodes.label: David L. Haberman
nodes.description: American indologist and historian of religion
nodes.summary: David L. Haberman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1972–1976). He held posts at the University of Arizona (~1987–1989) and Indiana University Bloomington (~1989; Professor Emeritus attested 2026).

nodes.label: P. S. Sivaswami Iyer
nodes.summary: P. S. Sivaswami Iyer was an Indologist who studied at Presidency College, Chennai (~1880–1884). In 1927, he served as the President of the Editorial Board for the Journal of Oriental Research.

nodes.label: K. Balasubrahmanya Iyer
nodes.summary: K. Balasubrahmanya Iyer was an Indologist who served as secretary at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945) and as managing editor of the Journal of Oriental Research.

nodes.label: Norvin J. Hein
nodes.summary: Norvin J. Hein was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion at Yale Divinity School, attested in 1965.

nodes.label: John James Jones
nodes.summary: John James Jones was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Aberystwyth University (~1912–1916). He served as Deputy-Keeper of the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales (~1926–1957).

nodes.label: Betty Heimann
nodes.summary: An Indologist and philosopher, Heimann earned doctorates at Strasbourg and Kiel and habilitated at Halle under Eugen Hultzsch. She taught at Halle, became associate professor at Hamburg, and held appointments at the universities of London, Oxford, and Colombo.

nodes.label: Ivo Fišer
nodes.summary: Ivo Fišer (1929–2004) was an Indologist. He held posts as a lecturer at Charles University (attested 1960) and at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology (attested 1970).

nodes.label: Herbert V. Guenther
nodes.summary: Herbert V. Guenther worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, studying at Munich and Vienna under Wilhelm Geiger and Wilhelm Havers. He held posts at Vienna, Lucknow, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and the University of Saskatchewan (1964–1984).

nodes.label: Ananda Guruge
nodes.summary: Ananda Guruge (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from the University of Ceylon and the University of London. He held posts at NIEPA, California State University, Fullerton, and the University of the West.

Carmen Meinert
nodes.summary: Carmen Meinert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn (2001) and has held research posts at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and Ruhr University Bochum.

nodes.label: Christoph Anderl
nodes.summary: Christoph Anderl (born 1963) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and linguistics. He earned an MA from the University of Vienna and a PhD from the University of Oslo under Christoph Harbsmeier, joining Ghent University as a permanent member around 2012.

nodes.label: N. Venkataramanayya
nodes.summary: N. Venkataramanayya (1891–1976) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras and as Deputy Director for Epigraphy at the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh.

nodes.label: Evan Thompson
nodes.summary: Evan Thompson works in philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Amherst College and the University of Toronto under teachers including Robert A. F. Thurman and Francisco J. Varela, he has held professorships at Toronto (~2005–2013) and the University of British Columbia (2013).

nodes.label: Dan Zahavi
nodes.summary: Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who earned his Ph.D. at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and his Dr.phil. at the University of Copenhagen. He has served as professor and Center for Subjectivity Research director at Copenhagen and as professor at Oxford.

nodes.label: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad
nodes.summary: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, working in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, earned a doctorate from the University of Oxford. He held posts at Clare Hall, Trinity College, Oxford, and National University of Singapore, before becoming Distinguished Professor at Lancaster University.

nodes.label: Eleanor Rosch
nodes.summary: Eleanor Rosch (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under Roger Brown in ~1963–1969. After positions at Connecticut College and Brown University, she became a professor of cognitive psychology at UC Berkeley in 1971.

nodes.label: Karen O'Brien-Kop
nodes.summary: Karen O'Brien-Kop works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After completing her PhD at SOAS University of London, she held teaching posts at SOAS, the University of Roehampton (attested 2020), and King's College London (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Daniela Bevilacqua
nodes.summary: Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned PhDs from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and was a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London as attested in 2020.

nodes.summary: Sravana Borkataky-Varma is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD ~2011–2016). She has taught at Rice, Montana, UNC Wilmington, Harvard, CSWR, and became Instructional Professor at the University of Houston (~2022).

nodes.label: Mikel Burley
nodes.summary: Mikel Burley is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Essex under Jay M. Bernstein, earned a PhD at Bristol supervised by John Peacock, and became an Associate Professor of Religion and Philosophy at the University of Leeds.

nodes.label: Philip Deslippe
nodes.summary: Philip Deslippe is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He has served as a graduate student and teaching associate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2020–2026).

nodes.label: Carl W. Ernst
nodes.summary: Carl W. Ernst (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford and Harvard, taught at Pomona College (1981–1992), and served as professor at UNC Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

variants: Muda Institute, Baruch Ivcher School of Psychology, IDC Herzliya

nodes.label: Gordon Hannington Luce
nodes.summary: Gordon Hannington Luce (1889–1979) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at Dean Close School and Emmanuel College, Cambridge (~1908–1912), he served as a professor at the University of Rangoon from ~1912 to 1964.

nodes.label: John Alexander Stewart
nodes.summary: John Alexander Stewart worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying at the University of Aberdeen (~1899–1903), he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1905–1933) and held posts at the University of London (~1933–1944) and SOAS (~1933–1948).

nodes.label: Nani Gopal Majumdar
nodes.summary: Nani Gopal Majumdar (1897–1938) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1918–1923). He served as Superintendent of the Indian Museum's Archæological Section (~1929–1938) and as Superintendent with the Archaeological Survey of India (1931).

nodes.label: Daya Ram Sahni
nodes.summary: Daya Ram Sahni was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Oriental College and University of the Punjab. He served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1931–1935) and Director of Archaeology for Jaipur (1935).

nodes.label: Sydney Frank Markham
nodes.summary: Sydney Frank Markham (1897–1975) was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at Wadham College, Oxford (~1919–1923), and served as Secretary and later President of the Museums Association (~1929–1942).

nodes.label: Ghulam Yazdani
nodes.summary: Ghulam Yazdani (1885–1962) was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar who studied at Aligarh Muslim University under C. F. Andrews, Mohammad Ishaq, and Nazir Ahmad Dehlvi. He directed the Archaeological Department of Hyderabad State from circa 1914 to 1943.

nodes.label: Hirananda Sastri
nodes.summary: Hirananda Sastri was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at DAV College and Oriental College. He held posts at DAV College, Panjab University, the Archaeological Survey of India, several museums, Jammu and Kashmir, and the Archaeological Department, Baroda State.

nodes.label: Ramaprasad Chanda
nodes.summary: Ramaprasad Chanda was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist educated at Scottish Church College and Dhaka College. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India, the University of Calcutta, and the Indian Museum (1921–1932), and presided over the Indian Anthropological Institute.

nodes.label: Jeffrey S. Lidke
nodes.summary: Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held a post as a visiting assistant professor of religion at the University of Virginia (attested 2003) and holds a post at Berry College.

nodes.summary: Anna Andreeva specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She has held posts at Heidelberg University and Ghent University, where she is a permanent member (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Georgios T. Halkias
nodes.summary: Georgios T. Halkias, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed his DPhil at Oxford under Charles Ramble. He held research posts at SOAS, the Warburg Institute, and Bochum before joining the University of Hong Kong (~2013).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Kotyk
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Kotyk works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA from Komazawa University (2015–2016) and a PhD from Leiden University (-2017) under James A. Benn. His posts include McMaster University (attested 2019) and the University of Bologna.

nodes.label: Eric Haruki Swanson
nodes.summary: Eric Haruki Swanson is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has held academic posts at Loyola Marymount University and served as a Senior Visiting Scholar at Stanford University, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Sthaneshwar Timalsina
nodes.summary: Sthaneshwar Timalsina is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. nodes.summary: John Chadwick worked in linguistics and classics/archaeology, studying at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He worked at Oxford (~1946–1952) and Cambridge (from 1952), serving as Perceval Maitland Laurence Reader in Classics (1969–1984) and Fellow of Downing College.

nodes.label: Bridget Allchin
nodes.description: English archaeologist, specializing in South Asian archaeology
nodes.summary: Bridget Allchin (1927–2017) was an archaeologist and Indologist who earned her Ph.D. from the UCL Institute of Archaeology. She was a Fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge, and served as Secretary General of the European Association of South Asian Studies.

nodes.label: Seema Alavi
nodes.summary: Seema Alavi is a historian who earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge (~1986–1991). She taught at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1991–1994) and the University of Delhi (~2008–2020), and served as professor of history at Jamia Millia Islamia (~1994–2008) and Ashoka University (~2020).

nodes.label: Ali S. Asani
nodes.description: Chair:Near Eastern Languages/Civilizations Department/Director:Prince Alwaleed bin Talal Islamic Studies Program/Harvard University
nodes.summary: Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Ali S. Asani studied at Harvard College (~1973–1977) and Harvard University (~1977–1984). He has served as a professor at Harvard University since ~1983.

nodes.label: Emmie te Nijenhuis
nodes.summary: Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, completing her PhD under Jan Gonda (~1964–1970). She taught Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988) and served at the University of Amsterdam.

nodes.label: Alexander C. McKay
nodes.summary: Alexander C. McKay (born 1953) is a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London in 1995 and held a research fellowship at University College London.

nodes.label: Shek-Wing Tam
nodes.description: Hong Kong Buddhist scholar, writer, and fortune-teller
nodes.summary: Shek-Wing Tam (1935–2024) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Taught by Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Yingguang Qu, and Yui Chi Lau, he founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies Association in North America and served as a professor at Renmin University.

nodes.label: Weirong Shen
nodes.summary: Weirong Shen (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Shen has held teaching positions at the University of Hong Kong and Renmin University of China (~2006–2019).

nodes.label: Henry Shiu
nodes.summary: Henry Shiu specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Toronto in 2006, having studied under Shek-Wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David B. Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.

nodes.label: Kapila Vatsyayan
nodes.summary: Kapila Vatsyayan was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who earned degrees at the University of Delhi, University of Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University. She taught at Delhi and BHU and held leadership roles at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

nodes.label: David J. Kalupahana
nodes.description: Sri Lankan Buddhist scholar and philosopher (1936–2014)
nodes.summary: David J. Kalupahana (1936–2014) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. Educated at the University of Ceylon and SOAS University of London (PhD under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman), he taught at Ceylon before becoming Philosophy Department Chairman at the University of Hawaiʻi in 1972.

nodes.label: N. A. Jayawickrama
nodes.summary: N. A. Jayawickrama (born 1920) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He served as professor at the University of Ceylon (~1958–1972) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Edward Vernon Arnold
nodes.summary: Edward Vernon Arnold was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Cambridge and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge, and professor at Bangor University (1884–1924).
