nodes.label: Carl Darling Buck
nodes.summary: Carl Darling Buck (1866–1955) was a linguist who studied at Yale University (~1882–1889) and the University of Leipzig (~1889–1892). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933, teaching Leonard Bloomfield and Fang-Kuei Li.

nodes.label: Lawrence Heyworth Mills
nodes.summary: Lawrence Heyworth Mills (1837–1918) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at New York University and held a professorship at the University of Oxford (attested 1903).

nodes.label: George Foot Moore
nodes.summary: George Foot Moore was a religious studies scholar who studied at Yale and Union Theological Seminary. He was a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and Frothingham Professor of the history of religion at Harvard University (1904–1928).

nodes.label: Pulinbihari Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Pulinbihari Chakravarti is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at The Asiatic Society (attested 1951).

nodes.label: Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi
nodes.summary: Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi is an Indologist and linguist who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, including serving as head of its Research Department (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Donald Capps
nodes.description: American professor and author of pastoral theology (1939–2015)
nodes.summary: Donald Capps was a religious studies scholar who studied at Lewis & Clark, Yale, and Chicago. He held faculty posts at the University of Chicago, UNC Charlotte, and Phillips University, before serving at Princeton Theological Seminary from 1981 to 2009.

nodes.label: Helen Hardacre
nodes.summary: Helen Hardacre specializes in Japanology and religious studies. She studied at Vanderbilt and Chicago under Joseph Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith, holding posts at Princeton (1980–1989), Griffith University (1990–1992), and Harvard University from 1992, including directing the Reischauer Institute.

nodes.label: James L. Taylor
nodes.summary: James L. Taylor is a scholar in Buddhist studies and anthropology. He earned his PhD at Macquarie University in 1989 and served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Syed Nawab Ali
nodes.description: Persian-English translator who worked as a professor in Baroda
nodes.summary: Syed Nawab Ali (1878–1958) was a scholar of history and archaeology. In 1932, he was attested as Professor of Persian at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and as Principal of Bahauddin College.

nodes.label: Catherine Prueitt
nodes.summary: Catherine Prueitt works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She earned a BA from the University of Rochester and a PhD from Emory University under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton, later becoming an assistant professor at the University of British Columbia (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yoshio Nishiguchi
nodes.summary: Yoshio Nishiguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.

nodes.label: Ester Bianchi
nodes.summary: Ester Bianchi is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Alfredo Cadonna and Jean-Noël Robert, completing her PhD at Ca' Foscari University and EPHE. She held posts at the University of Perugia and Florence.

nodes.label: Karl Debreczeny
nodes.summary: Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology and art history. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Hung Wu and Jenny Purtle, and served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art.

nodes.label: Fabienne Jagou
nodes.summary: Fabienne Jagou works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She completed her PhD at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences under Pierre-Étienne Will (~1994–1999) and was appointed Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

nodes.label: Rob Linrothe
nodes.summary: Rob Linrothe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009) and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

nodes.label: Paul K. Nietupski
nodes.summary: Paul K. Nietupski works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University and held an attested post at John Carroll University in 2008.

nodes.label: Abraham Zablocki
nodes.summary: Abraham Zablocki specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: American Academy of Religion
variants: Tibetan and Himalayan Religions Group of the American Academy of Religion
Confucian Traditions Group of the American Academy of Religion
Buddhism Section of the American Academy of Religion

nodes.label: Bal Krishen Thapar
nodes.summary: Bal Krishen Thapar (1921–1995) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at the University of the Punjab, the Institute of Archaeology in Taxila under Mortimer Wheeler, and Heidelberg University. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981).

nodes.label: Richard King
nodes.summary: Richard King is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster. He held posts at the University of Stirling, Vanderbilt University (circa 2003–2011), and the University of Glasgow (circa 2011).

nodes.label: Klaus Karttunen
nodes.description: Finnish ethnologist, indologist and university teacher
nodes.summary: Klaus Karttunen works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki under Pentti Aalto, Asko Parpola, Henrik Zilliacus, Holger Thesleff, and Maarit Kaimio. He held appointments at the University of Helsinki, the Academy of Finland, and Freiburg.

nodes.label: Henrik Zilliacus
nodes.summary: Henrik Zilliacus worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki from circa 1926 to 1936, where he later held a post from circa 1944 to 1974 and taught Klaus Karttunen.

nodes.label: Franz Ferdinand Schwarz
nodes.summary: Franz Ferdinand Schwarz specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Graz (~1953–1958) and later served there as a professor (~1976–1999).

nodes.label: Yaroslav Vasilkov
nodes.summary: Yaroslav Vasilkov (born 1943) is an Indologist who studied at St. Petersburg University (circa 1961–1967). He held posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences around 1967 and at Saint Petersburg State University, including its Faculty of Philosophy.

nodes.label: Katsutoshi Ono
nodes.summary: Katsutoshi Ono (1905–1988) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned degrees at Kyoto University, held posts there (1933–1943), at Nara National Museum (1949–1967), and served as professor at Ryukoku University (~1964–1980).

nodes.label: Rita Langer
nodes.summary: Rita Langer is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg (supervised by Lambert Schmithausen) and studied at SOAS and PGIBS. She has held posts at the University of Bristol (attested 2009; 2026).

nodes.label: Alexander Piatigorsky
variants: アレクサンデル・モイシェイェヴィチ・ピアティゴルスキー
nodes.jawiki: アレクサンデル・ピアティゴルスキー
nodes.summary: Alexander Piatigorsky (1929–2009) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. After studying at Moscow State University, he worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957–1968) and later served as Professor of the Ancient History of South Asia at SOAS (1990–2001).

nodes.label: J. B. Disanayaka
nodes.summary: J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Colombo from circa 1982 to 2002 and was attested at SOAS University of London in 1996.

nodes.label: Robert Alan Goodding
nodes.summary: Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle, completing his degree by 2002.

nodes.label: Purushottam Mahadev Joshi
nodes.summary: Purushottam Mahadev Joshi was a historian and archaeologist. He worked at the University of Mumbai Library (~1935–1947) and later served as Reader in Medieval History at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1964–1974).

nodes.label: St. Xavier's College, Mumbai
variants: St. Xaviers College der Universität Bombay

nodes.label: Frederick M. Smith
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and religious studies, Smith was a student of Ludo Rocher. He held posts at the University of Iowa as Professor (attested 2006–2008) and later as Professor Emeritus (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Philip Lutgendorf
nodes.summary: Philip Lutgendorf is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1967–1987) and served on the faculty at the University of Iowa from 1985, as well as president of AIIS (2010–2018).

nodes.label: Albert Grünwedel
variants: アルベルト・グリュンヴェーデル
nodes.jawiki: アルベルト・グリュンヴェーデル
nodes.summary: Albert Grünwedel (1856–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Munich and served extensively at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, including as director (1904–1921).

nodes.label: Ethnological Museum of Berlin
variants: ベルリン民族学博物館

nodes.label: Ajahn Sumedho
nodes.summary: Ajahn Sumedho is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Washington, UC Berkeley (MA), and under Ajahn Chah. He founded and served as abbot of Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and Amaravati Buddhist Monastery (1984–2010).

nodes.label: Ajahn Chah
nodes.native: ชา สุภทฺโท

nodes.label: Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi
nodes.summary: Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi (1907–1966) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Harvard University under George David Birkhoff, he held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Fergusson College, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962).

nodes.label: Elliot M. Stern
nodes.summary: Elliot M. Stern is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania, earning PhD degrees dated 1988 and 1998.

nodes.id: I:Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences
nodes.label: Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences
variants: Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences
Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences at Stanford University

nodes.label: Hans Henrich Hock
nodes.summary: Hans Henrich Hock is a linguist and Indologist who completed graduate studies at Northwestern University and Yale University under Warren Crawford Cowgill. He held a post as Professor of Linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign from ~1967.

nodes.label: Rama Nath Sharma
nodes.summary: Rama Nath Sharma is an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Banaras Hindu, Allahabad, Agra, and Rochester, and under traditional teachers Raghunatha Sharma and Ramaprasada Tripathi, he held posts at Allahabad (1962–1966), Rochester (1971–1976), and Hawaiʻi (from 1976).

nodes.label: Michael C. Shapiro
nodes.summary: Michael C. Shapiro is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served on the faculty at the University of Washington as a professor from circa 1974 to 2017 and was named Professor Emeritus of Hindi around 2017.

nodes.label: Satya Vrat Shastri
nodes.image: Ramashish Acharya with Padma Bhushan Satya Vrat Shastri.jpg
nodes.description: Jnanpith Award recipient in Sanskrit. Indian academic
nodes.summary: Satya Vrat Shastri was an Indologist and linguist who earned a PhD at Banaras Hindu University. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Delhi (1970–1995) and Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya (~1989–1991).

nodes.label: M. D. Balasubrahmanyam
nodes.summary: M. D. Balasubrahmanyam specialized in Indology and linguistics. He completed his dissertation and later held an academic post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967).

nodes.label: Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld
nodes.summary: Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He later served as associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen from 1978 to 1986.

nodes.id: I:Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine
nodes.label: Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine
variants: The Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine in London
Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine

nodes.label: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
nodes.summary: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani studied at Samaldas Arts College, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, and under Muni Jinavijaya. A scholar in Indology and linguistics, he held posts at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, Gujarat University, and the L. D. Institute of Indology.

nodes.label: Fabrizia Baldissera
nodes.summary: Fabrizia Baldissera is an indologist who studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" (1969–2004). She held academic posts at the University of Florence (~1998) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".

nodes.label: Yun Ji
nodes.summary: Yun Ji specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ji earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University by 2006 and served as librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Shanshan Jia
nodes.summary: Shanshan Jia is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. Supervised by Harunaga Isaacson, she pursued doctoral studies at the University of Hamburg (attested 2015, 2026), where she was also a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Eun-su Cho
nodes.summary: Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed her PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. She taught at the University of Michigan until 2004, when she joined Seoul National University.

nodes.label: Georges-Jean Pinault
nodes.summary: Georges-Jean Pinault is a linguist and Indologist who studied at ENS, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE under Jean Haudry. He taught at Sorbonne Nouvelle and Clermont Auvergne before becoming a professor at EPHE in 1999.

nodes.label: Jason Protass
nodes.summary: Jason Protass specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick (attested 2015–2016) and held posts as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica.

nodes.label: Nathan Sivin
nodes.summary: Nathan Sivin (1931-2022) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the Defense Language Institute, MIT, Kyoto University, and Harvard. He held faculty posts at MIT (1966-1977) and the University of Pennsylvania (1977-2006).

nodes.label: Joseph Needham
nodes.summary: Joseph Needham worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. Educated at Oundle School, Gonville and Caius College, and Cambridge, he held posts at Cambridge (ca. 1924–1966), Gonville and Caius College (1963), and the Needham Research Institute (ca. 1976–1990).

nodes.label: Sean D. Gaffney
nodes.summary: Sean D. Gaffney specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski (attested 2003) and also held a post there (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Bulcsu Siklós
nodes.summary: Bulcsu Siklós specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles Roskelly Bawden, later holding a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Yang-Gyu An
nodes.summary: Yang-Gyu An is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Hojin and earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1998 under Richard Gombrich.

nodes.label: Chikafumi Watanabe
nodes.summary: Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at the University of British Columbia and a PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, also studying under Karin Preisendanz, Ashok Narhar Aklujkar, and others.

nodes.label: Catherine Ludvik
nodes.summary: Catherine Ludvik specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto (by 2001) under David B. Waterhouse, and held posts at Hanazono University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

nodes.label: Akio Donohashi
nodes.summary: Akio Donohashi specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1967 to 1974 and served as a professor at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991.

nodes.id: I:Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
nodes.label: Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
variants: Forschungsstelle »Felsbilder und Inschriften am Karakorum Highway« der Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften
Forschungsstelle „Felsbilder und Inschriften am Karakorum Highway“ an der Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften
Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, University of Heidelberg

nodes.label: University of Cologne
variants: Indological Institute at the University of Cologne
Centre for Advanced Study of Humanities, University of Cologne

nodes.label: Robert E. Morrell
nodes.summary: Robert E. Morrell is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough. He held an academic post at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

nodes.label: Washington University in St. Louis
variants: Washington University in St. Louis Missouri

nodes.label: James W. Heisig
nodes.jawiki: ジェームズ・ハイジック
nodes.summary: James W. Heisig is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. After earning his PhD from Cambridge, he held long-term posts at Nanzan University and the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (circa 1978–2020).

nodes.label: Barbra R. Clayton
nodes.summary: Barbra R. Clayton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her Ph.D. at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Katherine K. Young
nodes.summary: Katherine K. Young (born 1944) specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned an M.A. at the University of Chicago and a Ph.D. at McGill University (~1970–1978), where she later served as Professor (~1978–2015).

nodes.label: Damien Keown
nodes.summary: Damien Keown (born 1951) is a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford, and served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, University of London, beginning in 1995.

nodes.label: Horst Brinkhaus
nodes.summary: Horst Brinkhaus is an Indologist who held a post at the University of Münster (attested 1978) and later served at Kiel University (~1995–2011).

nodes.label: Sarah Horton
nodes.summary: Sarah Horton works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Gopinath Kaviraj
nodes.summary: Gopinath Kaviraj (1887–1976) studied at Maharaja's College, Jaipur, and Allahabad University under Arthur Venis, Madhusudan Ojha, and Shashadhar Tarkachudamani. He served at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University as librarian (1914–1920), Principal (1923–1937), and Head of Yoga-Tantra (1964–1969).

nodes.label: Klaus-Dieter Mathes
nodes.summary: Klaus-Dieter Mathes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Klaus Sagaster, Michael Hahn at the University of Marburg, and Tibetan masters, habilitating at Hamburg. He held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, Hamburg, and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Melvyn C. Goldstein
nodes.summary: Melvyn C. Goldstein works in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Washington, and was a professor in the Department of Anthropology at Case Western Reserve University from 1968 to 2002.

nodes.id: I:Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School
nodes.label: Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School
Jay M. Bernstein
nodes.summary: Jay M. Bernstein is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1971–1975). He held academic posts at the University of Essex (~1978–1997), Vanderbilt University (~1997–2001), and The New School (~2001).

nodes.label: The New School
variants: The New School for Social Research, New York
The New School for Social Research

nodes.label: Osmund Bopearachchi
nodes.summary: Osmund Bopearachchi is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, CNRS, Panthéon-Sorbonne, and Paris-Sorbonne under Paul Bernard and Jean-Marie Dentzer, later holding posts at CNRS and UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Deborah Carlson
nodes.summary: Deborah Carlson is a history and archaeology scholar who held posts at Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology (both attested 2015).

nodes.label: Paul Bernard
nodes.summary: Paul Bernard (1929–2015) was a historian and archaeologist of Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and Sorbonne, he directed the DAFA (1965–1980) and held posts at the CNRS and EPHE (1981).

nodes.label: Doris Meth Srinivasan
nodes.summary: Doris Meth Srinivasan is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who earned a BA at Hunter College and a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. She curated at the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art (~1987–1993) and is a Research Scholar at Stony Brook University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Axel Michaels
nodes.summary: Axel Michaels works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Laxmi Nath Srestha, earned degrees at Hamburg and Kiel, and held professorships at the University of Bern (1992–1996) and Heidelberg University from 1996.

nodes.label: Hans Hartog
nodes.summary: Hans Hartog is an Indologist who studied at Tübingen, Kirchliche Hochschule Wuppertal/Bethel, Munich, and Marburg. He completed his PhD under Friedrich Heiler at Marburg in 1939, having also studied under Hanns Oertel, Walther Wüst, and others.

nodes.label: Friedrich Heiler
nodes.summary: Friedrich Heiler was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Munich (~1912–1917). He taught at the University of Munich (1918) and University of Marburg (1920), and directed the Religionskundliche Sammlung (~1927–1962).

nodes.label: Walther Wüst
nodes.description: Rector of the University of Munich and SS member (1901-1993)
nodes.summary: Walther Wüst specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich (1920–1923), where he became an extraordinary professor (1932) and Dean of the Philosophical Faculty (1935–1945), and held posts with the Ahnenerbe (1936) and Deutsche Akademie (1943).

nodes.label: Jakob Wilhelm Hauer
nodes.image: Bundesarchiv Bild 183-2004-0413-501, Prof. Jakob Wilhelm Hauer.jpg
nodes.summary: Jakob Wilhelm Hauer (1881–1962) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Oxford and the University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He held professorships at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and the University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

nodes.label: Kurt Huber
nodes.description: German folk song researcher, professor at the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität (LMU) in Munich, member of the White Rose (1893-1943)
nodes.summary: Kurt Huber was a philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Munich (~1913–1917). He went on to serve on the faculty at the University of Munich as an außerordentlicher Professor in 1926 and full professor in 1938.

nodes.label: Erich Rudolf Jaensch
nodes.summary: Erich Rudolf Jaensch was a philosopher who studied at Breslau, Göttingen (PhD 1905–1909), and Strasbourg. He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and as ordinary professor at the University of Marburg from 1913.

nodes.label: Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen
nodes.summary: Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who studied at the University of Munich. He held a professorship at the University of Bonn (1934), was at Munich (1936–1941), and held a chair at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (c. 1947–1969).

nodes.label: Wolfgang Schultz
nodes.description: German philosopher, historian and art historian (1881-1936)
nodes.summary: Wolfgang Schultz earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (~1900–1904). He worked at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and served as Professor and Chair of Philosophy at the University of Munich in 1934.

nodes.label: Ferdinand Sommer
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Sommer was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Rudolf Thurneysen at Freiburg. He completed his Habilitation at Leipzig and held professorships at Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and Munich (1926–1951).

nodes.label: Giovanni Vacca
nodes.summary: Giovanni Vacca was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology who earned his doctorate at the University of Genoa and studied at the University of Florence. He lectured at Florence and held the chair for History and Geography of East Asia at Sapienza University.

nodes.label: Sakkottai Krishnaswamy Aiyangar
nodes.summary: Sakkottai Krishnaswamy Aiyangar studied at the University of Madras (graduating in history by 1897, M.A. circa 1897-1899). He was a lecturer at Bangalore University (1899-1909) and held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914-1929).

nodes.label: John Kieschnick
nodes.summary: John Kieschnick is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at the University of Bristol (~2005–2011) before joining Stanford University (~2011) as the Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Professor of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Hellmuth Hecker
nodes.summary: Hellmuth Hecker was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (1942–1948, PhD) and under Paul Debes in 1945, later serving as a Referent at the University of Hamburg from ~1952 to 1988.

nodes.label: Rudrapatna Shamasastry
nodes.summary: Rudrapatna Shamasastry was an Indologist who completed degrees at the University of Madras, Government Sanskrit College, Mysore, Oriental University, and University of Calcutta. He was Principal at Sri Chamarajendra Samskrita Maha Patashala (1912–1918) and Curator at Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1918–1929).

nodes.label: Indologica Taurinensia
variants: Indologica Taurinensia, The Journal of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies

nodes.label: Richard A. Rosengarten
nodes.summary: Richard A. Rosengarten is a religious studies scholar at the University of Chicago, where he served as Dean (attested 2008–2012) and as Associate Professor of Religion and Literature, including in the College (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Daniel Dubuisson
nodes.summary: Daniel Dubuisson works in religious studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. Around 1993, he served as a director of research at CNRS and the University of Lille, and held a post at University Lille-III.

nodes.label: Elaine Fisher
nodes.summary: Elaine Fisher specializes in Indology and religious studies. She was a doctoral student at Columbia University (attested 2010) and is attested as a faculty member at Stanford University in 2026.

nodes.label: Jonathan Z. Smith
variants: ジョナサン・Z・スミス
nodes.summary: Jonathan Z. Smith was a religious studies scholar who studied at Haverford College, Yale University, and Yale Divinity School. He held posts at Dartmouth and UC Santa Barbara before serving as Dean of the College at the University of Chicago (1977–1982).

nodes.label: Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya is an Indologist who studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya. He held a position as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Meinrad Scheller
nodes.summary: Meinrad Scheller, a linguist and Indologist, studied under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch at the University of Zurich and the University of Paris. He held professorships at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (1975).

nodes.label: Gregory Max Seton
nodes.summary: Gregory Max Seton specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara, and Oxford (Wolfson College), completing doctoral supervision under Vesna A. Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

nodes.label: Martin Joachim Kümmel
nodes.summary: Martin Joachim Kümmel is an Indologist and linguist who completed his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Freiburg. He served as an assistant at Freiburg (~1999–2008) and was appointed chairholder at the University of Jena in 2013.

nodes.label: Helmut Rix
nodes.summary: Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg (PhD 1950), and Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, Augustana-Hochschule Neuendettelsau, the University of Regensburg (1966), and served as professor at the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

nodes.label: Jinzhang Peng
nodes.summary: Jinzhang Peng (1937–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held a post at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) before serving as a researcher and professor at the Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017).

nodes.label: Chih-mien Adrian Tseng
nodes.summary: Chih-mien Adrian Tseng is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at McMaster University under James A. Benn, also advised by Nobuyoshi Yamabe and Canshan Cheng. Tseng has held faculty posts at Fo Guang University.

nodes.label: Fo Guang University
variants: 佛光人文社會學院宗教學系

nodes.label: Peter Moran
nodes.summary: Peter Moran is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tufts University and earned his PhD at the University of Washington under doctoral supervisor Charles F. Keyes, as well as with several traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Thomas Watters
nodes.description: British diplomat in China and Korea, sinologist
nodes.summary: Thomas Watters was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at Queen's University Belfast, Queen's University of Ireland (BA ~1857–1861), and Queen's University at Kingston (BA completed by 1861).

nodes.label: Willem van der Molen
nodes.summary: Willem van der Molen worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1970–1983) and later held posts at Leiden University (~1979–2017) and the University of Indonesia.

nodes.label: Muhammad Ashraf Khan
nodes.summary: Archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar Muhammad Ashraf Khan served as Deputy Director of the Taxila Museum, Director of the Department of Archaeology and Museums in Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Zarawar Khan
nodes.summary: Zarawar Khan works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed an MA and PhD in archaeology at the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).

nodes.label: Jessie Pons
nodes.summary: Jessie Pons is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She completed her doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University in 2011 and served as Junior Professor in South Asian History of Religion at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Max Walleser
nodes.summary: Max Walleser worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nuremberg, and served at Heidelberg University as Privatdozent in 1911 and extraordinary professor of Indian philology from 1918 to 1936.

nodes.label: Michael Comans
nodes.summary: Michael Comans specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University, later serving as a faculty member at the University of Sydney (circa 1989–2002).

nodes.label: Swami Dayananda Saraswati
nodes.description: Hindu monk and founder of Arsha Vidya Gurukulam (1930-2015)
nodes.summary: Swami Dayananda Saraswati (1930–2015) was a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Sri Jayachamarajendra Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and under teachers including Chinmayananda Saraswati, Swami Pranavananda, Swami Tarananda Giri, Swami Tapovan Maharaj, Veeraraghavachariar, and P. S. Subramania Iyer.

nodes.label: Rahul Peter Das
nodes.description: German professor of South Asian studies (born 1954)
nodes.summary: Rahul Peter Das (born 1954), an Indologist and linguist, studied at Calcutta, Cologne, and Hamburg under Klaus Ludwig Janert and Albrecht Wezler. He taught and researched at Hamburg, Bonn, and Groningen before becoming Professor at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1994–2020).

nodes.label: Nagin J. Shah
nodes.summary: Nagin J. Shah is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. Succeeding Dalsukh Malvania, he served as Acting Director of the L. D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968).

nodes.label: Ernest John Henry Mackay
nodes.summary: Ernest John Henry Mackay was a scholar of archaeology and Indology who earned his BA, MA, and DLitt at the University of Bristol. He served as Custodian of Antiquities for the Government of Palestine from 1919 to 1922.

nodes.label: Rakhal Das Banerji
nodes.summary: Rakhal Das Banerji (1885–1930) was an Indologist and historian educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He served as an officer with the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1926) and held a professorship at Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).

nodes.label: Nathaniel Grove
nodes.summary: Nathaniel Grove works in Tibetology and computational studies. He held posts at the University of Virginia, where he was attested in 2006 and as a Research Associate in 2026.

nodes.label: Stephen Wootton Bushell
nodes.summary: Stephen Wootton Bushell was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Guy's Hospital Medical School and the University of London (MD), serving as house surgeon at Guy's Hospital (1866) and resident medical officer at Bethlem Royal Hospital (1867).

nodes.label: Alexander Rogers
nodes.summary: Alexander Rogers was an Indologist and historian who studied at the East India Company College from approximately 1843 to 1845. He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1845 to 1879.

nodes.label: Henry Beveridge
nodes.description: British linguist and Indian Civil Service officer
nodes.summary: Henry Beveridge was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Glasgow (~1853–1857) and Queen's University Belfast (1856). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1857–1893) and was President of The Asiatic Society (1890–1891).

nodes.label: Edgar Howard Sturtevant
variants: エドガー・H・スターティヴァント
エドガー・ハワード・スターティヴァント
nodes.jawiki: エドガー・ハワード・スターティヴァント
nodes.summary: Edgar Howard Sturtevant was a linguist working in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Illinois College and Indiana University Bloomington, he held academic posts at Columbia University (~1908–1920) and Yale University (~1923–1943).

nodes.label: Joanna Jurewicz
nodes.summary: Joanna Jurewicz is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied under Maria Krzysztof Byrski. She holds a professorship at the University of Warsaw (attested 2006, 2026).

nodes.label: University of Western Australia
variants: 西オーストラリア大学

nodes.label: Peterhouse, Cambridge
variants: Peterhouse College of the University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Klaus Ludwig Janert
nodes.description: born:1922|died:1994|; Janert, Klaus Ludwig, 1922-1994; Janert, Klaus L.
nodes.summary: Klaus Ludwig Janert specialized in Indology. He studied at Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg, Goethe University Frankfurt under Paul Thieme, and the University of Tübingen. He later held posts at the University of Göttingen and the University of Cologne.

nodes.label: Christophe Vielle
nodes.summary: Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who held a professorship at KU Leuven (attested 2009–2013) and an associate membership at Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Robert Deliège
nodes.summary: Robert Deliège (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford (~1978–1982). He held academic posts at the University of Kerala, Université catholique de Louvain (~1989), and KU Leuven (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Jacques Scheuer
nodes.summary: Jacques Scheuer (1942–2021) was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who studied under Madeleine Biardeau and attended Sorbonne Nouvelle and Université catholique de Louvain. He held academic posts at Université catholique de Louvain (~1978–2007), Centre Sèvres, and KU Leuven (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Utz Podzeit
nodes.image: Venia Legendi 1997- Dr. Utz Podzeit mit Mechthild.jpg
nodes.summary: Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna, where he was appointed Universitätsdozent in 1969. He also undertook a research stay at the University of Madras from 1972 to 1974.

nodes.label: Roderick M. Chisholm
nodes.summary: Philosopher Roderick M. Chisholm studied at Brown and Harvard. He held posts at the Barnes Foundation (~1946), Brown University (~1947–1987), and University of Graz (1974), alongside serving as president of the Metaphysical Society of America (1973).

nodes.label: Philip L. Quinn
nodes.summary: Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher who studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He served on the faculty at Brown University (~1971–1985) and as John A. O'Brien Professor of Philosophy at the University of Notre Dame from 1985.

nodes.label: Ernest Sosa
nodes.summary: Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He served as professor at Brown University starting in 1964 and at Rutgers University from 1998 to 2006.

nodes.label: Antoine Cabaton
nodes.summary: Antoine Cabaton worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École du Louvre and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1895–1898), and held a post at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1895).

nodes.label: Karunesh Shukla
nodes.summary: Karunesh Shukla is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1991, he served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University.

nodes.label: Eduard Müller-Hess
nodes.summary: Eduard Müller-Hess was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He completed his Inauguraldissertation at the University of Leipzig in 1874 and served as a professor at the University of Bern (attested 1897-1898).

nodes.label: Mabel Bode
nodes.summary: Mabel Bode (1864–1922) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bern and studied under T. W. Rhys Davids and Sylvain Lévi. She taught at University College London (1909–1917) and SOAS.

nodes.label: Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff
nodes.jawiki: ウルリヒ・フォン・ヴィラモーヴィッツ＝メレンドルフ
nodes.summary: Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Schulpforta, Bonn, and Berlin under Otto Jahn, Moriz Haupt, and others. He held professorial posts at Greifswald (1876–1883), Göttingen (1883–1897), and Berlin (1897–1921).

nodes.label: David Ludden
nodes.summary: David Ludden is an Indologist and historian. Educated at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania, he taught at the University of Virginia, the University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), and New York University, where he became Professor of Political Economy and Globalization in 2007.

nodes.label: Allison Busch
nodes.summary: Allison Busch was an Indologist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. She held an appointment as Associate Professor of Hindi Literature at Columbia University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: James B. Apple
nodes.summary: James B. Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his graduate education, including a PhD, at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where his doctoral supervisor was John D. Dunne.

nodes.label: Henepola Gunaratana
nodes.summary: Henepola Gunaratana works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Vidyasekhara Pirivena, Buddhist Missionary College, Kelaniya, and American University (PhD ~1975–1980), he served as principal at Kuala Lumpur's Buddhist Institute (~1958–1968) and held posts at American, Georgetown, Bucknell, and Maryland.

nodes.label: Geshe Lobsang Tenzin Negi
variants: Lobsang Tenzin Negi (legal name Satya Dev Negi)

nodes.label: Glenn H. Mullin
nodes.image: Visit of Telo Tulku to Roerich House, U.B. (3861963599).jpg
nodes.summary: Glenn H. Mullin is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Geshe Rabten. He founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.

nodes.label: Luciano Petech
nodes.summary: Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He taught at Allahabad (1938–1946) and held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984).

nodes.label: Reb Anderson
nodes.summary: Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker, whom he succeeded. He served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from ~1986 to 1995.

nodes.label: Elena De Rossi Filibeck
nodes.summary: Elena De Rossi Filibeck specializes in Tibetology. She studied East Asian history under Luciano Petech at Sapienza University of Rome (~1966–1971), where she later became an associate professor in 1980.

nodes.label: Stefan M. Maul
nodes.summary: Stefan M. Maul (born 1958) is an Assyriologist and historian who studied at Göttingen and Freie Universität Berlin. He held posts at FU Berlin, became Ordinarius at Heidelberg University in 1995, and joined the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2004.

nodes.label: Søren Sørensen
nodes.summary: Søren Sørensen (1848–1902) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Herlufsholm School (1876–1878) and the University of Copenhagen (~1887–1902).

nodes.label: Vilhelm Thomsen
variants: ヴィルヘルム・トムセン
ヴィルヘルム・ルズヴィ・ペーター・トムセン
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・トムセン
nodes.summary: Vilhelm Thomsen was a linguist and Central Asian studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Copenhagen (1859–1869). He served there as Privatdozent (1869), associate professor (1875), and Professor (1887–1913), later becoming President of the Royal Danish Academy (1909).

nodes.label: Karl Verner
variants: カール・アドルフ・ヴェルナー
nodes.summary: Karl Verner was a linguist who studied at Aarhus Katedralskole, the University of Copenhagen, and under August Leskien. He worked as a librarian at Halle-Wittenberg (~1876–1883) and became a lecturer in Slavic studies at Copenhagen in 1882.

nodes.label: Rosina Pastore
nodes.summary: Rosina Pastore is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne, supervised by Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere, and has held research posts at Lausanne and Ghent University.

nodes.label: Marianne Winder
nodes.summary: Marianne Winder worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of London, University of Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove. She held posts at Nottingham, the Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies, and the Wellcome Institute.

nodes.label: Nigel Allan
nodes.summary: Nigel Allan specializes in history and archaeology. He succeeded Marianne Winder as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine (attested 1993).

nodes.label: Charles Edmund Godakumbura
nodes.summary: Charles Edmund Godakumbura was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned multiple degrees from the University of London. He taught at SOAS, served as Commissioner of Archaeology for the Archaeological Survey of India (1956–1967), and presided over the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka.

nodes.label: Union Theological Seminary
variants: Union Theological Seminary in New York City
Union Theological Seminary in the City of New York
Union Theological Seminary in New York
Union Theological Seminary, New York City

nodes.label: Anne MacDonald
nodes.summary: Anne MacDonald is an indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Narhar Aklujkar, Geshe Tashi Namgyal, Lambert Schmithausen, and Karin Preisendanz. She has held posts at the University of Vienna and Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Bhagwan Dash
nodes.summary: Dash specialized in Indology and Tibetology, studying at Gujarat Ayurved University, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi, where he completed an MA and PhD. He served as a bibliographer and cataloguer at the Library of Congress.

nodes.label: Vaibhav Singh
nodes.summary: Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of Indology and history who earned his PhD from the University of Reading in 2017 and held a post there.

nodes.label: Fiona Ross
nodes.description: British type designer, academic and linguist
nodes.summary: Fiona Ross works in Indology and other fields. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1980–1988) and held posts at Tiro Typeworks and the University of Reading (~2003).

nodes.label: Richard Carnac Temple
nodes.summary: Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Harrow and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, he served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps, edited the Indian Antiquary (~1884–1921), and was vice-president of the Hakluyt Society.

nodes.label: Himanshu Prabha Ray
nodes.summary: Himanshu Prabha Ray works in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, having studied at Panjab University, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. She was Associate Professor at JNU (~1980–2012) and Chairperson of the National Monuments Authority (~2012–2015).

nodes.label: Kuvempu University
variants: Centre for the Study of Local Cultures, Kuvempu University

nodes.label: Geoff Childs
nodes.summary: Geoff Childs is an anthropologist of Tibet and historian who earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, studying under Tsetan Chonjore. He was an Andrew Mellon Postdoctoral Fellow at ANU and taught anthropology at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 2003–2005).

nodes.label: Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute
variants: 財団法人西蔵大蔵経研究会

nodes.label: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé
nodes.summary: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Leiden University in 1928 under J. J. L. Duyvendak, whom he later succeeded, serving as a lecturer in Chinese from 1946 and as professor from 1956 to 1975.

nodes.label: Robert H. Brower
nodes.description: Professor of far east language and literature (1923–1988)
nodes.summary: Robert H. Brower (1923–1988) was a Japanologist who studied at Harvard and Michigan. He held posts at Minnesota, Stanford, and the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, and chaired Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).

nodes.label: Arthur F. Wright
nodes.summary: Arthur F. Wright worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard under John King Fairbank. He taught at Stanford University from 1947 and became Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale in 1959.

nodes.label: University of Missouri
variants: University of the State of Missouri

nodes.label: Steven Lukes
nodes.jawiki: スティーヴン・ルークス
nodes.summary: Steven Lukes is a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at Oxford under E. E. Evans-Pritchard. He held faculty posts at Balliol College, Oxford, the University of Florence, European University Institute, LSE, and New York University.

nodes.id: I:Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh
nodes.label: Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh
variants: Department of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Andhra Pradesh
Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums

nodes.label: Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana
nodes.summary: Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana studied at Ayurveda College, Coimbatore, and the University of Amsterdam. He held research and visiting faculty posts at the Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions, Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and the University of Toyama.

nodes.label: Amala Institute of Medical Sciences
variants: Amala Cancer Hospital and Research Center

nodes.id: I:Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions
nodes.label: Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions
variants: Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions

nodes.label: Sebastian Pole
nodes.summary: Sebastian Pole works in Indology and related fields. He completed his studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.

nodes.label: Robert E. Svoboda
nodes.summary: Robert E. Svoboda (born 1953) is an Indology and religious studies specialist. He studied at the University of Oklahoma and mentored under Aghori Vimalananda (~1975–1983), holding adjunct appointments at Bastyr University, The Ayurvedic Institute, and the Institute for Religion and Health.

nodes.label: Soon-il Hwang
nodes.summary: Soon-il Hwang specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed an MA under Seung-won Seo at Dongguk University, earned a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, and later held a post at Dongguk University.

nodes.label: Andrew Amstutz
nodes.summary: Andrew Amstutz works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was a member at the Institute for Advanced Study in 2021 and served as Assistant Professor of History at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock as attested in 2022.

nodes.id: I:University of Arkansas at Little Rock
nodes.label: University of Arkansas at Little Rock
variants: University of Arkansas at Little Rock

nodes.label: Fawad Khan
nodes.summary: Fawad Khan is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University. In 2022, he was attested as Assistant Curator at the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Directorate of Archaeology and Museums.

nodes.id: I:Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

variants: Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province of Pakistan
Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Govt. of NWFP

nodes.label: Kirby Flower Smith
nodes.description: American classical philologist and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Kirby Flower Smith was an indology scholar who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Gildersleeve, Warren, and Bloomfield. He was a professor at Johns Hopkins (circa 1889-1918) and directed the American Academy in Rome (1914-1915).

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Anālayo
nodes.description: German Buddhist monk, scholar, and meditation teacher (born 1962)
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, Anālayo completed a PhD at Ceylon and Habilitation at Marburg. His academic career includes positions at Hamburg, Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy, and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Wataru Ryose
nodes.summary: Wataru Ryose specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under the doctoral supervision of Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances Wilson.

nodes.label: Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé
variants: Kong sprul Blo gros mtha’ yas
ジャムグン・コントゥル・ロドゥ・タイェ
nodes.jawiki: ジャムグン・コントゥル・ロドゥ・タイェ
nodes.summary: Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Tekchok Dorje, Gyurme Thutop Namgyal, and Tai Situ Pema Nyinje Wangpo, and also taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

nodes.label: David Higgins
nodes.summary: David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held an appointment at the University of Vienna (attested 2015) and serves as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala
nodes.summary: Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala (1884–1956) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He taught Prabodh Chandra Bagchi and Sukumar Sen, served at Deccan College (~1939–1942), and was Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (~1954–1956).

nodes.label: Sukumar Sen
nodes.image: Sukumar Sen linguist 2020 cover of India cr.jpg
nodes.summary: Sukumar Sen (1900–1992) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta under Suniti Kumar Chatterji and Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala. At Calcutta, he served as lecturer (1930) and later Khaira Professor (1954).

nodes.label: David Kopf
nodes.summary: David Kopf (1930–2023) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1960–1965) and served on the faculty at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1997.

nodes.label: Willard Van Orman Quine
variants: ウィラード・クワイン
ウィラード・ヴァン・オーマン・クワイン
nodes.image: Willard Van Orman Quine on Bluenose II in Halifax NS harbor 1980.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ウィラード・ヴァン・オーマン・クワイン
nodes.summary: Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher who studied at Oberlin College (1926–1930) and Harvard University (1930–1931). He held an Assistant Professorship at Harvard (1940–1978) and visiting posts at Oxford (~1953–1954) and Wesleyan University (1964–1965).

nodes.label: P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri
nodes.summary: P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bishop Heber College, IASE, and the University of Madras. He served as Principal of Rajah's College, Thiruvaiyaru, and Head of Sanskrit at Annamalai University (1942–1947).

nodes.label: Charles Cutler Torrey
nodes.summary: Charles Cutler Torrey worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and linguistics, having studied under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary from 1892 to 1900 and served as a professor at Yale University from 1900 to 1932.

National Museum of Denmark's Department of Research

nodes.label: Alexander W. Macdonald
nodes.summary: Alexander W. Macdonald worked in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Musée de l'Homme (circa 1958–1978) and as a professor at Paris Nanterre University (circa 1978–1991).

nodes.label: Rasmus Rask
variants: ラスムス・クリスチャン・ラスク
nodes.summary: Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen, where he later held posts as librarian and professor of literary history (1825) and Eastern languages (1831).

nodes.label: Stella Kramrisch
nodes.summary: Stella Kramrisch was an Indologist and art historian who completed her doctorate at the University of Vienna (~1914–1919) under Max Dvořák and Josef Strzygowski. She held posts at Visva-Bharati (1922–1950), Calcutta (1924–1950), and Pennsylvania (1950–1993).

nodes.label: Sarasi Kumar Saraswati
nodes.summary: Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (b. 1914) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. A student of Jitendra Nath Banerjea, he served as librarian at The Asiatic Society in 1943 and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: H. G. Narahari
nodes.summary: H. G. Narahari specialized in Indology. He studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras under Chittenjoor Kunhan Raja, and held research posts at Madras and the Adyar Library and Research Centre (both attested 1944).

nodes.label: Charles Philip Brown
nodes.summary: Charles Philip Brown (1798–1884) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Haileybury/East India Company College (~1814–1817) and under traditional teachers Kodandarama Panthulu, Venkatasivasastri Tippabhatla, and Advaitabrahmasastri Vatthyam. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1854) and was Professor of Telugu at the University of London (~1865–1879).

nodes.label: Frank F. Conlon
nodes.summary: Frank F. Conlon is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Minnesota (1969) and served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Washington (~1972–2010).

nodes.label: Daniel Clarke Waugh
nodes.summary: Daniel Clarke Waugh works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees from Yale and Harvard before joining the faculty at the University of Washington in 1972.

nodes.label: Katia Buffetrille
nodes.summary: Katia Buffetrille (born 1948) is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her PhD at Paris Nanterre University under Alexander W. Macdonald. She has held posts at EPHE, CRCAO, and as an editor for EMSCAT.

nodes.label: Baliram Shukla
nodes.summary: Baliram Shukla is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University, including Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and Professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Shunryu Suzuki
nodes.image: Shunryu Suzuki at Zen Mountain Center (cropped).png
nodes.summary: Shunryu Suzuki was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji, and under teachers including Gyokujun So-on. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsouin, and Sokoji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center.

nodes.label: Richard Baker
variants: ゼンテツ・リチャード・ベーカー
nodes.summary: Richard Baker (1936–) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard and UC Berkeley, and under Shunryu Suzuki. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center (1962), serving as its abbot (1971–1984), and founded Dharma Sangha.

nodes.label: Huston Smith
nodes.summary: Huston Smith (1919–2016) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1940–1945). He taught at MIT (1958–1973), Syracuse University (1973–1983), and UC Berkeley (~1990–1999).

nodes.label: Tassajara Zen Mountain Center
variants: タサハラ禅マウンテンセンター（禅心寺）

nodes.label: San Francisco Zen Center
variants: サンフランシスコ禅センター

nodes.label: Medawachchiye Dhammajothi
nodes.summary: Medawachchiye Dhammajothi works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having earned an MA at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and a PhD at Nanjing University. Publications from 2008 attest his teaching posts at Colombo, Buddhist and Pali University, and PGIPBS.

nodes.label: Srisa Chandra Vasu
nodes.description: Indian judge, writer, and scholar in Sanskrit
nodes.summary: Srisa Chandra Vasu (1861–1918) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Rang Mahal Mission High School and Government College University, Lahore (BA, ~1877–1881), worked as a Vakil at Allahabad High Court (~1888–1893), and was a Fellow at the University of Allahabad.

nodes.label: Johanna Narten
nodes.description: Professor of Indo-European and Indo-Iranian Linguistics (1930-2019)
nodes.summary: Johanna Narten worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Saarland University under Ernst Zinn and completed her PhD and habilitation under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where she was an Assistentin (1973-1977).

nodes.label: Jadunath Sarkar
nodes.summary: Jadunath Sarkar (1870–1958) was a historian educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at Patna College (1899–1926) and Ravenshaw University, and served as dean of history at Banaras Hindu University (1917–1919) and vice-chancellor of Calcutta University (1926–1928).

nodes.label: George V. Bobrinskoy
nodes.summary: George V. Bobrinskoy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lutheran Theological Seminary and under Franklin Edgerton at Yale. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as linguistics department chair from 1951 to 1966.

nodes.label: Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy
nodes.summary: Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy (1877–1947) studied at Wycliffe College and UCL. An Indologist, art historian, and philosopher, he directed the Geological Survey of Ceylon (c. 1903–1906) and served as a curator and fellow at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

nodes.label: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
variants: Museum of Fine Arts in Boston

nodes.label: Peter Masefield
nodes.summary: Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his studies under supervisors L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

nodes.label: Karel Werner
nodes.summary: Karel Werner was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Masaryk University and Palacký University under Robert Konečný, Jaroslav Průšek, and Vincenc Lesný. He held posts at Palacký, Cambridge, Durham University (1969–1990), Masaryk University, and SOAS.

nodes.label: Ninian Smart
nodes.summary: Ninian Smart (1927–2001) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher who studied at Oxford and Yale. He served as Foundation Professor of Religious Studies at Lancaster University (1967–1982) and as professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara (1976–1998).

nodes.label: Denis Sinor
nodes.summary: Denis Sinor was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, linguist, and historian. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at the University of Cambridge, where he later worked (1948–1962) before serving as a director at Indiana University Bloomington (1962–1986).

nodes.label: Griffith University
variants: グリフィス大学現代アジア研究所

nodes.label: S. N. Balagangadhara
nodes.summary: S. N. Balagangadhara works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at National College, Bangalore, and earned his doctorate at Ghent University (1977–1991) under Etienne Vermeersch. He was a director at Ghent University (~1991–2017) and co-chair at the American Academy of Religion (2004–2007).

nodes.label: Kazu Uehara
nodes.summary: Kazu Uehara (1924–2017) was an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who completed studies at Kyushu University by 1992. His career included serving as a lecturer at the University of Miyazaki and as professor emeritus at Seijo University (c. 1968–1995).

nodes.label: Yasuro Abe
nodes.summary: Yasuro Abe is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Wako and Otani universities. He held academic posts at Osaka, Otemae, and Ryukoku universities, and was a professor and professor emeritus at Nagoya University.

nodes.label: Masahiro Asada
nodes.summary: Masahiro Asada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1964–1974) and subsequently served there as an assistant professor (~1982–1992).

nodes.label: Akio Tatsuguchi
nodes.summary: Akio Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Ryukoku University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1987) and professor emeritus (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Otemae University
variants: 大手前女子大学文学部

nodes.id: I:Society for the History of Buddhism
nodes.label: Society for the History of Buddhism
Jacqueline I. Stone
nodes.summary: Jacqueline I. Stone is a scholar of Buddhist and Japanese studies who studied at SFSU and UCLA under William R. LaFleur. She served as Professor at Princeton University (1990–2019) and holds an affiliation with Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kuroda Institute
variants: Kuroda Institute for the Study of Buddhism and Human Values

nodes.label: Nanjing Normal University
variants: Nanjing Normal University, Research Center for the Nanjing Massacre

nodes.label: Qingzhi Zhu
nodes.summary: Qingzhi Zhu is a scholar in linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who has held professorial posts at Peking University (attested 2004) and the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Jinchuan Wan
nodes.summary: Jinchuan Wan specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, holding posts as a professor at both National Central University and Fo Guang University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Christoph Harbsmeier
nodes.description: German professor of Chinese linguistics and syntax
nodes.summary: Christoph Harbsmeier (born 1946) specializes in Sinology and linguistics, having studied at Merton College, Oxford, and the University of Copenhagen (Ph.D.). He held posts at Universiti Sains Malaysia and the University of Oslo, and advisory professorships at Peking, Fudan, and Shanghai Normal Universities.

nodes.label: Shu-Fen Chen
nodes.summary: Shu-Fen Chen works in linguistics and Indology. She studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien and completed doctoral work under Hans Henrich Hock, later holding a professorship at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Ryan Richard Overbey
nodes.summary: Ryan Richard Overbey specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Brown University (-2001) and Harvard University (-2010), later holding posts at UC Berkeley (2013–2015), Wesleyan University (attested 2016), Holy Cross, and Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Todd Thornton Lewis
nodes.summary: Todd Thornton Lewis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology who studied at Columbia University. He has held academic appointments at the College of the Holy Cross, including a distinguished professorship (attested 1996, 2016–2017).

nodes.label: Lothar Ledderose
nodes.summary: A scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history, Lothar Ledderose studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, Tokyo, Princeton, Harvard, and Cologne. He served as Professor at Heidelberg University (~1976–2010) and was President of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1978–1990).

nodes.label: Graduate Theological Union
variants: Graduate Theological Union in Berkeley, California

nodes.label: Wai Lun Tam
nodes.summary: Wai Lun Tam is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology who earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He became a professor and Chairperson in Cultural and Religious Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Michel Strickmann
nodes.summary: Michel Strickmann was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under Max Kaltenmark and Kristofer Schipper, later serving as an assistant professor at UC Berkeley (1978).

nodes.label: Dodrupchen Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dodrupchen Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under numerous teachers, including Thubten Chökyi Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Kunzang Pelden, and Jigdrel Changchub Dorje, 6th Dzogchen Rinpoche.

nodes.id: I:Government Vidarbha Institute of Science and Humanities
nodes.label: Government Vidarbha Institute of Science and Humanities
Qinni Liu
nodes.summary: Qinni Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

nodes.label: Kirill Solonin
nodes.summary: Kirill Solonin works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held professorships at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) and Renmin University of China (circa 2013).

nodes.label: Alf Sommerfelt
nodes.summary: Alf Sommerfelt was a linguist who founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924. He served as professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

nodes.label: Olivier Lacombe
nodes.summary: Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at École Normale Supérieure (~1925–1928) and the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1930–1939). He taught at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1959–1970) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).

nodes.label: Institut Français d'Histoire en Allemagne
variants: French Insitute at Frankfurt am Main

nodes.label: Tu Weiming
nodes.summary: Tu Weiming works in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Tunghai University, Tokai University, and Harvard under Mou Zongsan, Chun-i Tang, and Fuguan Xu. He held posts at Princeton, UC Berkeley, Harvard (1981–2010), and Peking University (~2010).

nodes.label: Harvard-Yenching Institute
variants: ハーバード燕京研究所

nodes.label: Urs App
nodes.description: Swiss historian of Ideas, Religion, and Philosophy
nodes.summary: Urs App is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at Temple University and studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Hanazono University and the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism.

nodes.label: Richard DeMartino
nodes.description: American psychoanalyst and religious studies scholar (1922-2013)

nodes.label: András Róna-Tas
nodes.image: András Róna-Tas is rector at the Univrsity of Szeged, 14.02.1991..JPG
nodes.summary: András Róna-Tas is a linguist and scholar of Tibetology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences under Gyula Ortutay and Lajos Ligeti, later serving as professor at the University of Szeged (1968–2002).

nodes.label: Anam Thubten Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a teacher of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation.

nodes.label: Vajrayana Foundation
variants: Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies

variants: Tritan Norbutse Bon Education Centre of Nepal
Khri brtan nor bu rtse Monastery

variants: Chinese Civilisation Centre, City University of Hong Kong
City University of Hong Kong Center for East Asian and Comparative Philosophy

nodes.label: Carl Olson
nodes.summary: Carl Olson specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied under mentor John Y. Fenton. He served as the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

nodes.label: Tai-shing Wut
nodes.summary: Tai-shing Wut specialized in Buddhist studies and earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Ming-Wood Liu (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Sangharakshita
nodes.description: Founder of the Friends of the Western Buddhist Order (1925–2018)
nodes.summary: Sangharakshita worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Banaras Hindu University and under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap, Jianmin Chen, and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje. He founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967.

nodes.label: Triratna Buddhist Community
variants: Friends of the Western Buddhist Order

nodes.label: Wilt L. Idema
nodes.summary: Sinologist Wilt L. Idema studied at Leiden University under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé, as well as at Hokkaido and Kyoto universities. He served as Professor of Chinese Literature at Leiden (1976–1999) and at Harvard University (2000–2013).

nodes.label: David Schaberg
nodes.summary: David Schaberg is a sinologist who earned his PhD from Harvard (~1990–1996) after studying at Stanford. He has spent his career at UCLA, where he joined the faculty in 1996, served as dean of Humanities (2012), and became Professor (2020).

nodes.label: Edward Kamens
nodes.summary: Edward Kamens is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University (~1970–1982) and later served there as Sumitomo Professor Emeritus of East Asian Languages & Literatures.

nodes.label: Shuming Liang
nodes.summary: Shuming Liang was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies who attended Shuntian Middle School. He joined the philosophy department at Peking University in 1917 and founded both the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and the China Democratic League.

nodes.label: Nicolas Revire
nodes.summary: Nicolas Revire is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University (2012–2013), under doctoral supervisors Claudine Bautze-Picron and Peter Skilling, and held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h
nodes.summary: Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Boisselier (1988) and served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1989–2003).

nodes.label: Silpakorn University
variants: Sanskrit Studies Centre at Silpakorn University
シラパコーン大学考古学部
シラパコーン大学大学院

nodes.native: อุเทศ หว่องสถิตย์

nodes.label: Thich Thien Nghiem
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies, Thich Thien Nghiem earned a PhD from the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor Shalini Singhal (attested 2012).

nodes.label: K. T. S. Sarao
nodes.summary: K. T. S. Sarao (b. 1955) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. He earned degrees at the University of Delhi and completed a PhD at Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin and K. R. Norman, becoming a professor at Delhi in 1995.

nodes.label: David Ownby
nodes.summary: David Ownby is a historian, sinologist, and scholar of religion who earned his PhD from Harvard (~1982–1989). He taught at Southern Methodist University (~1991–1993) and served as Professor of History at the University of Montreal (1994–2023).

nodes.label: Vincent Goossaert
nodes.summary: Vincent Goossaert is a historian of Chinese religion and Sinology who studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1992–1997). He held research posts at the CNRS (~1998–2012) and became Professor of Daoist History at EPHE in ~2012.

nodes.label: Ji Zhe
nodes.summary: Ji Zhe specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. After earning a Ph.D. in sociology from the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2007, he served as Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).

variants: ベンジャミン・エルマン
ベンジャミン・A・エルマン
nodes.image: Benjamin A. Elman (born 1946) at the lecture 'The Role of Shanghai in Building Modern Science in China in the 19th Century'.png
nodes.jawiki: ベンジャミン・エルマン
nodes.summary: Benjamin A. Elman is a historian and sinologist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He held faculty posts at Colby College, UCLA, and Princeton University, where he directed the East Asian Studies Program.

nodes.label: William M. Bodiford
variants: ウィリアム・ボディフォード
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ボディフォード
nodes.summary: William M. Bodiford is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned his Ph.D. from Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He taught at Davidson College and the University of Iowa before serving as Professor at UCLA from ~1992 to 2021.

nodes.label: Vasudha Narayanan
nodes.summary: Vasudha Narayanan is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the Universities of Madras and Mumbai, and Harvard University. She founded the University of Florida, where she became Distinguished Professor of Religion (~1982).

nodes.label: Mark Juergensmeyer
nodes.summary: Mark Juergensmeyer (born 1940) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at Illinois, Union Theological Seminary, Columbia, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1974), he held professorships at UC Santa Barbara (~1993) and Claremont McKenna College (~2017).

nodes.label: Nanyang Technological University
variants: Institute of Defence and Strategic Studies, Singapore
Institute of Defence and Strategic Studies (IDSS), Nanyang Technological University, Singapore
Institute of Defence and Strategic Studies, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore

nodes.label: Friederike Assandri
nodes.summary: Assandri works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Heidelberg University under Rudolf G. Wagner, Günther Debon, and Günther-Dietz Sontheimer, and held an attested post at Heidelberg University in 2013.

nodes.label: Tufts University
variants: Tufts University School of Veterinary Medicine

nodes.label: Karen Nelson Villanueva
nodes.summary: Karen Nelson Villanueva is a scholar of religious studies. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies and studied under the traditional teacher Geshe Ngawang Dakpa.

nodes.label: Stefan Larsson
nodes.summary: Stefan Larsson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Stockholm University by 2009 under Per-Arne Berglie, Erik af Edholm, and David Germano, and was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley in 2012.

nodes.label: Marta Sernesi
nodes.summary: Marta Sernesi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Turin in 2007 and was attested as a visiting professor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

nodes.label: Shayne Clarke
nodes.summary: Shayne Clarke is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Canterbury and a PhD at UCLA (2006). He has served as associate professor at McMaster University and research fellow at the IIBS.

nodes.label: Sonya S. Lee
nodes.summary: Sonya S. Lee earned a PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu. Specializing in art history, Buddhist studies, and sinology, she taught at Swarthmore College and Stanford, and held a post at the University of Southern California (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Hung Wu
nodes.summary: Hung Wu is an art historian and sinologist who earned a master's at CAFA (1978–1980) and a PhD from Harvard (~1980–1987). He held professorships at Harvard (1990) and the University of Chicago (from 1994).

nodes.label: Jerome Silbergeld
nodes.summary: Jerome Silbergeld (born 1944) specializes in Sinology and art history. He studied at Stanford (BA ~1962–1966; PhD ~1972–1974) and Oregon. He held major posts at the University of Washington (~1975–2001) and Princeton University (~2001–2018).

nodes.label: William L. Ames
nodes.summary: William L. Ames is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Caltech and the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, and later held posts at John F. Kennedy University and other institutions.

nodes.id: I:University of North Carolina at Charlotte
nodes.label: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
variants: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

nodes.label: Richard A. Hutch
nodes.summary: Richard A. Hutch (1945–) is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College (~1963–1967), Yale Divinity School (~1967–1970), and the University of Chicago (~1970–1974). He held posts at Southern Illinois University and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).

nodes.label: University of California, San Diego
variants: University of California at San Diego

nodes.label: William R. LaFleur
variants: ウィリアム・R・ラフルーア
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・R・ラフルーア
nodes.summary: William R. LaFleur was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago, he held faculty posts at Princeton, UCLA, and as E. Dale Saunders Professor at the University of Pennsylvania.

nodes.label: Sibaraj Chetry
nodes.summary: Sibaraj Chetry is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma and teachers including D. K. Chakravarty. He served as a lecturer of philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).
