nodes.label: Huiwen Zhuang
nodes.summary: Huiwen Zhuang works in Buddhist studies. Zhuang earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kirill Solonin, and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher
nodes.summary: Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher (1946–2023) was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. She earned her PhD at the University of Minnesota (~1975–1984) and served there as an Assistant Professor (~1980–2021).

nodes.label: Aaron P. Proffitt
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Japanology, he earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Micah L. Auerback (~2010–2015). Around 2015, he became assistant professor of Japanese Studies at the University at Albany, SUNY.

nodes.label: Valdo H. Viglielmo
variants: ヴァルド・ヴィリエルモ
nodes.jawiki: ヴァルド・ヴィリエルモ
nodes.summary: Valdo H. Viglielmo was a Japanologist and philosopher who earned his degrees at Harvard. After teaching at Harvard, Meiji Gakuin, International Christian University, and Princeton, he served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from 1965 to 2002.

nodes.label: Dan Smyer Yü
nodes.summary: Dan Smyer Yü works in religious studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of California, Davis, and served as a research group leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

nodes.label: University of California, Davis
variants: カリフォルニア大学デービス校

nodes.label: David L. McMahan
nodes.summary: David L. McMahan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He previously taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Vermont, and held positions at Franklin & Marshall College, including as Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Hugh Gray
nodes.summary: Hugh Gray was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Battersea Grammar School, he held posts at SOAS University of London and the University of London as a lecturer (~1960–1981).

nodes.label: Drolma
nodes.summary: Drolma is a Tibetologist who earned an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo, where she studied under supervisor Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Hanna Havnevik
variants: ハンナ・ハヴネヴィク
nodes.summary: Hanna Havnevik specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts as professor (attested 2006–2008) and professor emerita (attested 2026) at the University of Oslo.

nodes.label: J. Thomas Rimer
nodes.summary: J. Thomas Rimer is a Japanologist who studied at Princeton and Columbia. His academic career included positions at Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1983), the University of California, Los Angeles, the University of Pittsburgh (~1991–2011), and the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Tomoko Masuzawa
nodes.summary: Tomoko Masuzawa works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale, and UC Santa Barbara, and held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1987–2001) and the University of Michigan (from 1999).

nodes.label: James Robson
nodes.image: James Robson (academic) on Filled with Meaning.png
nodes.summary: James Robson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology who earned his PhD from Stanford. He taught at Williams College and Michigan before joining Harvard, where he became Harvard-Yenching Institute Director in 2024.

nodes.label: Lori Meeks
nodes.summary: Lori Meeks specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She earned her BA at Columbia and PhD at Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone. She held a postdoc at Stanford (~2004–2005) before joining the University of Southern California in ~2005.

nodes.label: Masayuki Taira
nodes.summary: Masayuki Taira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1970 to 1980 and held academic posts at Kansai University, Osaka University, and Kyoto Tachibana University.

nodes.label: Shunsho Manabe
nodes.summary: Shunsho Manabe worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, having studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963). He held a post at Hosen Gakuen College and served as a professor at Shikoku University (~1998–2012).

nodes.label: Shenpen Hookham
nodes.summary: Shenpen Hookham (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied at the University of Reading and completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford under Michael M. Broido, while also studying under Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche
variants: mKhan po Tshul khrims rgya mtsho
Mkhan po Tshul khrims rgya mtsho
nodes.summary: Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (1934–2024) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, later serving as principal teacher at Rumtek Monastery's shedra and spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery (1992).

nodes.label: Wilfred Cantwell Smith
variants: ウィルフレッド・キャントウェル・スミス
nodes.summary: Wilfred Cantwell Smith was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from Princeton. He taught at Forman Christian College (1940–1946) and held chairs and directorships at McGill University (1948–1951) and Harvard University (1964–1985).

nodes.label: Harvard Medical School
variants: ハーバード大学医学大学院

nodes.label: Lama Kunga Rinpoche
nodes.description: Buddhist Lama of the Sakya school
nodes.summary: Lama Kunga Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Ngor Monastery and served there as Thartse Shabthung in 1959. In 1973, he founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center.

nodes.label: Brian Cutillo
nodes.summary: Brian Cutillo (1945–2006) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology between circa 1963 and 1967 and was a student of Geshe Wangyal.

nodes.label: Supree Kanjanapisarn
nodes.summary: Supree Kanjanapisarn is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Assumption University under the supervision of Veerachart Nimanong.

nodes.label: Veerachart Nimanong
nodes.native: วีรชาติ นิมะนงค์

nodes.label: Jin Kemu
nodes.summary: Jin Kemu (1912–2000) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Sinology. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (1941–1945) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University beginning in 1948.

nodes.label: Fabio Rambelli
variants: ファビオ・ランベッリ
nodes.jawiki: ファビオ・ランベッリ
nodes.summary: Fabio Rambelli specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Ca' Foscari, Naples "L'Orientale", and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, he taught at Sapporo University (2001–2002) before becoming Shinto Studies Chair and Distinguished Professor at UC Santa Barbara (~2009).

nodes.label: Gregory P. A. Levine
nodes.summary: Gregory P. A. Levine is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University. He became Associate Professor at the University of California, Berkeley around 2000.

nodes.label: Lin Heng
nodes.summary: Lin Heng specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi, attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Roger T. Ames
nodes.summary: Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and sinologist who earned his bachelor's from the University of British Columbia, an MA from National Taiwan University, and a PhD from SOAS under D. C. Lau. He served at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1978–2016).

nodes.label: Steve Odin
nodes.summary: Steve Odin is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stony Brook University under Robert Cummings Neville, David A. Dilworth, Don Ihde, and Edward S. Casey, and became Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi in 1982.

nodes.label: Jason M. Wirth
nodes.image: Jason Martin Wirth (born 1963) in the video 'Everybody's Climate 2025 – Jason Wirth on Humanity in the Anthropocene'.png
nodes.summary: Jason M. Wirth works in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki (attested 2017–2019) and became a professor of philosophy at Seattle University around 2004.

nodes.label: Graham Priest
variants: グレアム・プリースト
nodes.jawiki: グレアム・プリースト
nodes.summary: Graham Priest is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge, St John's College, LSE under John Lane Bell, and Melbourne. He held posts at Melbourne (~2001), St Andrews (~2007), and CUNY Graduate Center (~2009).

nodes.label: Jan Westerhoff
nodes.summary: Jan Westerhoff is a philosopher and Indologist specializing in Buddhist studies. He earned PhDs from the University of Cambridge under Michael Potter and SOAS University of London. He became Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Oxford around 2012.

nodes.label: Lili Zheng
nodes.summary: Lili Zheng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi, attested in 2011.

nodes.label: Uma Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mount Carmel College, Banaras Hindu University, and under D. Devahuti at the University of Delhi. She served as an educator at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

nodes.label: D. Devahuti
nodes.description: D. Devahuti, 1929-1988; taught at universities of Malaya, Queensland, and Delhi

nodes.label: Ron Garry
nodes.summary: Ron Garry is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Stuart Ray Sarbacker
nodes.summary: Stuart Ray Sarbacker is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 2001 under the supervision of David M. Knipe.

nodes.label: Usha Nilsson
nodes.summary: Usha Nilsson was an Indologist and linguist who served as a faculty member and Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: B. Alan Wallace
nodes.description: American author, translator, teacher, researcher, interpreter, and Buddhist practitioner
nodes.summary: B. Alan Wallace works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teachers and at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt, taught at Tibet Institute Rikon and UCSB, and founded the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies.

nodes.label: Berthe Jansen
nodes.description: Assistant Professor of Tibetan Studies at Leiden University
nodes.summary: Berthe Jansen works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a BA and PhD at Leiden University under Jonathan A. Silk and an MPhil at Oxford, later serving as assistant professor at Leiden (2015–2016) and research fellow at Heidelberg (~2015–2016).

nodes.label: Vincent Breugem
nodes.summary: Vincent Breugem is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA (1996) and PhD (2012) from Leiden University, also studying under Lucia Dolce. He served as a research fellow at Leiden University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Tulku Thondup
nodes.summary: Tulku Thondup was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Dodrupchen Monastery and under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche. He held a post as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

nodes.label: David Edward Cooper
nodes.summary: David Edward Cooper (1942–) is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St Edmund Hall. He lectured at the University of Oxford (1967), served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008), and was a visiting professor at Peking University (2022).

nodes.label: Purushottama Bilimoria
nodes.summary: Purushottama Bilimoria specializes in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Shivesh Thakur and completed his PhD at La Trobe University. His academic positions include Deakin University (attested 2001–2009) and the University of Melbourne (attested 2001–2016).

nodes.label: Simon P. James
nodes.summary: Simon P. James is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Durham University as a tutor in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and as a lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).

nodes.label: University of Wisconsin–Stevens Point
variants: University of Wisconsin at Stevens Point

nodes.label: Latika Lahiri
nodes.summary: Latika Lahiri (b. 1923) is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under supervisor Xianlin Ji from around 1958 to 1961 and later held a post at the University of Delhi.

nodes.label: Tan Chung
nodes.summary: Tan Chung was a Sinologist and historian who earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Delhi (~1971–1978) and department head at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1978–1994).

nodes.label: Michael Kowalewski
nodes.summary: Michael Kowalewski works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

nodes.label: Sonam Chhoki
nodes.summary: Sonam Chhoki is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed an MA at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a PhD at SOAS University of London, and worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

nodes.label: Thierry Mathou
nodes.summary: Thierry Mathou (born 1963) works in Tibetology. He studied at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po, and served as an Associated Political Scientist at CNRS.

nodes.label: Françoise Pommaret
variants: フランソワーズ・ポマレ
nodes.summary: Françoise Pommaret is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Sorbonne University, INALCO, and the University of Paris, later holding posts at INALCO, the Royal University of Bhutan (~2005), and the CNRS (Directeur de recherche, 2002).

nodes.label: Karma Ura
nodes.summary: Karma Ura works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, Oxford (~1983–1986), and the University of Edinburgh (~1987–1988), and served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (1999–2008).

nodes.label: Ronald E. Purser
nodes.summary: Ronald E. Purser works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and management, having studied under traditional teacher Koshin Ogui in 1985. He held an associate professorship at Loyola University Chicago (~1989–1995) and became a management professor at San Francisco State University (~1995).

nodes.label: San Francisco State University
variants: School of Business der San Francisco State University
サンフランシスコ州立大学

nodes.label: David R. Loy
nodes.summary: David R. Loy is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the National University of Singapore. He taught at NUS (1978–1984), Bunkyo University (1990–2006), and Xavier University (~2006–2010).

nodes.label: David Forbes
nodes.summary: David Forbes held academic appointments at Brooklyn College and as affiliate faculty at the Graduate Center, CUNY, both attested in 2016.

nodes.label: Pamela D. Winfield
nodes.summary: Pamela D. Winfield specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held posts at Temple University (attested 2001) and Elon University, where she was Associate Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2015–2017).

nodes.label: Paula K. R. Arai
nodes.summary: Paula K. R. Arai specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned degrees from Kalamazoo College, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University. Her posts include Vanderbilt (1994–2002), LSU (2007), and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (2023).

nodes.label: Patricia Fister
variants: パトリシア・フィスター
nodes.jawiki: パトリシア・フィスター
nodes.summary: Patricia Fister is a Japanology and art history scholar who earned her Ph.D. from the University of Kansas. She held positions at the University of Kansas, Hakuho Women's College, and served as professor at Nichibunken (2007–2019).

nodes.label: Michaela Mross
nodes.summary: Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and completed her PhD at the University of Munich (2014) before teaching as a Japanese Buddhism professor at Stanford University (attested 2017, 2026).

nodes.label: Diane Elizabeth Riggs
nodes.summary: Diane Elizabeth Riggs is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned her PhD at UCLA under William M. Bodiford. She held visiting posts at Pepperdine and Kenyon College, later joining Western Michigan University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Daniel Timothy Aitken
nodes.summary: Daniel Timothy Aitken specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania, having studied under teachers Parimal G. Patil, Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, and Jay L. Garfield.

nodes.label: University of Tasmania
variants: Centre for Applied Philosophy and Ethics

nodes.label: Chan Ju Mun
nodes.summary: Chan Ju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (2001–2002) and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2002) under Charles Hallisey, John D. Dunne, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda.

nodes.label: Yifa
nodes.description: Taiwanese Buddhist nun, scholar and writer
nodes.summary: Yifa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. She served as dean and department head at University of the West and founded the Woodenfish Foundation.

nodes.label: Reginald A. Ray
nodes.summary: Reginald A. Ray is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under numerous academic and traditional teachers. He held teaching posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2001–2002) and Naropa University (attested 2001–2006).

nodes.label: Dosho Port
nodes.summary: Dosho Port is a Buddhist studies specialist who studied under traditional teachers Dainin Katagiri, Toni Packer, Thich Nhat Hanh, Tangen Harada, Shodo Harada, John Daido Loori, and James Ishmael Ford.

nodes.label: Dainin Katagiri
nodes.summary: Dainin Katagiri (1928–1990) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Eihei-ji and Komazawa University, served as a priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission, became interim abbot at San Francisco Zen Center (1984–1985), and founded Minnesota Zen Meditation Center.

nodes.label: Thich Nhat Hanh
variants: ティク・ナット・ハン
nodes.jawiki: ティク・ナット・ハン
nodes.summary: Thich Nhat Hanh (1926–2022) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Saigon, Princeton, and Columbia universities, and taught at Columbia (1961, 1963–1964), Van Hanh University (~1964–1966), and Cornell (~1966).

nodes.label: Shodo Harada
nodes.summary: Shodo Harada is a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Shofuku-ji and under Mumon Yamada (1962–1982), whom he succeeded. He became abbot of Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded Tahoma Sōgenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

nodes.label: John Daido Loori
nodes.image: Daido Roshi in the Buddha Hall.jpeg
nodes.summary: John Daido Loori worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Rutgers and under Soen Nakagawa and Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi. After a 1974 post at Naropa University, he served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery (~1980–2009).

nodes.label: Dagfinn Føllesdal
variants: ダグフィン・フェレスダール
ダグフィン・フォレスダール
nodes.jawiki: ダグフィン・フェレスダール
nodes.summary: Dagfinn Føllesdal was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at the University of Oslo and Harvard University under Willard Van Orman Quine. He taught at Harvard (1961–1964) and held posts at the University of Oslo and Stanford University (1968–2011).

nodes.label: Jiang Wu
nodes.summary: Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology, having studied at Nankai University and Harvard University under Tu Weiming, Robert M. Gimello, Peter K. Bol, and Zhichao Chen. He served as Professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).

nodes.label: Yonsei University
variants: Institute of East and West Studies at Yonsei University

nodes.label: Gregory Adam Scott
nodes.summary: Gregory Adam Scott works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history. Educated at Columbia University, he has held posts at the University of Edinburgh and as Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Thierry Meynard
nodes.summary: Thierry Meynard (born 1963), a scholar of sinology and philosophy, earned a PhD from Peking University under Yulie Lou (~1999–2003). He became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (~2006) and director of The Beijing Center (2012).

nodes.id: I:The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies
nodes.label: The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies
variants: The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies

nodes.label: Scott Pacey
nodes.summary: Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his doctorate from the Australian National University in 2011 and served as a lecturer in Buddhist thought and practice at the University of Manchester (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Ken McLeod
nodes.summary: Ken McLeod (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an MSc at the University of British Columbia (~1968–1970) and studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Dezhung Rinpoche. He taught at Kagyu Droden Kunchab (~1985–1990) and founded Unfettered Mind.

nodes.label: Kalu Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Kalu Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Osel Ling under Norbu Tondrup and others. He served as Vajra Master at Palpung Monastery and abbot at Changchub Chöling Monastery.

nodes.label: Stephen H. Phillips
nodes.summary: Stephen H. Phillips is a philosopher and Indologist who served as professor of philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 1999) and later became Professor emeritus (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Tomy Augustine
nodes.summary: Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Madras and Banaras Hindu University, studying under C. S. Sundaram and Munni K. Agrawal, and held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Michela Clemente
nodes.summary: Michela Clemente is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015), and held a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellowship at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Agnieszka Helman-Ważny
nodes.description: Polish bibliologist, paper historian, conservator of monuments.
nodes.summary: Agnieszka Helman-Ważny specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts, Warsaw, and Nicolaus Copernicus University (PhD ~2003–2007), holding posts at Cornell University (attested 2009) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

nodes.label: Field Museum of Natural History
variants: フィールド自然史博物館

nodes.label: Thomas Cleary
nodes.summary: Thomas Cleary (1949–2021) worked in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Ph.D. from Harvard University, where he studied under E. Bruce Brooks, and a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Jonathan Christopher Cleary
nodes.summary: Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral studies in East Asian Languages and Civilizations at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and taught as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

nodes.label: Kazuaki Tanahashi
nodes.summary: Kazuaki Tanahashi (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center from 1977 to 1984 and became a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

nodes.label: Mary Clabaugh Wright
nodes.summary: Mary Clabaugh Wright (1917–1970) worked in Sinology and history. She studied at Vassar College and Radcliffe College (MA, PhD). She was curator at the Hoover Institution (~1946–1959) and held professorships at Stanford (1947) and Yale (1959, 1964).

nodes.label: Torkel Brekke
nodes.summary: Torkel Brekke works in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oslo under Jens Braarvig and Georg von Simson, and at Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He held positions at PRIO, Oslo Metropolitan University, and MF Norwegian School of Theology.

nodes.label: Kenryu Tsuji
nodes.summary: Kenryu Tsuji was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: Gerd J. R. Mevissen
nodes.summary: Gerd J. R. Mevissen is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. His career includes posts at the Free University of Berlin, attested in 2017 and as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter in 2026.

nodes.id: I:National Museum Institute of the History of Art, Conservation and Museology
nodes.label: National Museum Institute of the History of Art, Conservation and Museology
Alka Patel
nodes.summary: Alka Patel, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, earned a bachelor's at Mount Holyoke College (~1985–1989) and a PhD at Harvard University (~1993–2000). She became associate professor at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

nodes.label: University of California, Irvine
variants: University of California, Irvine Seminar in Experimental Critical Theory
カリフォルニア大学アーバイン校

nodes.label: Edward S. Casey
nodes.summary: Edward S. Casey is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Northwestern, and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UC Santa Barbara and Yale before joining Stony Brook University in ~1978, later serving as APA president (2009–2010).

nodes.label: Rebecca Redwood French
nodes.summary: Rebecca Redwood French is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a J.D. from the University of Washington and an LL.M. and Ph.D. from Yale University by 1990. She held law faculty positions at CU Boulder and the University at Buffalo.

nodes.label: Rafal Stepien
nodes.summary: Rafal Stepien is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü and Bernard Faure, and held appointments at Wadham College, Oxford (2012–2013) and Harvard University (2015).

nodes.label: Chün-fang Yü
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology, Yü studied at Columbia University (~1968–1973). She held posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University, serving as Professor (~2001–2013) and later Sheng Yen Professor Emerita (~2013).

nodes.label: École Normale Supérieure
variants: Husserl Archives at the École normale supérieure (ENS/CNRS)

nodes.label: University of Sussex
variants: University of Sussex's School of African & Asian Studies

nodes.label: Philippe Turenne
nodes.summary: Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and McGill University (PhD, attested 2010) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori, Richard P. Hayes, Palden Sherab, and several other teachers.

nodes.label: Yaroslav Komarovski
nodes.summary: Komarovski specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at several Tibetan institutes, under multiple traditional teachers, and at the University of Virginia. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis and a post at University of Nebraska-Lincoln (attested 2011–2015).

nodes.label: Peter Schwieger
nodes.summary: Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who completed his doctorate (~1973–1982) and habilitation (~1982–1995) under Dieter Schuh at the University of Bonn. He held a guest professorship at Humboldt University (2001) and the Tibetology chair at Bonn (2001).

nodes.label: Dieter Schuh
nodes.summary: Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD and completed his Habilitation at the University of Bonn, where he served as a professor from 1978 to 2007. He also founded and managed the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Christian Wittern
nodes.summary: Christian Wittern specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational fields, having studied under Seizan Yanagida. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (attested 1993, 2008) and held a post at Hanazono University (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Eliot Deutsch
nodes.summary: Eliot Deutsch (1931–2020) was a philosopher and Indologist. He earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1960. He chaired philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from 1967 to 2006.

nodes.label: Sayadaw U Thittila
nodes.summary: Sayadaw U Thittila studied under Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University (~1933–1934). He served as librarian for the Buddhist Society (~1938–1944) and became a lecturer in Buddhist philosophy at the University of Rangoon in 1952.

nodes.label: Reiho Masunaga
nodes.summary: Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Kaiten Nukariya. He taught at Komazawa University from circa 1935 to 1973.

nodes.label: Kamala Tiyavanich
nodes.summary: Kamala Tiyavanich worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, later holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.

nodes.label: David K. Wyatt
variants: デビッド・K・ワイアット
nodes.jawiki: デビッド・K・ワイアット
nodes.summary: David K. Wyatt (1937–2006) was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell University (Ph.D. circa 1966). He taught at SOAS and Michigan before serving as History Department Chair at Cornell (1969–2002) and AAS president (1993).

nodes.label: Richard Polenberg
nodes.summary: Richard Polenberg was an American history scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University. He served as Professor of American History at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and was a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University.

nodes.label: Trung Huynh
nodes.summary: Trung Huynh is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of the West under the supervision of Darui Long (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Lama Jampa Thaye
nodes.summary: Lama Jampa Thaye is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned a PhD at the University of Manchester and studied under traditional teachers including Karma Thinley Rinpoche. He serves on the international teaching faculty at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

nodes.label: Susan Whitfield
nodes.summary: Susan Whitfield (born 1960) is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. She earned her PhD from SOAS, directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017), and became Professor at UEA in ~2017.

nodes.label: Imre Galambos
nodes.description: Scholar of medieval Chinese and Tangut manuscripts
nodes.summary: Imre Galambos is a scholar of Sinology and history who earned his PhD at UC Berkeley. He worked at the British Library, served as Professor at Cambridge (2012–2023), and held chairs at Hamburg and Zhejiang University in ~2021.

nodes.label: Joseph Margolis
variants: ジョセフ・ザルマン・マーゴリス
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・マーゴリス
nodes.summary: Joseph Margolis was a philosophy scholar who earned his M.A. at Columbia University (ca. 1947–1950). He served as the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University (1991).

nodes.label: Sandra A. Wawrytko
nodes.summary: Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She held positions at San Diego State University, where she is attested as Professor in 1999 and Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014.

nodes.label: Megan Bryson
nodes.summary: Megan Bryson, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, studied at Stanford University. Publications from 2017 attest her affiliation with the University of Tennessee.

nodes.label: Rachelle M. Scott
nodes.summary: Rachelle M. Scott is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay, and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2009–2017).

nodes.id: I:Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts
nodes.label: Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts
variants: Ferenc Hopp Museum of Eastern Asiatic Art

nodes.label: Hungarian Academy of Sciences
variants: Oriental Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences
Oriental Collection, Hungarian Academy of Sciences
Institut für Altaische Forschungen an der Ungarischen Akademie der Wissenschaften

nodes.label: Géza Bethlenfalvy
nodes.summary: Géza Bethlenfalvy worked in Tibetology and Indology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Lajos Ligeti, later holding posts at the University of Delhi (1970), Eötvös Loránd University, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and the University of Vienna (2007–2008).

nodes.label: Zsóka Gelle
nodes.description: Hungarian Tibetologist, translator, writer, filmmaker and guide
nodes.summary: Zsóka Gelle specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Teacher Training College, Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Vienna, and has held posts at Dharma Gate Buddhist College, the University of Vienna, and Eötvös Loránd University.

nodes.label: Benjamin Bogin
nodes.summary: Benjamin Bogin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr., and also studied under Janet Gyatso, Gareth Sparham, and Lopon Ugyen Rinpoche.

nodes.label: John J. Holder
nodes.summary: John J. Holder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies and studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research appointment at the University of Oxford and served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018).

nodes.label: Eric Huntington
nodes.summary: Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago, where he studied under the supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

nodes.label: Dina Bangdel
nodes.summary: Dina Bangdel (1964–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She held academic posts at Ohio State University from approximately 1999 to 2002 and at Virginia Commonwealth University from circa 2002 to 2017.

nodes.label: Virginia Commonwealth University
variants: Virginia Commonwealth University School of Medicine

nodes.label: Andrew Rotman
nodes.summary: Andrew Rotman works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Chicago (doctoral supervision by Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins). He holds posts at Smith College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo
variants: ジャムヤン・キェンツェ・ワンポ
nodes.summary: Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (1820–1892) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Rigdzin Zangpo, Gyurme Sangye Kunga, and Shechen Gyurme Thutob Namgyal, among others, while also teaching Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé.

nodes.label: Peter Alan Roberts
nodes.summary: Peter Alan Roberts is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed doctoral research supervised by Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

nodes.label: Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche
nodes.image: Thrangu Rinpoche on 24 May 2016 face detail, from- 17th Karmapa performs Long Life Offering to Kenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (1933–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Khenpo Gangshar. He served as abbot of Rumtek Monastery (~1968), Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981), and Gampo Abbey (~1984–2023).

nodes.label: Phramaha Somphong Santacitto
nodes.summary: Phramaha Somphong Santacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a master's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Phra Suthithammanuwat
nodes.native: พระสุทธิธรรมนิเทศ

nodes.label: Watchara Ngamchitcharoen
nodes.native: วัชระ งามจิตรเจริญ

nodes.label: Brian D. Ruppert
nodes.summary: Brian D. Ruppert specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Mentored by Willis Stoesz, he served at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1999–2018) before becoming Kazushige Hirasawa Professor of Japanese Studies at Bates College in 2018.

nodes.label: Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani
nodes.summary: Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a scholar in Sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) and earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.

nodes.label: Perry Link
nodes.summary: Perry Link (b. 1944) is a sinologist who earned a B.A. at Harvard University (~1962–1966). He held posts at Princeton University (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

nodes.label: James Ishmael Ford
nodes.summary: James Ishmael Ford is a scholar and teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Sonoma State University and the Pacific School of Religion, and founded Boundless Way Zen and the Empty Moon Zen Network.

nodes.label: Houn Jiyu-Kennett
nodes.summary: Houn Jiyu-Kennett was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Durham University, Trinity Laban, and Soji-ji (1962–1963) under teachers including Chisan Kohō. She served as head priest at Unpuku-ji and later founded and led Shasta Abbey.

nodes.label: Jonathan C. Gold
nodes.summary: Jonathan C. Gold works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He has taught at the University of Vermont, served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at Drew University (attested 2006), and held faculty posts in religion at Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

nodes.label: Michael Eido Luetchford
nodes.summary: Michael Eido Luetchford (1944–2023) focused on Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned an electronic engineering degree at the University of Bradford (~1964–1967) and studied under traditional teacher Gudo Wafu Nishijima.

nodes.label: Gudo Wafu Nishijima
nodes.summary: Gudo Wafu Nishijima, a Buddhist studies figure, earned a law degree at the University of Tokyo and studied under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa. He lectured at Toho Gakuin and founded Dogen Sangha International in 2007.

nodes.label: Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche, and founded Siddhartha's Intent, Khyentse Foundation, and Deer Park Institute.

nodes.label: Anna Balikci Denjongpa
nodes.summary: Anna Balikci Denjongpa works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London under Lionel Caplan, and also studied with traditional teachers Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku. In 2002, she became research coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Nathaniel DeWitt Garson
nodes.summary: Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and also studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Namdrol.

nodes.label: Southern Methodist University
variants: Perkins School of Theology, Southern Methodist University
Perkins School of Theology at the Southern Methodist University
Perkins School of Theology at Southern Methodist University

nodes.label: Alexander Macmillan
nodes.summary: Alexander Macmillan works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at SIT Graduate Institute, where he was advised by Elizabeth Morrison (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Elizabeth Morrison
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under Janet Gyatso, Susan Niditch, Bernard Faure, and Carl Bielefeldt. She held posts at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Chögyam Trungpa
variants: チョギャム・トゥルンパ
チョギャム トゥルンパ
チューギャム・ドゥンパ
nodes.image: Trungpa from Khenpo gangshar2 cropped image.jpg
nodes.jawiki: チョギャム・トゥルンパ
nodes.summary: Chögyam Trungpa was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Khenpo Gangshar and at Oxford (1963). He served at the Young Lamas Home School (1959–1963) and founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1967), Naropa University (1973), and Gampo Abbey.

nodes.label: Aruna Haldar
nodes.summary: Aruna Haldar worked in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Girindrasekhar Bose and Kedarnath Ojha, and held a teaching post at Patna University.

nodes.label: Girindrasekhar Bose
nodes.summary: Girindrasekhar Bose studied at Presidency University, Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949) and as president of the Indian Psychoanalytic Society (1922–1953).

nodes.label: Joachim Gentz
nodes.summary: Joachim Gentz is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He was Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and later served as Reader in Chinese Studies (attested 2013) and Professor (attested 2026) at Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Perry Schmidt-Leukel
nodes.summary: Perry Schmidt-Leukel (b. 1954) studied and completed his habilitation at the University of Munich (~1977–1996). He held posts at Munich, Innsbruck, Salzburg, the University of Glasgow (2000–2009), and the University of Münster (2009–2023).

nodes.label: Adam Yuet Chau
nodes.summary: Adam Yuet Chau works in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Williams College and earned his PhD from Stanford University (2001), later holding posts at Harvard University and the University of Cambridge, where he became Professor of the Anthropology of China.

nodes.label: Philip Clart
nodes.description: German Sinologist, Professor of Chinese Studies at Leipzig University, Germany
nodes.summary: Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied under Daniel L. Overmyer (~1991–1996) and became Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig around 2008.

nodes.label: Michael Stanley-Baker
nodes.summary: Michael Stanley-Baker works in Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology, having earned an MA at Indiana University Bloomington under Stephen R. Bokenkamp. He has held posts at MPIWG, University of Leipzig, University of Pittsburgh, and Nanyang Technological University.

nodes.label: Harold Stewart
nodes.summary: Harold Stewart was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his studies at the University of Sydney and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

nodes.label: David Tracy
nodes.summary: David Tracy worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University, then taught at Catholic University of America (1967–1969) and the University of Chicago (1969–2006).

nodes.label: Douglas L. Berger
nodes.summary: Douglas L. Berger works in philosophy, Sinology, and Indology. He taught philosophy at Southern Illinois University (attested 2007–2014) and serves as Professor and Director of the Centre for Intercultural Philosophy at Leiden University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Peter Schwabland
nodes.summary: Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his MA at the University of Washington under the supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Michael L. Walter
nodes.summary: Michael L. Walter worked in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, having studied under Larry William Moses. He was a research fellow at the Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000) and special languages cataloger at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Akimichi Eda
nodes.summary: Akimichi Eda specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Dr. phil. from the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under Michael Hahn, having also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Khangkar Tsultrim Kelsang.

nodes.label: Lita Peipina
nodes.summary: Lita Peipina specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under supervisor Jens Braarvig, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

nodes.label: Stephen Prothero
nodes.summary: Stephen Prothero is a religious studies scholar who studied at Yale University and Jonathan Edwards College (B.A.) and earned his M.A. and Ph.D. under William R. Hutchison at Harvard. He held a professorship at Boston University from around 1996.

nodes.label: Duncan Ryūken Williams
nodes.summary: Duncan Ryūken Williams works in Buddhist, religious, and Japanese studies. After studying at Reed College and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held posts at Harvard, UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.

nodes.label: Kenneth K. Tanaka
nodes.summary: Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and served as a professor and director at Musashino University between 1998 and 2014.

nodes.label: Kōshō Uchiyama
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, Kōshō Uchiyama earned a master's in Western philosophy from Waseda University and studied under Kodo Sawaki. He taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary (~1937–1941) and served as abbot of Antai-ji (1965–1975).

nodes.label: Kodo Sawaki
nodes.summary: Kodo Sawaki specialized in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Takada College, Senju-ji, Horyu-ji, and under Koho Sawada, Zenko Sawada, Ryoun Fueoka, Join Saeki, and Sotan Oka. He held posts at Komazawa University and Antai-ji.

nodes.label: Sotan Oka
nodes.summary: Sotan Oka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He was a professor, dean (1899), and president (1918) at Komazawa University, and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

nodes.label: Ian Kishizawa
nodes.summary: Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Saitama University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka, later teaching Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani.

nodes.label: See Mui Yian
nodes.summary: See Mui Yian is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She completed her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Warren Lee Todd
nodes.summary: Warren Lee Todd works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University under the doctoral supervision of Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, and also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Chogye Trichen Rinpoche, and Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: Alison Denton Jones
nodes.summary: Alison Denton Jones works in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Her teachers included Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish, and her doctoral supervisor was Martin King Whyte.

nodes.label: Martin King Whyte
nodes.summary: Martin King Whyte is a Sinologist and sociologist educated at Cornell and Harvard. He taught at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University (1994–2000), and joined Harvard University in 2000.

nodes.label: Allan H. Barr
nodes.summary: Sinologist Allan H. Barr earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford (until 1983). He has served as a professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Margaret Dornish
nodes.summary: Margaret Dornish works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Daniela Berti
nodes.summary: Daniela Berti works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Siena and was attested as a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya in 2004.

nodes.id: I:Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya
nodes.label: Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya
variants: Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya, Paris

nodes.label: Gilles Tarabout
nodes.summary: Gilles Tarabout is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Madeleine Biardeau. By 2004, he was a senior fellow at CNRS, a member of the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences, and an exchange program director at FMSH.

nodes.id: I:Fondation Maison des sciences de l'homme
nodes.label: Fondation Maison des sciences de l'homme
variants: Maison des Sciences de l'Homme, Paris

nodes.label: Cortland Dahl
nodes.summary: Cortland Dahl is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and received mentorship from Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.

nodes.label: Khunu Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khunu Rinpoche (1894–1977) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Rasvir Das, Sönam Gyaltsen, and Dev Narayan Tripathi. He held a teaching post at Men-Tsee-Khang.

nodes.label: Robert Charles Zaehner
nodes.image: Internationaal Theologisch Congres toekomst van de religie, religie van de toeko, Bestanddeelnr 925-4729.jpg
nodes.description: British spy and academic on Eastern religions (1913–1974)
nodes.summary: Robert Charles Zaehner (1913–1974) studied at Christ Church, Oxford, and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. Working in religious studies, Indology, and Iranian studies, he served as Oxford's Spalding Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics and All Souls College fellow (~1952–1974).

nodes.label: Stephen Harris
nodes.summary: Stephen Harris is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of New Mexico by 2014 and became University Lecturer in Indian and Comparative Philosophy at Leiden University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Channa Li
nodes.summary: Channa Li is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Jonathan A. Silk (attested 2015) and serves as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: James A. Benn
nodes.summary: James A. Benn is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., he held teaching posts at Lewis & Clark College and Arizona State University before becoming a professor at McMaster University.

nodes.label: Kyoko Tokuno
nodes.summary: Kyoko Tokuno is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held academic posts at the University of Oregon and at the University of Washington, where she was attested as a professor in 2017.

nodes.label: Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje
variants: ドゥジョム・ジグドラル・イェシェ・ドルジェ
nodes.summary: Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, founding the International Nyingma Society. He studied under teachers including Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Sera Khandro Dewé Dorje, and taught students including Matthew T. Kapstein and Alexander Berzin.

nodes.label: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley
nodes.summary: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under F. E. L. Priestley and doctoral supervisor A. K. Warder, and held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Julia Ching
nodes.summary: Julia Ching (1934–2001) specialized in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and the Australian National University (Ph.D.). After teaching at Columbia and Yale, she became a professor at the University of Toronto in 1978.

nodes.label: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby
nodes.summary: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby was a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard, and held posts at McGill (1960–1964), Yale (1966–1971), and the University of Toronto and Trinity College (~1971–1999).

nodes.label: Jacob Holubeck
nodes.summary: Jacob Holubeck is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Eric Stephen Goodell
nodes.summary: Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed master's degrees at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia, where he studied under the supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Georgetown University
variants: School of Foreign Service, Georgetown University

nodes.label: Kristin Johnston Largen
nodes.summary: Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies attested in 2018 as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean at Gettysburg College.

nodes.label: Brandon Dotson
nodes.summary: Brandon Dotson is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and completed his habilitation at the University of Munich, where he worked from circa 2010 to 2016.

nodes.label: Marcus Bingenheimer
nodes.summary: Marcus Bingenheimer works in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He studied at Nagoya University under Yasuhisa Matsumura and at the University of Würzburg under Huinan Yang. His posts include Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (2005–2011) and Temple University (2012–2015).

nodes.label: Jongmyung Kim
nodes.summary: Jongmyung Kim is a Buddhist studies and history scholar. He studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He served as Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

nodes.label: Roderick Whitfield
nodes.summary: Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London, where he was attested as professor emeritus in 2011.

nodes.label: Central Academy of Fine Arts
variants: Central Academy of Fine Arts in Beijing
国立北平芸術専科学校

nodes.label: Eugene Y. Wang
nodes.summary: Eugene Y. Wang is an art historian and scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Hung Wu and John M. Rosenfield. He taught at the University of Chicago before becoming a professor at Harvard University.

nodes.label: Kristofer Schipper
nodes.summary: Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a sinologist and religious studies scholar educated in Paris. He held major posts at EFEO (circa 1962–1973), EPHE (1972–2002), and the Institut des hautes études chinoises.

nodes.label: Erik Haarh
nodes.summary: Erik Haarh was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Copenhagen (attested 1969). He worked at the Royal Danish Library (1956–1962) and served as a department head and professor at Aarhus University (1969, 1983).

nodes.label: Helen J. Baroni
nodes.summary: Helen J. Baroni is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Paul B. Watt and held a post at the University of Hawaiʻi, attested in 2006.

nodes.label: Shou-chien Shih
nodes.summary: Shou-chien Shih works in history, archaeology, and sinology. Shih served as a professor at National Taiwan University (~1987) and as director of the National Palace Museum (~2000–2004).

nodes.label: Alice Y. Tseng
nodes.summary: Alice Y. Tseng specializes in Japanology and history/archaeology. She was a graduate student of Eugene Y. Wang (attested 2005) and served as a professor at Boston University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Heidelberg Society for Mahāyāna Research
variants: an active society for the study of Mahāyāna
Society for the Study of Mahāyāna
society for the study of Mahāyāna

nodes.label: Brian J. Nichols
nodes.summary: Brian J. Nichols is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and earned his Ph.D. from Rice University under the supervision of Anne C. Klein.

nodes.id: I:Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies
nodes.label: Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies
variants: Inter-University Program for Chinese language studies at Tsinghua University
Inter-University Board of Chinese Language Studies

nodes.label: Tansen Sen
nodes.summary: Tansen Sen works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Yinzeng Geng and Xianlin Ji, and earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair. He held a post at Baruch College (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Takeshi Umehara
nodes.summary: Takeshi Umehara was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi and Michitaro Tanaka. He held posts at Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto City University of Arts, and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

nodes.label: Derge Gonchen
variants: sDe dge dbon stod slob grwa at sDe dge dgon chen Monastery

nodes.label: Kuse Serjong Shedra
variants: sDe dge Ku se gSer ljongs bshad grwa

nodes.label: Khenpo Dragyab Lodrö
variants: mKhan Rinpoche Brag gyab Blos gros

nodes.label: Sarah Aoife Richardson
nodes.summary: Sarah Aoife Richardson specializes in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto by 2016 under Jenny Purtle, having also studied under teachers including Susan L. and John C. Huntington.

nodes.label: Julia F. Andrews
nodes.summary: Julia F. Andrews (born 1951) is a sinologist and art historian. She completed her studies at Brown University, UC Berkeley, and Harvard University (1976–1984), and joined the faculty at Ohio State University around 1987.

nodes.label: Frank J. Hoffman
nodes.summary: Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi under teachers including Stewart Sutherland, Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and K. N. Upadhyaya.

nodes.label: Trent Walker
nodes.summary: Trent Walker is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt.

nodes.label: Olivier de Bernon
nodes.summary: Olivier de Bernon (born 1957) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Pierre L. Lamant and has served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Jan Chozen Bays
nodes.summary: Jan Chozen Bays is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada. She served as a teacher at the Zen Community of Oregon from 1985 and as abbess of Great Vow Zen Monastery around 2002.

nodes.label: Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi
nodes.summary: Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi was a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, and San Francisco State University, under Hakujun Kuroda, Koryu Osaka, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani. He served as priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission in 1956.

nodes.label: Neal Donner
nodes.summary: Neal Donner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).

nodes.label: Wenjie Qin
nodes.summary: Wenjie Qin works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Qin completed a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wei-ming Tu and studied under Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.

nodes.label: Wei-ming Tu
nodes.summary: Wei-ming Tu (born 1940) studied at Tunghai and Harvard universities. Specializing in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies, he held posts at Princeton, UC Berkeley, the East-West Center, Harvard-Yenching Institute, and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Bing Chen
nodes.summary: Bing Chen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He worked as a professor at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences (~1981–1987) and Sichuan University (~1987).

nodes.label: Yun-hua Jan
nodes.summary: Yun-hua Jan (1923–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He was a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and a professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).

nodes.label: Lhakpa Tsering
nodes.summary: Lhakpa Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who has held posts as Professor at Tibet University and Assistant Professor of Tibetan Language and Literature at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Stephanie Roemer
nodes.summary: Stephanie Roemer is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her doctoral studies under the supervision of Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

nodes.label: Eberhard Sandschneider
nodes.summary: Eberhard Sandschneider, a sinologist, earned his PhD at Saarland University (~1981–1986). He served as professor at Mainz (1995–1998), professor and director at the Free University of Berlin (from 1998), and director at the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

nodes.label: German Council on Foreign Relations
variants: Forschungsinstitut der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Auswärtige Politik

nodes.label: Naoki Nabeshima
nodes.summary: Naoki Nabeshima (born 1963) is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2004).

nodes.label: David Matsumoto
nodes.summary: David Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as Director at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2004, 2013) and as President Emeritus of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jing-shen Tao
nodes.summary: Jing-shen Tao (born 1933) is a historian and Sinologist. After studying at National Taiwan University and earning his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, he served as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000) and at Academia Sinica.

nodes.label: Christian Coseru
nodes.description: American philosopher and scholar of Buddhist philosophy
nodes.summary: Christian Coseru is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Bucharest and the Australian National University, and became an Associate Professor of Philosophy at the College of Charleston around 2006.

nodes.label: C. W. Huntington, Jr.
nodes.summary: C. W. Huntington, Jr. specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis O. Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, and served as a professor at Hartwick College (~1992–2020).

nodes.label: Kevin Buckelew
nodes.summary: Kevin Buckelew specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College, and his teachers included doctoral supervisors Chün-fang Yü, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.

nodes.label: Chao-heng Liao
nodes.summary: Chao-heng Liao works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Liao held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018) and served as an adjunct researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Valeria Gazizova
nodes.summary: Valeria Gazizova works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Oslo, completing a master's thesis supervised by Per Kvaerne, and was also taught by Hanna Havnevik.

nodes.label: Loden Sherap Dagyab Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Loden Sherap Dagyab Rinpoche (born 1940) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche and Ling Rinpoche, directed Tibet House, New Delhi (1964–1966), joined the University of Bonn in 1966, and founded Tibethaus Deutschland in 2005.

nodes.label: Martin Brauen
nodes.summary: Martin Brauen is a Tibetologist who studied at Delhi and Zurich. He held curator and director roles at the Ethnographic Museum of the University of Zurich from 1975 and served as chief curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (2008–2012).

nodes.label: Michael Jay Sweet
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Michael Jay Sweet earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under Geshe Wangyal and Richard Robinson. He held clinical assistant professorships in psychiatry at Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche
variants: Thub bstan bzod pa rin po che
nodes.image: Kyabje Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche December 2008 Kopan monastery Nepal.jpg
nodes.summary: Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Yeshe Thubten, Geshe Rabten, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He founded Kopan Monastery, FPMT, Maitripa College, and served as FPMT's spiritual director from 1984.

nodes.label: John Ross Carter
nodes.summary: John Ross Carter (1938–2020) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard University under Wilfred Cantwell Smith, and held a long-term academic appointment at Colgate University from around 1972 to 2010.

nodes.label: Amita Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Amita Chatterjee is an Indologist and philosopher who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University (attested 1999, 2009).

nodes.label: Catholic University of America
variants: The Catholic University of America (Washington, DC)

nodes.label: Knut A. Jacobsen
nodes.summary: Knut A. Jacobsen works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held professorships at the University of Bergen starting in 1996 and at the University of Oslo from approximately 1996 to 1999.

nodes.label: John M. Koller
nodes.summary: John M. Koller specialized in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena, Charles A. Moore, and George T. Artola, and served as a philosophy professor at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.

nodes.label: Daya Krishna
nodes.summary: Daya Krishna was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as professor of philosophy and Ex-Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1969–1984) and chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (~1990–1993).

nodes.label: Shigenori Nagatomo
nodes.summary: Shigenori Nagatomo is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor of religious studies at Temple University (attested 1999 and 2017).

nodes.id: I:Institute of Philosophy of the Russian Academy of Sciences
nodes.label: Institute of Philosophy of the Russian Academy of Sciences
variants: Institute of Philosophy, Academy of Sciences USSR

nodes.label: Michiko Yusa
nodes.summary: Michiko Yusa is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed her doctoral studies under Raimon Panikkar (~1978–1983) and served as a professor in the Department of Foreign Languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2021).

nodes.label: Diego Loukota
nodes.summary: Diego Loukota is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed an MA at Peking University and earned his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2019.

nodes.label: Susan Andrews
nodes.summary: Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü.

nodes.label: Michael I. Como
nodes.summary: Michael I. Como specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and sinology, having studied under advisers Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. He holds the position of Tōshū Fukami Associate Professor of Shinto Studies at Columbia University (attested 2009, 2026).

nodes.label: Karma Thinley Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as abbot at the Young Lamas Home School (~1962–1963) and at Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery.

nodes.label: Gendun Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Gendun Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He founded several centres, including Dhagpo Kagyu Ling, where he served as abbot and retreat master from around 1977 to 1997.

nodes.label: Bokar Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Bokar Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under traditional teacher Kalu Rinpoche (~1960–1989) and was based at Bokar Monastery from ~1984 to 2004.

nodes.label: Michael M. Broido
nodes.summary: Michael M. Broido specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge and later held a post at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Geshe Tashi Tsering
nodes.summary: Geshe Tashi Tsering (born 1958) studied at Sera Monastery and Gyuto Monastery, later studying under Geshe Thubten Rinchen. A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, he taught at Kopan Monastery and became resident teacher at Jamyang Buddhist Centre in 1994.

nodes.label: Qiwen Xiao
nodes.summary: Qiwen Xiao is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under supervisor Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda
nodes.summary: Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She has served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).

nodes.id: I:Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies
nodes.label: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies
variants: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute for Asian Studies

nodes.label: Shri Krishna Saksena
nodes.summary: Shri Krishna Saksena worked in philosophy and Indology, holding professorships at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi.

nodes.label: East-West Center
variants: ハワイ東西センター文化・コミュニケーション研究所

nodes.label: Ashok Kumar Malhotra
nodes.summary: Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the East-West Center and founded the State University of New York at Oneonta.

nodes.label: Gregory Forgues
nodes.summary: Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher (attested 2011) and Birgit Kellner, alongside multiple traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Chanmyay Sayadaw U Janakabhivamsa
nodes.native: ဦးဇနကာဘိဝံသ

nodes.label: Pema Bhum
nodes.summary: Pema Bhum is a Tibetologist who served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington, and as director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

nodes.label: Morton Klass
nodes.summary: Morton Klass was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, where he was mentored by Conrad M. Arensberg. He held teaching posts at Bennington College, Barnard College, and Columbia University.

nodes.label: Margaret Mead
variants: マーガレット・ミード
nodes.jawiki: マーガレット・ミード
nodes.summary: Margaret Mead studied at Barnard and Columbia University under Franz Boas. Her career included posts at the American Museum of Natural History (1926, 1946–1969), Columbia University (1954–1978), Fordham University (1968–1970), and the University of Rhode Island (1970).

nodes.label: Jan Jakob Maria de Groot
nodes.jawiki: ヤン・ヤーコプ・マリア・デ・ホロート
nodes.summary: Jan Jakob Maria de Groot was a sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University. He served as a professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and as Professor of Sinology at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).

nodes.label: Xiaoting Wei
nodes.summary: Xiaoting Wei is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who completed an MA at the National University of Singapore under supervisor Cheng-Mei Ku (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Jinshi Fan
nodes.summary: Jinshi Fan (born 1938) is a specialist in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Bai Su (~1958–1963) and served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014), later holding a post at Lanzhou University.

nodes.label: Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan
nodes.summary: Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under M. K. Ganguli and received traditional training under A. P. Lama.

nodes.label: Bhajagobinda Ghosh
nodes.summary: A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ghosh served as Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and as an editorial board member for the Bulletin of Tibetology (both attested 1994).

nodes.label: Martin Collcutt
nodes.jawiki: マーティン・コルカット
nodes.summary: Martin Collcutt specializes in Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge and Harvard, he taught at Tokyo and Yokohama National universities before serving as Director of the East Asian Studies Program at Princeton University from 1975 to 2015.

nodes.label: Luangpor Teean Jittasubho
nodes.native: หลวงพ่อเทียน จิตฺตสุโภ

nodes.label: Andrew Quintman
nodes.summary: Andrew Quintman is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and held a post as assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

nodes.label: Masaharu Imai
nodes.summary: Masaharu Imai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology who earned a doctorate from Tokyo University of Education (1977). He taught at Ibaraki University (1977) and became professor emeritus at the University of Tsukuba in 2006.

nodes.label: Juhn Young Ahn
nodes.summary: Juhn Young Ahn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (ended 2007). He was attested in 2019 as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies at the University of Michigan.

nodes.id: P:Bstan 'dzin zla grags chos kyi rgyal mtshan
nodes.label: Bstan 'dzin zla grags chos kyi rgyal mtshan
Lobsang Yongdan
nodes.summary: Lobsang Yongdan works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. After studying at Kumbum Monastery and earning a PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger, he held postdoctoral posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science and the University of Bonn.

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for the History of Science
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science
variants: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science
Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, Berlin

nodes.label: Fernando Jose Benetti
nodes.summary: Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University and completed doctoral research supervised by Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

nodes.label: William H. Nienhauser, Jr.
nodes.summary: Sinologist William H. Nienhauser, Jr. studied at Indiana University under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff, and at Bonn. After visiting roles, he became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (from 1983; Halls-Bascom Professor from 1995).

nodes.label: Kristina Myrvold
nodes.summary: Kristina Myrvold is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied and held an editorial post at Lund University, and later served as assistant professor of religious studies at Linnaeus University.

nodes.label: Olle Qvarnström
nodes.summary: Olle Qvarnström is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Washington, Harvard University, and the University of Copenhagen, working under Tord Olsson, Karl H. Potter, Collett Cox, and Christian Lindtner, and held a post at Lund University.

nodes.label: Gurinder Singh Mann
nodes.summary: Gurinder Singh Mann is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD at Columbia University. He taught religion at Columbia (1988–1999) and held the Kapany Chair in Sikh Studies at UC Santa Barbara (1999–2015).

nodes.label: University of Bergen
variants: Department of Social Anthropology, University of Bergen

nodes.label: Anne Hardgrove
nodes.summary: Anne Hardgrove specializes in history, archaeology, and indology. She studied at Carleton College and the University of Michigan (until 1999) and served as Redaktionsråd at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

nodes.id: I:University of Texas at San Antonio
nodes.label: University of Texas at San Antonio
variants: University of Texas at San Antonio

nodes.label: Paul Copp
nodes.summary: Paul Copp specializes in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at UMass Amherst and Princeton (PhD attested 2005 under Stephen F. Teiser), he has held posts at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Ching-mao Cheng
nodes.summary: Ching-mao Cheng (1933–2025) was a scholar of Sinology and Japanology who earned a PhD from Princeton. Cheng held posts at UC Berkeley, chaired Asian Languages and Literatures at UMass Amherst, and was a founder and founding chair at National Dong Hwa University.

nodes.label: Donald Edward Gjertson
nodes.summary: Donald Edward Gjertson is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (attested 1975) and held a post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Stephen Batchelor
nodes.summary: Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher. He studied with teachers including Satya Narayan Goenka, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim. He directed Sharpham College (~1992–2000) and later joined the faculty of Bodhi College (~2015).

nodes.label: Mohan Wijayaratna
nodes.description: Sinhalese anthropologist and translator specializing in Buddhism

nodes.label: Kosai Fukushima
nodes.summary: Kosai Fukushima (1928–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Paul L. Swanson. At Otani University, he was attested as Dean of Students in 1985 and professor in 1992.

nodes.label: Royall Tyler
nodes.summary: Royall Tyler is a Japanologist who studied at Harvard and Columbia, completing a doctorate under Donald Keene. He taught at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, the University of Oslo, and the Australian National University (1990–2000), later visiting Harvard.

nodes.label: Huai-Chin Nan
nodes.summary: Huai-Chin Nan worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the ROC Military Academy and University of Nanking, and under Huanxian Yuan. His posts included the ROC Military Academy, Chinese Culture University (~1963–1975), National Chengchi University, and Fu Jen Catholic University.

nodes.label: Chinese Culture University
variants: College of Chinese Culture Graduate School in Taipei
Institute of Chinese Culture in Taipei
中国文化大学印度研究所

nodes.label: Huynh Kim Lan
