nodes.summary: Huynh Kim Lan works in Buddhist studies and earned an MA in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2010), advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.

nodes.label: Gareth Fisher
nodes.summary: Gareth Fisher works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (2006) and served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

nodes.label: Nirupam Chakma
nodes.summary: Nirupam Chakma specializes in Buddhist studies. Chakma earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Tilak Kariyawasam
nodes.summary: Tilak Kariyawasam is a Buddhist studies scholar who headed the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and served as Dean of the Graduate School at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Fa Qing
nodes.summary: Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a dissertation at the University of Calgary under doctoral supervisor Leslie S. Kawamura, interim supervisor A. W. Barber, and teacher Xiaojie Yang.

nodes.label: Wei Wu
nodes.summary: Wei Wu (born 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies. Wu founded the International Buddhist College and serves as Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ki-yong Rhi
nodes.summary: Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, holding a post at Dongguk University (attested 1983) and later serving as professor emeritus there (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Martin Willson
nodes.summary: Martin Willson (d. 2005) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Yeshe Thubten, Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

nodes.label: Michael Weiers
nodes.summary: Michael Weiers studied at the University of Bonn, completing his dissertation around 1965. A specialist in Iranian, Central Asian studies, and linguistics, he served as professor at Bonn (1972–2003) and honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University.

nodes.label: Geshe Jampa Tegchok
nodes.summary: Geshe Jampa Tegchok was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery and later as resident teacher at Land of Medicine Buddha.

nodes.label: Daniel L. Overmyer
nodes.description: Scholar of the history of Chinese popular religions
nodes.summary: Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn. He was a longtime professor at the University of British Columbia (~1973–2001).

nodes.label: Dieter B. Kapp
nodes.summary: Dieter B. Kapp was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his doctorate at Heidelberg University under Hermann Berger. He taught at Heidelberg and served as director of the Institute for Indology and Tamil Studies at the University of Cologne (1990–2006).

nodes.label: Peter James Gilks
nodes.summary: Peter James Gilks is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang with several traditional teachers and earned a PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Aleix Ruiz-Falqués
nodes.summary: Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs and has held posts at Shan State Buddhist University, Singapore University of Technology and Design, and the Pali Text Society.

nodes.label: Di Luo
nodes.summary: Di Luo is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who completed a PhD at the University of Southern California (attested 2016) under the supervision of Sonya S. Lee.

nodes.label: Richard von Glahn
nodes.summary: Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He held a professorship at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1987) and was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo (1988–1989).

nodes.label: Jeff Watt
nodes.summary: Jeff Watt is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.

nodes.label: Justin Shimeld
nodes.summary: Justin Shimeld is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania, where he was supervised by Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

nodes.label: Jeff Malpas
nodes.summary: Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who studied at the University of Auckland and Australian National University (PhD). He led Murdoch University's philosophy programme (~1990–1999) and served as Professor (1999) and Emeritus Distinguished Professor (2018) at the University of Tasmania.

nodes.label: Sonam Thakchoe
nodes.summary: Sonam Thakchoe, a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1999–2002) mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas. He also held a post at the University of Tasmania around 2003.

nodes.label: Barry Kerzin
nodes.image: Barry Kerzin, American Professor of Medicine and Buddhist monk.gif
nodes.summary: Barry Kerzin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley, USC, and Keck School of Medicine, and under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. His posts include Assistant Professor of Medicine at the University of Washington and adjunct professor at the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Shili Xiong
nodes.summary: Shili Xiong (1885–1968) was a philosopher, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at China Inner Studies College under Jian Ouyang (1920). He held posts at Boone University (~1920–1922), Peking University (1923–1955), and Zhejiang University (~1937–1938).

nodes.label: Mou Zongsan
nodes.summary: Mou Zongsan was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University under Shili Xiong. He taught at various institutions, including National Taiwan Normal University, the University of Hong Kong, and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies.

nodes.label: Philip Whalen
nodes.summary: Philip Whalen was a Buddhist studies practitioner and poet who earned a BA from Reed College and studied under Richard Baker. He served as head monk at Dharma Sangha (1984) and abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).

nodes.label: Noboru Miyata
nodes.summary: Noboru Miyata (1936–2000) was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and history. Educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba, he served as Professor of Folklore at Tsukuba (~1973–1999) and held posts at Tokyo Gakugei and Kanagawa Universities.

nodes.label: Oleg Grabar
nodes.summary: Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After degrees at Paris, Harvard, and Princeton, he directed the Albright Institute (1953) and held professorships at Michigan (1954–1969), Harvard (1969–1990), and IAS (1990–1998).

nodes.label: Jörg Heimbel
nodes.summary: Jörg Heimbel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Franz-Karl Ehrhard and David P. Jackson. He has held appointments at Hamburg, Munich, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Men-Tsee-Khang
variants: Tibetan Institute of Medicine and Astrology

nodes.label: Elizabeth English
nodes.summary: Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Harunaga Isaacson and completed her PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 1999.

nodes.label: Sung-Bae Park
nodes.summary: Sung-Bae Park (born 1933) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate under Lewis Lancaster (~1975–1979). He served as an assistant professor at Dongguk University and later taught at Stony Brook University from 1977.

nodes.label: Alfred Bloom
variants: アルフレッド・ブルーム
nodes.jawiki: アルフレッド・ブルーム
nodes.summary: Alfred Bloom studied at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. A scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology, he held faculty posts at the University of Oregon (1961–1970), University of Hawaiʻi (1970–1986), and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1986–1994).

nodes.label: University at Albany, SUNY
variants: State University of New York at Albany
University at Albany (State University of New York)
University at Albany, State University of New York

nodes.label: Ruben L. F. Habito
nodes.summary: Ruben L. F. Habito is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Jikidō Takasaki. He held posts at Sophia University, Southern Methodist University, and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Yutai Ikeda
nodes.summary: Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Otani University and Doho University (~1968–2005), where he became emeritus professor.

nodes.label: Kenshi Kusano
nodes.summary: Kenshi Kusano specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from ~1971 to 1980 and served as a professor there around 2003.

nodes.label: Ryoen Minamoto
nodes.summary: Ryoen Minamoto was a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1947–1952), he held posts at Japan Women's University (~1964–1972), International Christian University (~1984–1991), and Tohoku University (Emeritus Professor ~1984–2020).

nodes.label: Shunsho Terakawa
nodes.summary: Shunsho Terakawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held an appointment at Otani University (~1965–2000), becoming professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Michael Jerryson
nodes.summary: Michael Jerryson specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. After undergraduate studies at Wisconsin-Madison, he earned his PhD at UC Santa Barbara under Mark Juergensmeyer. He taught at Eckerd College (~2009–2012) and Youngstown State University (~2012–2021).

nodes.label: Daniel W. Kent
nodes.summary: Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia. In 2010, he held posts as an instructor at both the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University.

nodes.label: Brian Daizen Victoria
variants: ブライアン・アンドレー・ヴィクトリア
nodes.jawiki: ブライアン・ヴィクトリア
nodes.summary: Brian Daizen Victoria works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. After studying at Komazawa and Temple universities, his career included posts at the University of Auckland, Antioch University, and a senior lectureship at the University of Adelaide (2005–2015).

nodes.label: Nebraska Wesleyan University
variants: ネブラスカ・ウェズリアン大学

nodes.label: Xue Yu
nodes.summary: Xue Yu is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. Yu served as assistant professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2010), visiting professor at the University of Chicago (attested 2026), and professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Nancy S. Steinhardt
nodes.image: Nancy Steinhardt Keynote for Whitworth University Library.jpg
nodes.summary: Nancy S. Steinhardt is a historian, archaeologist, and sinologist. Since ~1982, she has served at the University of Pennsylvania as Professor of East Asian Art and Curator of Chinese Art at the Penn Museum.

nodes.label: Baruch College
variants: Baruch College, City University of New York

nodes.label: Franz-Karl Ehrhard
nodes.summary: Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Resident Representative for the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and as Professor at the University of Munich (2003–2019).

nodes.label: Navina Lamminger
nodes.summary: Navina Lamminger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: Orna Almogi
nodes.summary: Orna Almogi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, and under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. She has held posts at the University of Hamburg and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Stacey Van Vleet
nodes.summary: Stacey Van Vleet specializes in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Sinology. She studied at the University of Colorado Boulder (MA), at Columbia University (PhD, attested 2006), and under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, later holding an attested post at Columbia in 2013.

nodes.label: Geoffrey Barstow
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Hampshire College, Kathmandu University, and the University of Virginia, also training under Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, and became assistant professor at Oregon State University around 2013.

nodes.label: Takao Moriyasu
nodes.summary: Takao Moriyasu was an Iranian, Central Asian, and history scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University. He held faculty posts at Kanazawa University, Osaka University (1984; 1994–2012), Kindai University, Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, and Toyo Bunko.

nodes.label: Tokio Takata
nodes.summary: Tokio Takata is a sinologist, linguist, and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS. He held faculty posts at Otaru University of Commerce (1981–1983), Kyoto University (1983, 1997–2014), and Fudan University (2016–2022).

nodes.label: Yutaka Yoshida
nodes.summary: Yutaka Yoshida (born 1954) studied at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Hitotsubashi (1983–2018), Kyoto University (~2006–2019), Center for Peace and Reconciliation (2008), and Center of the Tokyo Raids (2019).

nodes.label: James Burnell Robinson
nodes.summary: James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa (~1975-2013).

nodes.label: Cuong T. Mai
nodes.summary: Cuong T. Mai specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD under John R. McRae at Indiana University Bloomington, later serving as Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

nodes.label: Reiko Ohnuma
nodes.summary: Reiko Ohnuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at UC Berkeley and completed her Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez. She held posts at UT Austin, the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.

nodes.label: Gereon Kopf
nodes.summary: Gereon Kopf specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Temple University and mentored by Yasuo Yuasa, he researched at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan Universities and held posts at Luther College and the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: John C. Maraldo
nodes.summary: John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He held an academic post at the University of North Florida (attested 1988), where he became distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Seijun Ishii
nodes.summary: Seijun Ishii (born 1958) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University from ~1977 to 1981 and became a professor there around 2003.

variants: Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich (ETHZ)

Swiss Federal Institute of Technology at Zurich

variants: Purchase College, State University of New York

nodes.label: Stephen G. Covell
nodes.description: professor of world religions and cultures
nodes.summary: Stephen G. Covell specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his doctorate at Princeton University (~1995–2001) under Jacqueline I. Stone and held a post at Western Michigan University (~2003).

nodes.label: Wendi L. Adamek
nodes.summary: Wendi L. Adamek works in Buddhist studies and sinology. After earning a PhD from Stanford in 1998, she held posts at Barnard College and the University of Calgary, where she is a professor and Numata Chair holder.

nodes.label: Sadajiro Sugiura
nodes.summary: Sadajiro Sugiura was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D.), and Philadelphia Divinity School. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania, the Army War College, and Rikkyo University, succeeding Sakunoshin Motoda in 1923.

nodes.label: Bo Jiang
nodes.summary: Bo Jiang specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from Columbia University, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman.

nodes.label: Soochow University
variants: School of Foreign Languages, Soochow University

nodes.label: Mary Evelyn Tucker
nodes.summary: Mary Evelyn Tucker (b. 1949) specializes in religious studies, Sinology, and Japanology. She studied at SUNY Fredonia, Sophia, Fordham, and Columbia (PhD). She served as Professor of Religion at Bucknell (~1989–2006) before becoming a professor at Yale (~2006).

nodes.label: Zhiru Shi
nodes.summary: Zhiru Shi works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello. She held an associate professorship at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014) and adjunct faculty status at Fo Guang University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Donald Harper
nodes.summary: Donald Harper is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He held an appointment at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and serves as Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ryoshun Okubo
nodes.summary: Ryoshun Okubo studied at Waseda University, specializing in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Okubo became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism at Waseda University (~2000) and held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Phanindra Nath Bose
nodes.description: Bengali historian, writer and professor at Santiniketan

nodes.label: Shashibhusan Dasgupta
nodes.description: Scholar in philosophy, languages and literature, particularly Bengali literature, literary critic, author, theologian
nodes.summary: Shashibhusan Dasgupta (1911–1964) was an Indian philosopher, Indologist, and religious studies scholar. Educated at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta (MA, PhD), he lectured at the University of Calcutta from circa 1945 to 1964.

nodes.label: Dung Ngoc Duong
nodes.summary: Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Boston University in 2001 under the supervision of Malcolm David Eckel.

nodes.label: Dudjom Rinpoche
nodes.image: Dudjom Rinpoche with Prince Paljor Namgyal and Maharani Kunzang Dechen Tshomo Namgyal.jpg
nodes.summary: Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jampal Delek Nyima, Min Ling Orgyen Namdrol Gyatso, and Pé Kö Lama Könchok Rabten, and taught numerous students, including Keith Dowman and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Antoine Lutz
nodes.summary: Antoine Lutz completed his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the doctoral supervision of Francisco J. Varela.

nodes.label: Christine Mollier
nodes.summary: Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié. She held researcher and Director of Research posts at CNRS and was a visiting professor at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Jacques Giès
nodes.summary: Jacques Giès (1950–2021) specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate from Paris-Sorbonne University under Flora Blanchon, taught at Paris-Sorbonne (1974–1998) and the École du Louvre (1998–2008), and served as president of the Musée Guimet (2008–2011).

nodes.label: Dzongsar Institute
variants: Dzongsar Institute for Advanced Studies of Buddhist Philosophy and Research in Bir, India
Dzongsar Institute of Advanced Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: James Leibold
nodes.summary: James Leibold is a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Southern California under Charlotte Furth and has held academic posts at the University of Melbourne and La Trobe University.

nodes.label: Charlotte Furth
nodes.summary: Charlotte Furth (1934–2022) was a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. She held professorial posts at California State University (~1969–1989) and the University of Southern California (~1989–2008).

nodes.label: Kumbum Monastery
variants: クンブム・チャンパーリン寺

nodes.label: Dhivan Thomas Jones
nodes.summary: Dhivan Thomas Jones is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He held positions at the Open University (attested 2017) and the University of Chester (2019).

nodes.label: Shan Shan Zhao
nodes.summary: Shan Shan Zhao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed a Master of Arts degree at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

nodes.label: Mark Rowe
nodes.summary: Mark Rowe is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has served as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at McMaster University (attested 2015, 2026).

nodes.label: St Edmund's College, Cambridge
variants: St. Edmunds College, University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Margaret Gouin
nodes.summary: Margaret Gouin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Paul Williams.

nodes.label: Thinh Canh Quang
nodes.summary: Thinh Canh Quang, working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed a PhD at the University of the West (attested 2007) supervised by Kottegoda Warnasuriya, having also studied under Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge.

nodes.label: Noa Ronkin
nodes.summary: Noa Ronkin specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She studied at Wolfson College, Oxford, earning a D.Phil. in 2003 under Richard Gombrich, and learned under Shlomo Biderman. She has served as a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University.

nodes.label: Patricia Buckley Ebrey
nodes.summary: Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and Sinologist who studied at the University of Chicago and Columbia University. She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the Institute for Advanced Study (1998), and the University of Washington (1997–2020).

nodes.label: Kate Wharton
nodes.summary: Kate Wharton works in philosophy and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London in 2008 and held a post at Birkbeck, University of London (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Peter Fenner
nodes.summary: Peter Fenner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held a post at Deakin University. He studied under advisers Noble Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, as well as traditional teacher Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Lindsay G. McCune
nodes.summary: Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She completed an MA under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas and studied under Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.

nodes.label: Nancy G. Lin
nodes.summary: Nancy G. Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley (PhD), and holds an endowed professorship in Buddhist chaplaincy and Tibetan and South Asian studies at the Numata Center (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hermann Kulke
nodes.summary: Hermann Kulke is an historian and Indologist who studied at Madras, Freiburg, and Heidelberg, where he studied under Hermann Goetz. He held faculty posts at Heidelberg University (1967–1988) and Kiel University (1988–2003).

nodes.label: Emanuel Sarkisyanz
nodes.summary: Emanuel Sarkisyanz (1923–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tehran and University of Chicago (PhD ~1948–1952), and became Head of the Political Science Department at Heidelberg University in 1967.

nodes.label: Werner Sundermann
nodes.summary: Werner Sundermann worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1967–1970), the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1970–1992), and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).

nodes.summary: Yanling Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA from Fo Guang University (attested 2012) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi, and also studied under Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Agehananda Bharati
nodes.summary: Agehananda Bharati was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1945–1948), taught across India and Japan in the 1950s, and was Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

nodes.label: Ron Leifer
nodes.summary: Ron Leifer was an author and psychiatrist active in Buddhist studies. He studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and with the traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (1924–2019) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Thrangu Monastery and under Khenpo Gangshar and the 8th Traleg Rinpoche, later teaching at Rumtek Monastery (1967) and serving as abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra (1978).

nodes.label: Tessa Bartholomeusz
nodes.summary: Tessa Bartholomeusz (1958–2001) specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Florida, Florida State, and Virginia (PhD 1991), and held posts at Virginia, Florida State (1993), and Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis (c. 1991–2001).

nodes.label: Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis
variants: Indiana University Herron School of Art and Design

nodes.label: Krishnanath Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Krishnanath Chatterjee is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under teachers including Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

nodes.label: Ramaranjan Mukherji
nodes.summary: Ramaranjan Mukherji was an Indologist educated at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. He served as Head of Sanskrit at Jadavpur, vice chancellor at Burdwan (1970–1984) and Rabindra Bharati (~1984–1987), and chancellor of National Sanskrit University (~2006–2010).

nodes.label: J. P. Mallory
nodes.summary: Specializing in linguistics, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, J. P. Mallory studied at Occidental College and UCLA. He served on the faculty at Queen's University Belfast (~1977–2011) and as Professor of Prehistoric Archaeology at Queen's University at Kingston (attested 2014).

nodes.label: James Matthew Baskind
nodes.summary: James Matthew Baskind specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Yale University under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein, attested in 2006.

nodes.label: Katsuhiro Yoshizawa
nodes.summary: Katsuhiro Yoshizawa (born 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University (~1964–1968) and served as a professor at Hanazono University around 1999.

nodes.label: Tsuneki Nishiwaki
nodes.summary: Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1963–1967). He held posts at Doshisha University (~1974–1990) and as professor at Kyoto University (~1990–2007).

nodes.label: Tom De Rauw
nodes.summary: Tom De Rauw is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Ann Heirman. He held an AAP post at Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Anthony Cerulli
nodes.summary: Anthony Cerulli is a scholar of indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Chicago from 2001 to 2007. Around 2014, he served as Professor of South Asian Studies and Director of Graduate Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: C. Pierce Salguero
nodes.description: professor of Asian history and religious studies
nodes.summary: C. Pierce Salguero is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University, later holding posts at Pennsylvania State University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Penn State Abington (~2011).

nodes.label: Christoph Kleine
nodes.description: German japanologist and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Christoph Kleine (born 1962) specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his MA, PhD, and Habilitation at the University of Marburg, and held posts at EFEO, Hōbōgirin, Marburg, Munich (2004–2008), and Leipzig (2002–2005; 2008).

nodes.label: Mervin Viggo Hanson
nodes.summary: Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1980), having also studied under Kathryn A. Cissell.

nodes.label: Kendall R. Marchman
nodes.summary: Kendall R. Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under Mario Poceski and completed his PhD at the University of Florida in 2015.

nodes.label: Si Ti La
nodes.summary: Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014). They also studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala and Sayadaw U Ghosita.

nodes.label: Osvald Sirén
nodes.summary: Osvald Sirén was a Sinologist and art historian who completed his doctorate at the University of Helsinki. He was a professor at Stockholm University (1908–1923), lectured at Harvard and Yale, and served as a curator at Paris's Musée Guimet and Stockholm's Nationalmuseum.

nodes.label: Erik-Jan Zürcher
nodes.summary: Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian and linguist who completed his BA and PhD at Leiden University. He held positions at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), the International Institute of Social History (1990–1999, 2008–2012), and Leiden University (from 1997).

nodes.label: Soko Morinaga
nodes.summary: Soko Morinaga worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Toyama High School and Daitoku-ji under Sesso Oda and Zuigan Goto, later serving as abbot at Daishuin (~1963–1995) and head of Hanazono University (1986–1994).

variants: College of the City of New York
City College in New York City

nodes.label: Arthur Hilary Armstrong
nodes.summary: Philosopher Arthur Hilary Armstrong studied at Jesus College, Cambridge. He taught at Swansea, the University of Malta, Beaumont College, and Cardiff, before serving as Gladstone Professor of Greek at the University of Liverpool (1950–1972).

nodes.label: Joseph Loizzo
nodes.summary: Joseph Loizzo specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College and Harvard University, and under Robert A. F. Thurman and Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche. He was a visiting scholar at Columbia University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science
variants: Nalanda Institute for Meditation and Healing

nodes.label: Kennard Lipman
nodes.summary: Kennard Lipman specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther and worked as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

nodes.label: Paul Rouzer
nodes.summary: Paul Rouzer is a scholar in the fields of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held attested academic appointments at Harvard University and the University of Minnesota in 2007.

nodes.label: Namgyal Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Namgyal Rinpoche (1931–2003) was a Buddhist studies teacher who studied at Jarvis Baptist Seminary, University of Michigan, and under traditional teachers Sayadaw U Thila Wunta, Mahasi Sayadaw, Chao Khun Phra Rajasiddhimuni, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1965) and the Dharma Centre of Canada (1966).

nodes.label: Sun-Ah Choi
nodes.summary: Sun-Ah Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at the University of Chicago, supervised by Juhyung Rhi and taught by Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

nodes.label: Robert S. Nelson
nodes.summary: Robert S. Nelson is an art historian and archaeologist who studied at Rice University and New York University. He held posts as professor at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and later at Yale University (~2005–2021).

nodes.label: Jaś Elsner
nodes.summary: Jaś Elsner works in archaeology and religious studies, earning a BA and PhD at King's College, Cambridge. He held positions at the Courtauld Institute, Corpus Christi College, Oxford (1999), and Oxford University as Professor of Late Antique Art (2014).

nodes.label: Aden Kumler
nodes.summary: Aden Kumler is an art historian who studied at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto, Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies, and Harvard University. She served as Assistant Professor at the University of Chicago (2007) and Professor of Older Art History at the University of Basel (2020).

nodes.label: Katherine R. Tsiang
nodes.summary: Katherine R. Tsiang is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the University of Chicago, attested in 2012 and as a faculty member in 2026.

nodes.label: Carl Gustav Jung
nodes.jawiki: カール・グスタフ・ユング
nodes.summary: Carl Gustav Jung (1875–1961) was a Swiss scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned a medical degree at the University of Basel. He held posts at the University of Zurich, ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and the University of Basel (1944).

nodes.label: Erwin Rousselle
nodes.summary: Erwin Rousselle specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies, earning doctorates at Heidelberg and habilitating at TU Darmstadt. He held professorships at Peking University and Tsinghua University, directed the Sino-Indian Institute, and held multiple appointments at Goethe University Frankfurt.

nodes.label: Richard Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Richard Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Tübingen (~1891–1895). He was a visiting professor at Peking University in 1923 and held the chair in Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt starting in 1924.

nodes.label: David L. Gosling
nodes.summary: David L. Gosling is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992 and was affiliated with the University of Cambridge in 2001.

nodes.label: Ramin Etesami

nodes.label: Benjamin Brose
nodes.description: American cultural historian of religion in China
nodes.summary: Benjamin Brose specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his Ph.D. at Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and became an assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan circa 2009.

nodes.label: Erik J. Hammerstrom
nodes.summary: Erik J. Hammerstrom is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010) and served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Randy J. LaPolla
nodes.summary: Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist and sinologist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley (1983–1990) under James A. Matisoff (~1985–1990). He served as professor at the City University of Hong Kong (~1996–2004) and joined Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai in 2021.

nodes.label: Tak Pui Sze
nodes.summary: Tak Pui Sze works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Sze pursued a PhD at the University of British Columbia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Mungunchimeg Batmunkh
nodes.summary: Mungunchimeg Batmunkh earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall (attested 2010), working in religious studies and Buddhist studies.

nodes.label: Brigitte Marschall
nodes.summary: Brigitte Marschall studied at the University of Vienna, where she earned her doctorate (Promotion) and later served as an extraordinary university professor (außerordentliche Universitätsprofessorin).

nodes.label: Guo Jun
nodes.summary: Guo Jun, active in Buddhist studies, studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, and trained under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin. He served as abbot of Maha Bodhi Monastery in Singapore (attested 2013).

nodes.label: George Lakoff
variants: ジョージ・P・レイコフ
nodes.summary: George Lakoff is a linguist and philosopher who studied at MIT and earned his doctorate at Indiana University. He taught linguistics at Harvard University (1965–1969) and served as a professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley (1972–2016).

nodes.label: Mark Johnson
nodes.jawiki: マーク・ジョンソン (哲学者)

nodes.label: Glenn Wallis
nodes.summary: Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter, and taught Sonam Kachru.

nodes.label: Alexander Berzin
nodes.summary: Alexander Berzin (born 1944) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard (PhD), studying under Masatoshi Nagatomi. From ~1972 to 1998, he was a founding member of the translation bureau at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

nodes.label: Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Ganden Monastery, earning a Geshe Lharampa degree. He held a post at Ganden Jangtse Monastery and taught the 14th Dalai Lama, Alexander Berzin, Joseph Loizzo, and Thubten Chodron.

nodes.label: Shikaripur N. Sridhar

nodes.label: Charles Taliaferro
nodes.summary: Charles Taliaferro (born 1952) is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College, Harvard Divinity School, the University of Rhode Island, and Brown University, and served as a professor at St. Olaf College (~1985–2022).

nodes.label: Charlene E. Makley
nodes.summary: Charlene E. Makley works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan in 1999 under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport, and has served as an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

nodes.label: Roy Rappaport
nodes.summary: Roy Rappaport was a scholar of religious studies who completed his doctorate at Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) as Chair of the Department of Anthropology.

nodes.label: Marco Walther
nodes.summary: Marco Walther is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: Jamie Hubbard
nodes.summary: Jamie Hubbard is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Kazuo Okabe and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held endowed professorships at Smith College, attested in 2016 and 2026.

nodes.label: Fung Kei Cheng
nodes.summary: Fung Kei Cheng specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Samson Tse at the University of Hong Kong, where he earned a Doctor of Philosophy (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Cécile Ducher
nodes.summary: Cécile Ducher specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD under Matthew T. Kapstein at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (-2017), where she is a research fellow.

nodes.label: Nicholas Justin Allen
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, Allen studied at Oxford and SOAS under Rodney Needham. He taught at Durham University (1972–1976) and Oxford, serving as Lecturer and later Reader in the Social Anthropology of South Asia.

nodes.label: Charles Taylor
nodes.jawiki: チャールズ・マーグレイヴ・テイラー
nodes.summary: Charles Taylor (born 1931) is a philosopher who studied at Selwyn House School, McGill University (~1948–1952), and Balliol College, Oxford (~1952–1955). He held faculty posts at McGill University (~1961–1998), the University of Montreal (~1967–1971), and Northwestern University (~2002–2008).

nodes.label: Zhiru Ng
nodes.summary: Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello.

nodes.label: Bryan W. Van Norden
nodes.summary: Bryan W. Van Norden specializes in philosophy and Sinology. He studied at Stanford University (~1985–1991) and served as a professor in the philosophy and Chinese & Japanese departments at Vassar College (~1996–2021).

nodes.label: Chi-wah Chan
nodes.summary: Chi-wah Chan works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Chan earned a PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles in 1993, having studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, and served as a Teaching Assistant at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Patrice Ladwig
nodes.summary: Patrice Ladwig is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

nodes.label: G. C. Nayak
nodes.summary: G. C. Nayak was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study and as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research in 1996.

nodes.label: Stephen J. Laumakis
nodes.summary: Stephen J. Laumakis specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, George J. Tanabe, and David West. He serves as Professor of Philosophy at the University of St. Thomas (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Sharon J. Roe

nodes.label: Shin'ichi Yoshinaga

nodes.summary: Christian Bernert is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

nodes.label: Hugh J. Silverman
nodes.summary: Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who completed a doctorate at Stanford (~1969–1973). He was a professor at Stony Brook University (1974) and held posts at Stanford (~1972–1974), University of Vienna (2000–2001), and Academy of Fine Arts Vienna (2009–2010).

nodes.label: Heeraman Tiwari
nodes.summary: Heeraman Tiwari is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the universities of Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He held positions at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~2000), Heidelberg University (2011–2012), and the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (2014–2015).

nodes.label: Lang Chen
nodes.summary: Lang Chen specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Chen completed a PhD at Yale University, studying with doctoral supervisors Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff as well as teacher Janet Gyatso.

nodes.label: Matthew Orsborn
nodes.summary: Matthew Orsborn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Guang Xing and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. In 2026, he was attested as professor and head of international affairs at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.summary: Sogyal Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Cambridge, and under traditional teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

nodes.label: Pham Thi Tuyet Tam
nodes.summary: Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, studying under supervisors Phra Maha Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Hansa Dhammahaso
nodes.summary: Hansa Dhammahaso is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as director at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and the International Buddhist Studies College, both attested in 2017.

nodes.label: Markus Viehbeck
nodes.summary: Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, worked as a researcher at Heidelberg University, and serves on the faculty at Vienna.

nodes.label: David R. Kinsley
nodes.summary: David R. Kinsley (1939–2000) was an Indologist and scholar of religion. He studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, and spent his career on the faculty at McMaster University (1969–2000).

nodes.label: Bihani Sarkar

nodes.label: Liang Cai

nodes.label: Kenneth Doo Young Lee

nodes.label: D. Phillip Stanley

nodes.label: Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Educated at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University, he studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and directed the Nitartha Institute and Kamalashila Institute.

nodes.label: Ethan Tischler
nodes.summary: Ethan Tischler specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan University, earning his BA under advisor Mary-Jane Rubenstein as attested in 2014.

nodes.label: W. F. Jayasuriya
nodes.summary: W. F. Jayasuriya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

nodes.label: Beata Grant
nodes.summary: Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. at Stanford University. She was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley and served as Associate Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Washington University in St. Louis.

nodes.label: Weiru Guan
nodes.summary: Weiru Guan specializes in Buddhist studies. Guan earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Mahasi Sayadaw
nodes.native: မဟာစည်ဆရာတော်
nodes.summary: Mahasi Sayadaw (1904–1982) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Aletawya Sayadaw, Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw U Narada, and Thelon Sayadaw. He was abbot of Mawlamyine Monastery (1941), resident teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha (1947), and founded the Insight Meditation Society (1979).

nodes.label: Vishwanathan Venkatachalam
nodes.summary: Indologist Vishwanathan Venkatachalam (1925–2002) studied at Madras, Nagpur, and Vikram universities. He directed the Scindia Oriental Institute, headed Sanskrit at Vikram University, served as vice-chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University, and chaired the ICPR.

nodes.label: Joanna Cook
nodes.summary: Joanna Cook is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under advisor James Laidlaw and held a post at Christ's College, University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Edo Shonin
nodes.summary: Edo Shonin works in religious studies and related fields. In 2015, he was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and as Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

nodes.label: William Van Gordon
nodes.summary: William Van Gordon is a researcher in religious and Buddhist studies. He founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and served as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Nirbhay N. Singh
nodes.summary: Nirbhay N. Singh works in Buddhist studies. He served as Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, Professor of Psychiatry, Pediatrics, and Psychology at Virginia Commonwealth University, and Clinical Professor at Augusta University (attested 2015–2018).

nodes.id: I:Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research
nodes.label: Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research
variants: Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research

nodes.label: Mark D. Griffiths
nodes.summary: Mark D. Griffiths (born 1966) earned a BSc from the University of Bradford and a PhD from the University of Exeter (1988–1990). He lectured at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) and became Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).

nodes.label: Charles Gabriel Seligman
nodes.summary: Charles Gabriel Seligman studied medicine at St Thomas' Hospital Medical School. From 1913 to 1934, he held the chair of Ethnology at the London School of Economics and the University of London.

nodes.label: James C. Dobbins
nodes.summary: James C. Dobbins specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at Yale University in 1984 and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015-2019).

nodes.label: Francis Harold Cook
nodes.summary: Francis Harold Cook is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral requirements at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970). He was a professor at the University of California, Riverside (~1970–1987) and chaired the Numata Center in 1999.

nodes.label: Taitetsu Unno
nodes.summary: Taitetsu Unno specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and earned an M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Tokyo, later serving at Smith College from 1971 to 1998.

nodes.label: Joshua W. C. Cutler
nodes.summary: Joshua W. C. Cutler specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. A student of Geshe Wangyal, he held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center, attested in 2004.

nodes.label: Anna Sawerthal
nodes.summary: Anna Sawerthal is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Johanna Buß, and completed a PhD at Heidelberg University, also studying with Dawa Tsering and Norbu Tashi.

nodes.label: Lauran R. Hartley
nodes.summary: Lauran R. Hartley is a Tibetologist who held positions at Indiana University Bloomington, Rutgers University, and the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library. As of 2026, she is Adjunct Assistant Professor and Modern Tibetan Studies Program Director at Columbia University.

nodes.label: Ann Appleby Hazlewood
nodes.summary: Ann Appleby Hazlewood worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a Master of Arts at the Australian National University (attested 1983), where she studied under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.

nodes.label: Nika Jovic
nodes.summary: Nika Jovic is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna (attested 2010), where she was supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes, and was taught by Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007–2008).

nodes.label: Conor Roddy
nodes.summary: Conor Roddy is a philosopher who completed a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011), having studied under teachers Arindam Chakrabarti and Roger T. Ames.

nodes.label: John W. Pettit
nodes.summary: John W. Pettit is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College, studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and completed doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman.

nodes.label: Haverford College
variants: Margaret Gest Center for the Cross-Cultural Study of Religion at Haverford

nodes.label: Lal Mani Joshi
nodes.summary: Lal Mani Joshi worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology, earning his PhD under Govind Chandra Pande at Gorakhpur University. He taught at Gorakhpur and Punjabi University, with visiting posts at Harvard, Amherst, Haverford, and CIHTS.

nodes.label: Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa
nodes.summary: Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught John W. Pettit.

nodes.label: New College of Florida
variants: New College of the University of South Florida

nodes.label: Rongdao Lai
nodes.summary: Rongdao Lai works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She received her PhD from McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates (attested 2013) and was appointed assistant professor there (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Robin D. S. Yates
nodes.summary: Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1975–1980) and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University (~2005).

nodes.label: Zhenhua
nodes.summary: Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tianning Buddhist Institute (1947) and under Yinshun (1952). He managed the Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992) and taught Chien Y. Hsu.

nodes.label: Robert Baker Aitken
nodes.summary: Robert Baker Aitken (1917–2010) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi, UC Berkeley, and Ryutaku-ji under teachers including Suzuki, Blyth, and Senzaki, later serving at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1958–1969).

nodes.label: Bruno Dagens
nodes.summary: Bruno Dagens was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the EFEO (1969), KU Leuven (1972–1977), French Institute of Pondicherry (1977), and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1986).

nodes.label: Constance Powell Chin
nodes.summary: Constance Powell Chin is an archaeologist and religious studies scholar who earned a master's degree at San Jose State University by 2012, having studied under Christian Luczanits.

nodes.label: Benjamin Wood
nodes.summary: Benjamin Wood specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett, and also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Shayne Clarke (2011), and Thupten Champa.

nodes.label: Donald Keene
nodes.summary: Donald Keene was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University and Harvard University, learning under William Theodore de Bary. He held appointments at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University from 1955.

nodes.label: Peipei Qiu
nodes.summary: Peipei Qiu is a scholar of Japanology and sinology. She studied at Peking University and Columbia University under Donald Keene and Paul Rouzer, and held an academic post at Vassar College, attested in 2005.

nodes.label: Kathleen M. Erndl
nodes.summary: Kathleen M. Erndl (1954–2017) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held posts at DePauw University, UW-Madison, Lewis & Clark College (~1987–1993), and Florida State University as Associate Professor of Religion (~1993–2017).

nodes.label: Allan G. Grapard
nodes.summary: Allan G. Grapard specialized in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. at INALCO (~1971–1978) and held professorships at the University of California, Santa Barbara (1985) and the University of California (~1986–2009).

nodes.label: Dennis Hudson
nodes.summary: Dennis Hudson was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who taught in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College, attested between 1987 and 2000.

nodes.label: Dominique-Sila Khan
nodes.summary: Dominique-Sila Khan was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University. She served as a research fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies from circa 1993 to 2016.

nodes.label: June McDaniel
nodes.summary: June McDaniel specializes in Indology and religious studies, earning an MTS from Emory University and a Ph.D. from the University of Chicago. She has held posts at the College of Charleston, attested in 2000 and 2015 as a professor.

nodes.label: Yu-Chen Tsui
nodes.summary: Yu-Chen Tsui works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Tsui completed master's studies at Columbia University supervised by Chün-fang Yü, pursued doctoral studies supervised by Natasha Heller (attested 2018), and had Sheng Yen as a traditional teacher.

nodes.label: Dermott Joseph Walsh
nodes.summary: Dermott Joseph Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (BA) and Leiden University (MA) before earning his PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles in 2018 under William M. Bodiford.

nodes.label: C. D. Sebastian
nodes.summary: C. D. Sebastian specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, studied under Paul Williams, Gavin D'Costa, Ashok Kumar Chatterjee, and Abhimanyu Singh, and became Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Gavin D'Costa
nodes.summary: Gavin D'Costa works in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Cambridge and at the University of Birmingham under John Hick (~1981–1985). He taught at West London Institute (~1985–1990) and became Emeritus Professor of Catholic Theology at Bristol (1993).

nodes.label: Ashok Kumar Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Ashok Kumar Chatterjee studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti. He served as professor and head of the philosophy department at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and at Banaras Hindu University (1963–1985).

nodes.label: Dennis A. Johnson
nodes.summary: Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Hiroko Kawanami
nodes.summary: Hiroko Kawanami is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott, and taught Shi Jiancheng. She held an appointment as senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).

nodes.label: Alfred Gell
nodes.summary: Alfred Gell studied at the University of Cambridge (~1965–1967) under Edmund Ronald Leach and earned his Ph.D. at LSE (~1968–1972). He taught at the University of Sussex (~1971–1974), Australian National University (1974–1979), and LSE (from 1979).

nodes.label: John Okell
nodes.summary: John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, and under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. He served as a research associate at SOAS University of London (1959–1999).

nodes.label: Sunhee Kim
nodes.summary: Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the supervision of Phillip B. Zarrilli (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Nancy McCagney
nodes.summary: Nancy McCagney is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson. She held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Jeong-Eun Kim
nodes.summary: Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Kim earned a PhD from SOAS University of London (-2011), studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

nodes.label: Giovanni Verardi
nodes.summary: Giovanni Verardi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Banaras Hindu, Gorakhpur, and Allahabad universities. He held academic posts at Ca' Foscari University of Venice, the University of Bologna, and as professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale."

nodes.label: Hiroshi Aoyagi
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Aoyagi (born 1957) specializes in linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University (~1980–1986) and the University of Southern California (PhD, ~1990–1998), later becoming a professor at Nanzan University (~2005).

nodes.label: Antonio Terrone
nodes.summary: Antonio Terrone is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and has served as scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

nodes.summary: Nicolas Sihlé is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He served as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Somboon Watana
nodes.native: สมบูรณ์ วัฒนะ
nodes.summary: Somboon Watana works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Panjab University (1999) under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma, and is an assistant professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Tulku Sherdor
nodes.summary: Tulku Sherdor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, and under Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Ted Norton, and Jeffrey Hopkins.

nodes.label: Yuko Matsuda
nodes.summary: Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held an affiliation with Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, attested in 2001.

nodes.label: Natalie Gummer
nodes.summary: Natalie Gummer is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She held a post at Harvard University (attested 2001) and became a professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

nodes.label: Barbara Gerke
nodes.summary: Barbara Gerke is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel, later working at Humboldt University of Berlin (2011–2015), Oxford (attested 2017), and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

variants: Centre for the Study of Developing Societies

nodes.label: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt
nodes.summary: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, and Marburg, and has held posts as Käthe-Leichter-Gastprofessorin at the University of Vienna (~2002–2003) and Privatdozentin at the University of Marburg (2009).

nodes.label: Huidi Zeng
nodes.summary: Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Yi-hsun Huang
nodes.summary: Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner.

nodes.label: Richard A. Gard
nodes.summary: Richard A. Gard (1914–2007) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at the Institute for the Advanced Study of World Religions and was its director (attested 1982–1989).

nodes.id: I:Institute for the Advanced Study of World Religions
nodes.label: Institute for the Advanced Study of World Religions
variants: Institute for the Advanced Study of World Religions

nodes.label: Alexander Kabanoff
nodes.summary: Alexander Kabanoff (1952–2000) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2000, he was a Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Phra Medhidhammaporn
nodes.summary: Phra Medhidhammaporn studied Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis in 1985 at the University of Delhi under Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

nodes.label: David Azzopardi
nodes.summary: David Azzopardi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. As attested in 2010, he completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby.

nodes.label: János Szerb
nodes.summary: János Szerb was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Eötvös Loránd University. He later worked as a research associate and lecturer at the University of Vienna and as a Buddhist studies researcher at IKGA.

nodes.label: Kurt Tropper
nodes.summary: Kurt Tropper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held posts as a Vertragsassistent at the University of Vienna and at the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Ñāṇavīra Thera
nodes.summary: Ñāṇavīra Thera (1920–1965) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge. He later trained under traditional teachers Pelene Siri Vajiragnana and Nyanatiloka Mahathera, and served in the Royal Artillery and Intelligence Corps.

nodes.label: Pelene Siri Vajiragnana
variants: Pälänē Siri Vajirañāņa Mahā Nāyaka Thera

nodes.label: Louis Komjathy
nodes.summary: Louis Komjathy specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Boston University under Paul Rouzer and served as Assistant Professor of Chinese Religions and Comparative Religious Studies at the University of San Diego (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Heng Sure
nodes.summary: Heng Sure specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD under Ronald Y. Nakasone), and has held professorships at the Graduate Theological Union, Bond University, and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.

nodes.label: Edmond Yee
nodes.summary: Edmond Yee works in religious studies and sinology. He served on the faculty at both the Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union from ~1986 to 2008.

nodes.label: Niras Ruangsan
nodes.summary: Niras Ruangsan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Sydney (attested 2015) under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.

nodes.label: Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle
nodes.summary: Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994) and held a post at the University of Sydney.

nodes.label: G. Clinton Godart
nodes.summary: G. Clinton Godart works in Japanology, philosophy, and history. He completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago under James Edward Ketelaar, held postdoctoral posts at Needham Research Institute and Cambridge, and later worked at USC and Hokkaido University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Chien-hsing Ho
nodes.summary: Chien-hsing Ho specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Ho served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Charles B. Jones
nodes.summary: Charles B. Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology who earned his PhD in History of Religions under Paul Groner at the University of Virginia. He served as Associate Professor and Associate Dean at the Catholic University of America.

nodes.label: Technical University of Berlin
variants: ベルリンのシャルロッテンブルク工科大学

nodes.label: David Sneath
nodes.summary: David Sneath is an Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Cambridge by 1991, held a fellowship at Oxford, and served as Director at Cambridge until 2009.

nodes.label: Hürelbaatar Ujeed
nodes.summary: Hürelbaatar Ujeed specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge, where he held a post (attested 2010), and became Professor at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

nodes.label: Dairyu Michael Wenger
nodes.summary: Dairyu Michael Wenger (born 1947) studied at The New School and under Sojun Mel Weitsman. A Buddhist studies scholar, he served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at the San Francisco Zen Center (~1984–1992) and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center.

nodes.label: Ralph Abraham
nodes.summary: Ralph Abraham (1936–2024) was a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts at Berkeley, Columbia, and Princeton before joining UC Santa Cruz as professor (1968, 1980).

nodes.label: Sisir Roy
nodes.summary: Sisir Roy is a scholar in philosophy and other fields who studied under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts as a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute and at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Ajahn Brahm
nodes.summary: Ajahn Brahm specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Emmanuel College, Cambridge (~1969–1972) and trained under Nai Boonman and Ajahn Chah (1974), later becoming the abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery in ~1995.

nodes.label: Terese Tse Bartholomew
nodes.summary: Terese Tse Bartholomew is a specialist in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology who earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles. She served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum.

nodes.label: Ryan Anningson
nodes.summary: Ryan Anningson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed studies at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2017) under the supervision of Jason Neelis.

nodes.label: Mireille Helffer
nodes.summary: Mireille Helffer (1928–2023) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and other fields. She served as Chargé de Recherche at CNRS (~1967–1989) and was affiliated with Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).

nodes.label: Dawa Norbu
nodes.summary: Dawa Norbu was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Delhi, St. Stephen's College, and UC Berkeley. He taught at several institutions in San Francisco before serving as professor of Central Asian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1987–2004).

nodes.label: Nawang Tsering
nodes.summary: Nawang Tsering is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under doctoral supervisor Lal Mani Joshi. He served as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).

nodes.label: Hsuan Hua
nodes.summary: Hsuan Hua was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Chang Chih/Chang Zhi (~1936–1946) and Hsu Yun (1948). He served as Abbot of Tathagata Monastery (~1976–1995) and founded the Buddhist Text Translation Society in 1970.

nodes.label: Hsu Yun
nodes.summary: Hsu Yun was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Changkai (~1858–1859), Miaolian (~1859), and Yaocheng. He founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1953, where he served as honorary chairman.

Gomang College of Drepung Monastic University

nodes.label: Chien Y. Hsu
nodes.summary: Chien Y. Hsu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies under Leslie S. Kawamura (through 2011) and James B. Apple, and studied under the traditional teacher Zhenhua (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Joseph D. Markowski
nodes.summary: Joseph D. Markowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his Master of Arts at McGill University, where he studied under supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Peter Francis Kornicki
nodes.summary: Peter Francis Kornicki (b. 1950) studied at Oxford (Lincoln and St Antony's colleges), Tokyo University of Education, and under Masamichi Asukai and Mitsukuni Yoshida. He taught at the University of Tasmania (1978–1982), Kyoto University (~1982–1985), and the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Rosemary Radford Ruether
nodes.summary: Rosemary Radford Ruether was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. She studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1960–1965) and held an academic post at Howard University from ~1965 to 1975.

nodes.label: E. W. Adikaram
nodes.summary: E. W. Adikaram was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Wesley College, the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede, later serving as principal of Ananda Sastralaya in 1934.

nodes.label: Arthur Philip McKeown
nodes.summary: Arthur Philip McKeown specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2005), where he studied under Parimal G. Patil, Pelri Sanggye, and Diana L. Eck.

nodes.label: Ruth Denison
nodes.description: Western Theravada meditation teacher resided in USA (1922-2015)

nodes.label: Polly Young-Eisendrath
nodes.summary: Polly Young-Eisendrath is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Ohio University, Goddard College, and Washington University in St. Louis, underwent Zen training under Philip Kapleau, and became clinical associate professor of psychiatry at the University of Vermont in 1994.

nodes.label: Hayao Kawai
nodes.summary: Hayao Kawai worked in religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1952), taught at Tenri University (~1962–1972), served as professor at Kyoto University (~1972–1992), and was director general of the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1995–2001).

nodes.label: Moriya Okano
nodes.summary: Moriya Okano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Kanto Gakuin University. He has held positions at Musashino University and as director of the Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies.
