variants: Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies

nodes.label: Yasuo Deguchi
nodes.summary: Yasuo Deguchi is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He taught at Nagoya Institute of Technology and held multiple posts at Kyoto University, including professor and dean, later joining ZEN University and founding the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy.

nodes.label: Constance Kassor
nodes.summary: Constance Kassor is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. After earning a BA at Smith College and a PhD at Emory University under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, she joined the Smith College faculty (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Karin Meyers
nodes.summary: Karin Meyers works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Jay L. Garfield and served at Kathmandu University as an assistant professor and director of the MA program in Buddhist studies at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Eyal Aviv
nodes.summary: Eyal Aviv is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisors Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

nodes.label: Annette Baier
nodes.summary: Annette Baier was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago (circa 1946–1952) and Somerville College (PhD 1952). She taught at Carnegie Mellon University (circa 1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh's philosophy department (circa 1973–1995).

nodes.label: Wilfrid Sellars
variants: ウィルフリド・ストーカー・セラーズ
nodes.jawiki: ウィルフリド・セラーズ
nodes.summary: Wilfrid Sellars was a philosopher who studied at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the University of Iowa (1938–1946), the University of Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale University (1958–1963), and held a professorship at Pittsburgh (1963–1989).

nodes.label: Zuicho Tachibana
nodes.summary: Zuicho Tachibana (1890–1968) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He studied under Kozui Otani (~1903–1914) and Edward Denison Ross (~1908–1910).

nodes.label: Ines Konczak
nodes.summary: Ines Konczak is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. She has held posts as a postdoctoral research fellow at the Berlin State Museums and as a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University in 2012.

nodes.label: Angela Falco Howard
nodes.summary: Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and art history/archaeology. She completed her doctoral dissertation at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and served as a professor at Rutgers University (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Vignato
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Vignato is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He pursued doctoral studies at Peking University under teachers including Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Bai Su, and Shichang Ma, and later held a post at Peking University.

nodes.label: Bai Su
nodes.summary: Bai Su worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Peking University under Chengjun Feng, Zuoyun Sun, Rong Geng, and Yongtong Tang, and served as a professor at Peking University from 1948 to 2004.

nodes.label: Shichang Ma
nodes.summary: Shichang Ma (born 1938) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and archaeology. He served as a Buddhist archaeology researcher at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and joined the Archaeology Department at Peking University in 1982.

nodes.label: Max Oidtmann
nodes.summary: Max Oidtmann works in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology. Educated at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard under Mark Elliott, he held posts at Georgetown University, Georgetown University in Qatar, and became a professor at the University of Munich around 2020.

nodes.label: Gustav Haloun
nodes.summary: Gustav Haloun was a sinologist who studied under August Conrady at Leipzig and completed his habilitation at Prague. He directed at Göttingen (1931–1938) and served as Chair of Chinese Language and History at Cambridge (1938–1951).

nodes.label: Jotika Khur-Yearn
nodes.summary: Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Rangama Chandawimala
nodes.summary: Rangama Chandawimala specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliya Anuruddha, also studying under Attaragama Gnanawimala. As of 2026, he is an associate professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Gregory Price Grieve
nodes.summary: Gregory Price Grieve studied at San Francisco State and the University of Chicago. A religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and Head of Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro in 2002.

nodes.label: Michael S. Drummond
nodes.summary: Michael S. Drummond specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from the University of Bristol and was attested as a PhD candidate at Utrecht University in 2006.

nodes.label: Michel Bitbol
nodes.summary: Michel Bitbol works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Paris Diderot University and under Pierre Mills, he has held posts as research director at CNRS (~1990) and affiliations with Linacre College, Oxford, and École Normale Supérieure.

nodes.label: Guy Claxton
nodes.summary: Guy Claxton, active in Buddhist studies and other fields, founded the Sharpham College for Buddhist Studies and Contemporary Enquiry. He served as Professor of the Learning Sciences at the University of Bristol's Graduate School of Education (attested 2006).

nodes.id: I:Sharpham College for Buddhist Studies and Contemporary Enquiry
nodes.label: Sharpham College for Buddhist Studies and Contemporary Enquiry
variants: Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry
Sharpham College for Buddhist Studies and Contemporary Enquiry

nodes.label: Owen Flanagan
nodes.summary: Owen Flanagan is a philosopher working in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed studies at Fordham University and Boston University before joining Duke University, where he served as Professor of Philosophy beginning around 1996.

nodes.label: Andrew Olendzki
nodes.summary: Andrew Olendzki works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi, later serving at the Insight Meditation Society, the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and the Mind and Life Institute (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Insight Meditation Society
variants: Insight Meditation Society in Barre, Massachusetts

nodes.label: University of Warwick
variants: Centre for Translation & Comparative Cultural Studies, University of Warwick

nodes.label: Fazun
nodes.summary: Fazun was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Taixu, Amdo Geshe, and Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo, among others. He directed the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute (1933) and served as vice president and president of the Buddhist Academy of China (1956).

nodes.label: Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute
variants: Institut d'études du bouddhisme sino-tibétain (Hanzang jiaoli yuan)
Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute (Hanzang Jiaoliyuan 漢藏教理院)

nodes.label: Tzungkuen Wen
nodes.summary: Tzungkuen Wen works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Queensland (–2009) and held posts at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (2005) and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Buddhadasa Bhikkhu
nodes.native: พุทธทาสภิกขุ

nodes.label: Robert A. Orsi
nodes.summary: Robert A. Orsi (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology who studied at Trinity College, Hartford, and Yale University. He held positions at Fordham, Indiana University Bloomington, Harvard (2001–2007), Northwestern (from ~2007), and Notre Dame (2020–2021).

nodes.label: Clara Sue Kidwell
nodes.description: Native American academic scholar, historian, feminist
nodes.summary: Kidwell studied at the University of Oklahoma (master's ~1963–1966, Ph.D. ~1966–1970). Her posts included UC Berkeley (~1980–1993), the National Museum of the American Indian (~1993–1995), the University of Oklahoma (from 1995), and UNC Chapel Hill (director ~2007–2011).

nodes.label: Karen McCarthy Brown
nodes.summary: Karen McCarthy Brown was a scholar of religious studies and anthropology. Educated at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University, she served as a professor of anthropology at Drew University from circa 1976 to 2009.

nodes.label: Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri
nodes.summary: Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nalanda College, the University of London, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Toronto. He founded the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies, serving as its president.

nodes.label: Christopher Hatchell
nodes.summary: Christopher Hatchell is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he studied under academic mentor David Germano.

nodes.label: Jason McCombs
nodes.summary: Jason McCombs specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a B.S. at the University of Michigan and completed his PhD at UCLA by 2014 under Gregory Schopen, later serving as a lecturer at UCLA.

nodes.label: Lobsang Tenpa
nodes.summary: Lobsang Tenpa specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He completed a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under Sharad K. Soni and taught Peter James Gilks.

nodes.label: Jigmeth Junu
nodes.summary: Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi and traditional teacher Hui Xian (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Miri Albahari
nodes.summary: Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD from the University of Calgary under John A. Baker, and held affiliations with the University of Western Australia and UNSW.

nodes.label: University of New South Wales
variants: The University of New South Wales

nodes.label: Martin Heidegger
variants: マルティン・ハイデッガー
nodes.jawiki: マルティン・ハイデッガー
nodes.summary: Martin Heidegger was a philosopher who studied under Heinrich Rickert at the University of Freiburg. He taught at the University of Marburg (1923–1928) and held posts at Freiburg between 1915 and 1940.

nodes.label: Christian Parker Haskett
nodes.summary: Christian Parker Haskett is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, Michael Witzel, Michael Chamberlain, Lobsang Jamspal, and Geshe Lobsang Gyaltsen, earning a PhD from UW–Madison (attested 2010), and held a post at Washington and Lee.

nodes.label: Graeme MacQueen
nodes.summary: Graeme MacQueen (1948–2023) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1973–1979) under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi (~1973–1978) and served as a Lecturer at McMaster University (~1977–2003).

nodes.label: Linda Jean LaMacchia
nodes.summary: Linda Jean LaMacchia specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under doctoral supervisor David M. Knipe, attested in 2001.

nodes.label: Martin Straube
nodes.summary: Martin Straube works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, his posts include Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeit at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Research Fellow at IIBS, Foreign Adjunct Professor at Pune University, and Honorary Research Associate at Bristol.

nodes.label: China Inner Studies College
variants: China Institute of Inner Learning (支那內學院)

nodes.label: Michael R. Sheehy
nodes.summary: Michael R. Sheehy works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD from CIIS under Steven D. Goodman. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019–2026).

nodes.label: Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences
variants: チベット社会科学アカデミー

nodes.label: Qingying Chen
nodes.summary: Qingying Chen was a scholar of Tibetology and history. After studying under Wang Yao at Minzu University of China, he taught there and later served as director of the Historical Research Institute at the China Tibetology Research Center (~1993–2012).

nodes.label: Anagarika Govinda
nodes.image: Lama Govinda in an internment camp during World War II.jpg
nodes.summary: Anagarika Govinda (1898–1985) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who received a doctorate from the University of Freiburg. He founded the Arya Maitreya Mandala, served as its Ācārya, and taught at Visva-Bharati and Patna universities.

nodes.label: Adeu Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Adeu Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Khamtrul Rinpoche, Samten Gyatso, and Chögon Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Zen Mountain Monastery
variants: Zen Mountain Monastery at Mt. Tremper

nodes.label: Hegoda Khemananda
nodes.summary: Hegoda Khemananda is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1993, he is attested as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

nodes.label: Dewei Zhang
nodes.summary: Dewei Zhang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen, attested in 2010.

nodes.label: Paul Crowe
nodes.summary: Paul Crowe works in sinology and religious studies. He completed graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and held a professorship at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: King Pong Chiu
nodes.summary: King Pong Chiu is a scholar of indology, philosophy, and religious studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under Jacqueline Suthren Hirst.

nodes.label: Thomé H. Fang
nodes.summary: Thomé H. Fang worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Nanking, with John Dewey, and earned an MA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

nodes.label: J. Mark G. Williams
nodes.description: English psychologist; works on depression, suicide; retired 2013 from Centre for Suicide Research
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and other fields, J. Mark G. Williams studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He served as Director at the University of Oxford from circa 2003 to 2016.

nodes.id: I:Medical Research Council Cognition and Brain Sciences Unit
nodes.label: Medical Research Council Cognition and Brain Sciences Unit
Ilkka Pyysiäinen
nodes.description: Finnish cognitive science of religion scholar
nodes.summary: Ilkka Pyysiäinen is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Juha Pentikäinen, René Gothóni, and Simo Knuuttila. He served as an Academy Research Fellow at the University of Helsinki from 1984 and visited Oxford.

nodes.label: Juha Pentikäinen
nodes.summary: Juha Pentikäinen is a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Helsinki (~1960–1963) and the University of Turku (~1963–1968). He served as Professor of Comparative Religion at the University of Helsinki (~1972–2008).

nodes.label: Hiram W. Woodward
nodes.summary: Hiram W. Woodward is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard and Yale. He held posts at Silpakorn University, University of Michigan (1972–1982), University of Vermont (~1982–1986), and Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

nodes.label: ISEAS–Yusof Ishak Institute
variants: Institute of Southeast Asian Studies, Singapore

nodes.label: Andrew B. Irvine
nodes.summary: Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Boston University and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Brooke Schedneck
nodes.summary: Brooke Schedneck specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.

nodes.label: Jacques Leider
nodes.summary: Jacques Leider (born 1962) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from INALCO—including a PhD under Denise Bernot—and Paris-Sorbonne University, later teaching at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) before joining the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2001.

nodes.label: William Edward Soothill
nodes.summary: Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar William Edward Soothill studied at the University of London. He served as president of Shanxi University (1911) and was appointed Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford in 1920.

nodes.label: Lewis Hodous
nodes.summary: Lewis Hodous was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Case Western Reserve, Hartford Seminary, and Halle-Wittenberg. He served as president of Foochow Union Theological School (1902–1912, 1914–1917) and professor at Hartford Seminary (1917–1945).

nodes.label: Adrian Zenz
nodes.summary: Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and sinology. He studied at the University of Auckland and the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger (PhD ~2006–2011), later holding posts at the European School of Culture and Theology and Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.

nodes.label: Xiuzhi Zeng
nodes.summary: Xiuzhi Zeng is a researcher in Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MA at Nanhua University under supervisor Meihua Chen (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Renda Zheng
nodes.summary: Renda Zheng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who received traditional training under Kai Zhi, Shengfa, and Kai Tong.

nodes.label: Ramon N. Prats
nodes.summary: Ramon N. Prats is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017), and he taught Antonio Terrone.

nodes.label: Pompeu Fabra University
variants: Department of Humanities of the University Pompeu Fabra

nodes.label: Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy
nodes.summary: Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy specializes in Tibetology. She studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, Tibet University, Harvard, and EPHE under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She held posts teaching anthropology at Laval University (~2004, 2007).

nodes.label: Tibetan Arts Research Bureau
variants: Tibetan Arts Research Bureau (Bod ljongs sgyu rtsal zhib 'jug khang)

nodes.label: James Whitehill
nodes.summary: James Whitehill is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He founded the Columbia Zen Center and held a post as Professor of Religion at Stephens College, attested in 2000.

nodes.label: Pinit Ratanakul
nodes.native: พินิจ รัตนกุล

nodes.label: David Bubna-Litic
nodes.summary: David Bubna-Litic works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned his PhD at Western Sydney University (attested 2000) and was a lecturer in strategic management and responsible business at the University of Technology Sydney (attested 2000).

nodes.label: University of Technology Sydney
variants: School of Management in the University of Technology, Sydney

nodes.label: Stephen G. Williams
nodes.summary: Stephen G. Williams is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oxford and earned an MA from Colorado State University (~2016–2018) under Andre Archie, later holding a post at Worcester College, Oxford.

nodes.label: Susan Naquin
nodes.summary: Susan Naquin (born 1944) is a historian and Sinologist. Educated at Stanford and Yale, she served as assistant professor of history at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).

nodes.label: Jiyu Ren
nodes.summary: Jiyu Ren was a scholar of religion, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University under Lin He and Yongtong Tang. He held positions at Peking University, the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, and the National Library of China.

nodes.label: Xiaoling Wu
nodes.summary: Xiaoling Wu (1914–1995) worked in Sinology and Indology. He held posts as a research scholar and lecturer at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1946), at Peking University (~1947–1949), and as professor at Academia Sinica (~1950–1977) and CASS (~1977–1995).

nodes.label: Marion L. Matics
nodes.summary: Marion L. Matics is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Matics studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, and was taught by Robert A. Fowkes.

nodes.label: Horace L. Friess
nodes.summary: Horace L. Friess was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Columbia University (~1915–1918) and Heidelberg University. He taught at Johns Hopkins and at Columbia University, where he became Buttenwieser Professor (1962–1966).

nodes.label: Sōtō Zen Buddhism International Center
variants: Soto Zen Education Center of North America

nodes.label: Susan L. Beningson
nodes.summary: Susan L. Beningson is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr.

nodes.label: Robert E. Harrist, Jr.
nodes.summary: Robert E. Harrist, Jr. is a scholar of Sinology and art history. He served on the faculty at Columbia University, where he is attested in 2009 and as Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History in 2026.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Wayne Bass
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Wayne Bass is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at UNC Wilmington, the University of Tennessee, and UCLA (PhD attested 2013) under Gregory Schopen. He held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego (attested 2013).

nodes.label: William P. Chu
nodes.summary: William P. Chu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an MA at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2006, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

IITB GmbH (International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies GmbH)

nodes.label: Dhirendra Sharma
nodes.summary: Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology who studied under David Friedman and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

nodes.label: John R. B. Campbell
nodes.summary: John R. B. Campbell is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisors Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, alongside instruction from traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama.

nodes.label: H. V. Nagaraja Rao
nodes.summary: H. V. Nagaraja Rao works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Geshe Karma Sonam
nodes.summary: Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. His career includes attested affiliations with the Gyume Tantric College in 1987 and Sera Monastery in 1992.

nodes.label: Lang Eun Ra
nodes.summary: Lang Eun Ra is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Temple University under supervisor Charles Wei-hsun Fu, also studying with Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

nodes.label: Norbert Samuelson
nodes.description: Scholar and professor of Jewish philosophy
nodes.summary: Norbert Samuelson was a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at Northwestern, HUC-JIR, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. His career included faculty posts at Brooklyn College, Rutgers, University of Virginia, Temple University (1975–1998), and Arizona State University (~1998–2016).

nodes.label: Leonard Swidler
nodes.summary: Religious studies scholar Leonard Swidler studied at St. Norbert College, Marquette, Wisconsin-Madison, Tübingen, and Munich. After teaching at Duquesne University (1960–1966), he was Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966–2022).

nodes.label: Alan Gerard Wagner
nodes.summary: Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He received his PhD from Harvard University, where he was supervised by Parimal G. Patil and taught by Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.

nodes.label: Iselin Frydenlund
nodes.summary: Iselin Frydenlund is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Attested in 2016, she held positions as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and a research fellow at the University of Oslo.

nodes.label: Martin Lehnert
nodes.summary: Martin Lehnert is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Freiburg and was attested as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich in 2016.

nodes.label: James Mark Shields
nodes.summary: James Mark Shields works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology. He was attested in 2016 as Associate Professor of Comparative Humanities and Asian Thought at Bucknell University and Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

nodes.label: Foundation for Buddhist Studies
variants: Foundation for Buddhist Studies in Hamburg

nodes.label: Kim Gutschow
nodes.summary: Kim Gutschow works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned a PhD at Harvard University, and served as a teacher at Wesleyan University.

nodes.label: Geshe Ngawang Nyima
nodes.summary: Geshe Ngawang Nyima (1907–1990) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Drepung Monastery (attested 1966 and 1976), Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1995), and Leiden University.

nodes.label: Kamaleswar Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Kamaleswar Bhattacharya was an Indologist and philosopher. He held academic posts at Brown University (c. 1968–1970), the University of Toronto (c. 1970–1971), and the University of Bonn.

nodes.label: Jenkuan Shih
nodes.summary: Jenkuan Shih is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Shih earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi, having also studied under MA supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

nodes.label: Mark Csikszentmihalyi
nodes.summary: Mark Csikszentmihalyi (born 1964) is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He served as Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2004) and became Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at UC Berkeley around 2004.

nodes.label: Robert Cummings Neville
nodes.summary: Robert Cummings Neville (born 1939) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who completed his studies at Yale University (~1960–1963). He held academic appointments at Yale (~1963–1965), Fordham University (~1965–1971), and Boston University (~1987).

nodes.label: David A. Dilworth
nodes.summary: David A. Dilworth (born 1934) is a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo, and he taught Steve Odin.

variants: Institute for Advanced Studies in World Religions
Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions, New York

nodes.label: Giuliana Martini
nodes.summary: Giuliana Martini is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Kyoto University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies in 2010.

nodes.label: Keith Dowman
nodes.description: Dzogchen teacher, translator of Tibetan Buddhist texts
nodes.summary: Keith Dowman (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and with traditional teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Kangyur Rinpoche. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

nodes.label: David Quinter
nodes.summary: David Quinter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and East Asian religions. After earning his PhD at Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, he became an associate professor of East Asian religions at the University of Alberta (attested 2019).

nodes.id: I:Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies
nodes.label: Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies
variants: Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies in Yokohama
Inter-University Center for Advanced Language Study
Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies

nodes.label: Kenji Matsuo
nodes.summary: Kenji Matsuo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1975 to 1985 and held a post at Yamagata University from circa 1987 to 2020.

nodes.label: Sonja Arntzen
nodes.summary: Sonja Arntzen is a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia (~1970–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz. She also studied under teachers Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

nodes.label: Shuichi Kato
nodes.summary: Shuichi Kato was a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo and University of Paris, he held teaching posts at Tokyo, Sophia, British Columbia, Berlin, Munich, and Ritsumeikan, directing the Kyoto Museum for World Peace.

nodes.label: Yang Wenhui
nodes.summary: Yang Wenhui (1837–1911) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897), Zhiheng Jingshe (1908), and Jetavana Hermitage (1908), and served as head of the Buddhist Research Society, which he founded in 1910.

nodes.label: Qichao Liang
nodes.summary: Qichao Liang worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying under Youwei Kang, he held posts at Shiwu Xuetang, the Translation Bureau, Nankai University, Tsinghua University, and the National Library of China (1925–1927).

nodes.label: Youwei Kang
nodes.summary: Youwei Kang was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who founded the Wanmu Caotang academy in 1890 and held a post there from around 1891 to 1898, where he taught Qichao Liang.

nodes.label: Cameron Bailey
nodes.summary: Cameron Bailey specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Indiana University Bloomington under Richard F. Nance, an MA at Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, and doctoral studies at the University of Oxford under Ulrike Roesler.

nodes.label: Lucia Galli
nodes.summary: Lucia Galli is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held a post there.

nodes.label: Rory Brendan Lindsay
nodes.summary: Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University, supervised by Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Donald K. Swearer
nodes.summary: Donald K. Swearer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held a post at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004) and served as a Distinguished Visiting Fellow at Harvard Divinity School's Center for the Study of World Religions (2004–2010).

nodes.label: Amanda Goodman
nodes.summary: Amanda Goodman is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, supervised by Robert H. Sharf, Luis O. Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr. She holds a teaching post at the University of Toronto.

nodes.id: I:Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
nodes.label: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
variants: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Hong Kong University of Science & Technology

nodes.label: Mamoru Tonami
nodes.summary: Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He taught at Kobe University and held successive posts at Kyoto University from 1965 to 2001, later serving as professor at Otani University in 2003.

nodes.label: Jeffery D. Long
nodes.summary: Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a BA from Notre Dame and an MA and PhD from the University of Chicago. In 2000, he became Associate Professor at Elizabethtown College.

nodes.label: Angela Sumegi
nodes.summary: Angela Sumegi is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa under Nalini Devdas and held an assistant professorship at Carleton University (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Beru Khyentse Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Beru Khyentse Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He received traditional training under teachers including Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Kalu Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying under Shenphen Nangwa and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang. He held teaching posts at Men-Tsee-Khang and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.id: I:Hongyi and Feng Zikai Research Centre
nodes.label: Hongyi and Feng Zikai Research Centre
variants: Hongyi and Feng Zikai Research Centre

nodes.label: Lucia Dolce
nodes.summary: Lucia Dolce works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held lecturer and associate professor posts at SOAS University of London (attested 2003–2015) and is attested as a guest researcher at Minobusan University in 2026.

nodes.label: Grace S. Fong
nodes.summary: Grace S. Fong is a Sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia (~1977–1984). She served as a Professor at Smith College (~1984–1990) and as Associate Professor and Department Chair at McGill University (~1992–2021).

nodes.label: Ching-mei Shyu
nodes.summary: Ching-mei Shyu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Shyu completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi under Jan Nattier and a PhD at Cornell University in 2008 under Daniel Boucher, Hubert Durt, and Jane-Marie Law.

nodes.label: Jane-Marie Law
nodes.summary: Jane-Marie Law works in Japanology and religious studies. She has served at Cornell University as Director of Graduate Studies (attested 2008) and as Associate Professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ellison Banks Findly
nodes.summary: Ellison Banks Findly specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied under Fred Pfeil and held positions at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford, where she was associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Kazuo Okabe
nodes.summary: Kazuo Okabe (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, subsequently teaching at Aichi Gakuin University and serving as a professor at Komazawa University from 1979 to 2006.

nodes.label: Ramendra Sundar Tribedi
nodes.summary: Ramendra Sundar Tribedi was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta (~1882–1887) and served as Principal of Surendranath College (1892), also holding a post at Presidency University.

nodes.label: Somdet Phra Ñāṇasaṃvara
nodes.native: สมเด็จพระญาณสังวร

nodes.label: Hanung Kim
nodes.summary: Hanung Kim specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Kim earned a Master's degree at Columbia University and a Ph.D. at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Ruth Gamble
nodes.summary: Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the Australian National University (-2014) supervised by John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman, later holding research posts at ANU and the University of Munich (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Petra Maurer
nodes.summary: Petra Maurer is a Tibetologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. Her posts include positions at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013, 2026) and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Cuilan Liu
nodes.summary: Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She has held posts as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and at the University of Munich (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Emanuela Garatti
nodes.summary: Emanuela Garatti is a scholar of Tibetology who has held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Pragati Sahni
nodes.summary: Pragati Sahni specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Damien Keown and has served as an associate professor at the University of Delhi (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Satya Narayan Goenka
variants: サティア・ナラヤン・ゴエンカ
nodes.image: The Kalyanmitra Satyanarayan Goenka who brought Vipassana Meditation technique to India after 2500 years is seen with his wife while speaking at a talk on "Values in Education - Good Governance through Vipassana Meditation" in.jpg
nodes.jawiki: サティア・ナラヤン・ゴエンカ
nodes.summary: Satya Narayan Goenka worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Sayagyi U Ba Khin (~1955–1969), taught students such as Joseph Goldstein and Stephen Batchelor, and founded the Vipassana Research Institute in 1985.

nodes.label: Phramonchai Saitanaporn
nodes.summary: Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney under the doctoral supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, attested in 2009.

nodes.label: Jeff Wilson
nodes.summary: Jeff Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, having studied under mentor Taitetsu Unno and postdoctoral mentor Myōsei Tatsuguchi.

nodes.label: Shuman Chen
nodes.summary: Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi and earned a PhD from Northwestern University under the supervision of Brook Ziporyn.

nodes.label: Brook Ziporyn
nodes.summary: Brook Ziporyn works in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Michigan under Donald J. Munro and has served as the Mircea Eliade Professor at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Sarah E. Fraser
nodes.summary: Sarah E. Fraser works in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, she became an associate professor at Northwestern University in 1996 and directrice d'études at the EPHE in 2000.

nodes.label: Anne Ruth Hansen
nodes.summary: Anne Ruth Hansen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies who studied under Charles Hallisey. She held an affiliation at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2007) and has served as professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (attested 2012–2026).

nodes.label: Thomas Nathan Patton
nodes.summary: Thomas Nathan Patton works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held a post at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Anne M. Blackburn
nodes.summary: Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar of Buddhist studies, indology, and religious studies who completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago (1991). She held posts at Harvard University (circa 1999–2000), Cornell University (circa 2000), and the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hoseok Leigh
nodes.summary: Hoseok Leigh is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010), having studied under Ha-u Kim and the traditional teacher Cheonghwa.

nodes.label: Carol S. Anderson
nodes.summary: Carol S. Anderson works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under John A. Brinkman and W. S. Karunatillake (1990–1991), and became Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

nodes.label: John A. Brinkman
nodes.summary: John A. Brinkman is a scholar of history and archaeology. He held a post at the University of Chicago (~1964) and served as a professor at the University of Oxford (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Catherine Bell
nodes.summary: Catherine Bell (1954–2008) was a religious studies and Sinology scholar. She studied at the University of Chicago (~1976–1983) under Joseph Kitagawa and served as Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

nodes.label: Swami Sivananda
nodes.summary: Swami Sivananda (1887–1963) was a figure in philosophy and religious studies who studied at Thanjavur Medical College (~1905–1909). He founded the Divine Life Society in 1936 and the Yoga Vedanta Forest Academy in 1948.

nodes.label: Kin Cheung
nodes.summary: Kin Cheung is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under doctoral supervisor Shigenori Nagatomo.

nodes.label: James Blumenthal
nodes.summary: James Blumenthal was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and held posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College (attested 2013-2015).

nodes.label: Kosen Imakita
nodes.summary: Kosen Imakita (1816–1892) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Shokoku-ji and Sōgen-ji under figures including Shoen Daisetsu and Gisan Zenkai. He served as abbot of Eikō-ji (1858) and Engaku-ji (1875–1892).

nodes.label: Josiah Royce
nodes.summary: Josiah Royce was a philosopher who studied at the University of California (~1871–1875), University of Göttingen under Hermann Lotze (~1875–1876), and Johns Hopkins University (~1876–1878). He served on the faculty at Harvard University from 1882 to 1916.

nodes.label: George Santayana
variants: ジョージ・サンタヤーナ
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・サンタヤーナ
nodes.summary: George Santayana was a philosopher who studied at Harvard, Berlin, and Cambridge, earning his PhD at Harvard under William James. He served on the philosophy faculty at Harvard University from 1907 to 1912.

nodes.label: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche
variants: ティンレー・ノルブ・リンポチェ
nodes.image: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche wearing a white shirt, red zen, pink curtain in background.jpg
nodes.summary: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche (1931–2011) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Rinpoche (Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje). He founded the White Lotus School.

nodes.label: Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Delog Dawa Drolma, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, Jangchub Dorje, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Thubten Chodron
nodes.summary: Thubten Chodron is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Educated at UCLA, USC, Kopan, and Dorje Pamo, she held posts at Istituto Lama Tzong Khapa, Amitabha Buddhist Centre, and Dharma Friendship Foundation, and founded Sravasti Abbey in 2003, serving as abbess.

nodes.label: Daniel R. Tuzzeo
nodes.summary: Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his thesis at Florida State University, where he studied under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

nodes.label: George A. Keyworth
nodes.summary: Keyworth works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara under Ronald Egan, William F. Powell, and Shuizhao Wang, and earned his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held posts at CU Boulder and Saskatchewan.

nodes.label: Ronald Egan
nodes.summary: Ronald Egan is a Sinologist who earned his PhD from Harvard University (~1970–1977). He held appointments at Harvard (~1977–1983), Wellesley College (~1983–1987), UC Santa Barbara (~1987–2012; emeritus ~2012), and Stanford University (~2012–2023).

nodes.label: Pieter Cornelis Verhagen
nodes.summary: Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University in 1991, where he was also attested as a research fellow in 1996.

nodes.label: Namio Egami
nodes.summary: Namio Egami (1906–2002) was a historian, archaeologist, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930), where he later held a post (~1948–1967), and served as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).

nodes.label: Ulrike Roesler
nodes.summary: Ulrike Roesler, a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD at the University of Münster. She taught at the universities of Freiburg and Marburg, and held posts at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College.

nodes.label: Nalini Devdas
nodes.summary: Nalini Devdas is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. She studied under Paul David Devanandan, C. T. Krishnamachari, Steven Collins, Richard P. Hayes, and supervisor Leslie C. Orr, earning a PhD from Concordia University (attested 2004), and held a post at Carleton University.

nodes.label: Paul David Devanandan
nodes.summary: Paul David Devanandan (1901–1962) was a religious studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Nizam College, Presidency University, and Yale (doctorate ~1931), he taught at United Theological College (1932–1949) and directed CISRS from 1956.

nodes.label: Tsultrim Gyatso
nodes.summary: Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held posts as senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as abbot at Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Hozen Seki
nodes.summary: Hozen Seki was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Susan Meinheit
nodes.summary: Susan Meinheit is a Tibetology scholar attested in posts at the Library of Congress in 1998 and 2007.

nodes.label: Boris Vladimirovich Semichov
nodes.summary: Boris Vladimirovich Semichov was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1922–1927) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1934).

nodes.label: Jørn Borup
nodes.summary: Jørn Borup was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and later served there as an associate professor from circa 2006 to 2023.

nodes.label: Ian Reader
nodes.summary: Ian Reader is a Japanology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Leeds (1983). He held posts at the University of Stirling (~1989–1995), Lancaster University (~2003–2008), and the University of Manchester (~2008).

nodes.label: Michaela Haas
nodes.summary: Michaela Haas is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2008) under the supervision of Peter Schwieger, and also studied with Rechungpa and Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul.

nodes.label: Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul
nodes.native: 'jigs med rnam rgyal 'dzi sgar kong sprul
variants: ‘Jigs med rNam rgyal ‘Dzi sgar Kong sprul

nodes.label: Günter Grönbold
nodes.summary: Günter Grönbold specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served at the Bavarian State Library from around 1975 to 2008, where he headed the Oriental Section from approximately 1988 to 2008.

nodes.label: Rudolf Kaschewsky
nodes.summary: Rudolf Kaschewsky was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Cologne and Bonn, worked at the University of Bonn (1974–2004), and taught Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt.

nodes.label: Andreas Doctor
nodes.summary: Andreas Doctor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, studied with traditional teachers including Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche
nodes.description: tibetan teacher and religious ritual master
nodes.summary: Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at the Young Lamas Home School. He served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery (~1976–2020) and was a board member of Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen.

nodes.label: Phakchok Rinpoche
nodes.description: Vajra Master of Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling monastery
nodes.summary: Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who earned a Khenpo title at Dzongsar Institute (~1995–2004) under numerous traditional teachers. He became Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery around 2004.

nodes.label: Ngodup Tsering
nodes.image: Ngodup Tsering, Geshe Lhakdor and Geshe Lobsang Monlam.jpg

nodes.label: Susan Niditch
nodes.summary: Susan Niditch (born 1950) is a religious studies scholar who served in the religion department at Amherst College from approximately 1978 to 2020.

nodes.label: Tenzin L. Mullin
nodes.summary: Tenzin L. Mullin is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. Mullin earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Otago, studying under the supervision of Elizabeth Guthrie.

nodes.label: Will Sweetman
nodes.description: professor of religion in New Zealand
nodes.summary: Will Sweetman is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University (~1989–1993) and the University of Cambridge (~1993–1997), and held a post at the University of Otago (~2004).

nodes.label: Dongchu
nodes.summary: Dongchu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He was dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy (~1934–1945) and abbot of Dinghui Monastery (~1946–1949).

nodes.label: Barry Sautman
nodes.summary: Barry Sautman specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. He earned degrees at UCLA, NYU, and Columbia University. He served as an adjunct assistant professor at California State University, Northridge, a visiting assistant professor at the Hopkins-Nanjing Center, and an assistant professor at HKUST.

nodes.label: Craig Preston
nodes.summary: Craig Preston is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Virginia under Joe Bransford Wilson and Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981).

nodes.label: Katherine Anne Paul
nodes.summary: Katherine Anne Paul works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her doctoral studies under supervisor Gudrun Bühnemann, and studied under Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

nodes.label: Philadelphia Museum of Art
variants: フィラデルフィア美術館

nodes.label: David Jones
nodes.summary: David Jones is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaiʻi. Attested in 2007, he served as a professor of philosophy in the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

nodes.id: I:Center for the Development of Asian Studies
nodes.label: Center for the Development of Asian Studies
variants: Center for the Development of Asian Studies

nodes.label: Max Kaltenmark
nodes.summary: Max Kaltenmark was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who succeeded Henri Maspero. He served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953) and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris (~1957–1979).

nodes.label: Léon Vandermeersch
nodes.summary: Léon Vandermeersch (1928–2021) was a Sinologist and philosopher. He studied at INALCO, the University of Paris, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. His posts included Aix-Marseille University, Paris Diderot, EPHE (director of studies, 1979–1993), and EFEO (director, 1989–1993).

nodes.label: Wen-ling Jane
nodes.summary: Wen-ling Jane specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jane earned a PhD from Columbia University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and also studied under Lobsang Jamspal.

nodes.label: Kammie Morrison Takahashi
nodes.summary: Kammie Morrison Takahashi is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and the University of Virginia (PhD 2009) under David Germano, Paul Groner, and Daishun Ueyama.

nodes.label: Sabine Löhr
nodes.summary: Sabine Löhr is an Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, completing an M.A. and doctoral studies under Lambert Schmithausen. She also served as a student/research assistant (Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft) at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Graham Lock
nodes.summary: Graham Lock is a scholar in linguistics and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

nodes.label: Robert Barnett
nodes.summary: Robert Barnett (born 1953) is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at Columbia University (~1999–2018), Tibet University (2000–2006), and both SOAS University of London and King's College London in ~2018.

nodes.label: Arthur F. Buehler
nodes.summary: Arthur F. Buehler is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied under Annemarie Schimmel and held an academic post at Victoria University of Wellington.

nodes.label: Halle O'Neal
nodes.summary: Halle O'Neal specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Kansas under Sherry Fowler and serves as Co-Director at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Palden Sherab
nodes.summary: Palden Sherab (1938–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Gochen Monastery and Riwoche Monastery (~1953–1959) under Dudjom Rinpoche, Tubten Tsondru, and others. He served as chair of the Nyingma section at CIHTS (~1967–1984).

nodes.label: David W. Tien
nodes.summary: David W. Tien works in sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Toronto, McGill University, and the University of Michigan (PhD attested 2009), studying under Julia Ching, Robert H. Sharf, and James Robson.

nodes.label: Jim Rheingans
nodes.summary: Jim Rheingans works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Hamburg and a PhD through the University of the West of England and Bath Spa University under David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery, later holding attested posts at Hamburg, Vienna, and Sydney.

variants: University of the West of England, Bristol
University of the West of England

nodes.label: Nicola Bajetta
nodes.summary: A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Nicola Bajetta is affiliated with the University of Hamburg as a doctoral local researcher and project staff member (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Stephen Suen
nodes.summary: Stephen Suen is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Mark Unno
nodes.summary: Mark Unno works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Oberlin College and Stanford University, he held posts at Brown University (~1994–2000) and the University of Oregon (~2000–2007).

nodes.label: Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir
nodes.summary: Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Lama Byambaa and completed an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under supervisor Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Agata Bareja-Starzyńska
nodes.summary: Agata Bareja-Starzyńska works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and University of Bonn (1995), and holds an affiliation at the University of Warsaw (attested 2008 and 2026).

nodes.label: Moscow State University
variants: Moscow State University's Institute of Asian and African Studies

nodes.label: Cameron Foltz
nodes.summary: Cameron Foltz focuses on religious studies and Japanology. He earned an MA at Florida State University (attested 2018) under Bryan J. Cuevas and Jimmy Yu, and was attested in 2026 as a Postdoctoral Fellow at Columbia University.

nodes.label: Yu Yan Pang
nodes.summary: Yu Yan Pang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, studying under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, as well as teacher Eric Kvan.

nodes.label: Miranda Shaw
nodes.summary: Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi, teacher Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

nodes.label: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza
nodes.summary: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza (born 1938) is a religious studies scholar educated at Würzburg and Münster. She held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard Divinity School as Krister Stendahl Research Professor (from 1988).

nodes.label: Ngawang Jorden
nodes.summary: Ngawang Jorden is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has held positions at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.

nodes.label: Bratindra Nath Mukherjee
nodes.description: Indian historian, numismatist, epigraphist and iconographist
nodes.summary: Bratindra Nath Mukherjee (1932–2013) was an Indologist and historian. He earned a master's at the University of Calcutta and a doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later serving as Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (1975–1998).

nodes.label: Sulak Sivaraksa
nodes.native: สุลักษณ์ ศิวรักษ์
nodes.summary: Sulak Sivaraksa (born 1933) is an author in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Wales, Lampeter (~1954–1957). He held visiting professorships at UC Berkeley, Harvard, Toronto, and Cornell, and was an honorary fellow at Lampeter.

nodes.label: Subhadradis Diskul
nodes.native: สุภัทรดิศ ดิศกุล
variants: モムチャオ＝スパトラディット・ディッサクン
nodes.image: สุภัทรดิศ ดิศกุล.jpg
nodes.jawiki: スパトラディット・ディッサクン
nodes.summary: Subhadradis Diskul (1923–2003) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Chulalongkorn, École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, and the University of London. He served at the Bangkok National Museum, as Silpakorn University's rector, and as SPAFA director.

nodes.label: David Kerman Tomlinson
nodes.summary: David Kerman Tomlinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold (attested 2019), having also studied under Jay L. Garfield and Andrew Rotman, and held a post at Smith College.

nodes.label: Sven Wittemann
nodes.summary: Sven Wittemann is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Juichiro Tanabe
nodes.summary: Juichiro Tanabe was a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford (2000–2001) and studied under the traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

nodes.label: Bong Seok Joo
nodes.summary: Bong Seok Joo specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD from Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Stout
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Stout (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Brown University (~1968–1972) and earned his PhD at Princeton University (~1972–1976), where he subsequently served as a professor from 1976 to 2018.

nodes.label: Jann Ronis
nodes.summary: Jann Ronis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor David Germano and teacher Jeffrey Hopkins, and held an affiliation there attested in 2007.

nodes.label: Faren
nodes.summary: Faren is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD from Lancaster University by 2008. In 2013, Faren is attested as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Wenbiao Mai
nodes.summary: Wenbiao Mai works in Indology and linguistics. Mai completed a PhD at Peking University, studied at the University of Hamburg and Kyoto University, and served as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Zhonghui Cui
nodes.summary: Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. She earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where she was an instructional consultant (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Christopher D. Emms
nodes.summary: Christopher D. Emms works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University (attested 2026), studying under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke (attested 2012–2026).

nodes.label: Jampa Samten
nodes.summary: Jampa Samten is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, serving as Director (attested 2015) and later as a re-employed Professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Gin Ling Liu
nodes.summary: Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, supervised by Jing Yin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Kim Knott
nodes.summary: Kim Knott is an indology and religious studies scholar. She held posts at the University of Leeds (circa 1983-2012) and Lancaster University (circa 2012).

nodes.label: Eleanor Nesbitt
nodes.summary: Eleanor Nesbitt (born 1951) works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at Girton College and the University of Oxford before serving as a professor in Education Studies at the University of Warwick (~1989–2011).

nodes.label: John Berthrong
nodes.summary: John Berthrong worked in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alfonso Verdu (~1974–1979) and served on the faculty at Boston University from ~1989 to 2013.

nodes.label: Elizabeth J. Harris
nodes.summary: Elizabeth J. Harris specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her doctorate under Ananda Guruge and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and University of Kelaniya, holding posts at Westminster College (~1993–1997) and Birmingham (~2017).

nodes.label: Michael Harack
nodes.summary: Michael Harack specializes in religious studies and sinology. Attested in 2007, he completed a Master of Arts degree at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn.

nodes.label: Robert J. Topmiller
nodes.summary: Robert J. Topmiller specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Kentucky under the supervision of George C. Herring.

nodes.label: Jang-Kil Chun
nodes.summary: Jang-Kil Chun specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chun studied under Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Frances Wilson, and doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota.

nodes.label: Alexander Rödel
nodes.summary: Alexander Rödel specializes in religious studies and Indology. He earned his Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh, where his supervisors were Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Christian Matthias Boehm
nodes.summary: Christian Matthias Boehm works in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London (attested 2005) under doctoral supervisor John T. Carpenter, having also studied under Toshifumi Konno.

nodes.label: Yongtong Tang
nodes.summary: Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Tsinghua and Harvard under Lanman and Babbitt, he held posts at Southeast, Nankai, and National Southwestern Associated Universities, and served as vice-president of Peking University.

nodes.label: Troy Organ
nodes.summary: Troy Organ was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa. He held academic posts at Parsons College (~1944–1946), the University of Akron (~1946–1954), and Ohio University (1954).

nodes.label: Surya Das

nodes.label: Aristotle C. Dy
nodes.summary: Aristotle C. Dy works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London, where he studied under Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Jacob Neusner

nodes.summary: Religious studies scholar Jacob Neusner studied at Harvard, Lincoln College, Columbia, and the Jewish Theological Seminary. He held positions at UW–Milwaukee (~1961–1962), Brandeis (~1962–1964), the University of South Florida (~1990–2000), and Bard College (~1994–2014).

nodes.label: Kristin Scheible
nodes.summary: Kristin Scheible is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Colby College, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University. She held posts at Harvard, Brown University, and Bard College.

nodes.label: Bruce Chilton
nodes.summary: Bruce Chilton works in religious studies. He studied at St John's College and held appointments at Yale University (~1985–1987) and Bard College, where he became Director (~1987).

nodes.label: Matthew Steven Mitchell
nodes.summary: Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Osaka City University, the IUC, the University of Hawaiʻi, and Duke University, completing his PhD under Richard M. Jaffe.

nodes.label: Richard M. Jaffe
nodes.summary: Richard M. Jaffe is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held a position at North Carolina State University from circa 1995 to 2000 before becoming Professor of Religious Studies at Duke University around 2000.

nodes.label: Chong Go

nodes.label: Bongkil Chung
nodes.summary: Bongkil Chung specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and served as a professor of philosophy at Florida International University (1991–1992, attested 2012).

nodes.label: Woosung Huh
nodes.summary: Woosung Huh, working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi and served as a professor of philosophy at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Patrick R. Uhlmann
nodes.summary: Patrick R. Uhlmann specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued his doctoral studies at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he was a PhD candidate attested in 2012, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.label: Woncheol Yun
nodes.summary: Woncheol Yun, a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at Stony Brook University and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Jin Y. Park
nodes.summary: Jin Y. Park works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Park served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and was a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

nodes.summary: E. D. Hirsch, a scholar in philosophy and other fields, studied at Metairie Park Country Day School and Cornell University (~1946–1950). He held posts at Wesleyan University (~1956–1957) and the University of Virginia (~1966).

nodes.label: Pema Chödrön
nodes.summary: Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist and religious studies figure. Educated at Sarah Lawrence and UC Berkeley, she studied under Chögyam Trungpa and other teachers. She served as director of Boulder Shambhala Center (~1981–1985) and led Gampo Abbey.

nodes.label: Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche works in Buddhist, religious, and Tibetan studies. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, taught at Naropa University (1990), and founded Mangala Shri Bhuti.

nodes.label: Geo Widengren
variants: ゲオ・ヴィデングレン
nodes.summary: Geo Widengren was a scholar of Iranian-Central Asian and religious studies. He studied at Stockholm University and Uppsala University under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, serving as professor of the history of religions at Uppsala (1940–1973) and president of the IAHR (~1960–1970).

nodes.label: Benoît Vermander
nodes.summary: Benoît Vermander specializes in Sinology and religious studies. Educated at Yale, Sciences Po, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres, he served as Academic Director of the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) and became professor of religious sciences at Fudan University in 2009.

nodes.label: Taipei Ricci Institute

nodes.label: Chiko Corona
nodes.summary: Chiko Corona is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kenko Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.

nodes.label: Mikaël Bauer
nodes.summary: Mikaël Bauer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned a PhD at Harvard under Ryuichi Abe; he is an Associate Professor of Japanese Religions at McGill University.

nodes.summary: Walther Heissig specialized in Iranian/Central Asian and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Vienna, Berlin, Göttingen, and Bonn, and held posts at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University (~1941–1945), and the University of Bonn (1964).

nodes.label: Nicholas Poppe
nodes.summary: Nicholas Poppe specialized in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies, studying at Saint Petersburg State University under Boris Vladimirtsov. He held professorships at Saint Petersburg State University (1923, 1925–1941) and served on the faculty at the University of Washington (1949–1968).

nodes.label: Heidi Fjeld
nodes.summary: Heidi Fjeld works in Tibetology and other fields. She studied at the University of Oxford and the University of Oslo under Signe Howell (~2001–2006), later serving as a postdoctoral fellow at Oslo (~2006–2010).

nodes.label: Ben Jiao
nodes.summary: Ben Jiao specializes in Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein and served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Alexander Ong Hsu
nodes.summary: Alexander Ong Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2017) under Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and later held a teaching position at North Dakota State University.

nodes.label: Anthony C. Yu
nodes.description: American scholar of literature and religion (1938-2015)
nodes.summary: Anthony C. Yu was a sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1969). He spent his career at the University of Chicago (circa 1968–2005) as a distinguished service professor.

nodes.summary: Joan Halifax is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Newcomb College and Union Institute & University. She held posts at Columbia, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and Harvard, and founded the Ojai Foundation and Upaya Zen Center.

nodes.label: Ajahn Sucitto
nodes.summary: Ajahn Sucitto specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a degree at the University of Warwick (circa 1968–1971), studied under Ajahn Sumedho in 1977, and served as abbot of Chithurst Buddhist Monastery from 1992 to 2014.

nodes.label: Franz Aubrey Metcalf
nodes.summary: Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago and served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

nodes.label: Paul David Numrich
nodes.summary: Paul David Numrich works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Michigan in 1992 and held posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Ann Gleig
nodes.summary: Ann Gleig works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Geshe Losang Chödar
nodes.summary: Geshe Losang Chödar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2010, his posts include Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics and an affiliation with the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Karl-Heinz Everding
nodes.summary: Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He served as Privatdozent at Hamburg in 1999 and worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Shri Krishna Sharma
nodes.summary: Shri Krishna Sharma was active in Indology and linguistics. Sharma founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

nodes.label: John B. Cobb Jr.
nodes.summary: John B. Cobb Jr. is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Chicago. He founded the Center for Process Studies and held professorships at Claremont School of Theology and Claremont Graduate University (attested 1989).

nodes.label: John Hick
nodes.description: English philosopher of religion and theologian (1922-2012)
nodes.summary: John Hick worked in philosophy and religious studies, studying at Edinburgh (~1945–1948) and Oxford (~1948–1950). He held posts at Cornell, Princeton Seminary, Cambridge, the University of Birmingham (~1967–1982), and Claremont Graduate University (~1979–1993).

nodes.label: Joseph Prabhu
nodes.summary: Joseph Prabhu works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied under Bernard Williams, Alasdair MacIntyre, and doctoral supervisor John Niemeyer Findlay, and held an associate professorship at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007).

nodes.label: Bossey Ecumenical Institute
variants: Ecumenical Institute of the World Council of Churches

nodes.label: Sushanta Sen
nodes.summary: Sushanta Sen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied at Visva-Bharati University, where he became a lecturer in 1986, and later served as Lecturer in Indian Religions at the University of Birmingham.

nodes.label: Sakyong Mipham
variants: サキョン・ミパム・リンポチェ
サワン・ウーセル・ランジュン・ムクポ
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, he studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, whom he succeeded. He served on the board of Naropa University until 2018.

nodes.label: Shinobu Arai Apple
nodes.summary: Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey (attested 2003), teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi (2000), and academic adviser Robert Bickner.

nodes.label: Robert Warren Clark
nodes.summary: Robert Warren Clark is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1994, he was attested studying under doctoral supervisor Karen C. Lang and adviser and teacher K. L. Seshagiri Rao.

nodes.label: Daniel Aaron Getz
nodes.summary: Daniel Aaron Getz specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, also studying under Ying-shih Yü and Tairyō Makita, and held a post as associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Sue Hamilton
nodes.summary: Sue Hamilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson, and was affiliated with King's College London (attested 2001–2003).

nodes.label: Tsukasa Mizushima
nodes.summary: Tsukasa Mizushima is an Indology and history scholar who earned his bachelor's, master's, and doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995) and the University of Tokyo (1997–2018), where he is professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Ankur Barua
nodes.summary: Ankur Barua works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned degrees from the Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MD 2003), Sikkim Manipal University (MBAIT 2007), and the University of Hong Kong (MBuddStud 2009) under supervisor Dorothy C. Wong, later holding a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Dorothy C. Wong
nodes.summary: Dorothy C. Wong is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She was a visiting professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) and affiliate faculty at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Randall Studstill
nodes.summary: Randall Studstill works in the fields of religious studies and philosophy. He studied under Steven D. Goodman and completed his doctoral studies under Richard Payne.

nodes.label: Chisan Kohō
nodes.summary: Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyodo Koshuin. He held leadership posts at Saijō-ji Senmon Sōdō, Nagano Ken Senmon Nisodo, and Soji-ji, and founded Tsurumi Women's University in 1966.

nodes.label: Maurine Stuart
nodes.summary: Maurine Stuart was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Manitoba and trained under Nadia Boulanger, Soen Nakagawa, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, and Eido Shimano. In 1979, she served as president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association.

nodes.label: Eido Shimano
nodes.summary: Eido Shimano (1932–2018) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozō, Soen Nakagawa at Ryutaku-ji, and at the University of Hawaiʻi, later serving as abbot of the Zen Studies Society and master at New York Zendo Shobo-ji.

nodes.label: Prabhasa Dharma
nodes.summary: Prabhasa Dharma was an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. She received traditional training under Zen masters Kyozan Joshu Sasaki starting in 1967 and Seikaku Hirata.

nodes.label: Seikaku Hirata
nodes.summary: Seikaku Hirata (1924–2008) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1946–1950) under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki, and later held an academic post at Hanazono University.

nodes.label: Yong Hua
nodes.summary: Yong Hua is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College by 2014, studying under MA supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.

nodes.label: Hyoung Seok Ham
nodes.summary: Hyoung Seok Ham specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Virginia (2010) and earned a PhD from the University of Michigan under Madhav M. Deshpande (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Charles H. Long
nodes.description: African-American cultural historian and religious studies scholar (1926–2020)

nodes.label: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje
