nodes.label: Philip Novak
nodes.summary: Philip Novak is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Notre Dame (~1968–1972) and Syracuse University (~1976–1981), and began teaching at Dominican University of California around 1980.

nodes.label: Zuigan Goto
nodes.summary: Zuigan Goto (1879–1965) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1903–1906) and under Sokatsu Shaku. He served as president of Hanazono University in 1932.

nodes.label: Dominic Sur
nodes.summary: Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard Divinity School and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Karen C. Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Khenpo Lama Chonam. He held a post at Utah State University.

nodes.label: Ravi M. Gupta
nodes.description: Vaishnava religious scholar, author and editor
nodes.summary: Ravi M. Gupta is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Boise State University and the University of Oxford. He taught at Florida, Centre College, and William & Mary before becoming the Charles Redd Chair of Religious Studies at Utah State University (~2013).

nodes.label: Sylvie Hureau
nodes.summary: Sylvie Hureau is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. She has held posts as maître de conférences at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2012) and as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Trevor Leggett
nodes.summary: Trevor Leggett worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and philosophy. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and under Hari Prasad Shastri and Arthur Waley, later heading the BBC Japanese Service (~1946–1970) and lecturing for the Buddhist Society.

nodes.label: John Riley Perks

nodes.label: Takeo Hibino

nodes.label: Abigail I. MacBain

Benn, Shayne Clarke, Mark MacWilliams, and Michael Greenwald, and holds a post at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Flavio Geisshuesler
nodes.summary: Flavio Geisshuesler specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Bern, Lausanne, and Virginia (PhD under David Germano ~2013–2019), and held posts at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Sydney.

nodes.label: Farzand Ali Durrani
nodes.summary: Farzand Ali Durrani was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of the Punjab, the University of Peshawar, and the University of London. He served as a professor at the University of Peshawar from approximately 1976 to 1993.

nodes.label: Yu-min Lee

nodes.label: Yaping Dou

nodes.label: Steffen Döll

variants: International Affairs Office of Dharma Drum Mountain
International Cultural and Educational Foundation of Dharma Drum Mountain

nodes.label: Hyejeong Choi
nodes.summary: Hyejeong Choi works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, completing a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington (attested 2015). Choi was a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara in 2015.

nodes.label: Archaeological Institute of Kashihara
variants: Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture

nodes.label: Karl Brunnhölzl
nodes.summary: Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, the 10th Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

nodes.label: Tenga Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tenga Rinpoche (1932–2012) was an expert in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Benchen Monastery. He founded Benchen Monastery in 1976 and served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery from around 1967 to 1980.

nodes.label: Ringu Tulku
nodes.summary: Ringu Tulku is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Namgyal Institute, CIHTS, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. His teachers included Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Tubten Tsondru, and he taught at Naropa University.

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity
variants: Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity
Max-Planck-Institut zur Erforschung multireligiöser und multiethnischer Gesellschaften

nodes.label: Peter van der Veer
nodes.summary: Peter van der Veer is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Groningen and Utrecht University, later serving as professor at Utrecht, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Amsterdam, and director at the Max Planck Institute (~2009–2021).

nodes.label: Polish Academy of Sciences
variants: Committee on Oriental Studies of the Polish Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: John M. Rosenfield
variants: ジョン・マックス・ローゼンフィールド3世
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・マックス・ローゼンフィールド
nodes.summary: John M. Rosenfield was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and art history. He earned a PhD from Harvard under Benjamin Rowland, later serving there as Professor (1965–1991) and Director of the Harvard Art Museums (~1982–1990).

nodes.label: Dhammanandā
nodes.summary: Dhammanandā is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007) under Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe, having also studied under Viên Minh, Toshiichi Endo, and N. A. Jayawickrama.

nodes.label: Sumanapala Galmangoda
nodes.summary: Sumanapala Galmangoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Senior Professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 2012) and Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007, 2012).

nodes.label: Toshiichi Endo
nodes.summary: Toshiichi Endo is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate degree at the University of Kelaniya and his doctoral thesis at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, supervised by Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake.

nodes.label: Ross Bolleter
nodes.summary: Ross Bolleter is a Buddhist studies scholar and Zen Buddhist teacher. He earned his bachelor's degree at the University of Western Australia, trained under Robert Baker Aitken and John Tarrant, and taught at the Zen Group of Western Australia (~1983–2023).

nodes.label: Hans-Joachim Klimkeit
nodes.summary: Hans-Joachim Klimkeit worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp (~1959–1963) and Gustav Mensching (~1965–1968), whom he succeeded in 1972 upon becoming Direktor at the University of Bonn.

nodes.label: Tara Doyle
nodes.summary: Tara Doyle works in Buddhist and religious studies. She served at Emory University as a lecturer and director of its Tibetan Studies Program (attested 2003) and later as Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jared Rhoton
nodes.summary: Jared Rhoton (1941–1992) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and completed his doctoral dissertation at Columbia University under Alex Wayman by 1985.

nodes.label: Richard D. McBride II
nodes.summary: Richard D. McBride II works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at UCLA mentored by Robert E. Buswell Jr., held a fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis, and held a post at Dongguk University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Seiichi Mizuno
nodes.summary: Seiichi Mizuno (1905–1971) was a scholar in archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1925–1928, DLitt 1962) under Kosaku Hamada. He held posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture's Kyoto Institute and was professor at Kyoto University (1949–1968).

nodes.label: Toshio Nagahiro
nodes.summary: Toshio Nagahiro was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He served as professor at Kyoto University (~1950–1969) and president of Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).

nodes.label: Lucy Annette Jones
nodes.summary: Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Anne C. Klein and Edith Wyschogrod.

nodes.label: Edith Wyschogrod
nodes.summary: Edith Wyschogrod worked in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Hunter College (~1947–1951) and Columbia University (~1965–1970), and was the J. Newton Rayzor Professor of Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University (1992–2002).

nodes.label: Helena Michie
nodes.summary: Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1979 to 1984. She held a post at Rice University beginning around 1990.

nodes.label: John Vincent Bellezza
nodes.summary: John Vincent Bellezza is a Tibetologist and archaeologist who studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel. He held a post at the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Konchok Gyatso
nodes.summary: Konchok Gyatso is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He held an attested post at the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences in 2014.

nodes.id: I:MF Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society
nodes.label: MF Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society
variants: Lutheran School of Theology in Oslo
MF Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society

nodes.label: Paul W. Kroll
nodes.summary: Paul W. Kroll is a sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan (circa 1967–1976). He served as Associate Professor of Chinese and department chair (~1979–1989) and held another post (~1989) at the University of Colorado Boulder.

nodes.label: Anna M. Shields
nodes.image: Anna M. Shields (born 1966) at the Center for Chinese Studies Annual Lim Lecture.png
nodes.summary: Anna M. Shields is a sinologist. She held academic posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and Princeton University (~2015).

nodes.label: Douglas Allen
nodes.summary: Douglas Allen is a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Yale, Banaras Hindu University, and Vanderbilt. He held teaching posts at Southern Illinois, Central Connecticut State, and the University of Maine, where he became Professor Emeritus of Philosophy in 2020.

nodes.id: I:State University of New York at Oneonta
nodes.label: State University of New York at Oneonta
variants: Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality at SUNY Oneonta

nodes.label: Rawi Bhavilai
nodes.native: ระวี ภาวิไล
variants: ラウィー・パーウィライ
nodes.summary: Rawi Bhavilai (1925–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Chulalongkorn University, the University of Adelaide, and the Australian National University, serving as a physics professor (1945–1986) and director at Chulalongkorn University, and as a Royal Institute fellow (~1986–2017).

nodes.label: Gary Snyder
nodes.jawiki: ゲーリー・スナイダー
nodes.summary: Gary Snyder (born 1930) studied at Reed, Indiana, and UC Berkeley under Shih-Hsiang Chen, plus Zen teachers Isshu Miura and Sesso Oda. Active in Buddhist studies and Japanology, he became a professor at UC Davis in 1986.

nodes.label: Enamul Haque
nodes.summary: Enamul Haque was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Dhaka and the University of Oxford. He led the Bangladesh National Museum (1962–1991) and the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art (1995–2022).

nodes.label: Matthew W. King
nodes.summary: Matthew W. King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett and also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thupten Champa.

nodes.label: Natalie Rothman
nodes.summary: Natalie Rothman (born 1976) is a history and archaeology scholar who completed her studies at the University of Michigan (1999–2006) and joined the University of Toronto in 2006.

nodes.label: Marylin Martin Rhie
nodes.summary: Marylin Martin Rhie works in Buddhist studies, art history, and Sinology. She studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra, and has served as a professor at Smith College.

nodes.label: Pramod Chandra
nodes.summary: Pramod Chandra was an art historian in South Asian archaeology and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Mumbai. He served as professor at the University of Chicago (1971–1980) and Bickford Professor at Harvard University (1980–2004).

nodes.label: Richard Foltz
nodes.jawiki: リチャード・フォルツ
nodes.summary: Richard Foltz (1961–) works in Iranian/Central Asian studies, religion, and history. Educated at Utah and Harvard (PhD ~1991–1996), he taught at Brown, Columbia, Kuwait, and Florida, and became Founding Director of Concordia University's Centre for Iranian Studies (~2006–2026).

nodes.label: Louise Child
nodes.summary: Louise Child works in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, studied under Ringu Tulku, and held a teaching post at Leeds.

nodes.label: Linda Hogan
nodes.summary: Linda Hogan (born 1964) is a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at Trinity College Dublin in 1991. She held posts at Chester, Leeds, and Trinity College Dublin, where she served as Vice-Provost and Chief Academic Officer (2011–2016).

nodes.label: Tyler Dewar
nodes.summary: Tyler Dewar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Nitartha Institute and under Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Acharya Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, and Acharya Tashi Wangchuk.

nodes.label: Qun Dai
nodes.summary: Qun Dai is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Bard College under the supervision of Patricia Eichenbaum Karetzky (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Mettanando Bhikkhu
nodes.summary: Mettanando Bhikkhu specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel.

nodes.label: Franz Xaver Erhard
nodes.summary: Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist who completed master's degrees at Freie Universität Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, followed by a PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Noa Gal
nodes.summary: Noa Gal is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Gal completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

nodes.id: I:Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore
nodes.label: Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore
variants: Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore
Buddhist and Pali College in Singapore

nodes.label: Julian Schott
nodes.summary: Julian Schott is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. In 2026, he is attested as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg and a faculty member at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Lama Jabb
nodes.summary: Lama Jabb is a Tibetologist who served as a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford. He is also attested in 2026 as the Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre at Wolfson College, Oxford.

nodes.label: Andrew P. Tuck
nodes.summary: Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Princeton University and under teachers including Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton.

nodes.label: Huaiyu Chen
nodes.summary: Huaiyu Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Chen earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong (1994), completed a doctorate under Stephen F. Teiser, and became assistant professor at Arizona State University (~2008).

nodes.label: Sally McAra
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Sally McAra completed her MA at the University of Auckland (1999-2000), where she studied under supervisors Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.

nodes.label: Karen Nero
nodes.description: professor of education in New Zealand
nodes.summary: Karen Nero is a scholar who held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (circa 1998–2004) and the University of Otago.

nodes.label: Cheung Tsui Lan Liza
nodes.summary: Cheung Tsui Lan Liza works in Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013), studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Toshiichi Endo.

nodes.label: Nikolai Solmsdorf
nodes.summary: Nikolai Solmsdorf is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard (attested 2013). He held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Martin Lowenthal
nodes.summary: Martin Lowenthal is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under traditional teachers Namkhai Norbu and Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche. He has held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Signe Howell
nodes.summary: Signe Howell studied at SOAS University of London (~1973–1975) and the University of Oxford (~1975–1980). In 1989, she held a post as professor at the University of Oslo.

nodes.label: René Gothóni
nodes.summary: René Gothóni is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Helsinki (~1969–1975) and later held a post there from circa 1975 to 2014.

nodes.label: Simo Knuuttila
nodes.description: Finnish professor (emeritus) of theological ethics and the philosophy of religion at the University of Helsinki, academy professor (Academy of Finland)
nodes.summary: Simo Knuuttila worked in philosophy and religious studies, completing studies at the University of Helsinki in 1976. He held academic posts there from ~1976 to 2014, including as professor from ~1981, and was affiliated with the Academy of Finland (1994–2004).

nodes.label: Michael Pye
nodes.summary: Michael Pye studied at Cambridge and Leeds (Ph.D.) and worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held lectureships at Leeds and Lancaster, a professorship at the University of Marburg (1982–2004), and a visiting professorship at Otani University.

nodes.label: Hung-Yi Yang
nodes.summary: Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Yang completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Roy Tzohar
nodes.summary: Roy Tzohar is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tel Aviv University and earned a PhD from Columbia University under Gary A. Tubb (~2004–2011). He joined the faculty of Tel Aviv University around 2011.

nodes.label: V. P. Bhatta
nodes.summary: V. P. Bhatta is an Indologist and linguist who has served as head and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary Project at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

nodes.label: Penghao Sun
nodes.summary: Penghao Sun works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. Sun studied under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Qingying Chen, Weirong Shen, Mark Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Peter K. Bol, Jay Jasanoff, James Robson, Ryuichi Abe, Jie Li, and Borjigidai Oyunbilig.

nodes.id: I:Society for the Study of Japanese Religions
nodes.label: Society for the Study of Japanese Religions
variants: Society for the Study of Japanese Religions

nodes.label: Kuntala Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Kuntala Bhattacharya is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra, and completed an MA under Prabal Kumar Sen. She held an attested post at Rabindra Bharati University in 2009.

nodes.label: Prabal Kumar Sen
nodes.summary: Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held posts at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and as a professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Yoshinori Takeuchi
nodes.description: Japanese historian of religion and philosopher (1913-2002)
nodes.summary: Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) studied philosophy, religion, and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (1959–1976) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1977–1988), and joined the Japan Academy in 1995.

nodes.label: Shu-chen Chen
nodes.summary: Shu-chen Chen works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned a PhD from the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen C. Lang, as well as Bradley W. Reed and Ronald G. Dimberg, and served there as a teaching assistant in 1996.

nodes.label: Willy Vande Walle
nodes.jawiki: ウィリー・ヴァンドゥワラ

nodes.label: Feng Youlan
nodes.summary: Feng Youlan was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking and Columbia universities. He held a long-term post at Tsinghua University (~1928–1952) and visiting appointments at the University of Pennsylvania and the University of Hawaiʻi (~1946–1947).

nodes.label: Soorakkulame Pemaratana
nodes.summary: Soorakkulame Pemaratana is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the National University of Singapore under Saranindranath Tagore. As of 2026, he is a Visiting Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Joy Cecile Brennan
nodes.summary: Joy Cecile Brennan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology who completed her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard A. Rosengarten, and Constance Furey.

nodes.label: Paul Mendes-Flohr
nodes.summary: Paul Mendes-Flohr (1941–2024) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He served as a director at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and held a professorship at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Zhiyi Yang
nodes.summary: Zhiyi Yang specializes in Sinology. She studied at Peking University and earned her PhD at Princeton University under Martin Kern. She has held posts at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kazuharu Mizuno
nodes.summary: Kazuharu Mizuno (born 1958) works in Tibetology and geography. He earned degrees from Nagoya University, Hokkaido University, and Tokyo Metropolitan University, and served as a geography professor at Kyoto University from approximately 2009 to 2024.

nodes.label: Guge Tsering Gyalpo
variants: Gu ge Tshe ring rgyal po

nodes.label: Martha Nussbaum
nodes.summary: Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher educated at NYU and Harvard. She taught at Harvard, Oxford, and Brown before joining the University of Chicago in 1995 as the Ernst Freund Distinguished Service Professor of Law and Ethics.

nodes.label: Yasuo Yuasa
nodes.summary: Yasuo Yuasa was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, University of Yamanashi, Osaka University, University of Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University.

nodes.id: I:American School of Classical Studies at Athens
nodes.label: American School of Classical Studies at Athens
variants: American School of Classical Studies at Athens
School of Classical Studies at Athens

nodes.label: Inyoung Chung
nodes.summary: Inyoung Chung specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Chung earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Seunghak Koh
nodes.summary: Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Seoul National University and a PhD from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. in 2011. He was appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: James Legge
nodes.summary: James Legge was a sinologist who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1831-1835) and Highbury College. He served as Professor at the University of Oxford beginning in 1876.

nodes.label: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche (born 1975) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sherab Ling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenchen Kunga Wangchuk, becoming abbot of Sherab Ling Monastery (~1998).

nodes.label: Sarah Harding
nodes.summary: Sarah Harding (b. 1951) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Drubpon Lama Tenpa. She served on the faculty at Naropa University (~1992–2018) and became a Tsadra Foundation fellow around 2001.

nodes.label: Lars Fogelin
nodes.summary: Lars Fogelin specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, completing a PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla M. Sinopoli. He has held academic posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University, and the University of Arizona.

nodes.label: Lilla Russell-Smith
nodes.summary: Lilla Russell-Smith specializes in history and archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London and studied under Anna Eörsi and Pál Miklós.

nodes.label: Wenjie Duan
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Wenjie Duan studied at Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and the Central Academy of Fine Arts. He served at the Dunhuang Academy as archaeological group head (1946), fine arts head (1950), and director (1991).

nodes.label: Helen Wang
nodes.summary: Helen Wang specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and sinology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1984–1988) and has served as Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum since around 1991.

nodes.label: Jennifer Jung-Kim
nodes.summary: Jennifer Jung-Kim works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, including assistant director (attested 2016) and Lecturer (attested 2026).

nodes.label: David A. Hall
nodes.summary: David A. Hall is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shōshin Ichishima and earned a doctorate from UC Berkeley (1990). He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and department chair at Montgomery College (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Guy G. Stroumsa
nodes.summary: Stroumsa studied at Paris, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Harvard, and EPHE, and founded Hebrew University of Jerusalem. In religious studies, he held lecturer, associate professor, and editor roles at Hebrew University, and was later Emeritus Professor at Oxford (2009–2013).

nodes.label: Heather Stoddard
nodes.summary: Heather Stoddard specializes in Tibetology and history-archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1964–1967) under D. C. Lau, as well as under Nicole Vandier-Nicolas and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

nodes.label: John Daishin Buksbazen
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist and religious studies, John Daishin Buksbazen studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi, Bernie Glassman, and Wendy Egyoku Nakao (all attested 2002).

nodes.label: Bernie Glassman
variants: バーニー・グラスマン・徹玄
nodes.summary: Bernie Glassman (1939–2018) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at NYU, Brooklyn Poly, and UCLA, and trained under Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka, later founding the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers.

nodes.label: Zen Center of Los Angeles
variants: Buddha Essence Temple, the Zen Center of Los Angeles

nodes.label: Soiku Shigematsu
nodes.summary: Soiku Shigematsu specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and Kyoto University, later holding posts at Shizuoka University (1975–2001) and Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).

nodes.label: Nguyen Thi Tuyet
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Nguyen Thi Tuyet earned a PhD from Punjabi University (attested 2012) under Inder Mohan Singh, and also studied under Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.

nodes.label: Punjabi University
variants: Guru Gobind Singh Department of Religious Studies, Punjabi University, Patiala

nodes.label: Wei Lin
nodes.summary: Wei Lin works in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, Lin held posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum, Transylvania University, and elsewhere.

nodes.label: Dagmar Schwerk
nodes.summary: Dagmar Schwerk specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Hamburg from around 2012 to 2017 and held a professorship at the University of Leipzig around 2022.

nodes.label: Eva Wilden
nodes.summary: Eva Wilden is an indologist who completed her MA, doctorate, and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She served as Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2003 and became a professor at the University of Hamburg in 2017.

nodes.label: Julie A. Gifford
nodes.summary: Julie A. Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Frank E. Reynolds. She held an attested post at Miami University in 2011.

nodes.label: Scott A. Mitchell
nodes.summary: Scott A. Mitchell works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008), served as professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, and held presidential posts at Numata Center (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Marybeth White
nodes.summary: Marybeth White works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned a double major honors degree from York University and was a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Araki
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Araki (born 1959), a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, completed degrees including a PhD at Kyoto University. He taught at Aichi Prefectural University, Osaka University, and was professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).

nodes.label: Aoyama Gakuin University
variants: 青山学院文学部英文科

nodes.label: Tao Jiang
nodes.summary: Tao Jiang works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo, among other teachers, and served as an Associate Professor of Religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Margarita Kleibel
nodes.summary: Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes and teacher Karin Preisendanz.

nodes.label: Siu-tong Kwan
nodes.summary: Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong, studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Zhihua Yao.

nodes.label: Marc-Henri Deroche
nodes.summary: Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein and was also taught by Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: In-gun Kang
nodes.summary: In-gun Kang is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, Jesuit School of Theology, and Heythrop College under Michael Barnes (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Aloysius Pieris
nodes.summary: Aloysius Pieris was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He earned degrees including a PhD from the University of Sri Lanka and a Th.D. from Tilburg University, and he founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre from 1974.

nodes.id: I:Jesuit School of Theology of Santa Clara University
nodes.label: Jesuit School of Theology of Santa Clara University
variants: Jesuit School of Theology at Berkeley
Jesuit School of Theology at Santa Clara University

nodes.label: Jungmin Ha
nodes.summary: Jungmin Ha works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Ha completed a master's degree at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and earned a PhD at Duke University under the supervision of Stanley Abe, attested in 2016.

nodes.label: Stanley Abe
nodes.summary: Stanley Abe is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who held attested academic posts at Duke University in 1995 and 2004.

nodes.label: Wei-Cheng Lin
nodes.summary: Wei-Cheng Lin works in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Lin served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015, joining the faculty at the University of Chicago in 2015.

nodes.label: Rafał Felbur
nodes.summary: Rafał Felbur is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He was a PhD candidate at Stanford University under Paul Harrison, having also studied under John R. McRae and Luis O. Gómez.

nodes.label: Vincent Lefèvre
nodes.summary: Vincent Lefèvre is an Indologist and historian who studied under Bruno Dagens and at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (HDR, 2007) and the École Nationale des Chartes. He has served as a curator at the Musée Guimet.

nodes.label: Jean-François Jarrige
nodes.summary: Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeology and Indology scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Paris and studied at École du Louvre and Lycée Claude Fauriel. He served as director (1986–2004) and president (~1986–2008) of the Musée Guimet.

nodes.label: Namita Das
nodes.summary: Namita Das is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

nodes.label: Alexander Coburn Soper
nodes.summary: Alexander Coburn Soper (1904–1993) worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned degrees from Hamilton College and Princeton University (PhD, 1944). nodes.label: Amod Jayant Lele
nodes.summary: Amod Jayant Lele works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Parimal G. Patil.

nodes.label: Michele Martin

nodes.label: Rudolf G. Wagner

nodes.label: Seong-Uk Kim

nodes.label: Chaisit Suwanvarangkul
nodes.summary: Chaisit Suwanvarangkul works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held researcher posts at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Huishan Lin

nodes.label: Jeff Shore
nodes.summary: Jeff Shore is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held an academic post at Hanazono University as Professor (~1987–2023) and subsequently became professor emeritus (~2023).

nodes.label: Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah
nodes.summary: Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah (1929–2014) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon, Cornell University (PhD), and Harvard. He held academic posts at Ceylon (1955–1960), Cambridge (1963–1973), Chicago (1973–1976), and Harvard (1976–2001).

nodes.label: Peter J. Wilson
nodes.summary: Peter J. Wilson earned his Ph.D. at Yale University. He taught at Yale (~1961–1964), Vassar College, the University of Washington (~1964–1968), Bennington College, and the University of Otago (~1971–1998).

nodes.label: Linda Penkower

nodes.label: Don A. Pittman

nodes.label: Martino Dibeltulo

nodes.summary: Hla Pe (1913–2007) was a linguist who studied at the University of Rangoon, the UCL Institute of Education, and SOAS University of London. He spent his career at SOAS teaching Burmese language and culture, serving as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.

nodes.label: Dungkar Lobzang Trinle
nodes.summary: Dungkar Lobzang Trinle (1927–1997) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sera and Gyuto Monasteries. He served as professor at Minzu University of China and Tibet University, and held leadership roles at TASS and CTRC.

nodes.label: Magdalene College, Cambridge
variants: ケンブリッジ大学のモードリン・カレッジ

nodes.label: Gisela Emma Full
nodes.summary: Gisela Emma Full is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster. In 2013, she held research fellow positions at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

nodes.label: Samueli Institute
variants: Samueli-Institute of Brain, Mind and Healing

nodes.label: Mingyu Fu
nodes.summary: Mingyu Fu works in Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

nodes.id: I:Buddhist Association of the United States
nodes.label: Buddhist Association of the United States
variants: Buddhist Association of the United States

nodes.label: Joey Hung
nodes.summary: Joey Hung works in computational and Buddhist studies. Educated at PLK Fong Wong Kam Chuen Primary School, Po Leung Kuk Centenary Li Shiu Chung Memorial College, and the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts, he held posts at DILA (~2014) and CIBS (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Vidya Dehejia
nodes.summary: Vidya Dehejia is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and art history. She earned her PhD from the University of Cambridge (~1963–1968). Her posts include Columbia University (associate professor 1982; professor 2002) and chief curator at the Smithsonian Institution (1994).

nodes.label: American Museum of Natural History
variants: アメリカ自然史博物館

nodes.label: James Miller
nodes.summary: James Miller is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who completed an MA at Cambridge (1997) and a PhD at Boston University (2000). In 2014, he was attested as Professor at Queen's University at Kingston.

nodes.label: Emily T. Yeh
nodes.summary: Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist who earned degrees at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993, 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003). She held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2003).

nodes.label: Surendra Man Bajracharya
nodes.summary: Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Tribhuvan University under doctoral supervisor Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

nodes.label: Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology, Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

nodes.label: Yungfen Ma
nodes.summary: Yungfen Ma works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ma completed a PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Paul Debes
nodes.summary: Paul Debes (1906–2004) was a Buddhist studies figure. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954), and the Deutsche Buddhistische Gesellschaft (1955), and served on the board of the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg.

nodes.label: Hari Shankar Prasad
nodes.summary: Hari Shankar Prasad works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, under Ramakant Tripathi, and under doctoral supervisor Jan Willem de Jong (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Mark A. Nathan
nodes.summary: Mark A. Nathan works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. His career includes posts at Kangwon National University, UCLA, and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Leopold Pospisil
nodes.summary: Leopold Pospisil studied law at Charles University, sociology at Willamette University, and anthropology at the University of Oregon and Yale University. He served as a professor at Yale (from 1956) and curator at the Peabody Museum (~1956–1993).

nodes.label: Harold C. Conklin
nodes.summary: Harold C. Conklin studied at UC Berkeley (1943–1950) and Yale (Ph.D. ~1953–1955). Active in linguistics, he held posts at Columbia University (1955), Yale University (1962–1996), and as Curator of Anthropology at the Peabody Museum (1974–1996).

nodes.label: Mirjan Damaška
nodes.summary: Mirjan Damaška studied at Zagreb, the Hague Academy, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, and Ljubljana (PhD 1960). He taught at Zagreb, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, Pennsylvania, and Yale, serving at Yale Law School from around 1976 to 2000.

nodes.label: J. J. L. Duyvendak
variants: ヤン・ユリウス・ローデウェイク・ドイフェンダック
nodes.jawiki: ヤン・ユリウス・ローデウェイク・ドイフェンダック
nodes.summary: Sinologist J. J. L. Duyvendak studied at Leiden, the Sorbonne, and Berlin, learning under Édouard Chavannes and Henri Cordier. After serving at the Dutch Legation in Peking (1912–1918), he taught at Leiden (1919; 1930–1954) and held visiting professorships at Columbia, Princeton, and Oxford.

nodes.label: Fu-shih Lin
nodes.summary: Fu-shih Lin specialized in sinology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. He completed graduate studies at Princeton University under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser, and held a post at Academia Sinica from c. 1994 to 2021.

nodes.label: Hwansoo Kim
nodes.summary: Hwansoo Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Kim held a professorship at Duke University (attested 2017) and serves as Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Helena Blankleder
nodes.summary: Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Taklung Tsetrul Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, as attested in 1999.

nodes.label: Marek Zemánek
nodes.summary: Marek Zemánek works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Seoul National University, Dongguk University, and Charles University, completing his dissertation under doctoral supervisor Radek Chlup.

nodes.label: Thich Nhat Tu
nodes.image: TT. Thích Nhật Từ phát biểu trong lễ bế mạc Đại lễ Vesak 2014.JPG

nodes.label: Tan Yun-shan
nodes.summary: Tan Yun-shan was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Taixu and Kshitimohan Sen, among others. He co-founded Visva-Bharati University, serving there as Professor of Chinese Studies (~1937–1968).

nodes.label: Kshitimohan Sen
variants: クシティモハン・セン
nodes.jawiki: クシティモハン・セン
nodes.summary: Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He worked in the Chamba State Department of Education and at Visva-Bharati University, serving as Adhyaksha (1953–1954).

nodes.label: Paul Kingsbury
nodes.summary: Paul Kingsbury is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona.

nodes.label: John Stevens
nodes.description: Buddhist priest, teacher of Buddhist studies and aikido teacher

nodes.label: Piotr Klafkowski
nodes.summary: Piotr Klafkowski is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under Jerzy Bańczerowski. He also studied under traditional teachers Lobsang Jamspal, Geleg Gyatsho, Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche, and Nyalo Tulku Jampa Kelsang Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Jerzy Bańczerowski
nodes.summary: Jerzy Bańczerowski (1938–2026) was a linguist and Sinologist. He studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961), where he later served as department head (1969) and professor (1977–1991). He became a member of the Polish Academy of Sciences (~1994).

nodes.label: Ruixuan Chen
nodes.summary: Ruixuan Chen works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leiden University (PhD attested 2018) under Paul Harrison, Jens-Uwe Hartmann, Adelheid Mette, Olav Hackstein, and Helmut Tauscher. He is attested at Peking University (2026).

nodes.label: Adelheid Mette
nodes.summary: Adelheid Mette was an Indologist who completed her doctoral and habilitation studies at the University of Hamburg. She was a professor of Indology at the University of Münster (1971; chair 1988–2000) and held professorial posts at the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Olav Hackstein
nodes.summary: Olav Hackstein (born 1962) specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Pennsylvania and Freiburg (Dr. phil. 1993), and held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1994–1999), Pennsylvania (1989), Munich (professor, 2008), and EPHE (2016).

nodes.label: Linda Learman
nodes.summary: Linda Learman works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentor Peter N. Gregory, both attested in 2005.

nodes.label: University of Nebraska Omaha
variants: ネブラスカ大学オマハ校

nodes.label: David W. Chappell
nodes.summary: David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale, he served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1972–2000) and taught at Soka University of America (~2001–2004).

nodes.label: Hajime Tanabe
nodes.summary: Hajime Tanabe was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, Kyoto University, Berlin, and Freiburg under Martin Heidegger and Heinrich Rickert. He held posts at Tohoku University (1913) and Kyoto University (1919–1945).

nodes.label: Cuma Ozkan
nodes.summary: Cuma Ozkan is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Stephan Marcus Salzberg
nodes.summary: Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

nodes.id: I:Institute for the Study of American Religion
nodes.label: Institute for the Study of American Religion
variants: Institute for the Study of American Religion

nodes.label: Edmund Ronald Leach
nodes.summary: Edmund Ronald Leach studied at Clare College, Cambridge, and the LSE. He held positions at the LSE (~1947–1953) and the University of Cambridge (1953–1978), where he was also provost of King's College (1966–1979).

nodes.label: Carolyn Woodford Schmidt
nodes.summary: Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington (attested 1990) and held posts at Ohio State University and Denison University.

nodes.label: Yanfei Zhou
nodes.summary: Yanfei Zhou specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and Sinology, and earned a PhD from the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo.

nodes.label: Yiliang Zhou
nodes.summary: Yiliang Zhou was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied at Fu Jen Catholic, Yenching, and Harvard universities, learning under Yinke Chen. He served as a professor at Peking University from around 1952 to 1998.

nodes.label: Yinke Chen
nodes.summary: Yinke Chen (1890–1969) was a historian, sinologist, and linguist who studied at institutions including Berlin, Harvard, and Zurich, and under Lanman, Lüders, Müller, and Haenisch. He held posts at Tsinghua, Peking University, Academia Sinica, and Sun Yat-sen University.

nodes.label: Norio Fujisawa
nodes.summary: Norio Fujisawa was a philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1953). He held a post at Kyoto University (~1957–1989) and served as Director of the Kyoto National Museum (~1993–2001).

nodes.label: Eberhard Fischer
nodes.image: The President, Smt. Pratibha Devisingh Patil presenting the Padma Shri Award to Dr. Eberhard Fischer, at an Investiture Ceremony-II, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, in New Delhi on April 04, 2012.jpg
nodes.summary: Eberhard Fischer specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. After earning his PhD from the University of Basel (~1960–1965), he served as director of the Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and president of the Rietberg Society (~1972–2001).

nodes.label: Kyotaro Nishikawa
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology, Kyotaro Nishikawa studied at Keio University (~1948–1952) and served as Director-General of the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties from circa 1990 to 1997.

nodes.label: Université libre de Bruxelles
variants: Center for Study of South and Southeast Asia at the University of Brussels

nodes.label: Chack-fan Lee
nodes.summary: Chack-fan Lee studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1964–1970) and the University of Western Ontario (~1970–1972). Active in Buddhist studies, he served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.

nodes.label: Sze-bong Tso
nodes.summary: Sze-bong Tso specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), studying under doctoral supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

nodes.label: Loukram Ibempishak Devi
nodes.summary: Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed her PhD at Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Kazuhiro Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Kazuhiro Yamamoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Silpakorn University, completing doctoral work under the supervision of Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Chirapat Prapandvidya
nodes.native: จิรพัฒน์ ประพันธ์วิทยา
nodes.summary: Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) works in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. Prapandvidya founded Silpakorn University, served as its Director in 1996, and taught Kazuhiro Yamamoto.

nodes.id: I:Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism
nodes.label: Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism
variants: Dawn Mountain Community Center & Research Institute

nodes.label: Phra Sigambhirayan
nodes.native: พระศรีคัมภีรญาณ
nodes.summary: Phra Sigambhirayan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Bachelor of Liberal Arts at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

nodes.label: Riika J. Virtanen
nodes.summary: Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.

nodes.label: Sandra Hochwarter
nodes.summary: Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Mag.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she studied under Anne MacDonald and completed her MA supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

nodes.label: Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu
nodes.summary: Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Oberlin College (~1967–1971) and under Fuang Jotiko (~1976–1986), whom he succeeded. He founded Metta Forest Monastery, where he served as abbot in 1993, and taught Khemako.

nodes.label: August Johan Bernet Kempers
nodes.image: Installatie nieuwe directeur van het Rijksmuseum voor Volkenkunde Het Nederland, Bestanddeelnr 909-2587.jpg
nodes.summary: August Johan Bernet Kempers worked in archaeology, history, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1926–1933) and directed the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1936–1956), later holding a post at the University of Amsterdam (1969–1984).

nodes.label: Jan Fontein
nodes.summary: Jan Fontein was a scholar of Asian art and sinology who earned his PhD at Leiden University. He held curatorial posts at the Museum of Asian Art and Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and was a visiting scholar at Royal Ontario Museum.

nodes.label: Theodoor van Erp
nodes.image: Portret van Dr Th. van Erp, luitenant der genie en restaurator van de Borobudur, RP-F-2013-61-1.jpg

nodes.label: Madhu Khanna
nodes.summary: Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. In 2012, she held attested posts at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

nodes.label: Khenpo Konchok Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Khenpo Konchok Gyaltsen (born 1946) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Suk Fun Ng
nodes.summary: Suk Fun Ng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa, having also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

nodes.label: Sarat Sarma
nodes.summary: Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Manipur University under S. Shyamkishor Singh, also studying under S. Lokendrajit Singh (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Jan Dolensky
nodes.summary: Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, attested in 2013, under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

nodes.label: Ming Mei
nodes.summary: Ming Mei works in Buddhist studies. She earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan, and studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

nodes.label: Andrey Terentyev
nodes.summary: Andrey Terentyev is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1970–1975) and held a post at the Museum of the History of Religion.

nodes.label: Wulstan Fletcher
nodes.summary: Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Taklung Tsetrul Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (both attested 1999).

nodes.label: Pei-jung Wu
nodes.summary: Pei-jung Wu works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. She earned a BA from National Taiwan University and a PhD from UCLA (2002), studying under Donald F. McCallum, Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee.

nodes.label: Ng-Fung Yuen
nodes.summary: Ng-Fung Yuen is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of the West under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda Warnasuriya (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Tsoknyi Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tsoknyi Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Khampagar Monastery and under teachers including Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse, and Tulku Urgyen. He held a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery and founded Pundarika Foundation.

nodes.label: Ling Ji
nodes.summary: Ling Ji is a Sinologist who completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Notto R. Thelle
nodes.summary: Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served as Associate Director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions (1974) and held a post at the University of Oslo (~1986–2011).

nodes.id: I:NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
nodes.label: NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
variants: National Christian Council (NCC) Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in Kyōto

nodes.label: Kiattisak Ponampon
nodes.summary: Kiattisak Ponampon works in Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Otago under Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie (attested 2015), and studied with Jinhua Chen and Seishi Karashima in 2013.

nodes.label: Win Than Tun
nodes.summary: Win Than Tun, a scholar in history and archaeology, studied at the National University of Singapore under Myo Myint.

nodes.label: Ann Grodzins Gold
nodes.summary: Ann Grodzins Gold is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD in anthropology at the University of Chicago (~1968–1984). She held posts at Cornell University (~1985–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993–2020) as Professor of Religion and Anthropology.

nodes.label: Mumon Yamada
variants: Mumon Yamada (山田 無文, Yamada Mumon)
nodes.summary: Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Hanazono University (~1922–1925) and under Seisetsu Seki (~1929–1945). He was president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), abbot of Shofuku-ji (~1949–1988), and head of The Institute for Zen Studies (1964).

nodes.label: Gianpaolo Vetturini
nodes.summary: Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of London under the doctoral supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

nodes.label: Keir Strickland
nodes.summary: Keir Strickland is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned a PhD at Durham University (~2007–2011) under Robin Coningham. He held academic posts at the University of the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016) and La Trobe University (2016).

nodes.label: Zeng Yang
nodes.summary: Zeng Yang works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen.

nodes.label: Tsering Shakya
nodes.summary: Tsering Shakya is a Tibetology and history scholar who earned his BA, MPhil, and PhD at SOAS University of London. He was a research fellow at SOAS (1999–2002), taught at Oxford, and joined the University of British Columbia (~2007).

nodes.label: Kang-nam Oh
nodes.summary: Kang-nam Oh is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed doctoral studies under Yun-hua Jan, later holding a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).

nodes.label: Hsu-feng Lee
nodes.summary: Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar. Lee completed a master's degree at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Yoshiaki Shimizu
nodes.summary: Yoshiaki Shimizu (1936–2021) was a scholar in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Harvard University (~1968–1975), he held posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1975–1984) and Princeton University (~1984–2009).

nodes.label: Douglas Q. Adams
nodes.summary: Douglas Q. Adams is a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago (through 1972) and held a post at the University of Idaho circa 1972.

nodes.label: Filippo Marsili
nodes.summary: Filippo Marsili works in Sinology and history and archaeology. He completed graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and held a post at Saint Louis University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Jane Bunnag
nodes.summary: Jane Bunnag is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of London in 1969, where she studied under supervisors Nathaniel Tarn and Barbara E. Ward.

nodes.label: Barbara E. Ward
nodes.summary: Barbara E. Ward (1919–1983) was a sinologist educated at Newnham College, the University of London, and the LSE. She held teaching posts at the University of London and the University of Cambridge, as well as visiting professorships at Cornell and CUHK.

nodes.label: David M. DiValerio
nodes.summary: David M. DiValerio is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the SIT Graduate Institute and the University of Virginia (PhD attested 2011) under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, among other teachers, he held a post at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Hubert Decleer
nodes.summary: Hubert Decleer was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Hoger Technisch Instituut Oostende, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte (1975). He held posts including academic director (1987) and senior faculty advisor (1999) at SIT Graduate Institute.

nodes.label: Maria Heim
nodes.summary: Maria Heim works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Reed College and earned her PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey. She was appointed Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

nodes.label: Lloyd W. Pflueger
nodes.summary: Lloyd W. Pflueger works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a doctorate from the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kshanika Saha
nodes.summary: Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Calcutta under the supervision of Nalinaksha Dutt.

nodes.label: Michael Baxandall
variants: マイケル・バクサンドール
nodes.jawiki: マイケル・バクサンドール
nodes.summary: Art historian Michael Baxandall (1933–2008) studied at Downing College, Cambridge, and the universities of Pavia and Munich. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum, Warburg Institute, Courtauld Institute of Art, Cornell University, and the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Jean-Pierre Drège
nodes.summary: Jean-Pierre Drège is a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yves Hervouet at the University of Burgundy and INALCO. He served as president of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1998–2004).

nodes.label: Mohammad Ashraf Dar
nodes.summary: Mohammad Ashraf Dar is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed a Master of Philosophy at Vikram University, where he was also attested as a research scholar in 2014.

nodes.label: Nyingcha Duoji
nodes.summary: Nyingcha Duoji is a Tibetologist who studied at Boston University and Harvard University, earning his PhD attested in 2014 under Mark Elliott and Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Chih-fu Li
nodes.summary: Chih-fu Li works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Li served as Director of the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2007) and later became its honorary director, having retired on December 26, 2006.

nodes.label: Stephen Fuchs
nodes.summary: Stephen Fuchs was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Wilhelm Schmidt and earned a Ph.D. at Vienna (~1948–1950). He founded the Anthropos Institute (1950) and taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1950–1954).

nodes.label: Ronald Neufeldt
nodes.summary: Ronald Neufeldt is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He spent his academic career at the University of Calgary (~1974–2006), serving as associate professor (~1980–1990) and later becoming Professor Emeritus (~2006).

nodes.label: Yoshinori Yasuda
nodes.summary: Yoshinori Yasuda (1946–2026) was an archaeologist and Japanologist. Educated at Ritsumeikan and Tohoku universities, he served at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1988–2012), Tohoku University (~2012–2014), and Reitaku University (~2014).

nodes.label: Fumio Tamamuro
nodes.summary: Fumio Tamamuro works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Meiji University (~1956–1965) and later held a post there from circa 1978 to 2006.

nodes.label: Yuan Ren
nodes.summary: Yuan Ren is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

nodes.label: Doris Unterthurner
nodes.summary: Doris Unterthurner is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

nodes.label: Manfred Taube
nodes.summary: Manfred Taube was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Friedrich Weller at the University of Leipzig, where he became Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology in 1991.

nodes.label: Diane L. Howard
nodes.summary: Diane L. Howard is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who conducted graduate studies at McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Lama Yeshe Gyamtso
nodes.summary: Lama Yeshe Gyamtso works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996) and Lama Norlha.

nodes.label: Loden Sherab Dagyab
nodes.summary: Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery and under the 14th Dalai Lama, Trijang Rinpoche, and Ling Rinpoche, joined the University of Bonn in 1966, and founded Tibethaus Deutschland in 2005.

nodes.label: Douglas Fairchild Ober
nodes.summary: Douglas Fairchild Ober is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 2016) under Harjot Oberoi.

nodes.label: Harjot Oberoi
nodes.summary: Harjot Oberoi studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University. Working in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology, he assumed a chair in Punjabi and Sikh Studies at the University of British Columbia (~1987).

nodes.label: Ter Ellingson
nodes.description: American ethnomusicologist and professor of music
nodes.summary: Ter Ellingson (born 1944) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin–Madison, and served as a professor of music at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

nodes.label: Alnis Dickson
nodes.summary: Alnis Dickson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Dickson earned an MA at McGill University (attested 2009), studying under MA supervisor Lara Braitstein and teacher G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

nodes.label: Ösel Tendzin
nodes.summary: Ösel Tendzin (1943–1990) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Fordham University and under Swami Satchidananda and Chögyam Trungpa. He served as executive vice president of Vajradhatu beginning in 1973 and succeeded Trungpa in 1987.

nodes.label: Chamnong Adivadhanasit
nodes.summary: Chamnong Adivadhanasit, active in Buddhist studies and religious studies, earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University. In 2012, he was attested as a Professor of Social Science at Kasetsart University and a part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University.

nodes.label: Lê Mạnh Thát
nodes.summary: Lê Mạnh Thát (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He earned a BA from Saigon University (~1962–1965) and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1965–1974), later holding a post at Van Hanh University (~1974–1975).

nodes.label: Pataraporn Sirikanchana
nodes.summary: Pataraporn Sirikanchana specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and served as a professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Ryoshin Nakao
nodes.summary: Ryoshin Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. Nakao served as a staff member at the Soto-shu Shumu Kenkyujo and as a professor (attested 1998) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Hanazono University.

nodes.label: Nobumi Iyanaga
nodes.summary: Nobumi Iyanaga (b. 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at EPHE. He held a research contract with EFEO (2008–2014) and served as a lecturer at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Phillip Bloom
nodes.summary: Phillip Bloom specializes in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

nodes.label: John Corrigan
nodes.summary: John Corrigan is a religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1978–1982). He held posts at Virginia, Arizona State (~1990–2000), and Florida State University, where he chaired the Department of Religion (~2001).

nodes.label: Françoise Robin
nodes.summary: Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who studied at INALCO under Heather Stoddard. She directed the Collège de France (2009–2015) and held leadership positions at INALCO, including head of the Tibetan department (2011) and department director (2013–2014).

nodes.label: Maurice Frank Wiles
nodes.summary: Maurice Frank Wiles was a religious studies scholar who studied at Cambridge. He held posts at Ridley Hall, the University of Ibadan, Clare College, and King's College London, before serving as Regius Professor of Divinity at Oxford from 1970 to 1991.

nodes.label: Iso Kern
nodes.summary: Iso Kern is a philosopher and scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at KU Leuven, University of Freiburg, Heidelberg University, and National Taiwan University. His posts include the Husserl Archives, Heidelberg University, and the University of Bern.

nodes.label: David Fiordalis
nodes.summary: David Fiordalis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. under Luis O. Gómez), later serving as associate professor and department chair at Linfield University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Burton Watson
nodes.summary: Burton Watson was a scholar of Sinology and Japanology who studied at Columbia University under William Theodore de Bary and at Kyoto University. He taught English at Doshisha University and held professorships at Columbia University and Stanford University.

nodes.label: Victor Forte
nodes.summary: Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from Temple University in 2004. He served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Albright College (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Robert Magliola
nodes.summary: Robert Magliola earned his PhD at Princeton (~1965–1970). A scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, he held posts at Purdue, Tamkang, Assumption, National Taiwan University, and Columbia University.

nodes.label: Roy W. Perrett
nodes.description: philosopher at the University of Melbourne
nodes.summary: Roy W. Perrett is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago (~1978–1981). He held academic posts at Massey University (~1987–2003), the University of Melbourne, and the University of Hawaiʻi (~2003).

nodes.label: Yingshan Chen
nodes.summary: Yingshan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who was attested as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies in 1996 and retired as an honorary research fellow on February 18, 2023.

nodes.label: Nile Green
nodes.summary: Nile Green (born 1972) is a historian of religion and Indology. He held a post at the University of Manchester (~2005–2007) before joining the University of California, Los Angeles in ~2007 as a history professor.

nodes.label: Rinzin Thargyal
nodes.summary: Rinzin Thargyal was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who completed his Magister degree at the University of Oslo in 1985, studying under supervisors Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.

nodes.label: Fredrik Barth
nodes.summary: Barth studied at the University of Chicago and Cambridge under Edmund Ronald Leach. He held professorships at the University of Bergen (1961–1972), University of Oslo (1974), Emory University (1989–1996), Harvard (~1989–1996), and Boston University (~1997–2008).

nodes.label: John Buescher
nodes.summary: John Buescher specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982 and served as Director at Voice of America (attested 2001).

nodes.label: James Duerlinger
nodes.summary: James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1961-1964) under Sheldon Pollock and served at the University of Iowa (~1971-2015), where he became Professor Emeritus.

nodes.label: Marshall Sahlins
nodes.jawiki: マーシャル・サーリンズ
nodes.summary: Marshall Sahlins worked in history and archaeology. Educated at the University of Michigan and Columbia University, he taught at Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago from 1973.

nodes.label: Jinping Liao
nodes.summary: Jinping Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

nodes.label: Gary D. DeAngelis
nodes.summary: Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious and Buddhist studies. Mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Daud Rahbar, he served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at Holy Cross (attested 2017).

nodes.label: George Rupp
nodes.summary: George Rupp is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Princeton, Yale, and Harvard. He held posts at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002).

nodes.label: Daud Rahbar
nodes.summary: Daud Rahbar (1926–2013) studied at Government College University, Lahore, and the University of Cambridge. Specializing in religious studies, he held posts at Punjab, Oriental College, McGill, Ankara, Wisconsin-Madison, and ultimately Boston University (circa 1968–1996).

nodes.label: Thomas Borchert
nodes.summary: Thomas Borchert, a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar, pursued doctoral research at the University of Chicago (attested 2005) and became Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Anna Brown
nodes.summary: Anna Brown works in religious studies and other fields. She was a Zen student under Robert Kennedy and has served at Saint Peter's University as chair of political science and director of the social justice program (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Robert Kennedy
nodes.description: American Jesuit priest, psychoanalyst and Zen rōshi

nodes.label: Hsiao-Lan Hu
nodes.summary: Hsiao-Lan Hu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a PhD from Temple University and served as an associate professor at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Richard Sylvan
nodes.summary: Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington (~1953–1957) and Princeton University (~1957–1961). He held positions at the University of Sydney (~1963–1964) and the Australian National University (fellow, 1971).

nodes.label: Sam Harris
nodes.summary: Sam Harris studied philosophy at Stanford (1997-2000), earned a Ph.D. at UCLA (~2003-2009), and studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje. His fields include philosophy and religious studies.

nodes.label: Mei Ching Hsuan
nodes.summary: Mei Ching Hsuan works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed a PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger and Dieter Schuh, and is attested as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies in 2026.

nodes.label: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche (born 1966) is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under spiritual teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and founded the organization Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

nodes.label: Matthieu Ricard
nodes.summary: Matthieu Ricard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a doctorate under François Jacob at the Pasteur Institute and studied with Kangyour Rinpoché and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, later serving on the Mind and Life Institute board.

nodes.label: Karolinska Institute
variants: Department of Histology at the Karolinska Institute

nodes.id: I:National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery
nodes.label: National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery
variants: National Hospital for the Paralysed and Epileptic

nodes.id: I:Research Institute for Brain and Blood Vessels-Akita
nodes.label: Research Institute for Brain and Blood Vessels-Akita
variants: Research Institute for Brain and Blood Vessels

nodes.id: I:National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry
nodes.label: National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry
variants: National Institute of Neurology and Psychiatry

nodes.label: Levi McLaughlin
nodes.summary: Scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies Levi McLaughlin studied at the University of Tokyo and Princeton University. He held positions at Kokugakuin University, University of Iowa, and North Carolina State University (from 2012).

nodes.label: Takashi Nakao
nodes.summary: Takashi Nakao is a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education. He held posts at Bunkyo University Women's College, the Society for the Study of Diplomatics in Japan, and Rissho University (1979–2002).

nodes.label: Axel Klein
nodes.summary: Axel Klein is a scholar of Japanology who studied at the University of Bonn. He worked at Bonn (1998–2007), the German Institute for Japanese Studies (2007–2011), and became a professor at the University of Duisburg-Essen in 2012.

nodes.label: Natasha Reichle
nodes.summary: Natasha Reichle works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Joanna Gottfried Williams, also studying with Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Alan Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.

nodes.label: Amin Sweeney
nodes.summary: Amin Sweeney was a linguist who earned his doctorate from the University of London (~1967–1970). He held posts at the National University of Malaysia (1970–1977) and the University of California, Berkeley (1986–1991, 1998).

nodes.label: Luboš Bělka
nodes.summary: Luboš Bělka is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from ~1978 to 1983 and held a post there around 1993.

nodes.label: Masaryk University
variants: Institute for the Study of Religions at Masaryk University of Brno

nodes.label: Diana Lange
nodes.summary: Diana Lange is a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history who studied at Leipzig, Tibet University, Humboldt University, and EPHE. She worked extensively at Humboldt University, the University of Hamburg, and became Professor of Central Asian History and Cultures at Humboldt in 2025.

nodes.label: Solomon George FitzHerbert
nodes.summary: Solomon George FitzHerbert is a Tibetologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford. He served as Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies at Oxford and as a researcher at the National Centre for Scientific Research (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Phramaha Phairoh Kritsanavadee
nodes.native: พระมหาไพโรจน์ กฤชนาวดี

nodes.label: Sangye Khadro
nodes.summary: Sangye Khadro is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Yeshe Thubten, Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Adam Pearcey
nodes.summary: Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, while also studying under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers.

nodes.label: Trulshik Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Trulshik Rinpoche was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and his students included the 14th Dalai Lama and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Daijaku Judith Kinst
