nodes.summary: Daijaku Judith Kinst works in Buddhist and religious studies. She served on the faculty at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013) and as Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Raimon Panikkar
nodes.summary: Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010), a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, studied under Juan Zaragüeta and earned doctorates at Madrid and Lateran. He was a philosophy professor at Madrid (1946–1953) and taught at Harvard (1967–1971) and UC Santa Barbara (1971–1978).

nodes.label: Zenkei Blanche Hartman
nodes.summary: Zenkei Blanche Hartman (1926–2016) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of California (~1943–1947), with traditional teachers including Richard Baker and Sojun Mel Weitsman, and served as co-abbess at San Francisco Zen Center (1996–2002).

nodes.label: Victor B. Lieberman
nodes.summary: Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who studied at Yale University (BA, ~1963–1967) and SOAS University of London (PhD, ~1969–1976). In 1984, he became Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History at the University of Michigan.

nodes.label: Christopher Jon Jensen
nodes.summary: Christopher Jon Jensen specializes in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University (PhD, 2018), working under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn alongside teachers Toru Funayama, Shayne Clarke, Mark Rowe, and Noel Salmond.

nodes.label: Kathrin Holz
nodes.summary: Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and holds a research affiliation post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Dzogchen Shri Sengha
variants: Shri Singha Shedra at Dzogchen Monastery

nodes.label: Hammalawa Saddhatissa
nodes.image: Most Venerable Hammalawa Saddhatissa Maha Thera (1914–1990).jpg
nodes.summary: Hammalawa Saddhatissa worked in Buddhist studies, earning degrees at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Edinburgh. He held positions at Vikramashila Pirivena, Sarnath, SOAS, Toronto, and served as head of the London Buddhist Vihara (~1957–1990).

nodes.label: Cheng Yen
nodes.summary: Cheng Yen (born 1937) is a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied as a disciple under Yinshun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.

nodes.label: Shenghai Li
nodes.summary: Shenghai Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Supervised by Donald R. Davis Jr., he completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2012) and studied under several teachers, including Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe and Charles Hallisey.

nodes.label: Bradley L. Herling
nodes.summary: Bradley L. Herling works in religious studies and philosophy. His career includes serving as Assistant Director at Boston University and holding an attested appointment at Marymount Manhattan College in 2008.

nodes.label: Sumi Lee
nodes.summary: Sumi Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned an MA at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Alexander Leonhard Mayer and a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.label: Christmas Humphreys
nodes.summary: Christmas Humphreys (1901–1983) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Malvern College and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1919–1922), and served as president of the Buddhist Society (~1924–1983).

nodes.label: Michael von Brück
nodes.description: German Protestant theologian and pastor, religious scientist and author, and Zen and yoga teacher
nodes.summary: Michael von Brück works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Rostock (1968–1973) and held professorships at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Mehlman
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Mehlman (born 1944) held posts at Cornell University (~1968–1973), Yale University (~1974–1977), and Johns Hopkins University (~1977–1983). In ~1984, he became University Professor and Professor of French Literature at Boston University, alongside several visiting professorships.

nodes.label: Timothy J. Dean
nodes.summary: Timothy J. Dean studied under Robert Clark at the University of East Anglia, later attending Brandeis and Johns Hopkins. He was a fellow at Stanford (1997–1998) and held a post at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

nodes.label: Stephanie Kaza
nodes.summary: Stephanie Kaza is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Thich Nhat Hanh and Joanna Macy, earning degrees from Oberlin, Stanford, UCSC, and Starr King School for the Ministry. She was a professor at Vermont (1991–2015).

nodes.label: Adrian Kuzminski
nodes.summary: Adrian Kuzminski is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He taught at the University of Hawaiʻi and served as a resident scholar in philosophy at Hartwick College in 1997.

nodes.label: Thi Xinh Nguyen
nodes.summary: Thi Xinh Nguyen, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed a PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Kathleen D. Morrison
nodes.summary: Kathleen D. Morrison (born 1963) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley, later serving as Assistant Professor at Northwestern University (~1995–1999) and holding a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

nodes.label: Joseph Walser
nodes.summary: Joseph Walser is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He pursued his studies under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenberg, and David S. Pacini.

nodes.label: Khenpo Dazer
nodes.summary: Khenpo Dazer, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima. He served as a teacher at both Dzogchen Monastery and Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.

nodes.label: Hisao Kanaseki
nodes.summary: Hisao Kanaseki (1918–1996), a scholar of Buddhist studies, studied at Doshisha University (~1937–1940). He held professorships at Kobe University (~1963–1969) and Komazawa University (~1982–1989), and was professor emeritus at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1982–1996).

nodes.id: I:International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism
nodes.label: International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism
variants: IRIZ (International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism)

nodes.label: King Chung Lo
nodes.summary: King Chung Lo is an indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Leipzig under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco.

nodes.label: Jinling He
nodes.summary: Jinling He is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.

nodes.label: Limei Chi
nodes.summary: Limei Chi works in Buddhist studies and Sinology and studied under Jinhua Chen. As of 2026, she is attested as a faculty member at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Karma Sonam Palmo
nodes.summary: Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She earned degrees from the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and a PhD from the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

nodes.label: Yui Suzuki
nodes.summary: Yui Suzuki works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Suzuki studied at the University of California, Los Angeles under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Davis Schoening
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Davis Schoening is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), where he studied under Collett Cox and Sanghasen Singh.

nodes.label: Chönyi Drolma
nodes.summary: Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Chönyi Drolma studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).

nodes.label: Lama Tsering Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Lama Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and with the traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

nodes.label: Mark Owen
nodes.summary: Mark Owen is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral work under the supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Stuart
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality. She served as Director (Direktorin) at the University of Winchester in 2021.

nodes.label: Jürgen Renn
nodes.description: German physicist, historian of science and university professor
nodes.summary: Jürgen Renn is a historian of science who completed his PhD at TU Berlin. He has served as a director at the Max Planck Institutes for the History of Science and Geoanthropology, alongside professorial posts at Boston University and Berlin.

nodes.label: Yulian Zeng
nodes.summary: Yulian Zeng works in the field of Buddhist studies. Zeng earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Phibul Choompolpaisal
nodes.native: พิบูลย์ ชุมพลไพศาล

nodes.label: Graham E. Clarke
nodes.summary: Graham E. Clarke (d. 1998) worked in Tibetology and other fields. He held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and at the University of Oxford, where he was a Senior Member (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Gelek
nodes.summary: Gelek is a scholar of Tibetology. He has worked as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998) and served as a visiting lecturer at the University of California and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Nancy E. Levine
nodes.summary: Nancy E. Levine is an anthropologist working in Tibetology and related fields. She has served on the anthropology faculty at the University of California, Los Angeles, as Associate Professor (attested 1998) and Professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Angela Manderscheid
nodes.summary: Angela Manderscheid is a scholar of Tibetology. She has held posts at Freie Universität Berlin and at the University of Oulu as a researcher (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Ronald D. Schwartz
nodes.summary: Ronald D. Schwartz is a sociologist specializing in Tibetology. He has served as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland (attested 1998) and as an Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Klaus-Josef Notz
nodes.summary: Klaus-Josef Notz was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Philosophisch-Theologische Hochschule Benediktbeuern and earned a Doctor theologiae from the University of Munich, where he served as a Lehrbeauftragter in 1996.

nodes.label: Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen
variants: Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen in München

nodes.label: Holmes Welch
nodes.summary: Holmes Welch (1924–1981) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, earning degrees at Harvard University (~1940–1957). He taught as a lecturer at Harvard and Yale, and served as assistant director of the Center for the Study of World Religions (~1964–1968).

nodes.label: Chuan-ying Yen
nodes.summary: Chuan-ying Yen specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Harvard University, where she studied under Chu-tsing Li, John Hay, and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield (attested 1986).

nodes.label: Chu-tsing Li
nodes.summary: Chu-tsing Li was a scholar of Sinology and art history who studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa. He taught English at Nanking (1943–1947), art history at Iowa (~1956–1965), and joined the University of Kansas faculty in 1966.

nodes.label: Kenneth J. Saunders
nodes.summary: Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara (~1908–1912). He served as a lecturer at the University of California and professor at the Pacific School of Religion (~1921–1935).

nodes.label: Takamaro Shigaraki
nodes.summary: Takamaro Shigaraki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies. At Ryukoku University, he became professor in 1970 and served as president from 1989 to 1995.

nodes.label: Ontario Tech University
variants: University of Ontario Institute of Technology

nodes.id: I:Vienna University of Economics and Business
nodes.label: Vienna University of Economics and Business
variants: Institut für Wirtschafts- und Sozialgeschichte, Wirtschaftsuniversität Wien

nodes.label: Monika Nowakowska
nodes.summary: Monika Nowakowska is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. Her academic career includes affiliations with the University of Warsaw, where she is attested between 2010 and 2026.

nodes.label: Kuno Lorenz
nodes.summary: Kuno Lorenz is a philosopher who studied at several universities, earning his PhD at Kiel and habilitation at Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held the chair of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and was a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).

nodes.label: Claus Oetke
nodes.summary: Oetke worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD (~1970–1973) and Habilitation (~1977–1983) at the University of Hamburg. He served as Dozent at Hamburg (~1983–1989) and head of Indology at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

nodes.id: I:International Consortium for Research in the Humanities
nodes.label: International Consortium for Research in the Humanities
Rolf Scheuermann
nodes.summary: Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Edward H. Schafer
nodes.summary: Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʱi, and Harvard. He spent his career at UC Berkeley (~1947–1984) and served as president of the American Oriental Society (1975–1976).

nodes.label: Paul Carus
nodes.summary: Paul Carus (1852–1919) was a philosopher and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Hermann Grassmann and attended Greifswald, Strasbourg, and Tübingen (PhD ~1876), later working at the Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919).

nodes.label: Thomas B. Ellis
nodes.summary: Thomas B. Ellis works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania and was appointed Assistant Professor of Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Jos Gommans
nodes.summary: Jos Gommans is a historian and Indologist who studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University under Jan Heesterman and André Wink. Since 1993, he has served as associate professor of South Asian history at Leiden University.

nodes.label: Dirk H. A. Kolff
nodes.summary: Dirk H. A. Kolff (born 1938) is an Indologist and historian. He earned his MA and doctorate at Leiden University, where he taught from 1991 to 2003 as Chair of Indian History after lecturing at the Kern Institute.

nodes.label: Delhi School of Economics
variants: Delhi School of Economics, University of Delhi

nodes.label: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph
nodes.summary: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was a political scientist and Indologist who studied at Sarah Lawrence, Radcliffe, and Harvard. She taught political science at Harvard (~1955–1963) and served as a professor at the University of Chicago beginning in 1964.

nodes.id: I:Fine Arts Institute of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan
nodes.label: Fine Arts Institute of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan
variants: Fine Arts Institute of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan
Fine Arts Institute, Academy of Sciences, Uzbekistan

nodes.label: Eiki Hoshino
nodes.summary: Eiki Hoshino (born 1943) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Taisho University (~1963–1969), he served as professor in the Faculty of Humanities and director at the same institution.

nodes.label: Paetpong Worapongpichet
nodes.native: แปดพงศ์ วรพงศ์พิเชษฐ

nodes.label: Yuri Parfionovich
nodes.summary: Yuri Parfionovich (1921–1990) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under George de Roerich and traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron.

nodes.label: N. J. Francis
nodes.summary: N. J. Francis is an indologist and historian-archaeologist. He completed a master's degree in ancient history at the University of Calicut and conducted doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).

nodes.label: M. R. Raghava Varier
nodes.summary: M. R. Raghava Varier (born 1936) is an Indologist, historian, and linguist. Educated at the University of Calicut, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, he served as a professor at the University of Calicut from ~1978 to 2000.

nodes.label: Rajan Gurukkal
nodes.summary: Rajan Gurukkal (born 1948), a historian and Indologist, studied at the University of Calicut and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He was on the faculty at JNU (~1983–1988) and became Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (1988).

nodes.label: Harold Scheub
nodes.summary: Harold Scheub studied at the University of Michigan (~1956–1960), UCLA (1965), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD ~1965–1969). He taught at Valparaiso University, Masindi Senior Secondary School, and served as Evjue-Bascom Professor of Humanities Emeritus at Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2013).

nodes.label: Thomas J. Mazanec
nodes.summary: Thomas J. Mazanec works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Calvin University, earned an MA from the University of Colorado Boulder, and completed his PhD at Princeton University under doctoral supervisors Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser.

nodes.label: Jeff Dolven
nodes.summary: Jeff Dolven studied at the University of Oxford and Yale University, where he earned a PhD in English. His academic appointments include a junior fellowship at Harvard and a professorship in English at Princeton University (~2002).

nodes.label: Joshua T. Katz
nodes.summary: Joshua T. Katz is a linguist who earned his BA at Yale (~1989–1993), MA at Oxford (~1993), and PhD at Harvard (~1995–1998). He served as Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022).

nodes.label: Christopher Braider
nodes.description: American French and Italian language professor

nodes.label: Nalini Bhushan
nodes.description: Andrew W. Mellon Professor in the Humanities at Smith College

nodes.label: Wilburn Hansen
nodes.summary: Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. Hansen pursued a master's program at the University of Colorado Boulder and studied at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

nodes.label: Yu-kwan Ng
nodes.summary: Yu-kwan Ng studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and McMaster University (PhD ~1980–1985 under Yun-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara). Ng held posts at Hong Kong Baptist University (1988) and National Central University (~1995–2011).

nodes.label: Bruce Charles Williams
nodes.summary: Bruce Charles Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.

nodes.label: Sodo Yokoyama
nodes.summary: Sodo Yokoyama was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Antai-ji from 1949 to 1957 under Kodo Sawaki, as well as under Eko Hashimoto.

nodes.label: Elena France Hanson
nodes.summary: Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Katherine Anne Narraway
nodes.summary: Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She completed her Master of Arts degree at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

nodes.label: Cheryl A. Crowley
nodes.summary: Cheryl A. Crowley is a scholar in Japanology. She completed her studies under William R. LaFleur, Philip B. Yampolsky, Ryuichi Abe, and Barbara Ruch.

nodes.label: Dawa Tsering
nodes.summary: Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobzang Trinle, held a post at Tibet University, and is attested at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as a Guest Lecturer cum Pharmacologist.

nodes.label: Wolfram Eberhard
nodes.summary: Wolfram Eberhard studied at Berlin under Ferdinand Lessing. He taught at several universities in China, worked at the Grassi and Berlin ethnological museums, and served as professor at Ankara University (1937–1948) and UC Berkeley (1948–1976).

nodes.label: Dörte Kamarid
nodes.summary: Dörte Kamarid works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, with Helmut Tauscher serving as her MA supervisor.

nodes.label: U Dhammissara
nodes.summary: U Dhammissara works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University for a Master of Arts under Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Asen Balikci
nodes.summary: Asen Balikci, who worked in Tibetology and other fields, earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University (1956). His career included posts at the Musée d'ethnographie de Neuchâtel, the Canadian Museum of History, the National Museum of Canada, and the University of Montreal.

nodes.label: Bo-Kwang Han
nodes.summary: Bo-Kwang Han is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2004 and 2015).

nodes.id: I:Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology
nodes.label: Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology
variants: Norwegian Institute for Palaeography and Historical Philology

nodes.label: Hoger Technisch Instituut Oostende
variants: Regent Hotel and Technical School in Ostend

nodes.label: Anne Nishimura Morse
nodes.summary: Anne Nishimura Morse is a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology who studied under John M. Rosenfield, Taka Yanagisawa, and Yutaka Hirata. She held posts at Smith College (1988–1989), Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (1988), Nara National Museum (1996), and Kyoto National Museum (1998).

nodes.label: Taka Yanagisawa
nodes.summary: Taka Yanagisawa worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Japan Women's University, Yanagisawa served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties from around 1984 to 1989.

nodes.label: Yutaka Hirata
nodes.summary: Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He earned a doctorate from Kyushu University, later serving at Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1961–1974), Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1995–2004).

nodes.label: Bunsaku Kurata
nodes.description: born:1918|died:1983|; 倉田, 文作, 1918-1983; Kurata, Bunsaku, 1918-....; 倉田, 文作; Kurata, Bunsaku
nodes.summary: Bunsaku Kurata was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda universities. He held posts at the Tokyo National Museum, the National Commission for the Protection of Cultural Properties, and served as Director of Nara National Museum (1975).

nodes.label: Takeo Izumi
nodes.summary: Takeo Izumi specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1973–1981) and later served there as a professor (~1997–2018).

nodes.label: Keizaburō Mizuno
nodes.summary: Keizaburō Mizuno (born 1932) is a scholar of archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He became Professor Emeritus at Tokyo Fine Arts School and served as director of The Niigata Prefectural Museum of Modern Art and Hanzomon Museum.

nodes.label: Seiji Nemoto
nodes.summary: Seiji Nemoto (born 1949) specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University (~1968–1972) and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~2001–2015).

nodes.label: Martin T. Adam
nodes.summary: Martin T. Adam works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes, also studying at CIHTS and under various teachers. He has served as an instructor at McGill University.

nodes.label: Michael P. Berman
nodes.summary: Michael P. Berman works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. By 2012, he was attested as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Bela Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Bela Bhattacharya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She has held posts as Professor in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and as Professor at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Bernard Williams
nodes.jawiki: バーナード・ウィリアムズ (哲学者)
nodes.summary: Bernard Williams (1929–2003) was a philosopher who studied at Chigwell School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). He held academic posts at University College London (~1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).

nodes.label: John Niemeyer Findlay
nodes.summary: John Niemeyer Findlay was a philosopher who studied at Pretoria, Oxford, and Graz. His main posts included the University of Pretoria (~1927–1934), King's College London (~1951–1966), Yale University (~1970–1972), and Boston University (~1972–1987).

nodes.label: Alasdair MacIntyre
nodes.jawiki: アラスデア・マッキンタイア
nodes.summary: Alasdair MacIntyre (1929–2025) was a philosopher who studied at Epsom College, Queen Mary University of London, and the University of Manchester. He held posts at Essex, Brandeis, Duke, London Metropolitan University, and the University of Notre Dame (~1988–2010).

nodes.label: Bruno Galasek
nodes.summary: Bruno Galasek specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Palmo Kyi
nodes.summary: Palmo Kyi is a Tibetology scholar. She studied under Per Kværne (attested 2012), Hanna Havnevik, and Rinzin Thargyal.

nodes.label: Hiroo Sato
nodes.summary: Hiroo Sato (born 1953) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1972–1981) and later served at Morioka College (~1984–1993) and as a professor at Tohoku University (~2001–2019).

nodes.label: Hsiu-hui Ji
nodes.summary: Hsiu-hui Ji is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

nodes.label: David Patt
nodes.summary: David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1993) under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under Geshe Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

nodes.label: Ngan-che Chan
nodes.summary: Ngan-che Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin (attested 2007) and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

nodes.label: Geshe Lhakdor
nodes.summary: Geshe Lhakdor studied at the Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling. In Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Tibet House, New Delhi, UBC, and the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

nodes.label: Tenzin
nodes.summary: Tenzin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Philosophy degree at the University of Oslo, where he studied under supervisor Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Meiping Li
nodes.summary: Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fo Guang University, earning a Master of Arts under Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Tao Jin
nodes.summary: Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under Alexander Leonhard Mayer.

nodes.label: Karl-Heinz Brodbeck
nodes.summary: Karl-Heinz Brodbeck works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After studying at Augsburg and the University of Munich, he held posts at Munich (1978–1988) and served as professor at the Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

nodes.id: I:Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt
nodes.label: Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt

nodes.id: I:Munich School of Politics and Public Policy
nodes.label: Munich School of Politics and Public Policy
Carlo Jamelle Harris
nodes.summary: Carlo Jamelle Harris works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in Philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Carl Shigeo Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Carl Shigeo Yamamoto is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano.

nodes.label: Richard P. Boyle
nodes.summary: Richard P. Boyle conducted graduate work at the University of Washington and studied under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki. He held a teaching post at UCLA and an affiliation with the University of New Mexico attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Tenshin Tanouye
nodes.summary: Tenshin Tanouye (1938–2003) specialized in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sogen Omori, whom he succeeded, and founded Daihonzan Chozen-ji.

nodes.label: Sogen Omori
nodes.summary: Sogen Omori worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Nihon University and under Jirokichi Yamada, Seisetsu Seki, and Bokuo Seki, later serving as professor (1970) and president (1978–1982) at Hanazono University.

nodes.label: Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach
nodes.summary: Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

nodes.label: Johannes Beltz
nodes.summary: Johannes Beltz works in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned doctorates by 1999 at the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, studying under supervisors Marie-Louise Reiniche and Johannes Bronkhorst.

nodes.label: Esben Andreasen
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology, Esben Andreasen studied at the University of Copenhagen. In 1992, he served as a visiting researcher at Otani University.

nodes.label: Daniel Borengasser
nodes.summary: Daniel Borengasser works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned his Master of Arts at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley.

nodes.label: Akiko Walley
nodes.summary: Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University and Harvard University, and held a position at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

nodes.label: Sonam Tsering
nodes.summary: Sonam Tsering specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, completing doctoral research under Gray Tuttle alongside several other teachers. As of 2026, he serves as Senior Lecturer in Tibetan and Director of the Tibetan Language Program at Columbia University.

nodes.label: Sudhir Kakar
nodes.summary: Sudhir Kakar (1938–2024) studied at Gujarat University, Mannheim, Vienna, and the Sigmund-Freud-Institut. A scholar of religious studies, he held posts at Harvard, IIM Ahmedabad (~1971–1975), and IIT Delhi (1976–1977), alongside visiting roles at institutions including INSEAD (1994–2013).

nodes.label: Naman P. Ahuja
nodes.summary: Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London and serves as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Jens Schlieter
nodes.summary: Jens Schlieter (born 1966) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1993–1999) under Josef Simon. He held posts at Bonn, Munich, Bayreuth, and became a professor at the University of Bern (~2007).

nodes.label: Yeshi Dhonden
nodes.summary: Yeshi Dhonden was a Tibetology scholar who studied at Chakpori Medical College under Khyenrab Norbu. He founded Men-Tsee-Khang in 1961 and served as its director from 1961 to 1966.

nodes.label: Chi Chen Ho
nodes.summary: Chi Chen Ho is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied under Hsuan Hua and doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr., earning a PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles (-2010), where she also served as a Teaching Assistant.

nodes.label: K. Venkata Ramanan
nodes.summary: K. Venkata Ramanan worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang, under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and at Visva-Bharati University, where he taught.

nodes.label: Satyendra Nath Bose
nodes.jawiki: サティエンドラ・ボース
nodes.summary: Satyendra Nath Bose studied at Presidency University and University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at the University of Dhaka (1921–1945), served as Professor of Physics at the University of Calcutta (1945), and was Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

nodes.label: Walter Liebenthal
nodes.summary: Walter Liebenthal specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, studying at Berlin, Marburg, Heidelberg, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau under Max Walleser, Johannes Nobel, and Otto Strauß. He held posts at the Sino-Indian Institute, Peking University, Visva-Bharati, Sorbonne/University of Paris, and Tübingen.

nodes.label: Norman Fischer
nodes.description: American Soto Zen roshi, poet and Buddhist author practicing in the lineage of Shunryu Suzuki
nodes.summary: Norman Fischer is a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied at Colgate, University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and Graduate Theological Union, and with teachers Sojun Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker. He founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.

nodes.label: Kichinosuke Ito
nodes.summary: Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosophy scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and University of Freiburg. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1923–1945), dean at Hokkaido University (1947; 1950–1951), and professor at Chuo University (1951–1958).

nodes.label: Huynh Thi Ha Vy
nodes.summary: Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, studying under Kapila Abhayawansa.

nodes.label: Douglas Gildow
nodes.summary: Douglas Gildow is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Princeton University, where he studied under Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou.

nodes.label: Ülo Valk
nodes.summary: Ülo Valk works in religious studies and indology. He studied at Miina Härma Gymnasium and the University of Tartu (~1981–1986), later holding a post at the University of Tartu around 1991 and serving as an editor at Numen.

nodes.label: David Gonsalez
nodes.summary: David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who pursued traditional studies under Gen Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Ngulchu Dharmabhadra
nodes.summary: Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ngulchu Dharmabhadra studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery around 1787 and under teachers including Yeshe Paldrup, Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen.

nodes.label: Warrin Ratanamalai
nodes.summary: Warrin Ratanamalai works in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2007) supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, and also studied under Phra Sudhivorayan and Somjin Sammāpañño.

nodes.label: Hae-ju Sunim
nodes.summary: Hae-ju Sunim is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and as an associate professor of Buddhist studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Dietmar Rothermund
nodes.summary: Dietmar Rothermund was a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (1959). He spent his main career at Heidelberg University, holding the Chair of the History of South Asia from 1968 to 2001.

nodes.label: Alan Watts
nodes.image: Alan Watts UVM 15 June 1958 Hon. D.D (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Alan Watts was a scholar and writer in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Dimitrije Mitrinović, Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, and Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki. He held positions at Northwestern University, the American Academy of Asian Studies, and the Esalen Institute.

nodes.label: Amar Singh
nodes.summary: Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under A. K. Warder (attested 1984) and studied with Rahul Sankrityayan, Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Shoryu Katsura, Masafumi Fujimoto, and Alasdair Urquhart.

nodes.label: Alasdair Urquhart
nodes.summary: Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (MA) and the University of Pittsburgh (PhD). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and became Emeritus Professor at the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: Tianshu Zhu
nodes.summary: Tianshu Zhu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Northwest University and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, and has held academic posts at Northwest University, Ohio State, Shaanxi History Museum, and Korea University.

nodes.label: Paul Tillich
nodes.summary: Paul Tillich (1886–1965) studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau. He held professorships at TU Dresden, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary, Harvard University, and the University of Chicago in theology, philosophy, and sociology.

nodes.label: Jacob N. Kinnard
nodes.summary: Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He held posts as Assistant Professor of Religion at the College of William & Mary and at the Iliff School of Theology.

nodes.label: Bryce Ryan
nodes.summary: Bryce Ryan was a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon, where he taught Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah.

nodes.label: Nguyen Van Thuong
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Nguyen Van Thuong studied at the University of Delhi under MA supervisor K. T. S. Sarao.

nodes.label: Xinru Liu
nodes.summary: Xinru Liu is a historian specializing in Indology and Central Asian history. She completed her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher (~1980–1985) and held posts at CASS (1993) and The College of New Jersey (~1993–2018).

nodes.label: Lawrence William Nelson
nodes.summary: Lawrence William Nelson is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed studies across several institutions, including Butler, Indiana, NYU, Northwestern, and St. John's College, ultimately earning a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion from the California Institute of Integral Studies.

Bryan D. Lowe
nodes.summary: Bryan D. Lowe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under Jacqueline I. Stone, among others, and held a post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Andrew Watsky
nodes.summary: Andrew Watsky (born 1957) is a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University (PhD circa 1988–1994) and held a post at Vassar College from circa 1995 to 2008.

nodes.label: Towao Sakaehara
nodes.summary: Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Osaka City University (1994, 2001–2010) and later as director of the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).

nodes.label: Ben Joffe
nodes.summary: Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Saba Mahmood
nodes.description: American anthropologist, Professor, University of California, Berkeley
nodes.summary: Saba Mahmood was a scholar of religious studies and anthropology. She studied at the University of Washington and completed her PhD at Stanford (~1992–1998). She held posts at the University of Chicago (~2000–2004) and UC Berkeley (2004–2018), where she taught Thomas Borchert.

nodes.label: Winnifred Fallers Sullivan
nodes.summary: A religious studies scholar, Sullivan earned degrees from Cornell and the University of Chicago. She held posts at Washington and Lee, Chicago, University at Buffalo, and Indiana University Bloomington.

nodes.label: Martin Riesebrodt
nodes.summary: Martin Riesebrodt (1948–2014) worked in religious studies. He studied at Tübingen, Humboldt, Heidelberg (Promotion), and Munich (Habilitation). He was a professor at the University of Chicago and its Divinity School (1990–2011) and at the Graduate Institute (2013).

nodes.label: Joanne Punzo Waghorne
nodes.summary: Joanne Punzo Waghorne is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago. She held posts at the University of Massachusetts Boston, Bowdoin College, UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University.

nodes.label: Takahiko Kameyama
nodes.summary: Takahiko Kameyama works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Attested in 2015, Kameyama held posts as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Courtney Bruntz
nodes.summary: Courtney Bruntz works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015) and later as a professor of East Asian Buddhism at the Numata Center (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Wes Borton
nodes.summary: Wes Borton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Borton studied at East Carolina University under Derek F. Maher and also studied at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer
nodes.summary: Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer is a scholar in religious studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower and conducted postdoctoral studies under Xiuping Hong.

Biología del Conocer (Biology of Knowing) research center

nodes.label: Yangdon Dhondup
nodes.summary: Yangdon Dhondup is a Tibetologist who earned a PhD from SOAS University of London (~2000–2004) under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.

nodes.label: Christopher Byrne
nodes.summary: Christopher Byrne specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at McGill University (attested 2015) for his PhD under doctoral supervisor Grace S. Fong, and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates.

nodes.label: Alexander James O'Neill
nodes.summary: Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. A PhD candidate at the University of Toronto, he has served as a research fellow at Taisho University.

nodes.label: Kenneth J. Guest
nodes.summary: Kenneth J. Guest is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. He studied at Columbia, Union Theological Seminary, Peking University, and the CUNY Graduate Center, and held teaching posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

nodes.label: Vishwanath Prasad Varma
nodes.summary: Vishwanath Prasad Varma (born 1924) is a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and history. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta, Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, doctoral supervisor Kali Kinkar Datta, and Joachim Wach.

nodes.label: Dhirendra Mohan Datta
nodes.summary: Dhirendra Mohan Datta was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held appointments at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).

nodes.label: Joachim Wach
nodes.summary: Joachim Wach was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Leipzig and Heidelberg. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1924–1935), Brown University (1935–1946), and the University of Chicago (1945–1955).

nodes.label: Don Handelman
nodes.summary: Don Handelman is an anthropologist and scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester, and was Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1972–2007).

nodes.label: Charles Malamoud
nodes.description: French historian of religion and orientalist
nodes.summary: Charles Malamoud is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris. He held positions at the University of Lyon and served as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1979 to 1998.

nodes.label: Laren Hogen Bays
nodes.summary: Laren Hogen Bays specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies and studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada. Bays founded Great Vow Zen Monastery and serves as its co-abbot.

nodes.label: Mikio Otsuki
nodes.summary: Mikio Otsuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. In 2007, he held attested posts as a professor at Hanazono University and as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji.

nodes.label: Mary Margaret McCabe
nodes.summary: Mary Margaret McCabe (b. 1948) is a philosopher. She studied at Newnham College (BA) and Cambridge (PhD). She was a Fellow at Murray Edwards College (1981–1990) and Professor at King's College London (1990–2014).

nodes.label: Verity Harte
nodes.summary: Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge. She held research posts at St Edmund's College and St Hilda's College, taught at King's College London, and was named professor at Yale University in 2006.

nodes.label: Raimond Gaita
nodes.summary: Raimond Gaita (born 1946) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Melbourne and the University of Leeds. He served as Professor of Moral Philosophy at King's College London (1977–2011) and Foundation Professor of Philosophy at Australian Catholic University (1993–2011).

nodes.label: Jonathan Lear
nodes.summary: Jonathan Lear was a philosopher who studied at Yale, Cambridge, and Rockefeller University. He taught at Yale (1978–1996), Cambridge and Clare College (1979–1985), and served as John U. Nef Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago (2014–2022).

nodes.label: Susan Neiman
nodes.description: American philosopher, essayist and cultural commentator (born 1955)
nodes.summary: Susan Neiman (born 1955) is a philosopher who studied at Harvard and the Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and has served as Director of the Einstein Forum since 2000.

nodes.label: Jonathan Glover
nodes.summary: Jonathan Glover is a philosopher educated at Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He served as a fellow and tutor at New College, Oxford (~1967–1998), held a post at King's College London (~1998–2013), and was a research fellow at Oxford.

nodes.label: Songeun Choe
nodes.summary: Songeun Choe is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Michael W. Meister
nodes.summary: Michael W. Meister specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at Harvard University and also studied at the University of Pennsylvania, where he became a professor around 1976, succeeding Stella Kramrisch.

nodes.label: Melissa R. Kerin
nodes.summary: Melissa R. Kerin is a scholar in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter.

nodes.label: Tashi Samphel
nodes.summary: Tashi Samphel works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has served as director of the Songtsen Library (attested 2015) and as an Associate Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Manfred B. Steger
nodes.summary: Manfred B. Steger studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and Rutgers University under Robert Baker Aitken. His career includes posts at Illinois State University, RMIT University, the University of Hawaiʻi, and Western Sydney University.

nodes.label: Keenan W. Cox
nodes.summary: Keenan W. Cox is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Cox earned an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Brian Bocking
nodes.summary: Brian Bocking is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Leeds, where he studied under Michael Pye.

nodes.label: André Couture
nodes.summary: André Couture is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at Laval University (~1964–1970), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1972–1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1972–1977), later holding a post at Laval University (~1978).

nodes.label: Shi Xianda
nodes.summary: Shi Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from the University of Kelaniya and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where he studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Seung-yeon Lee
nodes.summary: Seung-yeon Lee works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Supervised by Sang-hae Lee for doctoral studies, Lee held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties.

nodes.label: Yunxi Wang
nodes.summary: Yunxi Wang (1926–2014) was a Sinologist who studied at Fudan University from circa 1947 to 1951 and held a post there from circa 1952 to 2014.

nodes.label: Salvador E. Luria
nodes.jawiki: サルバドール・エドワード・ルリア
nodes.summary: Salvador E. Luria studied at Turin, Rome, and Columbia. He held posts at Columbia (~1940-1942), Indiana (1943), Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1950-1959), and MIT (~1959-1991).

nodes.label: Jampa Mackenzie Stewart
nodes.summary: Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and Jamgon Kongtrul Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Norihisa Baba
nodes.summary: Norihisa Baba is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda. He held posts at Darwin College, Stanford, and the University of Tokyo, where he became professor in 2019.

nodes.label: Robert Zydenbos
nodes.summary: Robert Zydenbos specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. After studying at Utrecht University (~1974–1983), he held posts at the University of Toronto, University of Munich (~2003), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Alessandro Giudice
nodes.summary: Alessandro Giudice is an Indologist and linguist. He holds a post at the University of Munich and serves as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Athanaric Huard
nodes.summary: Athanaric Huard, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, studied under Georges-Jean Pinault and is attested in 2026 as an Assistent at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Yannick Laurent
nodes.summary: Yannick Laurent works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He held posts as Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and Dr. at the University of Munich, both attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Danping Long
nodes.summary: Danping Long specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. As attested in 2026, she has studied as a doctoral student at the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Richard Bowring
nodes.summary: Richard Bowring (1947–) is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge (BA, doctorate, Litt.D), and held posts at Columbia, Princeton, Selwyn College (Master 2000–2012), and Cambridge, where he became Emeritus Professor (1985).

nodes.label: Sherry B. Ortner
nodes.summary: Sherry B. Ortner (born 1941) works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Bryn Mawr College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan, and held posts at Sarah Lawrence College (~1971–1977), University of Michigan (~1977–1994), and UCLA (~2004).

nodes.label: Anuj Misra
nodes.summary: Anuj Misra is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker and has served as an external researcher at the University of Copenhagen (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Dan Li
nodes.summary: Dan Li works in linguistics and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sherab Gyatso and served as an associate professor at Soka University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hoko Kuwana
nodes.summary: Hoko Kuwana is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (attested 2015) and holds a director post at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hoju Shioda
nodes.summary: Hoju Shioda is a Buddhist studies scholar. Affiliations attested in 2026 include Minobusan University (assistant professor and assistant director), the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, and part-time lectureships at Doho University and the Daido University graduate school.

nodes.label: Gyoon Iotani
nodes.summary: Gyoon Iotani works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a post as deputy director (副主任) at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Fumihiro Okada
nodes.summary: Fumihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and holds a post as specially appointed associate professor at Minobusan University.

nodes.label: Akiko Kikuchi
nodes.summary: Akiko Kikuchi works in Buddhist studies. She was a research student at Minobusan University (attested 2026) and served as a professor at Musashino University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Takahiko Sato
nodes.summary: Takahiko Sato works in Buddhist studies. Sato held a post as a professor at Koyasan University, attested in 2015 and 2026.

nodes.label: Kazuhiro Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Kazuhiro Kawasaki (born 1974) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies at Koyasan University. He has held positions there as a researcher (attested 2005) and special appointed professor (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Thomas Dreitlein
variants: トーマス・ドライトライン

nodes.label: Jun Yang
nodes.summary: Jun Yang works in linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Yang's affiliations include serving as a Senior Lecturer in Chinese Language at the University of Chicago and as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University, both attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Bożena Śliwczyńska
nodes.summary: Bożena Śliwczyńska is an Indologist who studied under Maria Krzysztof Byrski. She held a faculty post at the University of Warsaw around 1989.

nodes.label: Zev Handel
nodes.description: professor of Asian languages and literature
nodes.summary: Zev Handel works in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard College (1988) and the University of California, Berkeley (1992, 1998). He became a professor at the University of Washington around 1999 and taught Zhihua Li.

nodes.label: Fuyuan Luo
nodes.summary: Fuyuan Luo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He pursued a PhD at the University of Cambridge under the supervision of Adam Yuet Chau (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Mathew Varghese
variants: マシュー・ヴァルギース

nodes.label: Jampa Lhundup
nodes.summary: Jampa Lhundup is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. Attested in 2026, he studied as an Assistant Professor of Art History and served on the faculty at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Jan Christian Schaffert
nodes.summary: Jan Christian Schaffert works in Indology and computational studies. Attested in 2026, he studied and worked as a collaborator on the EdiKILex project at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Xiaoming Hou
nodes.summary: Xiaoming Hou is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Hou was a doctoral student at Ghent University (attested 2026) and served there as a postdoctoral researcher (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jens Peter Laut
nodes.summary: Jens Peter Laut (born 1954) is a scholar in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2008) and the University of Göttingen (~2008–2020).

nodes.label: Paul R. Brass
nodes.summary: Paul R. Brass (1936–2022) specialized in Indology. He studied at Harvard College, Harvard University, and the University of Chicago, and spent his career as a professor at the University of Washington.

nodes.label: Yadi Qu
nodes.summary: Yadi Qu works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational studies, and is attested in 2026 as a student and Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Barbara Harriss-White
nodes.summary: Barbara Harriss-White (born 1946) is a development studies scholar in Indology. Educated at Newstead Wood School, she held posts at the University of East Anglia (1975–1979), Queen Elizabeth House (~1987–2011), Wolfson College, and the University of Oxford (~1987–2011).

nodes.label: Rajesh P. N. Rao
nodes.description: Indian computer scientist, computational neuroscientist and academic
nodes.summary: Rajesh P. N. Rao (born 1970) works in computational fields and Indology. He studied under Dana H. Ballard at the University of Rochester and at Angelo State University. In 2000, he became a professor of computer science at the University of Washington.

nodes.label: Purnima Dhavan
nodes.summary: Purnima Dhavan is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Virginia. She held posts at Bowdoin College, St. John's University, and the University of Washington, where she became Associate Professor in 2005.

nodes.label: Anand A. Yang
nodes.summary: Anand A. Yang is a historian and Indologist who studied at Swarthmore College and the University of Virginia. He held positions at Sweet Briar College and the University of Utah before becoming a professor at the University of Washington around 2002.

nodes.label: Chris Williams
nodes.summary: Chris Williams is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied and served as teaching staff at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Rita Langer (attested 2026).

variants: ライアン スミザース

nodes.label: Caroline Bergmann
variants: カロリーネ ベルグマン

nodes.label: Qian Cao
nodes.summary: Qian Cao works in Indology and religious studies, serving as both a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Corinna May Lhoir
nodes.summary: Corinna May Lhoir works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Attested in 2026, she is a PhD student at Ghent University, a doctoral researcher at the University of Hamburg, and a yoga studies program coordinator and lecturer at Hamburg.

nodes.label: Simon Winant
nodes.summary: Simon Winant is an Indology and linguistics scholar. As of 2026, he is attested as both a PhD student and a faculty member at Ghent University.

nodes.label: Yifan Zhang
nodes.summary: Yifan Zhang is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who is attested in 2026 as a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

nodes.label: Edwin Arnold
variants: エドウィン・アーノルド
nodes.jawiki: エドウィン・アーノルド
nodes.summary: Edwin Arnold was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Japanologist who studied at King's College London and Oxford. He served as principal of Deccan College (1856), taught at Keio University, and founded the Maha Bodhi Society.

nodes.label: Francis William Bain
nodes.summary: Francis William Bain was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Westminster School and Christ Church, Oxford (~1882–1889), he served as Professor of History and Political Economy at Deccan College (~1892–1919).

nodes.label: Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist. In 1884, he was Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, later serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College and permanently at Wilson College, Mumbai.

nodes.label: Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia
nodes.summary: Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at University College London from around 1934 to 1936 and served as a professor at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from around 1939 to 1973.

nodes.label: Irawati Karve
nodes.description: Indian sociologist, anthropologist, educationist, and writer (1905-1970)
nodes.summary: Irawati Karve (1905–1970) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Fergusson College, Huzurpaga, and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. She served at Deccan College (~1939–1970) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1951–1952).

nodes.label: Ashok Ramchandra Kelkar
nodes.summary: Ashok Ramchandra Kelkar was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Cornell University. He held posts at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1967–1989).

nodes.label: Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar
nodes.summary: Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar was an Indian historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai (~1913–1917) and served on the faculty at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1939–1955).

nodes.label: Divyaraj Amiya
nodes.summary: Divyaraj Amiya is an Indologist and linguist attested in 2026 as faculty at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich.

nodes.label: Amara Ali
nodes.summary: Amara Ali is an Indologist and linguist who has served as a Lecturer in Urdu at the University of California, Berkeley, and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Munis D. Faruqui
nodes.summary: Munis D. Faruqui (born 1967) works in Indology and history. He has served as professor and undergraduate advisor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2006) and as Director and Sarah Kailath Chair of India Studies at the Numata Center (~2015).

nodes.label: Martha Ann Selby
nodes.summary: Martha Ann Selby is an Indologist who is Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin. Attested in 2026, she serves as Sangam Professor of South Asian Studies and chair of the Department of South Asian Studies at Harvard University.

nodes.label: Orion Klautau
variants: オリオン・クラウタウ

nodes.label: Marielle Harrison
nodes.summary: Marielle Harrison works in religious and Buddhist studies. A doctoral student at the University of Chicago (attested 2026), she served as an HCBSS Postdoctoral Fellow Lecturer in the Department of Religious Studies at Stanford University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Eiichi Otani
nodes.summary: Eiichi Otani (born 1968) works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Toyo University (~1987–1991) and was attested in 2026 as dean and professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University.

nodes.label: Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran
nodes.summary: Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran works in Indology and philosophy. A doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago, Parmeswaran is attested as a researcher at Ghent University in 2026.

nodes.label: August Sundin
nodes.summary: August Sundin is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar attested in 2026 as a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

nodes.label: Iona Macgregor
nodes.summary: Iona Macgregor is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Nantu Shaw
nodes.summary: Nantu Shaw is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Stony Brook University as a visiting scholar under doctoral supervisor Sthaneshwar Timalsina (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Christopher Framarin
nodes.summary: Christopher Framarin is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi (-2001) and a PhD at the University of New Mexico (-2005). He held faculty posts at the University of Calgary (attested 2014, 2026).

nodes.label: Imre Bangha
nodes.description: Hungarian orientalist, Indologist, translator, university lecturer (1967–)
nodes.summary: Imre Bangha is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Visva-Bharati University. He has served as Associate Professor of Hindi at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College since ~2003, and at ELTE.

nodes.label: Sarath Piyananda Weerasekara
nodes.summary: Sarath Piyananda Weerasekara works in Buddhist and religious studies. He pursued a Sinhala-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under Deshapriya Gunasena / G. A. Gamini (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Huabei Tan
nodes.summary: Huabei Tan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Tan pursued an English-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under supervisor Medawachchiye Dhammajothi (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Caixi Chen
nodes.summary: Caixi Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the doctoral supervision of Wadinagala Pannaloka (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Amelia Bonea
nodes.summary: Amelia Bonea is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo and Heidelberg University (~2005–2009). She became Senior Lecturer in Global History of Science, Technology and Medicine at the University of Manchester (~2018).

nodes.label: Wayne Chandira
nodes.summary: Wayne Chandira focuses on Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Mark Rowe.

nodes.label: Joshua Ereshefsky
nodes.summary: Joshua Ereshefsky works in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn.

nodes.label: Benjamin Goldstein
nodes.summary: Benjamin Goldstein works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. As attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.

nodes.label: Pema Sherpa
nodes.summary: Pema Sherpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Attested in 2026, she is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.

nodes.label: Mery Cecconi
nodes.summary: Mery Cecconi is an Indologist. Attested in 2026, she is a PhD candidate at Leiden University, studying under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop.

nodes.label: Olli Littunen
nodes.summary: Olli Littunen works in Indology and religious studies. Littunen is a PhD candidate at Leiden University studying under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Kexin Zheng
nodes.summary: Kexin Zheng is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied as a PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Thomas Blom Hansen
nodes.summary: Thomas Blom Hansen (born 1958) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Aalborg University. He held posts at the University of Natal, Edinburgh (~2000–2003), Yale (~2001–2003), Amsterdam (~2003–2011), and Stanford University (Professor of Anthropology, 2010).

nodes.label: Paride Stortini
nodes.summary: Paride Stortini specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied as a doctoral student at the University of Chicago (attested 2026) and was appointed as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Tashi Rabgey
nodes.summary: Tashi Rabgey specializes in Tibetology and studied at Magdalen College, Harvard University, the University of Cambridge, and University College, Toronto. She held posts at the University of Virginia (~2008–2011) and Georgetown University.

nodes.label: Soshuku Shibatani
nodes.summary: Soshuku Shibatani is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at Waseda and Koyasan University (PhD ~2008–2013). He taught at Sonoda Women's University and served as a researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2015, 2026).

nodes.label: Litian Fang
nodes.summary: Litian Fang (1933–2014) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. After studying at Peking University under Feng Youlan, Yongtong Tang, and Zhang Dainian (ca. 1956–1961), he served as professor, doctoral supervisor, and founding director at Renmin University of China (ca. 1961–2014).

nodes.label: Nira Wickramasinghe
nodes.summary: Nira Wickramasinghe (born 1964) is a scholar of history and Indology who studied at the University of Paris (~1981–1984) and the University of Oxford (~1985–1989). She became Professor of Modern South Asian Studies at Leiden University (~2010).

nodes.label: Klaus Pinte
nodes.summary: Klaus Pinte is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and served on the postdoctoral teaching staff at Ghent University in 2006.

nodes.label: Zhengyan Fan
nodes.summary: Zhengyan Fan works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, he was a PhD researcher and faculty member at Ghent University.

nodes.label: Arghyadip Mondal
nodes.summary: Arghyadip Mondal works in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and Indology. He has been a PhD researcher and faculty member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Balram Shukla
nodes.summary: Balram Shukla (born 1982) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Delhi from circa 2003 to 2010 and became a professor there around 2013.

nodes.label: Sambhavi Ganesh
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, Sambhavi Ganesh is attested in 2026 as a doctoral student at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Radhika Govinda.

nodes.label: Geetha K. Wilson
nodes.summary: Geetha K. Wilson is an Indologist who has been a doctoral student under Claire Maes and a faculty member at the University of Tübingen (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sonam Choden
nodes.summary: Sonam Choden works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She is a doctoral local researcher and project staff member (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin) at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sonam Jamtsho
nodes.summary: Sonam Jamtsho is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who taught Gembo Dorji. As of 2026, he is a doctoral local researcher and Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Jingyi Yang
nodes.summary: Jingyi Yang works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational fields. Yang studied at the University of Hamburg and held a post there as a research project employee (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Takahiro Kato
nodes.summary: Takahiro Kato works in Indology and philosophy. As attested for 2026, Kato serves as a professor at the University of Tokyo and holds a post at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Fumi Yao

nodes.label: Satoru Fujiwara
