nodes.label: Hiroshi Arami
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Arami works in sinology and Buddhist studies. In 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Shunji Hosaka
nodes.summary: Shunji Hosaka specializes in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Waseda University (~1975–1980), he taught at Reitaku University (~1988–1996) and Chuo University (~1996), and held posts attested in 2026 at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Iwao Ishikawa
nodes.summary: Iwao Ishikawa is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He was a researcher at Toho Kenkyukai (attested 2000) and has held lecturer and researcher roles at ICPBS, IIBS, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yasuko Kojima
nodes.summary: Yasuko Kojima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, she holds lecturer positions at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Shoko Miyata
nodes.summary: Shoko Miyata works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Miyata's affiliations include lecturer posts at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Ryuken Nawa
nodes.summary: Ryuken Nawa works in Indology and Buddhist studies. His posts include lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, both attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Ryushin Sudo
nodes.description: Japanese bhikkhu, historian and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Ryushin Sudo studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Taisho University around 1948–1953. He later held lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Masataka Suzuki
nodes.summary: Masataka Suzuki works in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Keio University and held a post there from circa 1980 to 2015. He also served as a lecturer attested at ICPBS and IIBS in 2026.

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama (born 1950) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, he serves as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Masayuki Tsukimoto
nodes.summary: Masayuki Tsukimoto is a scholar of Japanology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. His career includes lecturer posts attested in 2026 at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Shuichi Nara
nodes.summary: Shuichi Nara is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Keio University. He held positions as a full-time researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and lecturer at Chuo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jifu Lan
nodes.summary: Jifu Lan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Tunghai University (~1965–1969). He served as a full-time researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies from circa 1985 until his retirement in 2019.

nodes.label: Zack Beer
nodes.summary: Zack Beer is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of California, Berkeley and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger
nodes.summary: Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Goshen College (~1970–1974) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1974–1984). She served at Emory University (~1991–2022), where she became Professor Emerita.

nodes.label: Maanasa Visweswaran
nodes.summary: Maanasa Visweswaran works in Indology and computational studies. In 2026, Visweswaran is attested as a student and project staff member (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin) at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Ferenc Ruzsa
nodes.summary: Ferenc Ruzsa specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium (~1971–1975) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1976–1982), where he held a post as kari munkatárs starting around 1982.

nodes.label: Roland Ferenczi
nodes.summary: Roland Ferenczi is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. His academic posts (both attested 2026) include visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University and project staff member at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Chuichi Kimura
nodes.summary: Chuichi Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an associate professor (attested 2015) and former professor (attested 2026) at Minobusan University.

nodes.label: Ryoji Kishino
nodes.summary: Ryoji Kishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held appointments at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).

nodes.label: Yuki Sasaki
nodes.summary: Yuki Sasaki is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. In 2026, Sasaki was attested as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Yoshimi Nozawa
nodes.summary: Yoshimi Nozawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. As of 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Taichi Tado
nodes.summary: Taichi Tado is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology. In 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Vinay Lal
nodes.summary: Vinay Lal is a scholar of history and Indology who studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1980–1984). In ~1993, he became a professor in the Department of History and Asian American Studies at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Saloni Mathur
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, history, and archaeology, Saloni Mathur holds posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, attested as Associate Professor of Art History in 2011 and as Department Chair and Professor of Modern & Contemporary South Asian Art in 2026.

nodes.label: Monica L. Smith
nodes.summary: Monica L. Smith is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied at the University of Michigan (ca. 1991–1997). She held a post at the University of Pittsburgh (2000–2002) before joining the University of California, Los Angeles in 2002.

nodes.label: Daniel M. Neuman
nodes.summary: Daniel M. Neuman specializes in Indology and ethnomusicology. He studied at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago, holding academic posts at Dartmouth College, the University of Washington, and UCLA.

nodes.label: Cynthia Talbot
nodes.summary: Cynthia Talbot is an Indologist and historian. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1980–1988) and has served at the University of Texas at Austin (~1995), where she is Professor Emeritus.

nodes.label: Winfred P. Lehmann
nodes.summary: A specialist in linguistics and Indology, Winfred P. Lehmann studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1937–1941). He was Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (~1986–2007).

nodes.label: Edgar Polomé
nodes.summary: Edgar Polomé was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Université catholique de Louvain (~1938–1949). He later served on the faculty at the University of Texas at Austin (~1961–1990).

nodes.label: Melvin Pötzsch
nodes.summary: Melvin Pötzsch works in linguistics and Indology. Publications from 2026 attest his positions as a research fellow and academic staff member (Wiss. Mitarbeiter) at the University of Marburg.

nodes.label: Mirella Lingorska
nodes.summary: Mirella Lingorska works in Indology and linguistics. She has held posts as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich and at the University of Tübingen, both attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Rebecca Hufen
nodes.summary: Rebecca Hufen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, she is a doctoral student under Dorji Wangchuck and a lector for Tibetan Studies at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Andrew Ollett
nodes.summary: Andrew Ollett (born 1986) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oxford (circa 2008–2010) and Columbia University (circa 2010–2015), becoming an associate professor at the University of Chicago circa 2020.

nodes.label: Uta Reinöhl
nodes.description: researcher in the field of digital humanities
nodes.summary: Uta Reinöhl is a linguist and Indologist who held a post at the University of Cologne in 2018 and serves as Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg.

nodes.label: Sarah Merkle-Schneider
nodes.summary: Sarah Merkle-Schneider is an Indologist. She completed an M.A. at the University of Tübingen and held an M.A. post there as of 2026.

nodes.label: Klaus Butzenberger
nodes.summary: Klaus Butzenberger works in Indology, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned his master's at the University of Munich and pursued doctoral studies under Friedrich Wilhelm. He held academic positions at Munich, Freie Universität Berlin, Humboldt University, and the University of Tübingen.

nodes.label: Mahiro Ito
nodes.summary: Mahiro Ito (born 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar who succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021. Ito has held professorships at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Hironobu Minami
nodes.summary: Hironobu Minami works in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a research assistant at the Chion'in Jodo Sect Research Institute (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Ryūshin Saitō
nodes.summary: Ryūshin Saitō specializes in Buddhist studies. Affiliations include the Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2001), a professorship at Bukkyo University (attested 2015), and a faculty position at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Danuta Stasik
nodes.summary: Danuta Stasik (born 1956) is an Indologist. She studied at the University of Warsaw (circa 1975–1980) under Maria Krzysztof Byrski (circa 1980–1989), and held posts at the University of Warsaw, including in 1986 and circa 1980.

nodes.label: Eiju Fukushima
nodes.summary: Eiju Fukushima works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and religious studies. Fukushima is attested in 2026 as a faculty member at both Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.

nodes.label: Norihiro Matsuura
nodes.summary: Norihiro Matsuura is a scholar in history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held faculty posts at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society, both attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Y. B. Damle
nodes.summary: Y. B. Damle studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and served as Professor of Sociology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Peri Bhaskararao
nodes.jawiki: バースカララーオ・ペーリ
nodes.summary: Peri Bhaskararao (b. 1947) is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Phonetics and Phonology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1986–1998) and held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1998–2012).

nodes.label: Amartya Sen
nodes.summary: Amartya Sen is a philosopher and economist who studied at the University of Calcutta and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held positions at Jadavpur University, the University of Delhi, the London School of Economics, and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Remeen Firoz
nodes.summary: Remeen Firoz is a researcher in Indology who is attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. student at the Australian National University under the supervision of Assa Doron.

nodes.label: Ranu Kunwar
nodes.summary: Ranu Kunwar is a PhD student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.

nodes.label: Giti Dutt
nodes.summary: Giti Dutt is a PhD student at the Australian National University, studying under the supervision of Assa Doron.

nodes.label: Muhamad Saputra
nodes.summary: Muhamad Saputra is a doctoral student at the Australian National University, attested in 2026 studying under supervisor Assa Doron.

nodes.label: Azizah Nur
nodes.summary: Azizah Nur is a doctoral student attested at the Australian National University in 2026, studying under supervisor Assa Doron.

nodes.label: Camillo Formigatti
nodes.summary: Camillo Formigatti is an Indologist who studied at the University of Milan. He worked on Cambridge's Sanskrit Manuscripts Project (2011–2014), taught Sanskrit at SOAS, served as Bodleian Sanskrit Librarian (attested 2019), and was a Research Fellow at Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sabine Klein-Schwind
nodes.summary: Sabine Klein-Schwind works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Harunaga Isaacson and was attested as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg in 2026.

nodes.label: Leo Rishi Nelson Jones
nodes.summary: Leo Rishi Nelson Jones works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a project staff member (attested 2026).

nodes.label: William C. Chittick
nodes.summary: William C. Chittick works in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tehran (~1966–1974), he held positions at Sharif University of Technology (~1970–1978), University at Albany, SUNY (~1980–1983), and Stony Brook University (~1983).

nodes.label: Lakshmi Swaminathan
nodes.description: officer in the Indian National Army (INA) and former presidential candidate of India
nodes.summary: Lakshmi Swaminathan worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Queen Mary's College (~1930–1932) and Madras Medical College (~1932–1938), later serving as a retired lecturer at Stony Brook University.

nodes.label: Sara Frumento
nodes.summary: Sara Frumento is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar attested in 2026 as studying for a DPhil in Area Studies (South Asia) at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.

nodes.label: Sondra L. Hausner
nodes.summary: Sondra L. Hausner is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, she serves as Professor of Anthropology of Religion at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.

nodes.label: Mallica Kumbera Landrus
nodes.summary: Mallica Kumbera Landrus works in Indology and history/archaeology. As of 2026, she is Keeper of Eastern Art at the Ashmolean Museum of Art and Archaeology and Associate Professor of Indian Art at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College.

nodes.label: Gyokusen Hosaka
nodes.summary: Gyokusen Hosaka studied at Komazawa University in the field of Buddhist studies. He later served as president (学長) of Komazawa Junior College.

nodes.label: Reirin Yamada
nodes.summary: Reirin Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and served as president of Komazawa Junior College from circa 1958 to 1968.

nodes.label: Muzaffar Alam
nodes.description: historian at the University of Chicago
nodes.summary: Historian and Indologist Muzaffar Alam (born 1947) was educated at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He taught at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1973–2001) and was appointed George V. Bobrinskoy Professor at the University of Chicago (~2001).

nodes.label: Elena Bashir
nodes.summary: Elena Bashir specializes in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Michigan (~1980–1988) and later held positions at the University of Chicago, serving as Senior Lecturer Emerita around 2005.

nodes.label: Benedetta Lomi
nodes.summary: Benedetta Lomi specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London and held teaching positions at the University of Virginia (circa 2014–2017) and the University of Bristol (circa 2018).

nodes.label: Ritu Birla
nodes.summary: Ritu Birla is a historian and Indologist who studied at Columbia University (~1990–1996). She has served as Professor Emerita in the Department of History at the University of Toronto (~2001).

nodes.label: Arti Dhand
nodes.summary: Arti Dhand is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Calgary (~1989–1993) and McGill University (~1993–2000). Around 2003, she served as Associate Professor in the Department for the Study of Religion at the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: Kajri Jain
nodes.description: Indian art historian, writer, and professor

nodes.label: Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti
nodes.description: Indologist, scholar of Onomastics & Vedic Studies, Author & Editor. Emeritus Fellow, UGC.
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and religious studies, Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti held a post at the University of Calcutta from circa 1974 to 2005 and is attested in 2026 as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Kumkum Bandyopadhyay
nodes.summary: Kumkum Bandyopadhyay works in history and archaeology, having completed doctoral studies under Rupendra Kumar Chattopadhyay. Bandyopadhyay held an attested post as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

nodes.label: Sampan Chakrabarty
nodes.summary: Sampan Chakrabarty works in Indology. Attested in 2026, he studied for his doctorate under Pallab Sengupta and held a position as a Research Scholar/Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Tista Biswas
nodes.summary: Tista Biswas is an Indologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Subuddhi Charan Goswami and holds the post of Sir William Jones Research Fellow in Sanskritic Studies at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Smita Halder
nodes.summary: Smita Halder is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. In 2026, she is attested as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society and studying under doctoral supervisor Susmita Basu Majumdar.

nodes.label: Susmita Basu Majumdar
nodes.summary: Susmita Basu Majumdar is an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Lady Brabourne College and the University of Calcutta, where she later held a academic post and taught Smita Halder.

nodes.label: Priyanku Chakraborty
nodes.summary: Priyanku Chakraborty works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Supervised for doctoral studies by Aishwarya Biswas, Chakraborty holds the post of Rajendralal Mitra Research Fellow in Buddhist Studies at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Praggnaparamita Biswas
nodes.summary: Praggnaparamita Biswas is an Indologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Ratna Basu. She has held an appointment as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Imran Philip
nodes.summary: Imran Philip is an Indology and history researcher who studied for a doctorate under Kaustubh Mani Sengupta and held a Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

nodes.label: Manasi Dilip Nadkarni
nodes.summary: Manasi Dilip Nadkarni specializes in linguistics and Indology. She conducted doctoral studies under Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and is attested as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

nodes.label: Biswajit Biswas
nodes.summary: Biswajit Biswas works in religious studies and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das and served as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Moumita Hossain
nodes.summary: Moumita Hossain is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She conducted doctoral research under the supervision of Ranjit Sen and has held an appointment as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Poulami Ray
nodes.summary: Poulami Ray is an archaeology and history researcher who studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen. She held an appointment as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sulagna Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Sulagna Bhattacharya is an Indologist who conducted doctoral research under Pratap Bandyopadhyay and held an H P Shastri Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Tanaya Afroz
nodes.summary: Tanaya Afroz is a linguistics scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and held a post as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sunanda Mukhopadhyay
nodes.summary: Sunanda Mukhopadhyay works in linguistics and Indology. She completed doctoral research under Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and held a post as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Minakshi Banerjee
nodes.summary: Minakshi Banerjee works in Indology, having completed her doctorate under Debarchana Sarkar. As of 2026, she holds the James Prinsep Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Ankita Chakraborty
nodes.summary: Ankita Chakraborty is an Indology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Bijoya Goswami (attested 2026). She served as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Rebecca Sundén
nodes.summary: Rebecca Sundén works in Indology and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: Neelima Mundayar
nodes.summary: Neelima Mundayar is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She is a PhD student at the University of Edinburgh, studying under doctoral supervisor Wilfried Swenden (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Jiaqi Wang
nodes.summary: Jiaqi Wang was a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who studied under Gangkar Rinpoche and was a PhD student at Columbia University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Sravani Kanamarlapudi
nodes.summary: Sravani Kanamarlapudi works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Washington (2019) and under Richard G. Salomon, and is a PhD student at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Christophe Jaffrelot
nodes.summary: Christophe Jaffrelot (born 1964) is a scholar of Indology who studied under Jean Leca at Sciences Po (~1987–1991). He held posts at Sciences Po (~1991), CNRS (~1991), and King's College London (~2012) as Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology.

nodes.label: Jean-Luc Chevillard
nodes.summary: Jean-Luc Chevillard is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Culioli. He has held positions as a CNRS researcher (attested 2009) and Lehrbeauftragter at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Charles Li
nodes.summary: Charles Li is a scholar working in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. He has held posts as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of British Columbia and as a project researcher at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Koichi Hiraoka
nodes.summary: Koichi Hiraoka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1980–1984) and held a visiting professorship at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Alastair Gornall
nodes.summary: Alastair Gornall is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge. He has held positions at SOAS, the Singapore University of Technology and Design, and the Pali Text Society.

nodes.label: Tom Ginsburg
nodes.summary: Tom Ginsburg, a scholar of law and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1985–1999). He held a post at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2000–2008) before joining the University of Chicago (~2008).

nodes.label: Aritri Dutta
nodes.summary: Aritri Dutta is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. She pursued an external PhD at Leiden University under the doctoral supervision of Henk Blezer (attested 2026).

nodes.label: S. N. Krishna
nodes.summary: S. N. Krishna is an Indology researcher who was a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor T. V. Vasudeva (attested 2026).

nodes.label: R. Gayathri
nodes.summary: R. Gayathri is an Indologist. She studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi, attested in 2026.

nodes.label: V. R. Srinivasan
nodes.summary: V. R. Srinivasan is an Indology and history scholar who pursued PhD research at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the doctoral supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.

nodes.label: P. S. Chandrasekharan
nodes.summary: P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indologist who worked as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Vijayalakshmi Mani
nodes.summary: Vijayalakshmi Mani is a scholar of Indology and history who studied as a PhD scholar under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2026).

nodes.label: Lavanya V. Eswar
nodes.summary: Lavanya V. Eswar is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. Attested in 2026, she is a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

nodes.label: Yukihiko Asayama
nodes.summary: Yukihiko Asayama worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was attested as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education in 1986 and as an overseas research fellow at South China Normal University in 1991.

nodes.label: Ernst Gombrich
variants: エルンスト・ゴンブリッチ
nodes.summary: Ernst Gombrich studied at the University of Vienna and worked in the fields of history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of London (1956–1959) and the Warburg Institute, where he served as research assistant (1936) and director (1959–1976).

nodes.label: Toshihiko Izutsu
nodes.description: Japanese author of many books on Islam and other religions (1914–1993)
nodes.summary: Toshihiko Izutsu was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies who studied at Keio University. He held academic positions at Keio University, McGill University, and the Iranian Research Institute of Philosophy.

nodes.label: Tadashi Inoue
nodes.summary: Tadashi Inoue was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1956). He served at Kyoto National Museum (1967, 1979), Iida City Museum (1988–2006), Nara University (1987), and Bukkyo University (1995).

nodes.id: I:K. J. Somaiya Centre for Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: K. J. Somaiya Centre for Buddhist Studies
Sally Mellick Cutler
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, Sally Mellick Cutler earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1993. In 1997, she is attested as manager of the Pali Text Society Office.

nodes.label: Hamamatsu University
variants: 常葉学園浜松大学経営情報学部

nodes.label: Kenpon Hokke Sect Research Institute
variants: 顕本法華宗教学研究所

nodes.label: Kansei Tamura
nodes.summary: Kansei Tamura is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (both attested 1962).

nodes.label: Katsuji Fujioka
nodes.summary: Katsuji Fujioka (1872–1935) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and the University of Leipzig (1901–1905). He served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.

nodes.label: Leonard Bloomfield
variants: レナード・ブルームフィールド
nodes.jawiki: レナード・ブルームフィールド
nodes.summary: Linguist Leonard Bloomfield studied at Harvard, Wisconsin, Chicago under Francis Asbury Wood, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Illinois (1910–1921), Ohio State (1921–1927), Chicago (1927–1940), and Yale as Sterling Professor of Linguistics (1940–1949).

nodes.label: Kaigen Noritake
nodes.summary: Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Kenyo Mitomo. He held an assistant professorship at Rissho University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Daito Shimaji
nodes.summary: Daito Shimaji (1875–1927) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Ryukoku and Otani universities, he taught at Toyo University (~1903–1927), Rissho University (~1904–1927), Komazawa University (~1906–1927), and the University of Tokyo (1923).

nodes.label: Toho Gakkai
variants: Gesellschaft für Ostasienwissenschaft (東方学会; Tōhōgaku-kai)

nodes.label: Amalia Pezzali
nodes.summary: Amalia Pezzali is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under T. R. V. Murti and Michel Hulin.

nodes.label: Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff
nodes.summary: Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) was a linguist and historian. After studies at Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin, he served as a professor of Greek language and literature at the University of Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht University (1917–1946).

nodes.label: Fumio Masutani
nodes.summary: Fumio Masutani worked in Buddhist and religious studies, earning his literature doctorate from the University of Tokyo. His career included professorships at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1952–1965) and Taisho University (~1965–1973), and serving as president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).

nodes.label: Kumataro Kawada
nodes.summary: Kumataro Kawada was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Tokyo Imperial University and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Japan Women's University and the University of Tokyo, and later became professor emeritus at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Daegu University
variants: 大邱大学校日語日文学科

nodes.label: Hoseong Kim
nodes.summary: Hoseong Kim is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He founded the Nihon Bukkyoshi Kenkyujo and was attested as a professor at Dongguk University in 2011.

nodes.label: Chandima
nodes.summary: Chandima is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

nodes.label: Jogendra Singh
nodes.summary: Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

nodes.label: Hartmut Scharfe
nodes.summary: Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme. He later held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Carl Friedrich Gauss
variants: ヨハン・カール・フリードリヒ・ガウス
カール・フリードリヒ・ガウス
nodes.summary: Carl Friedrich Gauss (1777–1855) studied at TU Braunschweig, the University of Göttingen (under G. C. Lichtenberg and C. G. Heyne), and the University of Helmstedt. From 1807 to 1855, he served as full professor and director of the Göttingen Observatory.

nodes.label: Daijo Tokiwa
nodes.summary: Daijo Tokiwa (1870–1945) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora, he held professorships at the University of Tokyo (1925–1931) and Toyo University (1931).

nodes.label: Yuishin Ito
nodes.summary: Yuishin Ito specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. He held positions at Bukkyo University, including lecturer in 1961 and professor emeritus (1974–1997), and served as president of Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College in 1997.

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried Eichhorn
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried Eichhorn (1752–1827) was a scholar in religious studies and linguistics. Educated at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, he held professorships at the University of Jena (1775) and the University of Göttingen (1788).

nodes.id: I:Institute for Materials Research, Tohoku University
nodes.label: Institute for Materials Research, Tohoku University
variants: 東北大学金属材料研究所

nodes.label: Keiki Yabuki
nodes.summary: Keiki Yabuki (1879–1939) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Taisho University and the University of Tokyo (~1909–1913), he served as professor at Taisho University (1909) and associate professor at the University of Tokyo (~1924–1930).

nodes.label: Shigeru Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Shigeru Matsumoto (1933–2010) was a religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1960) and Harvard University (~1960–1967), and later held posts at Tenri University and the University of the Sacred Heart.

nodes.label: Unsho Shaku
nodes.summary: Unsho Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded both the Kairitsu Gakko and the Juzenkai in 1884.

nodes.label: Kozen Shaku
nodes.summary: Kozen Shaku (1849–1924) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Senmyō. He served as abbot at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sannei-ji (1882), and taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin.

nodes.label: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
variants: ゲオルク・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・ヘーゲル
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・ヘーゲル
nodes.summary: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tübingen, Evangelisches Stift Tübingen, and University of Jena. He held academic posts at Jena, Heidelberg University, and Frederick William University Berlin from circa 1818 to 1831.

nodes.label: Bernhard Kölver
nodes.summary: Bernhard Kölver (1938–2001) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt, and Cologne. He held posts at Cologne, the Nepal Research Centre, and occupied chairs of Indology at Kiel (1974–1993) and Leipzig (1993–2001).

nodes.label: Mabel Haynes Bode
nodes.summary: Mabel Haynes Bode (1864–1922) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Notting Hill and Ealing High School, University College London, under T. W. Rhys Davids (~1893–1905), and at the University of Bern (~1905–1908). She held posts at UCL (~1912–1917) and SOAS (~1917–1922).

nodes.label: Georges Dumézil
variants: ジョルジュ・デュメジル
nodes.jawiki: ジョルジュ・デュメジル
nodes.summary: Georges Dumézil was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Indology who studied under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at Istanbul, Uppsala, and Warsaw before teaching at EPHE (~1933–1968) and holding a chair at Collège de France (1949–1968).

nodes.label: Claude Lévi-Strauss
variants: クロード・レヴィ＝ストロース
nodes.jawiki: クロード・レヴィ＝ストロース
nodes.summary: Lévi-Strauss studied at the Paris Law Faculty (~1927–1931) under Marcel Mauss. He held posts at the University of São Paulo (~1935–1939), EPHE (~1951–1974), EHESS (~1975–1982), and Collège de France as chair of Anthropologie sociale (1959–1982).

nodes.label: Antoine Meillet
variants: アントワーヌ・メイエ
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ・メイエ
nodes.summary: Antoine Meillet was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris, Sorbonne, and EPHE under Saussure, Darmesteter, and Lévi, later holding posts at EPHE, INALCO, and the Collège de France (1905–1936).

nodes.label: Émile Benveniste
variants: エミール・バンヴニスト
エミール・バンヴェニスト
nodes.jawiki: エミール・バンヴェニスト
nodes.summary: Émile Benveniste (1902–1976) was a linguist specializing in Iranian/Central Asian studies and Indology, educated at EPHE and under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He was directeur d’études at EPHE (1927–1969) and Chair of Comparative Grammar at Collège de France (1937–1969).

nodes.label: Theodore Dwight Woolsey
nodes.description: American jurist; president of Yale University (1801–1889)
nodes.summary: Theodore Dwight Woolsey (1801–1889) was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Yale and Princeton. He served as president of Yale University from 1831 to 1871 and was president of the American Oriental Society (~1863–1881).

nodes.label: Sures Chandra Banerji
nodes.description: born:1917-08-04|died:2000|; Sureśa Candra Bandyopādhyāya 1917-; Banerji, Sures Chandra; Banerji, Sures Chandra 1917-2000

nodes.label: Toru Takahashi
nodes.summary: Toru Takahashi was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Daegu Higher Common School, Keijo Imperial University, Dongguk University, Fukuoka University, and Tenri University.

nodes.label: Seok-hyeong Kim
nodes.summary: Seok-hyeong Kim (born 1904) specialized in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Educated at Taisho University, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University and as a professor at Dongguk University.

nodes.label: Tsutomu Kubo
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Kubo was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University (1929–1946), and Toyo University (~1949–1954).

nodes.label: Ernest Renan
variants: ジョゼフ・エルネスト・ルナン
nodes.summary: Ernest Renan worked in religious studies, linguistics, and archaeology, studying under Eugène Burnouf and Étienne Marc Quatremère at the Collège de France. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and the Collège de France (from 1861).

nodes.label: Gyoei Fukuda
nodes.summary: Gyoei Fukuda studied at Taisho University in the field of Buddhist studies. He later served as president (学長) of Taisho University (~1926–1944), professor (教授（嘱託）) at the University of Tokyo (1928), and lecturer (講師) at Toyo University.

nodes.label: Victor Henry
nodes.summary: Victor Henry was an Indologist and linguist who taught at the University of Douai (~1884–1887), the University of Lille (~1887–1888), and the École Centrale de Lille. In 1888, he became professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at the University of Paris.

nodes.label: Auguste Barth
nodes.summary: Auguste Barth worked in Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Strasbourg (~1852–1856), he taught at Collège Poincaré Saverne (~1856–1860) and was a member of the Institut de France (~1893–1916).

nodes.label: Jean Deloche
nodes.summary: Jean Deloche was an Indologist and historian. He taught at Suryavarman II School, directed the Alliance Française of Madras, was a researcher and associate member at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, and was an associate member at the French Institute of Pondicherry.

nodes.label: Anna Seidel
nodes.summary: Anna Seidel was a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Munich, Hamburg, and under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. She held posts at the EFEO (1969), the Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1969–1991), and was a visiting professor at Hawaiʻi (1978) and UCSB (1988).

nodes.label: Götz von Selle
nodes.summary: Götz von Selle worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin, Kiel, and Göttingen, and later served at Göttingen and as professor and library director at the University of Königsberg (~1928–1945).

nodes.label: John Borthwick Gilchrist
variants: ジョン・ボースウィック・ギルクリスト
nodes.image: John Borthwick Gilchrist, cropped from UCL portrait by Blanconi.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・ギルクリスト
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology and linguistics, John Borthwick Gilchrist studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the East India Company, headed Fort William College (1800–1804), and became the first Professor of Hindustani at UCL (~1828–1831).

nodes.label: Claudius Buchanan
nodes.summary: Buchanan, active in Indology and religious studies, studied at the University of Glasgow (1782) and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1791–1795). In 1801, he was appointed Vice-Provost of Fort William College.

nodes.label: Bruno Petzold
variants: ブルーノ・ペツォルト
nodes.jawiki: ブルーノ・ペツォルト
nodes.summary: Bruno Petzold studied at the Universities of Leipzig and Strasbourg, and under Hikoshiro Hoshino and Daito Shimaji. Working in Buddhist studies and Japanology, he taught at First Higher School, Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei Senior High School.

nodes.label: Seiichiro Ono
nodes.summary: Seiichiro Ono (1891–1986) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his degrees from the University of Tokyo (~1914–1917, LLD 1933) under Eiichi Makino. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1922–1951) and Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977).

nodes.label: Haya Akegarasu
nodes.summary: Haya Akegarasu was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and Shimei Futabatei at Otani University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, later serving as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954).

nodes.label: Sydenham College
variants: Sydenham College of Commerce and Economics

nodes.label: Siddharth College
variants: シッダールタ女子大学

nodes.label: Poerbatjaraka
nodes.summary: Poerbatjaraka was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate from Leiden University under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. He founded Udayana University and was a professor at Gadjah Mada University (~1950–1964), the University of Indonesia (~1950–1964), and Udayana (~1958–1964).

nodes.label: Herman Kellgren
nodes.summary: Herman Kellgren was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1846–1848), Eugène Burnouf (~1849–1851), and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (~1849–1851), and held a post at the University of Helsinki from 1849 to 1856.

nodes.label: David Brown
variants: デイヴィッド・ブラウン
nodes.summary: David Brown (1762–1812) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society. He studied under Joseph Milner and at Magdalene College, Cambridge, later serving as provost at Fort William College in 1800.

nodes.label: William Kirkpatrick
variants: ウィリアム・カークパトリック
nodes.description: British army officer in the East India Company and diplomat (1754 or 1756-1812)

nodes.label: Francis Gladwin
variants: フランシス・グラッドウィン
nodes.description: British scholar of the Persian language
nodes.summary: Francis Gladwin worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1812) and served as professor of Persian at Fort William College (~1801–1805).

nodes.label: William Shi-Yuan Wang
nodes.summary: William Shi-Yuan Wang is a linguist and sinologist who studied at Columbia and Michigan. He was a professor at UC Berkeley (1966–1994) and held posts at City University of Hong Kong, CUHK, and Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

nodes.label: Albert Thumb
nodes.image: Professor Albert Thumb 18.05.1865 bis 14.08.1915 Sohn von Ida Schanzenbach und Albert Alois Thump.jpg
nodes.summary: Albert Thumb (1865–1915) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Karl Brugmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Rudolf Thurneysen, completing habilitation at Freiburg. He held posts at the University of Freiburg, the University of Strasbourg, and the University of Marburg.

nodes.label: Genro
nodes.summary: Genro was an 18th-century Buddhist figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and held the senior monastic rank of daiichiza at Myoshin-ji.

nodes.label: Hakuin Ekaku
nodes.summary: Hakuin Ekaku was an active figure in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Dōkyō Etan (~1708) and Hakuyūshi (~1710–1711), and later taught Suiō Genro.

nodes.label: Julius Klaproth
nodes.jawiki: ユリウス・ハインリヒ・クラプロート

nodes.label: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland
nodes.summary: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland was an Indologist. He studied at the East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck, and later served as professor of law at Presidency University.

nodes.id: I:Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
nodes.label: Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
variants: ノルウェー科学文学アカデミー

nodes.label: Benkyo Shiio
nodes.summary: Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1902–1915). He taught at Taisho, Nihon, and Waseda universities, became president of Tokai Gakuen Junior College (1963), and directed Sanko Library and Sanko Research Institute.

nodes.label: Sanko Library
variants: 三康文化研究所附属三康図書館

nodes.label: Karl Ferdinand Johansson
nodes.summary: Karl Ferdinand Johansson was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University, where he later served as University Professor of Sanskrit and the Comparative Philology of the Indo-European Languages from circa 1893 to 1925.

nodes.id: I:W. F. Albright Institute of Archaeological Research
nodes.label: W. F. Albright Institute of Archaeological Research
variants: American School of Oriental Research in Jerusalem
オルブライト考古学研究所

nodes.label: Oostersch Genootschap in Nederland
variants: Dutch Oriental Society (Oostersch Genootschap in Nederland)

nodes.label: Louis Herbert Gray
nodes.summary: Louis Herbert Gray was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Princeton and Columbia (PhD ~1896–1900), and held posts at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (1921).

nodes.id: I:Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH
nodes.label: Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH
variants: Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH Research
Centre for Bhutan Studies and Gross National Happiness Research
Centre for Bhutan and GNH Studies

nodes.label: Sangay Dorji
nodes.summary: Sangay Dorji is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Tengtho Goenpa and Semtokha Rigney School. He served as a teacher at Semtokha Rigney School and as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission.

nodes.label: Ugyen Pelgen
nodes.summary: Ugyen Pelgen works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a master's degree at Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

nodes.label: John A. Ardussi
nodes.summary: John A. Ardussi works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He was supervised by Turrell V. Wylie for his MA, completed a PhD at Australian National University (attested 1977), and served as a research team member at CNRS.

nodes.label: Phuntsok Tashi
nodes.summary: Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a BA at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and an MA at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

nodes.label: George van Driem
variants: ジョージ・ヴァン・ドリーム
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ヴァン・ドリーム
nodes.summary: George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Virginia and Leiden. He held professorial chairs at Leiden University (1996–1999, ~2001–2009) and served as Professor of Historical Linguistics at the University of Bern (2010–2022).

nodes.label: Kees W. Bolle
nodes.summary: Kees W. Bolle (1927–2012) was a religious studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Leiden, Madras, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. Bolle taught at Brown (~1960–1964) and UCLA (~1969–1994), where he became Professor Emeritus.

nodes.label: Thinley Dorji Bhutia
nodes.summary: Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, and served as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

nodes.label: Choying Wangmo Dorji
nodes.summary: Choying Wangmo Dorji (1897–1994) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She founded the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as a member of its General Council from 1964 to 1965.

nodes.label: Henry Creswicke Rawlinson
nodes.image: Rawlinson, Sir Henry Creswick, par Arthur J.Melhuish, BNF Gallica.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ヘンリー・ローリンソン (初代準男爵)
nodes.summary: Henry Creswicke Rawlinson specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Great Ealing School and Middlesex University, he served in the East India Company (~1827–1858) and as Director (1862) and President (1878–1881) of the Royal Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Georg von der Gabelentz
variants: ゲオルク・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
ハンス・ゲオルク・コーノン・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
nodes.summary: Georg von der Gabelentz was a Sinologist, linguist, and Japanologist who studied at Jena, Leipzig, and TU Dresden. He served as professor of East Asian languages at the University of Leipzig (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1889).

nodes.label: Alexander Cunningham
variants: アレキサンダー・カニンガム
nodes.jawiki: アレキサンダー・カニンガム
nodes.description: British army engineer and amateur archaeologist (1814-1893)
nodes.summary: Alexander Cunningham (1814–1893) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary and under James Prinsep. He founded the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as its first director (1861–1865) and later as director-general (1871–1885).

nodes.label: Robert Hyde Colebrooke
nodes.description: British infantry officer and surveyor in India (1762–1808)

nodes.label: John Herbert Harington
nodes.description: British administrator in India and Persian scholar
nodes.summary: An Indologist, John Herbert Harington served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of The Asiatic Society. He was also an honorary professor of British government laws and regulations at Fort William College (~1801–1823).

nodes.label: Amaranatha Jha
nodes.summary: Amaranatha Jha studied at Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).

nodes.label: Charles Elliott
nodes.summary: Charles Elliott was an Indologist and historian who worked for the East India Company and served as Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from circa 1837 to 1856.

nodes.label: George Thomas Staunton
nodes.summary: George Thomas Staunton was a sinologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1797–1798). He served as Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1823–1859).

nodes.label: Andover Theological Seminary
variants: アンドーヴァー神学校

nodes.label: Edmund Nathaniel Snyder
nodes.summary: Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist. He graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University in 1886 and pursued studies under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

nodes.label: Flinders Petrie
nodes.jawiki: フリンダーズ・ピートリー

nodes.label: British School at Athens
variants: British School of Archaeology in Athens

nodes.label: B. R. Ambedkar
variants: ビームラーオ・ラームジー・アンベードカル
nodes.jawiki: ビームラーオ・アンベードカル
nodes.description: Indian jurist, economist, and social reformer (1891–1956)
nodes.summary: B. R. Ambedkar worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Columbia under Dewey, Seligman, Shotwell, and Robinson, and at LSE under Cannan and Mackinder, later holding posts at Sydenham College, Government Law College, and Ramjas College.

nodes.label: James Irving Manatt
nodes.summary: James Irving Manatt was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Grinnell and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, later holding posts at Denison, Marietta, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and Brown University (~1892-1915).

nodes.label: James Hadley
nodes.summary: James Hadley worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Yale College and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury. He served as Professor of Greek at Yale University (1845-1872) and as a leading member of the American Oriental Society (1871-1872).

nodes.label: Francis Robinson
nodes.summary: Francis Robinson is a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD from Trinity College, Cambridge (1970). He served as Professor of History of South Asia at the University of London and head of history at Royal Holloway (1990–2004).

nodes.label: Royal Holloway, University of London
variants: Royal Holloway College der University of London

nodes.label: Gordon Johnson
nodes.summary: Gordon Johnson (b. 1943) studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. In the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology, he served as President of Wolfson College, Cambridge (1993–2010), Cambridge's Deputy Vice-Chancellor (1974–2010), and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).

nodes.label: Kurfürst-Ruprecht-Gymnasium Neustadt
variants: Gymnasium at Neustadt an der Haardt

nodes.label: Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe
nodes.summary: Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe was an Indologist, archaeologist, and linguist. Educated at Richmond College and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, he served as epigraphist for the Government of Sri Lanka (~1899–1928) and taught at the University of London (~1917–1936).

nodes.label: Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner
nodes.summary: Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner (1840–1899) studied at King's College London and Heidelberg. He taught at King's College, served as Principal of Government College Lahore (1864), founded the University of the Punjab, and later led the Oriental Institute, Woking (~1884–1899).

nodes.label: George Uglow Pope
nodes.summary: George Uglow Pope worked in Indology and linguistics. He founded and headed both Breeks Memorial School and Bishop Cotton Boys' School, and later served as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford (~1884–1907).

nodes.label: Narada Maha Thera
nodes.image: Portrait Of Most Venerable Narada Maha Thera (1898-1983).jpg
nodes.summary: Narada Maha Thera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at St. Benedict's College, Ceylon University College (~1921–1924), and under Pelene Siri Vajiragnana (~1916–1955). He served as Superior of Vajiraramaya (~1955–1983).

nodes.label: C. R. Krishnamacharlu
nodes.summary: C. R. Krishnamacharlu was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Madras Christian College and completed his university degree at Pachaiyappa's College.

nodes.label: Oliver Codrington
nodes.summary: Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (attested 1892).

nodes.label: José Gerson da Cunha
nodes.description: Indo-Portuguese physician, orientalist, historian, linguist, and numismatist

nodes.label: Dermot Killingley
nodes.summary: Dermot Killingley is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Oxford and SOAS. He taught at the University of Malaya (1961–1968) and served as Reader at Newcastle University (1970–2000).

nodes.label: Institute of Economic Growth
variants: Institute of Economic Growth (University of Delhi)

nodes.label: Sumathi Ramaswamy
nodes.summary: Sumathi Ramaswamy (born 1961) is a historian and Indologist educated at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Pennsylvania. She held faculty appointments at the University of Pennsylvania (~1993–2000) and the University of Michigan (~2000–2007).

nodes.label: Declan Quigley
nodes.summary: Declan Quigley is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He has taught at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

nodes.label: Gauri Viswanathan
nodes.summary: Gauri Viswanathan is an Indologist who studied at the University of Delhi (~1968–1973) and Columbia University (~1978–1985). She lectured in English at Delhi, held fellowships at IISH (1998) and Princeton (2000), and became Class of 1933 Professor at Columbia (~1989).

nodes.label: Henry Herbert Dodwell
nodes.summary: Henry Herbert Dodwell, active in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Educational Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History and Culture of the British Dominions at SOAS (1922–1946).

nodes.label: Suzanne Karpelès
nodes.summary: Suzanne Karpelès (1890–1968) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the EPHE and became a member of EFEO (1922–1925), first curator of the National Library of Cambodia (1925), and secretary-general of the Buddhist Institute (1930).

nodes.label: Henry Sullivan Jarrett
nodes.summary: Henry Sullivan Jarrett, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, succeeded Heinrich Blochmann. From circa 1870 to 1894, he served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners in Calcutta.

nodes.label: Heinrich Blochmann
nodes.summary: Heinrich Blochmann was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies and history. He studied at Leipzig under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, Paris under Karl Benedikt Hase, and Calcutta. His career included posts at Fort William College, Doveton College, and Aliah University.

nodes.label: Ian James Coghlan
nodes.summary: Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University (2004) and served as a research fellow at the Monash Asia Institute at Monash University (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Holly Gayley
nodes.summary: Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Harvard University (~2002–2009). She joined the faculty at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2008.

nodes.label: Heinz Adolf Mode
nodes.description: German art historian, orientalist and indologist (1913-1992)
nodes.summary: Heinz Adolf Mode worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Humboldt University, Basel, and under G. P. Malalasekera and Otto Fischer, later serving as professor of Oriental archaeology at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1948–1978).

nodes.id: I:Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Buddhistische Forschungen in der DDR
nodes.label: Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Buddhistische Forschungen in der DDR
variants: Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Buddhistische Forschungen in der DDR

nodes.label: Otto Fischer
nodes.description: German art historian, director of Kunstmuseum Basel (1886–1948)
nodes.summary: Otto Fischer was a Sinologist and art historian who studied at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen. He served as director of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart and Kunstmuseum Basel, and was an art history professor at the University of Basel (c. 1927–1937).

nodes.label: Willem Bollée
nodes.summary: Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University (~1946–1956) and completed his Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1972–1975). He was an assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and taught at Heidelberg University (~1970–1993).

nodes.label: William Frederic Sinclair
nodes.summary: William Frederic Sinclair worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal School Dungannon and Armagh, and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

nodes.id: I:Oriental Translation Fund of Great Britain and Ireland
nodes.label: Oriental Translation Fund of Great Britain and Ireland
Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・フォン・ハンマー・プルグスタル
nodes.summary: Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (ca. 1788–1799) and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (ca. 1847–1849).

nodes.label: Dilli Raman Regmi
nodes.summary: Dilli Raman Regmi (1914–2001) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees from the University of Madras and Patna University, and he served as a teacher at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

nodes.label: William Rainey Harper
nodes.summary: William Rainey Harper was a linguist and religious studies scholar educated at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale before becoming president and department head at the University of Chicago (1891–1906).

nodes.label: Daniel Coit Gilman
nodes.summary: Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Berlin, and Cambridge. He served as librarian at Yale, president of the University of California, founding president of Johns Hopkins University, and president of both the American Oriental Society and the Carnegie Institution.

nodes.label: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh
nodes.summary: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.

nodes.label: Thomas Jülch
nodes.summary: Thomas Jülch is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, the University of Hull (MA ~1999–2000), Heidelberg University, and the University of Munich (PhD ~2006–2011), later serving as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2013–2019).

nodes.id: I:Singapore University of Technology and Design
nodes.label: Singapore University of Technology and Design
variants: Singapore University of Technology and Design

nodes.label: Thomas Roebuck
nodes.summary: Thomas Roebuck was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh. In 1811 he became assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George, and was a member of The Asiatic Society (~1811–1819).

nodes.id: I:Keio Institute of Cultural and Linguistic Studies
nodes.label: Keio Institute of Cultural and Linguistic Studies
variants: Keio Institute of Cultural & Linguistic Studies (慶應大學言語文化研究所)
Keio Institute of Cultural & Linguistic Studies

nodes.label: Lionel Obadia
nodes.summary: Lionel Obadia (born 1971) is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Lille University of Science and Technology in 1997. He held posts at INALCO, EPHE, KU Leuven, Lille 3, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

nodes.label: Lille 3 University
variants: Charles-de-Gaulle University of Arts and Social Sciences

nodes.label: Richard Hughes Seager
nodes.summary: Richard Hughes Seager is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD). He served as Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College from circa 1994 to 2014.

nodes.label: Michelle Spuler
nodes.summary: Michelle Spuler is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1996–2001) and taught at Colorado College and Victoria University of Wellington (~2002–2004).

nodes.label: William Muir
nodes.summary: William Muir was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. He studied at Kilmarnock Academy, the University of Edinburgh (~1834–1836), and Haileybury, later serving as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Edinburgh (~1885–1903).

nodes.label: Robert Maclagan
nodes.description: British Army officer and military engineer (1820–94)
nodes.summary: Robert Maclagan (1820–1894) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering. He served as Principal of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

nodes.label: Erberto Lo Bue
nodes.description: Italian indologist, tibetologist, translator and university teacher
nodes.summary: Erberto Lo Bue was a scholar of Tibetology and history who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London (~1976–1981). He lectured in Tibetan language and literature at the University of Milan (~1995–2002) and later taught at the University of Bologna (~2002–2016).

nodes.label: Corpus Christi College, Cambridge
variants: Corpus Christi College der Universität Cambridge
ケンブリッジ大学コーパス・クリスティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Edward Delavan Perry
nodes.summary: Edward Delavan Perry was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University (~1871-1875) and the University of Tübingen (~1877-1879), and served as Jay Professor at Columbia University from 1891 to 1931.

nodes.label: Theodorus Willem Juynboll
nodes.summary: Theodorus Willem Juynboll (1866–1948) studied at Leiden University (~1884–1893) and held a post at Utrecht University in 1916. He taught Jan Gonda.

nodes.label: Rajendralal Mitra
nodes.summary: Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891), an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He served as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary (1846–1856) and president (1885) of The Asiatic Society, and directed Wards' Institution (1856–1881).

nodes.label: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton
nodes.jawiki: フランシス・ブキャナン＝ハミルトン
nodes.summary: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. After completing his MD at the University of Edinburgh (1783), he served in the Bengal and Indian Medical Services (1794–1815) and directed the Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

nodes.label: Mona Schrempf
nodes.summary: Mona Schrempf is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a doctorate in anthropology from the Free University of Berlin (2001) and held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University (both attested 2006).

nodes.label: Jogindra Nath Samaddar
nodes.summary: Jogindra Nath Samaddar (1884–1929) studied at Bangabasi College and Presidency University, working in Indology and history/archaeology. He taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College (~1908–1917), Patna College (1912), and Patna University (1923).

nodes.label: Winfred Robert Martin
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and linguistics, Winfred Robert Martin served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

nodes.label: Daniel John Gogerly
nodes.summary: Daniel John Gogerly worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He led the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818–1822), chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society in 1838, and served as secretary, vice-president, and president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka.

nodes.label: Graves Chamney Haughton
nodes.summary: Graves Chamney Haughton (1788–1849) studied at Fort William College in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor at East India Company College (1819–1827) and as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland, which he founded.

nodes.label: Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study
variants: Netherlands Institute for Advanced Studies in the Humanities and Social Sciences

nodes.label: John Caspar Leyden
nodes.summary: John Caspar Leyden was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1790–1797) and under Henry Thomas Colebrooke (~1803–1811). He was professor of Hindustani at Fort William College (1808) and secretary of The Asiatic Society (~1810–1811).

nodes.label: J. M. E. McTaggart
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・マクタガート
nodes.summary: J. M. E. McTaggart was a philosopher who was educated at Clifton College (~1882–1885). He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1897 to 1923.

nodes.label: Parul Dave-Mukherji
nodes.summary: Parul Dave-Mukherji specializes in Indology. She completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and served as professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: John Hallett Batten
nodes.summary: John Hallett Batten was active in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Charterhouse School (~1823–1827) and the East India Company College (~1827–1829).

nodes.label: Kazuaki Komine
nodes.summary: Kazuaki Komine (born 1947) specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned undergraduate and doctoral degrees from Waseda University and held posts at Waseda Jitsugyo High School, Tokushima University, the National Institute of Japanese Literature, and Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

nodes.label: Hermann Sauppe
nodes.summary: Hermann Sauppe worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology, completing his doctorate at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. His career included posts at the University of Zurich, Zentralbibliothek Zürich, University of Vienna, Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar, and a professorship at the University of Göttingen (1855).

nodes.label: Addiscombe Military Seminary
variants: Hon. East India Company's Military Seminary, Addiscombe
Honourable East India Company's Military Seminary, Addiscombe
アディスコム軍事神学校

nodes.label: Thomas Jarrett
nodes.summary: Thomas Jarrett was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St Catharine's College (~1823–1827). He served as Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from ~1831 to 1854.

nodes.label: Henry George Keene
nodes.description: English employee of the East India Company and Persian scholar
nodes.summary: Henry George Keene worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at Fort William College and Sidney Sussex College, served in the East India Company, and became Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature at East India Company College (1824–1834).

nodes.label: William Price
nodes.summary: William Price was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He served as Professor of Hindústaní at Fort William College (~1813–1830) and taught oriental languages at Netherstone House Seminary (~1823–1830).

nodes.label: David Ruddell
nodes.summary: David Ruddell (1943–2015) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He was educated at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.

nodes.label: John Shakespear
nodes.summary: John Shakespear (1774–1858) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under John Richardson. He held an orientalist professorship at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805–1809) and served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).

nodes.label: David Shea
nodes.summary: David Shea worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at Trinity College Dublin in 1793 and served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Languages at East India Company College until 1836.

nodes.label: Sensho Murakami
nodes.summary: Sensho Murakami (1851–1929) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani and Toyo universities under Yukitada Takeda, Ryomon, and Gokan Unyei, later serving on the faculties of Tokyo Imperial University, Toyo University, and Otani University.

nodes.label: Emil Rödiger
variants: エミル・レーディガー
nodes.jawiki: エミル・レーディガー
nodes.summary: Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. Educated at Halle-Wittenberg (1821–1828), he held professorships there (1830–1860) and at Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1860), and managed the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (~1845–1853).

nodes.label: Alfred Master
nodes.description: Master, Alfred (1883-1978) Lecturer in Indian Philology

nodes.label: Mannudeva
nodes.summary: Mannudeva was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bālakṛṣṇa Pāyaguṇḍa (Bala Sharman Payagunde).

nodes.label: William Erskine
nodes.summary: William Erskine worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He was educated at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1787–1792).

nodes.label: James Atkinson
nodes.description: English surgeon, artist and Persian scholar (1780–1852)
nodes.summary: James Atkinson (1780–1852) was an Edinburgh-educated scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He served as Assistant and Deputy Assay Master at the India Government Mint in Kolkata and was appointed Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.

nodes.label: Dayong
nodes.summary: Dayong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute, where he taught in 1923, and studied under Taixu, Paldan Tenzin Nyandrak, Puren Bai, and Dorje Geshe.

nodes.label: Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo
variants: Pha bong kha pa dbe chen snying po

nodes.label: Buddhist Academy of China
variants: Institute of Buddhist Studies of Beijing

nodes.label: Eberhard Schrader
nodes.summary: Eberhard Schrader worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. After studying under Heinrich Ewald at Göttingen (~1854–1858), he held posts at Zurich (~1863–1870), Giessen (~1870–1873), Jena (~1873–1875), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).

nodes.label: John Thompson Platts
variants: ジョン・トンプソン・プラッツ
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・トンプソン・プラッツ
nodes.summary: John Thompson Platts (1830–1904) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford, he taught at Benares Sanskrit College and became Teacher of Persian at Oxford in 1880.

nodes.id: P:Richard Fleming St Andrew St John
nodes.label: Richard Fleming St Andrew St John
nodes.enwiki: Richard Fleming St Andrew St John

nodes.label: Finnian M. M. Gerety
nodes.summary: Finnian M. M. Gerety is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his doctorate at Harvard in 2015, held a postdoctoral fellowship at Yale (2017–2018), and was a visiting assistant professor at Brown University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Andrea R. Jain
nodes.summary: Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University (PhD 2010), later holding posts at IUPUI and Indiana University Bloomington, where she became full professor in 2021.

nodes.label: Hidehiko Kurita
nodes.summary: Hidehiko Kurita is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who completed a PhD at Tohoku University. Kurita held a lecturer post at Aichi Prefectural University, attested in 2020.

nodes.label: Kwangsoo Park
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Kwangsoo Park earned an MA from the University of Iowa and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as a professor at Wonkwang University, attested in 2020.

nodes.label: Samani Pratibha Pragya
nodes.summary: Active in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, Samani Pratibha Pragya earned a PhD at SOAS University of London and held a post there as a research assistant, attested in 2020.

nodes.label: Julian Strube
nodes.summary: Julian Strube (born 1985) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. After completing his habilitation at Heidelberg, he held posts at Münster, Hamburg, and the University of Vienna (2021–2024), before becoming chair of religious studies at the University of Göttingen in 2024.

nodes.label: Edward Clive Bayley
nodes.summary: Edward Clive Bayley was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College and East India Company College (~1840-1842), entering the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

nodes.label: Henry Miers Elliot
nodes.summary: Henry Miers Elliot was an Indologist and historian who studied at Winchester College (~1820–1826). He served as a civil servant with the East India Company from circa 1826 to 1853.

nodes.label: Justus Olshausen
variants: ユストゥス・オルスハウゼン
nodes.summary: Justus Olshausen specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. After studies at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris, he served as a professor at Kiel and later as Chief Librarian and Professor of Oriental Languages at Königsberg.

nodes.label: Étienne Marc Quatremère
nodes.image: Portret van de oriëntalist Étienne Marc Quatremère Quatremère, Etienne-Marc (titel op object) Leden van het Institut Royal de France (serietitel) Iconographie de l'Institut royal de France (serietitel op object), RP-P-1911-978.jpg
nodes.summary: Étienne Marc Quatremère (1782–1857) worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and served as a professor at the Collège de France from 1819 to 1857.

nodes.label: Carl Paul Caspari
nodes.summary: Carl Paul Caspari (1814–1892) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig under H. L. Fleischer and at Berlin, and spent his career at the University of Oslo as a lektor (1847) and professor (1857).

nodes.label: Hokkaido University of Education
variants: 北海道教育大学岩見沢分校
北海道教育大学函館分校

nodes.label: Asahikawa University Junior College
variants: 旭川大学女子短期大学部

nodes.label: Doranne Jacobson
nodes.summary: Doranne Jacobson works in Indology and related fields. She earned her doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

nodes.label: McKim Marriott
variants: マッキム・マリオット
nodes.jawiki: マッキム・マリオット
nodes.summary: McKim Marriott worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University and the University of Chicago under Clyde Kluckhohn, later serving as professor of anthropology and social sciences at the University of Chicago from 1955 to 1998.

nodes.label: Gore Ouseley
nodes.summary: Gore Ouseley (1770–1844) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He served at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (~1810–1814) and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1823–1844).

nodes.label: George Ritso Jervis
nodes.description: George Ritso Jervis (1794-1851) 1841 Lieut-Col George Ritso Jervis of the Engineers, Bombay Company

nodes.label: S. Sankaranarayanan
nodes.summary: S. Sankaranarayanan was an Indologist and historian. He served as an honorary professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1985–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

nodes.label: Chinmaya International Foundation
variants: Adi Sankara Nilayam, Chinmaya International Foundation

nodes.label: R. Thangaswami Sarma
nodes.summary: R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Madras Sanskrit College and Annamalai University. He held posts at Presidency College, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Adyar Library and Research Centre (1994–2000).

nodes.label: Sree Sarada Education Society
variants: Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre

nodes.label: Geoffrey Goble
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Virginia and a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington, and served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Oklahoma.

nodes.label: August Boeckh
nodes.summary: August Boeckh worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at Halle-Wittenberg under F. A. Wolf and F. Schleiermacher, he held professorships at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and the University of Berlin (1811–1861).

nodes.label: Max Leopold Margolis
nodes.summary: Max Leopold Margolis was a linguist and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at Columbia. He held posts at Columbia, Hebrew Union College, UC Berkeley, and held the chair of biblical philology at Dropsie College from 1909 to 1932.

variants: 和歌山赤十字看護専門学校

nodes.label: Yuka Otani
nodes.summary: Yuka Otani is a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 2015, she was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University.

nodes.id: I:Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
nodes.label: Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
variants: Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes

nodes.label: Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies
George Cœdès
nodes.summary: George Cœdès studied Indology, sinology, and history at EPHE under Finot, Lévi, and Foucher. He was director of the EFEO (1929–1947), led the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929), and taught at INALCO and the Sorbonne.

nodes.id: I:Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi
nodes.label: Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi
variants: Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi
