variants: Ceylon Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society
Sri Lanka branch of the Royal Asiatic Society

nodes.label: Arthur Emanuel Christensen
nodes.summary: Arthur Emanuel Christensen was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding the first chair of Oriental studies at Copenhagen from 1919 to 1945.

nodes.label: Friedrich Carl Andreas
nodes.jawiki: フリードリッヒ・カール・アンドレアス
nodes.summary: Andreas was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1868–1870) and held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1889) and the University of Göttingen (~1903–1930).

nodes.label: Henrik Samuel Nyberg
variants: エンリコ・サムエリ・ニーベリ
nodes.summary: Henrik Samuel Nyberg worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Uppsala University, taught at the Fjellstedt School (~1916–1919), and served as docent and professor of Semitic languages at Uppsala University (~1919–1956).

nodes.label: Otto Höfler
nodes.summary: Otto Höfler worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Vienna (PhD 1920–1926 under Rudolf Much; Habilitation ~1928–1931), Lund, and Kiel. He held posts at Uppsala, Lund, Kiel, Munich, and Vienna (1957–1971).

nodes.label: George Shirt
nodes.summary: George Shirt was an Indologist and linguist. He earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge by 1864 and studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington (~1864–1866).

nodes.label: Jean Humbert
nodes.description: academic (1792 - 1851), member of the Accademia delle Scienze di Torino since 1832

nodes.label: Syed Ali Bilgrami
nodes.summary: Syed Ali Bilgrami (1853–1911) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Patna College, IIT Roorkee, the Royal School of Mines, and the Universities of Lucknow and London, later serving Hyderabad State and as Reader in Marathi at Cambridge (1901).

nodes.label: Sukumari Bhattacharji
nodes.summary: Sukumari Bhattacharji (1921–2014) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University, she taught English at Lady Brabourne College (1945) and was a faculty member at Jadavpur University (1957–1986).

nodes.label: Johann Tobias Beck
nodes.summary: Johann Tobias Beck worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tübingen (~1822-1826), he held posts at the University of Basel (~1836-1843) and the University of Tübingen (~1843-1878).

nodes.label: Gerardus van der Leeuw
variants: ヘラルドゥス・ファン・デル・レーウ
nodes.jawiki: ゲラルダス・ファン・デル・レーウ
nodes.description: Dutch religious studies scholar and politician (1890–1950)
nodes.summary: Gerardus van der Leeuw was a religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University between circa 1908 and 1916. He held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.

nodes.label: Edward Albert Gait
nodes.summary: Edward Albert Gait was an Indologist and historian who studied at University College London. He founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914 and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

nodes.label: Frederick James Furnivall
nodes.summary: Working in linguistics and other fields, Furnivall studied at University College London and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He co-founded and taught at the Working Men's College, served as Secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910), and was an Honorary Fellow at Trinity Hall.

nodes.label: Royal Masonic School for Boys
variants: Royal Masonic School for Boys at Wood Green

nodes.label: Tanzan Hara
nodes.summary: Tanzan Hara (1819–1892) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Yushima Seido, Shoheizaka Gakumonjo, and under Genken Taki, Eizen Jitsuyama, and Honko Fugai. He held posts at the Ministry of Religion (1872–1874), University of Tokyo (1879), and Komazawa University (1891).

nodes.label: 13th Dalai Lama
nodes.summary: The 13th Dalai Lama worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Agvan Dorjiev, Terton Sogyal, Pa Ri Rabsal, and Yeshe Chopel, and taught numerous students, including Chogye Trichen Rinpoche and the 9th Panchen Lama.

nodes.label: Kumja Paik Kim
nodes.summary: Kumja Paik Kim is a specialist in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology who earned her doctorate from Stanford University. In 1989, she served as curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum.

nodes.label: Leedom Lefferts
nodes.summary: Leedom Lefferts is a scholar in Buddhist studies and anthropology. Attested in 2011, he served as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus at Drew University and Research Associate in the Department of Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.

nodes.label: Louise A. Cort
nodes.summary: Louise A. Cort specializes in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College, Oxford, and served as curator of ceramics at the Smithsonian Institution's Freer and Sackler Galleries from ~1981 to 2020.

nodes.label: Kavita Singh
nodes.summary: Kavita Singh (1964–2023) worked in art history and Indology. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College, MS University of Baroda, and Panjab University. A founder of Jawaharlal Nehru University, she served there as dean, alongside roles at Marg Publications and other institutions.

nodes.label: Jules Michelet
nodes.description: French historian; popularized the historical concept of the Renaissance
nodes.summary: Jules Michelet (1798–1874) was a historian educated at Lycée Charlemagne. He held teaching posts at the École Normale Supérieure, served at the Archives nationales (1830–1851), and was professor of history at the Collège de France from 1838 to 1852.

nodes.label: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
nodes.summary: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya was an Indology scholar who studied under Ramamohana Brahmachari, Shivakumar Shastry, and others at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Mysore. He taught at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College.

nodes.label: Catherine Cornille
nodes.summary: Catherine Cornille works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at KU Leuven (~1979–1989) and the University of Hawaiʻi (~1983–1984), and served as Associate Professor of Comparative Theology at Boston College (~2004).

nodes.label: Manshi Kiyozawa
nodes.summary: Manshi Kiyozawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Ernest Fenollosa and Mokurai Takeda at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He taught at Toyo University and became the founding president of Otani University in 1901.

nodes.label: Ernest Fenollosa
variants: アーネスト・フランシスコ・フェノロサ
nodes.jawiki: アーネスト・フェノロサ
nodes.summary: Ernest Fenollosa was a philosopher, Japanologist, and historian who studied at Harvard and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1878) and served as curator of the Oriental Collection at the MFA Boston (1890–1896).

nodes.label: Kyoto Ordinary Middle School
variants: Jinjō Middle School 尋常中学校

nodes.label: Khenpo Gangshar
nodes.summary: Khenpo Gangshar (1925–1980) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Shechen Monastery under Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drime Lekpe Lodro. He served as senior teacher at Shechen Monastery and founding dean at Surmang Monastery (~1957–1958).

nodes.label: Gembo Dorji
nodes.summary: Gembo Dorji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Jigme Choedra. He completed his education at Tango Buddhist Institute, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo.

nodes.id: P:Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drime Lekpe Lodro
nodes.label: Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drime Lekpe Lodro
variants: Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drimé Lekpé Lodrö

nodes.label: Khakyab Dorje
variants: 15世カルマパ・カキャブ・ドルジェ
nodes.summary: Khakyab Dorje was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and the 1st Beru Khyentse Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Karuna Kusalasaya
nodes.native: กรุณา กุศลาสัย
nodes.summary: Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahamakut Buddhist University.

nodes.label: Fafang
nodes.summary: Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He held a position as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Satiranjan Sen
nodes.summary: Satiranjan Sen was an Indologist and sinologist who studied at Peking University, founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti, and served as a research scholar and junior research fellow at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.id: P:Rong tha Dam chos rgya mtsho
nodes.label: Rong tha Dam chos rgya mtsho
variants: Rong tha Dam chos rgya mtsho

nodes.label: Yuexia
nodes.summary: Yuexia was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Huayan University and served as a teacher there.

nodes.label: Dixian
nodes.summary: Dixian (1858–1932) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu from circa 1882 to 1886 and later served as abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

nodes.label: Vladimir Kalyanov
nodes.summary: Vladimir Kalyanov (1908–2001) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Institute for Philosophy, Literature and History in Leningrad and under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy, and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts from circa 1938 to 2001.

nodes.label: Nicholas Roerich
variants: ニコライ・コンスタンティノヴィチ・リョーリフ
nodes.jawiki: ニコライ・リョーリフ
nodes.description: Russian painter, writer, archaeologist and philosopher (1874–1947)
nodes.summary: Working in history/archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and religious studies, Roerich studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts. He directed the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts and founded Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute.

nodes.label: Evgenij Ivanovich Kychanov
nodes.image: Portrait photo of Evgeny Ivanovich Kychanov.JPG
nodes.summary: Evgenij Ivanovich Kychanov worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University, he served as head of the St. Petersburg branch of the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts in 2002.

nodes.label: New Asia College
variants: New Asia College der Chinesischen Universität Hongkong
New Asia College in Hong Kong
香港中文大学新亜書院

nodes.id: P:Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
nodes.label: Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
John Lockwood Kipling
nodes.image: John Lockwood Kipling és Rudyard Kipling.jpg
nodes.summary: John Lockwood Kipling worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He taught at Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (~1865–1875), was Principal of the National College of Arts (1875–1893), and served as Curator of Lahore Museum (1875–1893).

nodes.label: Alfonsa Ferrari
nodes.summary: Alfonsa Ferrari was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1937–1941) under Giuseppe Tucci and Carlo Formichi, later conducting post-graduate research there from approximately 1941 to 1954.

nodes.label: Jacques Bacot
nodes.image: Tchraker lama, Jacques Bacot et moines.png
nodes.summary: Jacques Bacot (1877–1965) was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot in 1908. He held teaching posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1919–1938), the University of Paris (~1936–1958), and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1945–1954).

nodes.label: Yu Daoquan
nodes.summary: Yu Daoquan worked in Tibetology and linguistics, studying at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1934–1936). He was a professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China from 1953 to 1992.

nodes.label: Lorna Srimathie Dewaraja
nodes.summary: Lorna Srimathie Dewaraja worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Ceylon and University of London (~1963–1966), later serving as Associate Professor of History at the University of Ceylon and faculty at the University of Colombo (~1978).

nodes.label: Senarat Wijayasundara
nodes.summary: Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

nodes.label: Dorje Geshe
variants: Duojie gexi zunzhe 多傑格西尊者

nodes.label: Wilhelm Wundt
variants: ヴィルヘルム・ヴント
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・ヴント
nodes.description: German physician, physiologist, philosopher and professor (1832–1920)
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Wundt worked in philosophy. He studied at Tübingen (~1851–1852), Heidelberg (~1852–1855), and Berlin (~1856), and later held posts at the University of Zurich (1857), University of Leipzig (1858), and Heidelberg University (1864).

nodes.label: Edvard Westermarck
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・ウェスターマーク
nodes.summary: Edvard Westermarck worked in philosophy. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1881-1889) and held academic posts at the London School of Economics (~1904-1930) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918-1932).

nodes.label: Dedong Wei
nodes.summary: Dedong Wei is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Renmin University of China around 1995–1998, where he became an associate professor of religious studies around 1998.

nodes.label: Claude Jacques
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and history/archaeology, Jacques studied under George Cœdès (~1960–1969). He taught epigraphy and history at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1970–1998) and served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1989–1992).

nodes.label: Amy Paris Langenberg
nodes.image: Amy Paris Langenberg in the video 'Accomplished women Female leadership and reproductive health in the Bhikṣuņī-Vinaya'.png
nodes.summary: Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She received her PhD from Columbia University and became an assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College around 2008.

nodes.id: P:sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan
nodes.label: sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan
variants: sGangs ru tshul khrims rgyal mtshan

nodes.label: Marsha Weidner
nodes.summary: Marsha Weidner is a scholar of Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from UC Berkeley. She held an assistant professorship at the University of Virginia and later became Professor of the History of Art at Kansas.

nodes.label: Damdin Badaraev
nodes.summary: Damdin Badaraev is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

nodes.label: Adhémard Leclère
nodes.summary: Adhémard Leclère worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Résident de France at Kratié in the French Protectorate of Cambodia and was vice-president of the Société Ethnologique de Paris, which he founded.

nodes.label: Douglas J. Penick
nodes.summary: Douglas J. Penick is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Princeton University (~1962–1966) and studied under the traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1971.

nodes.label: Tokiyoshi Hōjō
nodes.summary: Tokiyoshi Hōjō studied at the University of Tokyo (~1881–1885). Over his career, he held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1894–1896), Kanazawa University (~1898–1908), and Tohoku University (~1913–1917).

nodes.label: Giovanni Gentile
variants: ジョヴァンニ・ジェンティーレ
nodes.jawiki: ジョヴァンニ・ジェンティーレ
nodes.description: Italian philosopher, educator, fascist theoretician and politician (1875-1944)
nodes.summary: Giovanni Gentile was an Italian philosopher who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and the University of Pisa. He held professorships at the universities of Palermo, Pisa, and Rome, and was president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

nodes.label: 14th Shamarpa Mipham Chökyi Lodrö
nodes.summary: Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Kalu Rinpoche in 1973, and Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

nodes.label: First Zen Institute of America
variants: Kyoto branch of the First Institute of America
First Zen Institute of America in Japan
First Zen Institute of America in Kyoto

nodes.label: King's College, Cambridge
variants: ケンブリッジ大学キングズコレッジ
ケンブリッジ大学キングズ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Bart Gruzalski
nodes.summary: Bart Gruzalski specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Maryland, College Park, and served as a professor of philosophy at Northeastern University.

nodes.label: Emmanuel College, Toronto
variants: Emmanuel College of Victoria University in the University of Toronto

nodes.label: Tao Pan
nodes.summary: Tao Pan works in Indology and linguistics. He completed a BA at Fudan University in 2010 and earned a Magister Artium from the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Nicholas Witkowski
nodes.summary: Nicholas Witkowski works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Stanford University by 2015 and was a research fellow at the University of Tokyo (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Yingguang Qu
nodes.summary: Yingguang Qu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School and under teachers including Nordan Hutuktu, Puren Bai, Nona Hutuktu, and Gangkar Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Yuanxing Guo
nodes.summary: Yuanxing Guo was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Gongga Rinpoche and Gangkar Rinpoche. Guo held posts at the Jinling Scriptural Press and as a researcher at the Institute of Chinese Buddhist Culture.

nodes.label: Institute of Chinese Buddhist Culture
variants: Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism (Zhongguo Fojiao Wenhua Yanjiusuo 中國佛教文化研究所)

nodes.label: Nianzu Huang
nodes.summary: Nianzu Huang worked in Buddhist studies, studying at Beijing Institute of Technology and under Lianju Xia, Gongga Rinpoche, and Hsu Yun. He headed the Central Broadcasting System and became a professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications around 1955.

nodes.label: Voice of America
variants: Tibetan Broadcast Service for Voice of America

nodes.label: René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz
nodes.summary: René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz (1923–1959) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Vienna (Dr. phil. 1946–1949; Habilitation ~1953–1955), Berlin, SOAS (~1950–1953), and LSE under Koppers, Haekel, Bleichsteiner, Tucci, and Rock, later serving at Weltmuseum Wien (1958).

nodes.label: Pieter Hendrik Pott
nodes.summary: Pieter Hendrik Pott worked in Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He served as a curator at Museum Volkenkunde (~1940–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

nodes.label: Constantin Regamey
nodes.summary: Constantin Regamey (1907–1982) was an indologist, tibetologist, and linguist educated at Warsaw (PhD ~1935) and Paris. He taught at Warsaw (1936), Fribourg (1945), and Lausanne (1945; extraordinary professor 1949–1957), and served as Swiss Asia Society president (1962–1971).

nodes.label: Lajos Ligeti
nodes.summary: Specializing in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Lajos Ligeti studied at Eötvös Loránd University and in Paris under Paul Pelliot. He held academic posts in Inner Asian studies at Pázmány Péter Catholic University and Eötvös Loránd University.

nodes.label: Chogye Shabdrung
nodes.summary: Chogye Shabdrung (b. 1981) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 and under Sonam Gyatso.

nodes.label: Krisztina Teleki
nodes.description: (1978–) Hungarian literary translator, linguist, orientalist, tibetologist and mongolist
nodes.summary: Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her MA and served as a research fellow at Eötvös Loránd University.

nodes.label: Immanuel Kant
nodes.summary: Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) was a philosopher who studied at the Collegium Fridericianum and the University of Königsberg (1740–1746). He later held the chair of logic and metaphysics at Königsberg from 1770.

nodes.label: August Conrady
variants: アウグスト・コンラーディ
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・コンラーディ (中国学者)
nodes.summary: August Conrady specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Würzburg and Leipzig, later holding academic posts at the University of Leipzig from 1891 to 1922 and at Peking University (1903–1904).

nodes.label: Berthold Laufer
variants: ベルトルト・ラウファー
nodes.image: Annual report of the Director to the Board of Trustees for the year .. (1933) (17811378703).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ベルトルト・ラウファー
nodes.summary: Working in Sinology, Tibetology, and Central Asian studies, Laufer studied at Berlin and Leipzig under August Conrady (PhD). He held positions at the American Museum of Natural History, lectured at Columbia (1905–1907), and became curator at the Field Museum in 1907.

nodes.label: Bruno Schindler
variants: ブルーノ・シンドラー
nodes.summary: Bruno Schindler was a Sinologist who studied under August Conrady (~1912–1919). He founded the journal Asia Major in 1923 and later worked as a Verlagslektor at Lund Humphries (~1939–1964).

nodes.label: Johannes Schubert
nodes.summary: Johannes Schubert worked in Tibetology and Sinology, studying at the University of Leipzig under teachers including Conrady, Francke, and Franke. He served at the Leipzig University Library (~1927-1954) and held a Tibetology chair at Leipzig University (1960-1962).

nodes.label: Stanisław Schayer
nodes.summary: Stanisław Schayer (1899–1941) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 1922, he founded and became a professor at the University of Warsaw, and was later a member of the Warsaw Scientific Society and Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences.

nodes.label: Jan Jaworski
nodes.summary: Jan Jaworski was a scholar of sinology, japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Warsaw under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski.

nodes.label: Ludwik Skurzak
nodes.summary: Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer and served as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.

nodes.label: Maryla Falk
nodes.description: Polish indologist and historian of religions
nodes.summary: Maryla Falk (1906–1980) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She held a post at the University of Warsaw from circa 1934 to 1939.

nodes.label: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz
nodes.summary: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (circa 1919–1924). He later held posts at Lviv, Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, and the University of Warsaw (circa 1953–1971).

nodes.label: Paul Ekman
nodes.summary: Paul Ekman (1934–2025) studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He held a long-term academic post at the University of California, San Francisco (~1960–2004).

nodes.label: Somchai Kusalacitto
nodes.summary: Somchai Kusalacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

nodes.label: François Jacob
nodes.summary: François Jacob earned doctorates at the University of Paris (~1944–1947) and Sorbonne University (~1950–1954). He held posts at the Centre National de Transfusion Sanguine, the Pasteur Institute (from 1960), and the Collège de France (from 1964).

nodes.label: Stephen Addiss
nodes.summary: Stephen Addiss was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan (1971–1977). He served as professor of art history at Kansas (1977–1992) and Richmond (1992–2013).

nodes.label: Juan Wu
nodes.summary: Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Cardiff University under the supervision of Max Deeg, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Laurence Austine Waddell
nodes.summary: Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies after earning a medical degree at the University of Glasgow. He served in the British and Indian military services, taught at Kolkata's Medical College, and was Professor of Tibetan at UCL (1906–1908).

nodes.label: Dzogchen Monastery
variants: monastische Kolleg Shri Singha des Dzogchen-Klosters

nodes.label: Yuanying
nodes.summary: Yuanying was a Buddhist studies figure who served as abbot of Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan Temples, and as councilor and president of the Buddhist Association of China. He also founded and served as president of the Yuanming Lengyan School (1945).

nodes.label: Marian Ury
nodes.summary: Marian Ury specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She completed her undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and served as professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at the University of California, Davis (1969–1995).

nodes.label: Seán McLoughlin
nodes.summary: Seán McLoughlin works in religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Manchester and was a lecturer in South Asian, Islamic, and religious studies at the University of Leeds, attested in 2005.

nodes.label: Eric J. Sharpe
nodes.summary: Eric J. Sharpe was a religious studies scholar and Indologist who studied at the University of Manchester and Uppsala University. He held the First Chair of Religious Studies at the University of Sydney (1977–1996) and a professorship at Uppsala University (1978–1981).

nodes.label: Phra Rajavaramuni
nodes.native: พระราชวรมุนี
nodes.summary: Phra Rajavaramuni studied philosophy at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and education at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. He was attested in 2012 as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

nodes.label: Tampalawela Dhammaratana
nodes.summary: Tampalawela Dhammaratana is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kelaniya, University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

nodes.label: Liu Liqian
nodes.summary: Liu Liqian (1910–2008) was a Tibetologist. He held posts at West China Union University (ca. 1944–1949), the State Council of the PRC's translation administration department (ca. 1952–1958), and the Ethnic Publishing House.

nodes.label: West China Union University
variants: Border Area Institute of Research of the West China University

nodes.id: I:State Council of the People's Republic of China
nodes.label: State Council of the People's Republic of China
Genzao
nodes.summary: Genzao was a practitioner and scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche, and trained at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950.

nodes.id: I:Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
nodes.label: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
variants: Beijing Institute of Post and Telecommunications

nodes.id: P:lcang can sras bsod nams rgyal po
nodes.label: lcang can sras bsod nams rgyal po
Charles Alfred Bell
nodes.summary: Charles Alfred Bell worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He completed his studies at Winchester College from circa 1884 to 1889 and at New College from circa 1889 to 1891.

nodes.label: Augustus William Heyde
nodes.description: German missionary to Tibetans in Northern India; b. Wilhelm Heide, Feb. 16, 1825; later changed surname to Heyde; d. Aug. 27, 1907

nodes.label: John Claude White
nodes.description: British engineer, civil servant and photographer in India (1853–1918)
nodes.summary: John Claude White worked in Tibetology and archaeology. He studied at the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876) and was appointed Assistant Engineer in the Bengal Public Works Department in 1876.

nodes.label: Edward Sapir
nodes.summary: Edward Sapir was a linguist who studied at Columbia University under Franz Boas and Wilhelm Wundt. He headed the Geological Survey of Canada's Division of Anthropology (~1910–1925) and taught at the University of Chicago and Yale University.

nodes.label: Friedrich Schleiermacher
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュライアマハー
nodes.description: German theologian, philosopher, and biblical scholar (1768-1834)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Schleiermacher was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Halle-Wittenberg (~1787–1789). He later held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1804–1807) and the University of Berlin (~1810–1834).

nodes.label: Józef Szczepan Kowalewski
nodes.summary: Józef Szczepan Kowalewski was a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After studying at Vilnius and Kazan, he became a professor and rector at Kazan Federal University before holding a professorship at the University of Warsaw.

nodes.label: Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk
nodes.summary: Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Palyul Choktrul Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Akyong Tokden Lodrö Gyatso.

nodes.label: Bhikshuni Longlian
nodes.summary: Bhikshuni Longlian was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Fazun beginning in 1939 and also trained under traditional teacher Nenghai Shi.

nodes.label: Guankong
nodes.summary: Guankong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and was appointed professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

nodes.label: D. Neil Schmid
nodes.summary: D. Neil Schmid is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, Waseda University, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he pursued doctoral studies under Victor H. Mair.

nodes.label: Rachel H. Pang
nodes.summary: Rachel H. Pang specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia and was attested in 2019 as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College.

nodes.label: Sangseraima Ujeed
nodes.summary: Sangseraima Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2013–2018) and held a postdoctoral fellowship in Buddhist Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2018–2020).

nodes.label: Mother Sayamagyi
nodes.summary: Mother Sayamagyi was a teacher in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Sayagyi U Ba Khin and eventually succeeded him.

nodes.label: Sayagyi U Ba Khin
nodes.description: Burmese civil servant and Vipassana meditation master
nodes.summary: Sayagyi U Ba Khin was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher who studied under Saya Thetgyi (~1937–1945). He founded the International Meditation Centre and taught students including Satya Narayan Goenka, Ruth Denison, and Mother Sayamagyi.

nodes.label: Sokatsu Shaku
nodes.summary: Sokatsu Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kosen Imakita (1889) and Soyen Shaku (1893–1898), later founding Tokyo Ryobokai (1901), the Ryobokai Dojo of North America (1906), and Ningen Zen Kyodan.

nodes.label: Peter Connolly
nodes.summary: Peter Connolly works in religious studies and Indology. He completed his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and was appointed Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

nodes.label: Lynn Thomas
nodes.summary: Lynn Thomas works in Indology and religious studies. Thomas earned a BA and MA at Lancaster University and completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford in 1987, later serving as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Agvan Dorjiev
nodes.summary: Agvan Dorjiev was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang (1880–1888), earning the Geshe-Lharampa degree. He founded Datsan Gunzechoinei and taught the 13th Dalai Lama and Geshe Wangyal.

nodes.id: I:Lille University of Science and Technology
nodes.label: Lille University of Science and Technology
P. Pratap Kumar
nodes.summary: P. Pratap Kumar is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as a Professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal (attested 2010) and as a Visiting Professor at Colorado College (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Heinrich R. Zimmer
nodes.summary: Heinrich R. Zimmer was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Wilhelm Schulze (~1909–1913) and held posts at the University of Greifswald (~1920–1924) and Heidelberg University (~1924–1938).

nodes.label: Eiichi Makino
nodes.summary: Eiichi Makino (1878–1970) worked in philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1900–1903) and later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1938), Shiraume Gakuen Junior College (~1953–1965), Kyushu University, Tohoku University, and Chuo University.

nodes.label: Shigemitsu Dando
nodes.summary: Shigemitsu Dando (1913–2012) studied under Seiichiro Ono at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University, and the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz (~1889–1893) and Karl Foy.

nodes.label: Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal
nodes.summary: Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the universities of Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, and later held a post at Heidelberg University from circa 1836 to 1845.

nodes.label: Shenphen Nangwa
nodes.summary: Shenphen Nangwa (1871–1927) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Mipam Gyatso. He taught at Dzogchen Shri Sengha, became the first khenpo at Dzongsar Monastery, and founded Dzongsar Shedra.

nodes.label: Patrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Patrul Rinpoche (1808–1887) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu (~1828–1843) and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught figures such as Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

nodes.label: Denise Bernot
nodes.summary: Denise Bernot was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the École des chartes and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes. She held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from circa 1960 to 1989.

nodes.label: Georg Ruppelt
nodes.image: Georg Ruppelt Direktor der Gottfried-Wilhelm-Leibniz Bibliothek anläßlich der Buchvorstellung Alles über Wikipedia im Werner Kraft Vortragssaal.jpg

nodes.label: Sven Hedin
nodes.description: Swedish geographer, topographer, explorer, photographer, travel writer and illustrator (1865-1952)
nodes.summary: Sven Hedin (1865–1952) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Stockholm University, Uppsala University, the University of Halle-Wittenberg, and the University of Berlin under Ferdinand von Richthofen.

nodes.label: Staatsgalerie Stuttgart
variants: Württembergische Museum der Bildenden Künste in Stuttgart

nodes.label: Eileen Power
nodes.summary: Eileen Power (1889–1940) was a historian who studied at Girton College and the University of Paris. From circa 1921 to 1940, she held posts at the London School of Economics and the University of London.

nodes.label: James Darmesteter
nodes.jawiki: ジャーム・ダルメステテール
nodes.summary: James Darmesteter worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault and Michel Bréal at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, later holding posts there (~1877-1894) and at the Collège de France (1885-1894).

nodes.label: Marcel Cohen
nodes.summary: Marcel Cohen was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He served on the faculties of the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1919–1954) and the University of Paris (1920–1954).

nodes.label: Matteo Bartoli
